articles.title: Après un lancement chaotique, Google rattrape ses Googlebook à coups de correctifs
articles.text:
Google a dévoilé le Googlebook en mai comme l’héritier du Chromebook, avec un système dérivé d’Android et l’ambition affichée de se mesurer au MacBook Air. En France, les premières machines sont arrivées le 5 octobre, de 1 099 euros pour le modèle de HP à 1 399 euros chez Asus. Un peu plus d’un mois après, la firme de Mountain View déploie sa mise à jour de novembre.
Des PC qui redémarraient sans prévenir
La mise à jour aligne 31 correctifs, sécurité comprise, dont plusieurs visent le micrologiciel, qui provoquait des redémarrages inattendus. Une mise à jour interrompue pouvait aussi enfermer l’ordinateur dans une boucle de redémarrage (de quoi transformer un portable neuf en presse-papiers haut de gamme). Tous les Googlebook embarquent au moins 16 Go de mémoire vive et une puce dédiée à l’IA de plus de 40 TOPS. Google revoit pourtant la façon dont l’IA embarquée occupe cette mémoire, afin de stabiliser le multitâche sur les modèles d’Acer, d’Asus et de Lenovo. Le navigateur gagne enfin en stabilité lorsqu’une session accumule les onglets.
Avec des écouteurs Bluetooth, le son se décalait de l’image sur le HP Googlebook 14 et sur le modèle de Dell, réservé pour l’instant au marché américain. Les appareils auditifs Bluetooth peuvent désormais servir de sortie audio. La mise à jour corrige également une barre des tâches qui disparaissait après le débranchement de plusieurs écrans externes, ainsi qu’un son de Netflix qui continuait de jouer sur un moniteur resté noir. Le terminal Linux gère mieux les sessions SSH et préserve les fichiers de l’environnement Linux pendant les mises à jour du système.
Le déploiement se fait par vagues sur les cinq modèles de la gamme, signés Acer, Asus, Dell, HP et Lenovo. Pour vérifier sa disponibilité, il faut passer par les Paramètres, rubrique Système, puis le menu des mises à jour.
Un mois à rattraper le retard sur ChromeOS
Dès les premières semaines, des testeurs ont relevé des fonctions manquantes et des régressions par rapport à ChromeOS, le système que le Googlebook doit remplacer. La configuration initiale réclamait trop d’étapes et laissait un code QR affiché à l’écran une fois le téléphone associé. Surtout, les smartphones Samsung restaient exclus des fonctions de continuité, comme la reprise d’une tâche d’un appareil à l’autre ou la synchronisation des notifications.
Google a réagi avec une mise à jour des services Google Play pour alléger la configuration, et a annoncé la compatibilité des Galaxy sous Android 17 et One UI 9.0. En octobre, Chrome 156 a apporté quatorze améliorations pensées pour ces machines, pendant que d’autres défauts du navigateur disparaissaient discrètement, sans mise à jour visible pour l’utilisateur. Une correction a aussi mis fin au scintillement des applications web installées.
Google a déjà fixé à la mi-2034 la fin des mises à jour de ChromeOS, au profit du Googlebook. Aux États-Unis, la gamme démarre à 899 dollars, tandis qu’en France l’entrée de gamme s’affiche à 1 099 euros avec l’HP Googlebook 14.

articles.title: Zipline recauda USD 1.500 millones y acelera su alianza de entregas con drones con Walmart a 300 nuevos sitios
articles.text:
Zipline, una empresa de drones de entrega con sede en California, anunció el 5 de noviembre una ronda de USD 1.500 millones que la valora en USD 21.500 millones. El mismo día, Walmart informó que sumará 300 sitios de entregas en Estados Unidos, frente a los 21 que operan hoy entre ambas empresas.
La ronda fue liderada por Paradigm, WCM Investment Management y Layer Global. También participaron Valor Equity Partners, Fidelity, Uber, Tiger Global, J.P. Morgan, ARK Invest y Salesforce Ventures, según el comunicado de Zipline. La empresa dijo que usará el dinero para ampliar sus fábricas en Estados Unidos y contratar más personal, con el objetivo de construir una red nacional de entregas con drones.
El acuerdo con Walmart es de varios años y, según ambas compañías, tiene margen para crecer más allá de los 300 sitios. Walmart y Zipline trabajan juntas desde 2021, según TechCrunch.
Cómo creció el valor de Zipline en diez meses
El sitio especializado DroneXL señaló que la valuación actual equivale a 2,8 veces los USD 7.600 millones que Zipline tenía en enero. La nueva cifra también supera los USD 20.000 millones que Bloomberg informó en septiembre, cuando surgieron las negociaciones.
Según DroneXL, la empresa había cerrado en enero una ronda de más de USD 600 millones y sumó una extensión de USD 200 millones en marzo. Con la ronda actual, el capital captado en diez meses alcanza los USD 2.300 millones.
Zipline también informó que su participación en los ingresos por entregas pasó del 10,8% al 34,9% entre marzo y octubre de este año, según TechCrunch. La compañía afirmó que la nueva financiación busca elevar todavía más esa cifra.
Walmart ya completó más de 2 millones de entregas con drones
Walmart afirmó en su comunicado que su programa es el mayor entre los minoristas de Estados Unidos y que superó los 2 millones de entregas. Los clientes ven la opción en la aplicación o en el sitio de la cadena si su dirección está dentro del alcance, y el pedido llega en un plazo de hasta 30 minutos.
El programa de Walmart no depende solo de Zipline. DroneXL recogió que, junto con Wing, la cadena operaba en 66 tiendas de cuatro estados cuando anunció su entrega número un millón, en mayo. Wing tiene un contrato para más de 270 ubicaciones hasta 2027.
Los 300 sitios nuevos de Zipline equivalen a más de cuatro veces esa huella, según el cálculo de DroneXL. Hasta ahora, la actividad de Zipline con Walmart se concentraba en el área de Dallas-Fort Worth y en un centro cercano a la sede de la cadena, en Arkansas.
Los drones domiciliarios de Zipline, llamados Platform 2, cargan hasta unos 3,6 kilos y llegan a clientes en un radio de unos 16 km, según TechCrunch. Los modelos Platform 1, más grandes, hacen entregas de largo alcance de hasta unos 193 km de ida y vuelta.
Zipline nació en 2014 y empezó entregando sangre en Ruanda en 2016. Hoy reparte alimentos, productos minoristas, agrícolas y de salud en cinco países de África, varias ciudades de Estados Unidos y Japón. En 2022 obtuvo de la Administración Federal de Aviación la certificación que autoriza entregas comerciales de largo alcance.

articles.title: ASRock Radeon RX 7900 XT/XTX VBIOS Update Bricks Some Cards
articles.text:
Friday, November 6th 2026
ASRock Radeon RX 7900 XT/XTX VBIOS Update Bricks Some Cards
When ASRock joined the group of AIBs patching Radeon RX 7900 XT/XTX GPUs late last month, everything seemed fine for a few days. However, multiple users are now reporting that their ASRock GPUs have been bricked after updating the firmware with the latest VBIOS. ASRock has released VBIOS updates for ten of its Radeon RX 7000 series graphics cards, joining Sapphire and GIGABYTE. The new firmware, version 1.0.5, was made available on ASRock's support pages on October 29 and includes updates for the RX 7600 XT Challenger and Steel Legend, RX 7700 XT Challenger, RX 7800 XT Challenger and Steel Legend, RX 7900 XT Phantom Gaming (including the White version), and the RX 7900 XTX Phantom Gaming and Taichi, along with the Taichi White.
However, several users have reported that VBIOS version 1.0.5 bricked their cards. The issue occurs when users start the ASRVBFlash 1.0.5 utility; Windows begins its reboot sequence, and the system then fails to boot. A solution to this problem appears to be reinstalling an older VBIOS, which some users have downloaded from TechPowerUp's VBIOS hosting. This can help if your PC is bricked by any VBIOS update, and you need to find an older version to flash.ASRock is reportedly removing VBIOS version 1.0.5 from its download pages, but it is still accessible through FTP connections, indicating that it is only temporarily hidden. We are awaiting an update from ASRock, but in the meantime, those who haven't updated their VBIOS and have a Radeon RX 7900 XT/XTX GPU should be a little more patient. If readers recall, most of AMD's add-in board partners issued new VBIOS security updates for Radeon RX 7600, RX 7600 XT, RX 7650 GRE, RX 7700 XT, RX 7800 XT, RX 7900 GRE, RX 7900 XT, and RX 7900 XTX models as a security fix, but we still don't know what the original vulnerability was.
Sources:

articles.title: “Does Meta think we can’t read?” Meta abandons sketchy commercial terms update.
articles.text:
After weeks of backlash—and a failed attempt to quell it—Meta has indefinitely delayed plans to update its commercial terms and require Meta Business account users to allow extensive AI training on external websites linked on Facebook.
“We’re pausing the changes as we continue to engage with stakeholders and take our time to get this right. In the meantime, our existing terms remain in effect,” a Meta spokesperson told Reuters.
Soon after Meta notified business account holders of the upcoming changes, legal experts warned Nieman Lab that the vague language could allow the company to ignore scraping preferences specified in robots.txt files and exhaustively crawl vast amounts of off-Facebook content for AI training. Since virtually every news publisher has a Facebook page, Nieman Lab sounded the alarm that Meta could potentially avoid millions in licensing fees if the TOS update happened as planned.
Ars broke down the changes after Meta announced them, noting that businesses—including news publishers involved in drawn-out legal battles over unwanted AI scraping—had no way to opt out. To keep a business Facebook page, they had to allow Meta to crawl any linked external sites. The terms even required publishers to create test credentials so Meta’s bots could reliably bypass paywalls.
Meta faced global scrutiny
The changes were initially supposed to take effect on October 30. But Meta pushed that date back to November 20 amid pushback from Facebook users, courts, and regulators around the world. Courts in Brazil and Norway issued preliminary injunctions blocking the terms after organizations in those countries promptly filed lawsuits, Nieman Lab reported.
The United Kingdom’s Competition and Markets Authority also opened a formal investigation into whether Meta was exploiting a dominant position to seize valuable AI training data. In a LinkedIn post, Theo Bamber, chief executive of the UK’s News Media Association, pointed to “the continued arrogance of this company to think everyone will just be OK with its actions” as “staggering.”

articles.title: Elegoo M1 Ultra review: A good first entry into the scanner market
articles.text:
Tom's Hardware Verdict
The Elegoo M1 Ultra has a lot going for it, but it is not a standalone system. You’ll need to combine it with a powerful laptop to process the scanning data into anything useful. The good news it can be tethered via Wi-Fi.
Reasons to buy
- + Easy to calibrate
- + Long battery life
- + Onboard screen
Reasons to avoid
- - Turntable not included
- - Most projects require multiple scans
- - Needs a high end laptop for best results
Why you can trust Tom's Hardware
Our expert reviewers spend hours testing and comparing products and services so you can choose the best for you. Find out more about how we test.
The M1 Ultra is Elegoo’s first entry into the 3D scanner market. It is a feature-rich scanner with five scanning modes, four blue light laser modes, and a NIR binocular structured light mode. Most importantly, the scanner has a 3-in color touch screen and long battery life. It even includes a spare rechargeable battery, so you’re always prepared.
The scanner can’t run without a fairly high end PC or Mac for processing power. It will need to be tethered to the laptop with a UBS-C cable or connected via Wi-Fi. I was able to get about five feet away from my subject in a harsh RF environment. I didn’t test it further than that, so it may go farther. The cable connection provides the fastest connectivity, making tethered scanning worth the hassle.
The scanner’s output rivals any of the scanners I’ve tested, but it did require a little extra work to get there. At a current price of $1,599 at Elegoo, the M1 Ultra has features not found in other scanners at this price point.
Specifications: Elegoo M1 Ultra
| Scanning Mode | Blue Laser | NIR Infrared Binocular Structured Light | 
| Light Type | Single, 7, and 34-Line Laser | NIR (Near-Infrared) | 
| Accuracy | Up to 0.02 mm | Up to .05mm/m | 
| 3D Resolution | 0.05-2mm | 0.1-2mm | 
| Working Distance | 200mm-600mm | Between 170 and 1200 mm | 
| Min Scan Volume | 5 x 5 x 5 mm | 170mm-1200mm | 
| Scan Speed (Standalone) | ≤ 100fps | ≤ 30fps | 
| Alignment | 170mm-1200mm | Geometry/Texture | 
| Connectivity | Wired USB, Optional Wi-Fi | Row 8 - Cell 2 | 
| Color Texture | Supported | Row 9 - Cell 2 | 
| Output Format | OBJ/STL/PLY/ASC | Row 10 - Cell 2 | 
| Operating System | Windows or Mac | Row 11 - Cell 2 | 
| Release Date | October 29, 2026 | Row 12 - Cell 2 | 
| Pricing | $1,699 | Row 13 - Cell 2 | 
Included in the Box: Elegoo M1 Ultra
The Elegoo M1 Ultra comes with a nice hard case for travel, with a padded interior to protect the scanner, glass calibration board, spare battery, NIR filters, and a USB-C cable. Also included are a lens cleaning cloth and a packet of marker dots. Noticeably absent is a turntable for scanning smaller objects. (We borrowed a turntable from another scanner during this test.)
Design of the Elegoo M1 Ultra
The Elegoo M1 Ultra weighs 511g (1.12lbs) with its battery installed. It has a rubber grip below the screen and is nicely balanced. Users with large hands may find their thumbs blocking the screen.
The onboard screen can be used to set the scanning parameters, start and stop scans, and monitor the scans as they progress. The 3-inch screen is small, but the UI is laid out perfectly. When setting parameters for a scan, the touch screen takes precedence over the tethered computer if you’re starting the scan from the scanner itself.
The business end of the scanner has a series of blue, white, and infrared LEDs, blue lasers, and cameras. The included NIR filters are needed when scanning outdoors or in harsh light conditions. The battery and the spare can be charged using a USB-C cable when unmounted, and can be charged from the computer when operating the scanner in USB mode. The battery life is excellent. Almost all of our testing was done with one charge of the battery and its spare.
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
Getting Started and Calibrating the Elegoo M1 Ultra
Calibrating the Elegoo M1 Ultra is fairly easy given its light weight and the easy-to-follow software. Using the glass calibration board, the scanner is aimed at various angles and heights, following the directions on screen. The software shows an image of where the scanner should be and an image of the scanner as you move it. You have to match the two before moving on to the next spot. Scanner calibration can be a chore, but calibrating the M1 Ultra was simple.
Installing the Software for Elegoo M1 Ultra
Elegoo Scan can be downloaded from Elegoo’s website for Windows and Mac. The software works and looks like CrealityScan, which is a good thing since both make cleaning up individual scans and stitching multiple scans together fairly easy. The software does require a bunch of memory, with the more, the merrier. I tried running the software on an older PC laptop which met the minimum requirements, except it had only 8 GB of RAM, and it was not enough.
Elegoo recommends a PC with Windows 10/11 (64-bit), an Intel Core i7 (13th Gen) or higher, an NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4060 or higher (8 GB VRAM), and 32 GB or more of RAM. For Mac, they recommend macOS 14 or later, with an Apple M4 or later, and 32 GB or more of RAM. Minimum specs for both are 16gb of RAM, with Windows 10/11 (64-bit), Intel Core i7 (7th Gen), and an Nvidia GPU (6 GB VRAM) for PC, and macOS 14 or later, with an Apple M2 CPU.
Blue Laser Line 3D Scanning with the Elegoo M1 Ultra
The Elegoo M1 Ultra has 4 blue laser scanning modes: 34 crossed laser lines for quick scanning, 7 parallel lines for finer details, 1 line for scanning deeper, more difficult-to-capture holes, and markerless. The fewer the lines, the more time the scans take. I should point out that the turntable in the photo was borrowed from the Creality Pika Scanner, which we reviewed previously.
One of my favorite use cases is scanning an item for import into a 3D printing project I am working on. I scanned a cheap 895 brushed motor commonly found in drills. The motor required several scans, and the M1 Ultra seemed to have trouble capturing the shinier parts of the object. Ultimately, I captured two scans that had enough data to be useful. The software has an automatic alignment tool which does a good job in most cases. In this case, it was baffled by the geometry. The manual alignment worked perfectly.
Manual alignment requires adding markers matching points on both images. You do not have to be super exact with the placement. The software will smooth out any overlaps.
Part of the mesh processing is hole filling. This also has an automatic and manual mode. Since the automatic mode was going to fill in the screw holes and cooling holes, I had to fill in the holes manually by clicking on them. This is a little tedious, but it worked well.
After hole filling, smoothing, and simplifying, I was able to export the file as an STL and open it in Tinkercad.
The size, and hole alignment were perfect for integrating the motor into a project.
This bust of Michelangelo’s David came with an early Creality scanner and has become my main test file. It took three scans for me to get a good model, which was a recurring theme with the Elegoo M1 Ultra.
Fortunately in this case, the auto alignment function worked perfectly.
Even with multiple scans, there were still a few holes to fill. One of these can be seen in the finished model in the smooth, flat area above David’s left ear.
Overall, the model generated is one of the best I’ve seen, and it printed extremely well once exported. The flaw at the bottom of the print was a bed adhesion issue rather than a problem with the model.
NIR 3D Scanning with the Elegoo M1 Ultra
Since I could not find a willing human victim…I mean, subject…to scan, I tried using the NIR mode to scan Clyde, our family’s favorite stuffed Clydesdale. This is a cautionary tale because 3D scanners in general have a tough time scanning black objects, as they absorb light rather than reflecting it.
The scans weren’t bad, but they did leave big holes where the mane and tail were too dark to read.
I was able to do a much better scan of Ali the Alligator. In NIR mode, the scanner is capable of 30fps. Even with the slower frame rate, the scanner was able to quickly capture Ali in two scans, without a ton of multiple passes. Each time you go over the same spot on an object, it’s possible to generate garbage data that has to be removed in the meshing process. The two scans align together automatically, and the finished model is pretty darn good.
The scanner does feature color texture mapping. Other than the mouth, where a large hole needed to be filled, the color mapping was spot on.
Bottom Line
The Elegoo M1 Ultra is a good scanner that has a good feature set for the price. The light weight, onboard screen, long battery life, and stable Wi-Fi connection make it a joy to use.
The ElegooScan software is fairly intuitive. It makes calibrating the scanner and turning the raw scans into usable models fairly easy. The Elegoo M1 Ultra did require multiple scans to get good coverage of objects, while other scanners I’ve tested could do it in one pass. The added complexity takes up a good deal of time and requires a fair amount of computer power, especially when cleaning up and aligning multiple scans. ElegooScan has the tools to make it work. Even with a pretty good model, you’ll likely also need a CAD program or other design tools to make the best use of the scans.
If you’d like to save a few bucks and get a still excellent scanner, check out the Creality Pika, which is currently $699. If you want a scanner with a little more horsepower, check out the Creality Sermoon S1, which retails for $2,069. Creality also makes the Sermoon P1, which can run completely untethered and retails for $3,299.
Denise Bertacchi is a Contributing Writer for Tom’s Hardware US, covering 3D printing. Denise has been crafting with PCs since she discovered Print Shop had clip art on her Apple IIe. She loves reviewing 3D printers because she can mix all her passions: printing, photography, and writing.

articles.title: Blue Origin presenta Northstar, su esperadísimo motor mucho más potente que los actuales y muchísimo más barato
articles.text:
Blue Origin tiene que intentar destacar después de que su plataforma de lanzamiento se incendiara con la explosión de un cohete New Glenn. La compañía de Jeff Bezos quiere demostrar que sigue siendo de las más punteras de la industria espacial. Por eso, acaba de presentar un motor para sus cohetes que promete ser mucho más potente, pero a un 25% del precio de fabricación habitual.
Northstar. Así se llama el motor que complementará y con el tiempo sustituirá al tradicional BE-4 de la primera etapa de los cohetes de Blue Origin. Tiene la mitad de piezas, un 30% menos de masa y alrededor del 65% de sus piezas se pueden imprimir en 3D, lo cual abarata muchísimo los costes. Con todo esto, la compañía espera poder llegar a montar cada motor en menos de un día.
En cuanto al combustible, el Northstar quemará metano líquido, igual que el BE-4, pero proporcionará un empuje mayor. Mientras que el de los motores tradicionales es de 290 toneladas de fuerza, el de la nueva propuesta de Blue Origin es de 324.
Una segunda propuesta. Además de este nuevo motor para la primera etapa de algunos de sus cohetes, Blue Origin ha anunciado también que están trabajando con una tercera etapa, llamada GS3. Esta funciona con hidrógeno y oxígeno, con el motor BE-7 que ya usan los módulos lunares de la compañía. Aunque cabe dentro de la interetapa y no resta volumen bajo la cofia, no la llevarán todos los cohetes. Aporta un tercer impulso para llegar más lejos, así que la incluirán aquellos que lleven cargas a la órbita geoestacionaria o fuera de la Tierra. Por ejemplo, sería ideal para la inyección translunar.
Combinaciones con la tercera etapa. La tercera etapa puede ser funcional con cualquier configuración de primera y segunda. Los cálculos se han hecho para un 7x2 y un 9x4. Con 7 motores BE-4 en la primera etapa y 2 BE-3U en la segunda, sumadas a la tercera etapa, se conseguiría llevar 8 toneladas a órbita geoestacionaria y 10 toneladas a inyección translunar. En cambio, con una versión de 9 motores BE-4 y 4 motores BE-3U se podrían llevar 14 y 20 toneladas respectivamente.
Materiales más ligeros. La tercera etapa está hecha de materiales como el composite, que aporta buen rendimiento, pero también es muy ligero. El problema es que las moléculas de hidrógeno son muy pequeños y permean fácilmente hacia fuera. En un principio existían dudas sobre si el composite podría retener posibles fugas cuando se aumente la presión. Por suerte, en las pruebas que se han realizado hasta el momento ha soportado un el 100% de la presión máxima de operación durante 2,5 horas e incluso un 150% durante 10 minutos.
Ya hay fecha. Por ahora, todos estos nuevos componentes están en fase de pruebas, aunque ya hay fecha para su debut. Si todo va bien, podrían incluirse la tercera etapa en los cohetes New Glenn en 2028. Con respecto al Northstar, aún no hay fecha. Lo que sí se sabe es que el BE-4 tradicional seguiría usándose en el Vulcan de ULA. Con los New Glenn debe aumentar su rendimiento, pues cada vez hay más clientes dispuestos a impulsar sus cargas útiles con este cohete. articles.title: Mamaearth parent Honasa's Q2 net profit rises 87%
articles.text:
Mamaearth parent Honasa's Q2 net profit rises 87%
The company reported a net profit of Rs 73.24 crore in Q2FY27. Revenue rose 36% YoY to Rs 731.18 crore.
Honasa Consumer, the parent company of beauty & personal care brand Mamaearth, registered an 87% year-on-year (YoY) rise in net profit for the second quarter of the current fiscal, while revenue rose 36% driven by strong growth across categories.
The company reported a net profit of Rs 73.24 crore in Q2FY27, compared with Rs 39.22 crore in the similar period of FY26. Revenue during the quarter was Rs 731.18 crore, compared with Rs 538.06 crore a year ago.
According to Honasa Consumer, the second quarter revenue growth is the highest it has recorded since its public listing in November 2023.
However, sequentially, profit fell from Rs 90.44 crore in the first quarter. Revenue in the first quarter was Rs 755.94 crore.
Honasa also operates the brands Dermacare and Aqualogica.
CEO Varun Alagh said, “At the brand level, each business is writing its own growth story. Mamaearth has sustained its high-teens growth, The Derma Co. continues to grow profitably. Our Younger Brands grew over 45% YoY, reflecting highlighting the potential of our emerging portfolio.”
He added that each brand has a distinct consumer, proposition and opportunity and the goal is to build a sustainable business in each category.
The omnichannel channel retailer noted that its offline business saw growth, with general trade expanding to over 3.2 lakh outlets and modern trade (large-format retail outlets) recording a 40% YoY growth in offtake.
“As we enter the next phase of growth, we will continue to push the boundaries of innovation, deepen our presence in core categories, and make our products accessible to more consumers across channels,” said Ghazal Alagh, CIO & Co-founder, Honasa Consumer.
For the six months of the fiscal year, the company reported a revenue of Rs 1,487.13 crore, a YoY growth of 31%. The net profit for the period was Rs 163.69 crore, a YoY rise of 103%.

articles.title: Details zu OneUI 9.5: Diese 2 Apps soll Samsung verbessern
articles.text:
Details zu OneUI 9.5: Diese 2 Apps soll Samsung verbessern
Ganz anders als bei iOS laufen Updates auf die nächste Android-Version. Während Apple eine neue Version sofort für alle kompatiblen Geräte freigibt, läuft der Rollout bei Android-Geräten selbst bei den einzelnen Herstellern fragmentiert. Bei Samsung profitieren beim Sprung auf Android 17 mit der OneUI-9-Oberfläche zunächst Top-Geräte. Später folgen dann ältere und günstigere Smartphones. Und doch ist das nächste Update bereits in Arbeit. OneUI 9.5 wird ebenfalls auf Android 17 basieren, aber neue Funktionen auf Smartphones bringen.
Es gibt auch schon erste Hinweise auf Apps, die neue Funktionen bekommen sollen. Eine davon ist der Samsung Kalender, die andere die Health-App.
OneUI 9.5: Mehr Übersicht im Samsung Kalender
Nach eigenen Angaben hat Sammobile Zugriff auf eine frühe Version der Kalender-App erhalten. Die Anwendung wird demnach nicht komplett erneuert, erhält aber ein paar praktische Designänderungen. So wandert der Such-Button vom oberen an den unteren Bildschirmrand und wird prominenter hervorgehoben. Wer drauf tippt, sieht in der Vorschau künftig bereits eingetragene Termine. Zuvor konnte man lediglich die Volltextsuche bedienen, nach vorgegeben Stichworten oder Einträge mit bestimmten Farbmarkierungen suchen.
In der Seitenleiste hat Samsung zudem die Menüpunkte neu gruppiert. Die Einträge Synchronisieren, Papierkorb und Einstellungen sind nun direkt mit den anderen Kalenderfunktionen geclustert. Die Einstellungen tauchten vorher nur als (obligatorisches) Zahnrad-Symbol aus, die anderen zwei Optionen waren unter der Liste mit den verknüpften Konten versteckt.
Health-App mit Journal-Funktionen in OneUI 9.5
Eine komplett neue Funktion bekommt die Health-App mit Mindful Note, wie ebenfalls Sammobile berichtet. Wie in einer Tagebuch-App können Nutzer:innen hier auf Tagesbasis über Gefühle und Erfahrungen schreiben. Dazu stehen die sogenannten “Everyday Moments” mit einer blanken Seite zur Verfügung. Wer Hilfe für den Anfang braucht, kann aber auch eine von vier Kategorien auswählen: “Über dich selbst”, “Beziehungen”, “Arbeit und Ziele”, “Was wäre, wenn?” Dieser unterstützen jeweils mit einleitenden Fragen.
Darüber hinaus passt Samsung auch das Aussehen der Health-App an. Die neu gestalte Startseite weist künftig auf die Tagebuch-Funktion hin, Grafiken erscheinen in gedeckter Farben und große Illustrationen zu Fitnessdaten werden künftig kleiner gehalten.
Wann genau OneUI 9.5 erscheint, ist noch nicht klar. Wahrscheinlich wird die neue Software auf den kommenden Top-Geräten der Galaxy-S-Serie installiert sein, die Samsung in der Regel zum Jahresanfang vorstellt. Das Update dürfte danach dann wie üblich zuerst auf der Vorgänger-Generation, also der S26-Serie und den aktuellen Foldables rund um das Galaxy Z Fold 8 landen.

articles.title: Le RGB MiniLED gagne du terrain, mais Panasonic fait un autre choix pour ses téléviseurs
articles.text:
Alors que le RGB MiniLED s'impose progressivement sur le marché des téléviseurs haut de gamme, Panasonic préfère miser sur le SQD MiniLED pour ses nouveaux modèles présentés au Japon. Un choix qu'il partage avec TCL et que le fabricant japonais vient de justifier en mettant notamment en avant la régularité des couleurs.
Hisense, Samsung et plusieurs autres fabricants ont fait du RGB MiniLED l'une de leurs principales innovations de 2026. Cette technologie, qui utilise des LED rouges, vertes et bleues pour le rétroéclairage, promet notamment des couleurs plus riches et une meilleure maîtrise de leur restitution. Panasonic a toutefois décidé de privilégier une autre évolution du MiniLED.
Le constructeur japonais a choisi le SQD MiniLED pour sa nouvelle gamme Viera X97C, une technologie déjà mise en avant par TCL sur son modèle haut de gamme X11L. Lors d'une présentation organisée au Japon le 5 novembre, Panasonic a pu expliquer les raisons de ce choix
Le SQD MiniLED comme porte étendard
La différence tient principalement à la manière dont le rétroéclairage produit ses couleurs. Là où le RGB MiniLED utilise trois couleurs de LED, le SQD MiniLED conserve des LED bleues associées à une feuille de points quantiques améliorée, qui convertit une partie de la lumière en rouge et en vert. Un filtre couleur à large gamut complète l'ensemble pour obtenir des couleurs plus pures.
Panasonic revendique ainsi une surface de gamut équivalente à environ 100 % du BT.2020, un espace colorimétrique particulièrement étendu. Cela représente une surface environ 25 % plus importante que celle du W95A, un précédent téléviseur à points quantiques de la marque.
Le constructeur met également en avant un contrôle plus précis du rétroéclairage, avec environ deux fois plus de zones de gradation que sur ses anciens modèles, sans préciser lesquels. Face aux autres téléviseurs SQD MiniLED, Panasonic entend se différencier grâce à la combinaison de son pilotage du rétroéclairage et de son circuit de gestion colorimétrique dédié, baptisé Hexa Chroma Drive Ultra.
Pourquoi Panasonic privilégie cette technologie
Selon les représentants de Panasonic interrogés par Phile Web, le SQD MiniLED correspond mieux, à ce stade, à leur philosophie de traitement de l'image. Leur argument porte notamment sur la régularité des couleurs : un téléviseur doit pouvoir restituer fidèlement des scènes complexes, où différentes teintes et plusieurs niveaux de luminosité cohabitent, et pas seulement des images de démonstration particulièrement saturées.
Un discours qui fait écho à celui de TCL. Le fabricant chinois commercialise lui aussi des téléviseurs RGB MiniLED, mais réserve le sommet de sa gamme au X11L, équipé du SQD MiniLED. Il défend ce positionnement par plusieurs arguments, notamment les contraintes liées à la multiplication des sources lumineuses par zone de gradation, comme l'explique Phile Web. Lors d'une présentation à la conférence ICDT de la SID, TCL a également évoqué les risques d'interférences entre couleurs et de vieillissement inégal des LED RGB.
Ces arguments ne démontrent toutefois pas une supériorité générale du SQD MiniLED. Les deux approches présentent leurs propres contraintes, tandis que le traitement d'image reste déterminant.
Ce choix ne signifie pas pour autant que Panasonic écarte le RGB MiniLED. En février dernier, lors de l'événement organisé à Munich pour annoncer son partenariat avec le chinois Skyworth, le constructeur avait justement présenté un prototype utilisant cette technologie. Nous avions pu le découvrir sur place, aux côtés de plusieurs concepts OLED. Doté de 3 432 zones de rétroéclairage RGB, avec plus de 10 000 éléments lumineux contrôlables individuellement, ce prototype n'a toutefois donné lieu à aucune annonce commerciale. Le SQD MiniLED apparaît donc comme le choix retenu pour les nouveaux Viera X97C japonais, et non comme un abandon définitif du RGB MiniLED.
Annoncés courant octobre, les Viera X97C doivent être commercialisés au Japon à la mi-novembre, en 65, 75, 85 et 98 pouces. Le modèle de 98 pouces marque d'ailleurs le retour de Panasonic sur le segment des téléviseurs de plus de 90 pouces, quelque 18 ans après son plasma de 103 pouces. Aucune disponibilité française n'est confirmée pour cette gamme.

articles.title: Após supermercados, hackers atacam freezers de bancos de sangue na França • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Após supermercados, hackers atacam freezers de bancos de sangue na França
Invasores alteraram remotamente a temperatura de equipamentos que armazenavam plasma e amostras.
Equipamentos de armazenagem de plasma e amostras de sangue foram alvo de um ciberataque em três instalações do Estabelecimento Francês de Sangue (EFS). Os freezers, normalmente mantidos próximos a -30 ºC, chegaram a ser programados para atingir 110 ºC.
O ataque não chegou a comprometer os estoques, segundo o jornal Le Canard Enchaîné, porque sistemas de monitoramento identificaram as alterações. Funcionários também participaram do controle e transferiram material antes que houvesse danos. O EFS afirma que nenhum produto foi perdido e não houve impacto à saúde dos pacientes.
O ataque ocorreu em 2 de novembro. Segundo o EFS, os invasores modificaram remotamente os limites de temperatura e os parâmetros de degelo dos sistemas para valores extremamente altos. Parte dos equipamentos armazenava bolsas de plasma destinadas a transfusões e à fabricação de medicamentos.
De acordo com a imprensa local, alarmes foram acionados antes que os produtos atingissem temperaturas capazes de danificá-los. Dependendo da unidade, os equipamentos foram colocados novamente sob controle, desligados ou tiveram o conteúdo transferido para locais seguros por funcionários, segundo a Associated Press.
A invasão teria ocorrido através da infraestrutura de TI do EFS. A Coolworld, responsável pelos sistemas atingidos, afirmou que a vulnerabilidade explorada estava em um componente fornecido por uma terceira empresa e que atingiu apenas um número limitado de unidades.
O Ministério da Saúde da França e a agência nacional de cibersegurança do país investigam o caso. O acesso remoto aos equipamentos foi desativado, e o EFS afirma ter reforçado o monitoramento de temperatura em suas instalações.
O ataque aos estoques de plasma acontece poucos dias após incidentes envolvendo sistemas de refrigeração de supermercados na Europa. No começo da semana, redes na Bélgica, Luxemburgo, Suécia, Estônia e outros países relataram alterações remotas em freezers e refrigeradores. Em uma loja sueca, por exemplo, os equipamentos foram configurados para atingir 50 ºC.
Mas ocorrências do tipo já vêm de antes. Novamente na França, sistema de refrigeração em centenas de supermercados foram comprometidos, levando ao descarte de alimentos e a prejuízos milionários, de acordo com a agência Reuters.
Apesar das semelhanças, ainda não está claro se a tentativa de sabotagem dos equipamentos usados pelo EFS está diretamente relacionada aos ataques contra o varejo.
A sequência de incidentes levou autoridades dos Estados Unidos a publicar, na quinta-feira (05/11), um alerta sobre ataques contra sistema de refrigeração industrial e monitoramento de cadeia fria. Segundo o comunicado, esse tipo de invasão pode ter consequências como perda de estoques, danos aos equipamentos e até risco de incêndio.
As autoridades recomendam retirar os controladores da internet pública sempre que possível, proteger o acesso remoto por firewalls, substituir senhas padrão e instalar atualizações de segurança.
“Toda organização que depende de sistemas de refrigeração e monitoramento deve presumir que pode ser alvo”, afirmou Chris Butera, responsável interino pela área de cibersegurança da CISA, agência vinculada ao Departamento de Segurança Interna (DHS).
O episódio ocorre em meio a uma série de ataques contra sistemas de refrigeração conectados à internet na Europa, e até problemas em geladeiras smart convencionais. Em setembro, na Coreia do Sul, usuários de um modelo da Samsung viram os eletrodomésticos pararem de refrigerar — no caso, porém, o problema se deu por uma atualização da própria fabricante.

articles.title: Ce constructeur automobile chinois veut lui aussi produire en Europe pour éviter les taxes
articles.text:
Après une vague d’arrivée de constructeurs chinois en Europe qui importent leurs modèles hybrides ou électriques produits sur le Vieux Continent, ces nouveaux acteurs cherchent pour certains à installer une partie de leur production en Europe. C’est désormais le cas de Great Wall Motor (GWM), qui va s’appuyer sur la Hongrie.
L’Europe accueille de nouveaux investisseurs
Si les constructeurs chinois sont toujours mal vus par la concurrence européenne puisqu’ils arrivent avec de fortes ambitions et parfois des modèles très concurrentiels, les pays d’Europe changent peu à peu leur vision du sujet. Si l’Europe a d’abord mis des barrières à l’entrée pour favoriser les constructeurs européens historiques, la perspective de voir les constructeurs chinois investir en Europe pour produire des véhicules séduit certains pays.
Great Wall Motor s’affaire à démarrer une production européenne pour ses véhicules électriques dès 2027. Le constructeur, dont le nom signifie littéralement « La Grande Muraille », devrait produire son SUV Ora 5 en Bulgarie chez Litex Motors. Dans le cadre des activités de GWM, cette collaboration n’est pas vraiment nouvelle : la société bulgare produisait déjà pour Great Wall Motor des véhicules à partir de kits expédiés depuis la Chine.
Et le cas de Great Wall Motor n’est pas isolé. Plusieurs constructeurs chinois veulent produire en Europe pour éviter les taxes d’importation appliquées par l’Europe sur les véhicules électriques produits en Chine. BYD a construit une usine en Hongrie pour la production des BYD Dolphin Surf et BYD Atto 2, MG s’intéresse à des sites de production en Espagne et Dongfeng devrait voir certains modèles être produits dans l’usine Stellantis de Rennes, tout comme Leapmotor produit les B10 et C10 dans l’usine de Saragosse de Stellantis. Cela permet de stimuler l’appareil industriel européen, qui avait vu son activité ralentir à mesure que les ventes de voitures neuves se sont réduites.
Des objectifs ambitieux
Si GWM prévoit de produire son SUV électrique Ora 5 en Bulgarie, c’est que la marque a des objectifs ambitieux. Pour l’instant, seul ce modèle électrique au format plutôt adapté à l’Europe sera produit sur le Vieux Continent, mais plusieurs modèles devraient le rejoindre dans l’usine de Litex Motors. En effet, Great Wall Motor a un objectif de 60 000 ventes annuelles en 2027, mais espère produire 300 000 véhicules en Europe d’ici deux ans. On dépasse alors le stade de la petite production en Europe d’un modèle spécifique pour éviter les taxes : GWM semble vouloir mettre un pied en Europe en étant très ambitieux sur les volumes de production.
Avec cette production en Europe, GWM pourrait éviter les 30,7 % de taxes d’importation que l’Europe applique sur ses voitures électriques produites en Chine. Ce qui pourrait grandement améliorer la compétitivité tarifaire de ses produits. En revanche, l’obtention du bonus écologique n’est pas garantie en France, car il s’agit d’une production à partir de kits venant de Chine. L’histoire nous a montré, avec les kits de la Leapmotor T03 assemblée à Tychy, en Pologne, que cette stratégie n’était pas toujours suffisante pour satisfaire à l’éco-score nécessaire à la prime Coup de pouce CEE en France.

articles.title: How Bihar Museum ranked ahead of the Met and Louvre
articles.text:
How a Rs 500 Cr bet put Bihar Museum ahead of the Met and Louvre
Built despite opposition, legal challenges and questions over its cost, Bihar Museum has entered the global top 10. For YourStory Founder Shradha Sharma, its journey is a reminder of what ambition and persistence can achieve.
Bihar Museum in Patna was recently ranked ahead of New York's Metropolitan Museum of Art and the Louvre in Paris. The museum has secured the ninth place on The World's 100 Best Museums 2026, published by German travel guide Worth a Journey. The Met stands tenth and the Louvre 31st. It is the only Indian institution on the list and the highest-ranked museum in Asia. For a museum that opened barely a decade ago, it is a significant achievement. More so because there was a time when the project itself faced serious opposition, with questions raised about its cost, relevance and the way it was being executed.
Reflecting on the recognition in a recent LinkedIn post, YourStory Founder and CEO Shradha Sharma recalled the roles played by two people in getting the museum built: Nitish Kumar, who championed the project as Bihar's Chief Minister, and 1992-batch IAS officer Chanchal Kumar, who was entrusted with its execution. When the state government proposed spending nearly Rs 500 crore on a world-class museum in Patna, the decision attracted criticism. Why should a state struggling with basic infrastructure invest so much in a museum? Who would visit it? Could the money have been better spent elsewhere? According to Sharma, even people within the political establishment questioned the proposal. Nitish Kumar, however, stood by the project, convinced that Bihar needed an institution worthy of its historical and cultural heritage.
Getting the museum built
The challenges began with the land. According to Sharma, the proposed 13-acre site had seven government bungalows, some occupied by senior officials and a state minister. Getting the occupants to vacate required considerable administrative effort and legal intervention. She also recounted an incident in which men allegedly linked to local politicians entered the construction site demanding subcontracts, prompting police intervention. The museum was designed by Pritzker Prize-winning Japanese architect Fumihiko Maki in collaboration with Mumbai-based architectural firm Opolis, while Larsen & Toubro was selected to construct it. But appointing internationally recognised architects and an established construction company was only part of the challenge. Getting the project completed was another matter.
The museum also faced judicial scrutiny. In June 2015, the Patna High Court, hearing a public interest litigation, criticised the expenditure of approximately Rs 500 crore and questioned the transparency of the contracting process. The court held that the project was not in the public interest but declined to halt construction because the building was nearing completion. Those findings remain an important part of the museum's history. Its international recognition does not erase the questions raised about public spending and governance, although the institution has since gained recognition well beyond Bihar.
Sharma credits much of the execution to Chanchal Kumar, who held the dual responsibility of Secretary of Art and Culture and Secretary of the Building Construction Department.
The arrangement meant that both the museum's cultural vision and its construction came under the same officer. Sharma said she recently read his account of how the museum came together and was struck by how little he spoke about his own contribution. Behind the finished building were years of navigating approvals, land disputes, administrative resistance and the many complications that accompany a large public project. In Sharma's telling, Nitish Kumar's political backing and Chanchal Kumar's persistence were crucial to seeing it through.
A reminder of Bihar's strengths
For Sharma, who grew up in Bihar, the recognition carries a more personal meaning. Few places in India can claim the kind of historical and intellectual inheritance that Bihar possesses. Bodh Gaya is where the Buddha attained enlightenment. Vaishali is closely associated with Mahavira. Ancient Pataliputra was the capital of the Mauryan Empire under Ashoka, while Patna is the birthplace of Guru Gobind Singh. Nalanda and Vikramshila were among the great centres of learning in ancient India. Yet Bihar's present-day image often has little to do with this extraordinary history. Its achievements are celebrated in textbooks, but the state has struggled to build contemporary institutions that attract the same admiration.
Sharma drew on an episode from the Ramayana to explain what the museum means to her. Before Hanuman makes his leap across the ocean to Lanka, Jambavan reminds him of the strength he has forgotten. Bihar, she suggested, needed a similar reminder of what it is capable of achieving. The museum offers one. Its galleries house sculptures, coins, manuscripts and artefacts that bring the region's history to life, including the celebrated Didarganj Yakshi. And now, a German travel publication has placed it among the world's ten best museums, ahead of institutions with far longer histories and international reputations. The ranking is one publication's assessment, but it is nevertheless a significant moment for a museum that faced so many questions during its creation.

articles.title: 70 000 exemplaires écoulés et clap de fin : pourquoi le Tesla Cybertruck s’arrête déjà au profit du Cybercab
articles.text:
Fin du Tesla Cybertruck : Elon Musk confirme l’arrêt de la production de son pick-up électrique en 2027
Elon Musk confirme l’arrêt progressif de la production du Tesla Cybertruck dès l’été 2027. Un choix qui permettra de libérer de l’espace sur les lignes d’assemblage pour un autre produit qui doit faire ses preuves : le robotaxi Cybercab.
Le controversé pick-up électrique de Tesla, le Cybertruck, continue de confirmer son échec commercial. Sur les routes américaines depuis fin 2023, ce modèle n’aura finalement pas réussi à convaincre les foules, forçant sa mise au placard. Elon Musk vient en effet d’annoncer sur X une fin de production au cours de l’année 2027… mais pour une très bonne raison.
Des ventes décevantes et une flambée des prix qui ont eu raison du Cybertruck
Sur son compte X, le milliardaire a ainsi annoncé que Tesla s’apprête à “réduire progressivement la production du Cybertruck” dans sa Gigafactory texane “vers le milieu de l’année prochaine”. Une décision destinée à augmenter la production du robotaxi Cybercab, souligne Elon Musk à la fin de sa publication.
Derrière cette réorganisation se cache en réalité un essoufflement rapide du pick-up électrique du constructeur. Après un bref engouement à son lancement, l’intérêt est vite retombé. Cox Automotive rapporte d’ailleurs que seules 4 323 unités ont trouvé preneur au troisième trimestre 2026, pour un total de 11 586 ventes de janvier à septembre.
Au total, les estimations du secteur évaluent les livraisons globales du modèle à environ 70 000 exemplaires, bien loin des centaines de milliers de Model 3 et Model Y écoulés chaque trimestre. Un constat d’échec pour les pick-up électriques qui rappelle l’arrêt du Ford F-150 Lightning l’an dernier, plombé par des ventes poussives et l’envolée des coûts. Souvent moqué pour son design angulaire et son allure de réfrigérateur métallisé, il aura tout de même eu le mérite d’introduire auprès du grand public la direction steer-by-wire et une architecture basse tension 48 V.
En marge de cette annonce, Tesla a immédiatement fermé les commandes de la version d’entrée de gamme du Cybertruck (Dual-Motor à transmission intégrale). Seules les déclinaisons Premium AWD et Cyberbeast restent au catalogue, avec une nouvelle hausse tarifaire qui succède à celle du mois d’août. Le premier modèle passe ainsi de 89 990 à 92 490 $, tandis que le second grimpe de 99 990 à 102 490 $.

articles.title: Unlimited 5G mobile data for just AU$19/m is frankly a great reason to sign up for Dodo NBN
articles.text:
Unlimited 5G mobile data for just AU$19/m is frankly a great reason to sign up for Dodo NBN
Throw in some low-cost NBN plans, and you have yourself a perfect package
When I’m searching for the best NBN deals, the main factor I’m taking note of is the monthly price. Second to that come perks which, to be honest, are becoming rarer and rarer. So when Dodo announced it’s now offering its NBN customers totally unlimited mobile data via its postpaid SIM plans, I simply had to take notice.
This offer, available to new and existing customers, works as follows — sign up for any Dodo NBN plan, and you’re eligible for the new Infinity plan, a AU$19/m SIM-only offer that includes unlimited data, capped at 50Mbps.
Unlimited 5G mobile data on the Optus network for just AU$19/m is a standout deal in itself. But combine it with Dodo’s low-cost NBN plans — now on the receiving end of an AU$30/m discount for six months — and you've got a package that's hard to ignore.
Dodo NBN + unlimited SIM plan from AU$62.99/m
The unlimited data Infinity plan is available with any Dodo NBN plan. To order, you first need to complete the sign-up process for an NBN plan, including making a payment. Once that’s done, you’ll be able to sign up for the Infinity plan via the Dodo mobile app.
Unlimited mobile plans aren’t entirely new. While virtually all telcos will allow you to continue using data, if you exceed your monthly allowance, download speeds are usually throttled to around 2Mbps. However, Felix has been offering truly unlimited data SIM plans for some time, and while speeds are restricted, they're now available at up to 80Mbps.
Unlimited data at 80Mbps, of course, sounds great, but it'll cost you AU$50/m. Dodo's unlimited data plan, meanwhile, is capped at 50Mbps but costs just AU$19/m, making it arguably the better-value option.
Take my favourite NBN speed tier of all — NBN 500 — as an example. You'll pay just AU$62.99/m for the first six months for Dodo's plan (far less than the current AU$95/m average). Throw in the unlimited mobile data plan, and your monthly total comes to AU$81.99/m — that's cheaper than some NBN 25 plans! Once the six-month introductory period is up, your ongoing monthly total will be AU$111.99.
There's no end date to Dodo's unlimited mobile data offer, but the discounted NBN plans for Black Friday sales in Australia are time-sensitive. So, to secure the lowest possible price, you'll need to sign up before December 8.

Max is a senior staff writer for TechRadar who covers home entertainment and audio first, NBN second and virtually anything else that falls under the consumer electronics umbrella third. He's also a bit of an ecommerce fiend, particularly when it comes to finding the latest coupon codes for a variety of publications. He has written for TechRadar's sister publication What Hi-Fi? as well as Pocket-lint, and he's also the editor of Australian Hi-Fi and Audio Esoterica magazines. Max also dabbled in the men's lifestyle publication space, but is now firmly rooted in his first passion of technology.

articles.title: GlobalFoundries VP details FDX Fusion technology, sporting 7nm-class performance without the need for EUV tools — company targets 2030 for high-volume manufacturing, with planar transistors in tow
articles.text:
GlobalFoundries VP details FDX Fusion technology, sporting 7nm-class performance without the need for EUV tools — company targets 2030 for high-volume manufacturing, with planar transistors in tow
Albeit at a low transistor density.
Eight years after GlobalFoundries abandoned the development of its 7nm FinFET technology, the company is preparing to return to 7nm-class performance, this time by going via a different route. Its FDX Fusion process, built on FD-SOI (fully depleted silicon-on-insulator) technology, promises 7nm-class performance using advanced planar transistors, with no EUV lithography necessary.
In an interview with Tom's Hardware Premium, GlobalFoundries' Sudipto Bose, vice president of the FD-SOI business unit, shared new details about its FDX Fusion technology, including its 8nm-class logic density, advanced planar transistors, manufacturing costs, and plans to begin commercial production in 2028. The company also explained how it intends to compete with conventional FinFET technologies and why it believes FD-SOI has a future beyond the 22nm-class generation. Some elements of this interview transcript have been edited for flow and clarity.
Sudipto Bose: I have been at GlobalFoundries (GF) for a little bit over six years, and I have been in the industry for 25+ years. I spent the rest of my career at Texas Instruments (TI), so it's really two jobs that I have done: TI and GF. Half and half engineering and business. I spent a lot of my business days in the automotive segment. This was what I was doing at GF when I joined, and now I have the FDX product line role.
Sudipto Bose: A little bit on the history of FDX at GF. GF has been investing in FD-SOI for a long time. It started [these efforts] before I joined. So I would say almost eight years now. And a lot of the investment thesis that drove us towards FDX Fusion is based on the traction that we have in the market today, right? We have quite a few customers who are ramping up. And I say quite a few; this is like high double-digit customers in the nineties that are ramping up right now.
Applications for FDX Fusion
Anton Shilov: What specific types of chips and devices is FDX Fusion designed for? Which application will benefit most from its capabilities?
Sudipto Bose: FDX Fusion will try to enhance the applications in which we play today. What do I mean by that? If you look at our current customers, they are designing chips, everything to do with connectivity. When I say connectivity, think of Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, cellular, satcom, all of that. So that is one class of customers.
There's another class of customers who are designing processors at the edge, so these are MCUs (microcontroller units) with some level of inference sitting inside. Think of customers like Alif Semiconductors. So that is another class: MCUs at the edge.
Then in automotive, we have a disproportionate exposure to radar, and this is because of the eighty-one gigahertz performance that FDX brings to the table. So we will engage with them as they try to enhance their portfolio. We also have an automotive MCU, but radar is where you will see a lot of press releases that we have done.
Last but not least, we also have exposure in the data center segment. This also goes back to the fT/fmax, the high-performance RF that we have, which is a good candidate for designing TIAs and clock recovery circuits.
Anton Shilov: By applications inside data centers, what exactly do you mean? CPUs?
Sudipto Bose: Not CPUs. It is in the connectivity space. So, if you think about GF's focus, we are very focused on two things in data centers: power and connectivity. So in the connectivity space, we have silicon photonics, or turning electrons into photons. But then when you receive them, you have the optical diode, again, a GF silicon photonics technology. After that, you need circuits that will amplify those weak electrical signals and drive them to the compute chip. This circuit, which amplifies the weak electrical signals, is right now being done by GF silicon-germanium, but once FDX Fusion is there, we'll offer them both [as] options. And so, to be very specific to your answer, these are data/signal paths inside the data center that feed into CPUs.
7nm-class FD-SOI node
GlobalFoundries' FDX Fusion is a new manufacturing technology that promises 8nm-class logic density and 7nm-class power and performance without EUV lithography or FinFET transistors, which greatly reduces design costs and manufacturing costs at the cost of significantly lower transistor density compared to 7nm-class nodes.
Instead, the process relies on advanced planar fully depleted silicon-on-insulator (FD-SOI) transistors, strained silicon substrates, and aggressive optical patterning techniques to achieve transistor dimensions comparable to those of conventional 8nm-class FinFET nodes.
FDX Fusion also retains support for adaptive body biasing and combines high-density digital logic with RF, analog, and embedded memory capabilities. The technology will be manufactured using deep ultraviolet (DUV) lithography, although its tighter gate and metal pitches will likely require extensive multipatterning for the most critical layers.
Anton Shilov: What are the key innovations of FDX Fusion compared to predecessors and other nodes that are currently used?
Sudipto Bose: The key things that we're improving from the current-generation FDX, the first one is fT/fmax, this is 500 GHz, or 0.5 THz fT/fmax. This helps the first segment that I talked about, which is connectivity. This helps automotive radar, and this definitely helps the data center segment as they try to improve data speeds. So this is not really competing with silicon germanium. Think of it as silicon germanium at the very high end, and FDX in the 100 – 200 Gb per lambda space. That is one. The second one is the inference at the edge. So we can call it physical AI, and we look at physical AI as sense, think, act, and connect. But the kind of feature set we are putting in starts with improving the digital gate density. This is 2.2 times more dense than the current generation FDX (22FDX and 22FDX+).
Sudipto Bose: We are putting in a lot of flavors of eNVM, a lot of flavors of SRAM, because in edge AI, and in fact for any AI, the real game is how much memory you can pack without increasing the cost. So we are adding a lot of flavors of those. The way we architected FDX Fusion is that we set a goal of how much performance we can deliver to our customer base without increasing their operating expenses.
If you look at classic 7nm, 6nm, they require EUV tools. The mask set is costly; the tool chain is costly. The FDX Fusion platform that we've built isn't going to use EUV tools. It is also based on planar technology. So there are two advantages to this. One is that we can support a much more competitive mask set price compared to 6nm. We can also offer [customers] a lot more flexibility in terms of cycle time and in how many places we manufacture, because FDX Fusion does not need EUV tools.
So, to summarize the answer? We are trying to improve RF and analog performance, digital gate density, and the classes of memory that we offer. What applications are we trying to target? It is connectivity, edge AI, high-frequency mmWave, automotive radar, and definitely applications inside data centers.
