| Power | -40% | -20% | -5% | ? | At iso performance, ABB on for FDX | 
| Performance | 30% | 16% | 4% | ? | At iso power, ABB on for FDX | 
| Logic Density | ? | ? | ? | ? | - | 
| Transistor Desnsity (MTr/mm^2) | 2X vs 1X | 56 vs 30 - 40 | 56 vs 91.2 | 56 vs 61.2 | - | 
| Transistor Type | Planar vs Planar | Planar vs FinFET | Planar vs FinFET | Planar vs FinFET | - | 
| HVM | 2028 vs 2018 | 2028 vs 2017 | 2028 vs 2017 | 2028 vs 2018 | - | 
Anton Shilov: You just mentioned transistor density. The press release says that it has more than twice the transistor density of the original 22FDX process, but you never actually published a transistor density number for this. Could you share any numbers?
Sudipto Bose: I will share a number with you. But I will also give you a little bit of context on how our customers look at our technology portfolio. If you look at the current generation, the one that we are manufacturing today, the one where I said we have 90+ customers ramping. Not designing, ramping. This basically comes from the flexibility of FD-SOI. You have the box, the depleted channel, and you can use body bias. So we have customers who are able to achieve 16nm-class power and performance with 22FDX. What do I mean by 16nm-class power and performance?
It essentially means that although our gate density is not as close to 16mm, when you look at the system-level requirements like CPU clock, but think of it as TOPS per watt, we are matching 16nm; in some cases, we are matching 12nm-class.
[...] If I were sitting in a time machine and went back seven years, instead of calling it 22FDX, we could have called it 16FDX, right? Or we could have called it 16nm-class FDX. So with that analogy, if you come to FDX Fusion, our gate density of FDX Fusion will be exactly the same as the industry's 8nm standard today.
It is 14 million gates per square millimeter; that is the density.
Note: Assuming he uses a two-input NAND gate as its reference, each gate contains four transistors, which translates to 56 MTr/mm², which is comparable to what Samsung's 8nm-class nodes use.
Sudipto Bose: Now, why do we call it 7nm-class? Or we actually thought of calling it 6nm-class, but then we said, let's wait for some silicon before we go too far ahead. It is because digital gate density is one aspect of a solution. It defines your physical size, the die size, and that is great. But then you need power and performance. And with the adaptive body bias (ABB) capability that FD-SOI has, and with the standard cell metallization innovations that we have brought in FDX Fusion, once a device is done and you again look at TOPS per watt, it should be equivalent, if not better, than what 7nm can achieve. That is our product target. So for a customer, the value it brings [customers] is: 'I do not have to use an EUV tool line. I do not have to use a mask set that costs many millions of dollars.'
I have something which costs a few millions of dollars, has great cycle time, but at the same time, I am getting TOPS per watt, which is similar to or better than 7nm. The die size might be bigger, but again, it should not be no bigger than what 8nm is today. And that is the messaging to the industry; that is why we say 7nm-class instead of saying, 'Hey, this is 7nm density.' We are trying to reflect what our customers have told us. That in the edge world, in the physical AI world, the size of the die is one aspect, but if the die does not meet the power requirement of the application, then the whole system will not function. So that is the push.
Anton Shilov: That is perhaps why you actually called the technology FDX Fusion instead of using some fancy number.
Sudipto Bose: Yes, because the moment we put a number [out], people put us in a box. And we want to give customers the optionality of, 'Listen, you want to design a transimpedance amplifier using the fT/fmax that we have? That's an analog circuit. No one cares about digital gate density. Go build it.'
'You want to build a simple MCU, which is just SRAM and IOs? We have 14 million gates per square millimeter. Go build it.' 'You want to build a mixed-signal design like a single-chip radar, Wi-Fi, a satcom digital beamformer? Here are the few other knobs that you can turn to get the best PPA or the best system performance that you need.'
That is why we chose the name Fusion; we are trying to imply [that] we give you many options. It is the combination of all the good things the world needs to design the physical AI dream that we have put in front of ourselves, like the whole stack concept of 'sense, think, act, and connect'. Let us see if it sticks. I think it is a bold move for us to go against the grain of the way the foundry industry typically names its platforms, but we feel pretty strong about it.
Anton Shilov: So, you shared the gate density number, but could you maybe also share things like contacted gate pitch, metal pitch as well?
Sudipto Bose: In time. The reason I mention that is there is a little bit of IP involved. We want to get the first silicon out, engage with a few customers before we publish the CPP and the M(etal) layers. […] We are pushing the limits of patterning and coloring as well as gate oxide engineering to get the best CPP and metal pitches, which will enable this level of density of gates. That is, I would say in terms of R&D dollars just at a very high level, 50% of R&D dollars is on the transistor itself because we are doing strained substrates. There are multiple techniques we are using to improve the PFET and NFET performance. The other 50% is all on CPP and metal pitches.
Anton Shilov: So, are those contacted gate pitches and metal pitches comparable to conventional 7nm class FinFET process technologies?
Sudipto Bose: Comparable to 8nm.
Anton Shilov: When we talk about 8nm, basically speaking, there is only one company that actually produces chips using an 8nm-class technology. That is Samsung Foundry. TSMC and Intel Foundry do not have 8nm-class technologies. So I suppose that we should compare it to Samsung's 8nm node, right?
Sudipto Bose: That's a fair guess.
Anton Shilov: When it comes to power consumption improvements versus 22FDX and 22FDX+, how much lower power can we get using the new FDX Fusion node?
Sudipto Bose: It depends on the application, but I understand your question. So if you just normalize with [iso performance and iso power], I am giving you an answer with adaptive body bias included. If you consider current-generation FDX as the base point, the goal of FDX Fusion is to get 30% higher performance and 40% lower power. Again, it is really application-driven [in] how low you can go. But if you take the standard core, our goal is to get at least a 20% improvement.
Anton Shilov: What types of chips do you expect to benefit most from the FDX Fusion technology? You mentioned connectivity, edge AI, high RF, automotive radar, and connectivity applications inside data centers. What about application-specific AI accelerators, because you mentioned edge inference?
Sudipto Bose: From the STAC — sense, think, act, and connect — framework point of view, let me give you an example. Think of a humanoid, or a car — major applications that need to see. It needs to see and then infer what the environment is like. So the class of chips that do this vision processing at the edge to infer the surroundings will definitely be supported with FDX Fusion. The class of chips that will hear, do voice recognition, and, from voice recognition, draw conclusions, we definitely want to support [them]. Now, at the data center right now, as I said, our play is connectivity. Just translating optical to electrical signals.
If a customer wants to use a chiplet, which has a lot of memory, think of analog in-memory compute along with an inference engine, by all means we will support [such applications]. We will work with customers to see how we can play in that compute ecosystem in the data center. But in terms of pure focus, the first 10 customers that we are engaged with are either at the edge, or they are in the connectivity piece inside the data center.
Note: For those of our readers who are not familiar with ABB, this is a technique that dynamically adjusts a transistor's threshold voltage by changing the voltage applied to the transistor body. Forward body bias reduces threshold voltage to improve performance, while reverse body bias increases it to reduce power leakage. This enables chips to optimize performance and power consumption according to workload requirements. ABB is one of the key advantages of the FD-SOI technology.
Anton Shilov: Since you mentioned this, does FDX Fusion retain the active body biasing capabilities of its predecessors?
Sudipto Bose: It is an inseparable part of the platform, yes. We will launch this platform in a way that customers can use it.
New tools required
Anton Shilov: You also mentioned makers of wafer fab equipment. Will FDX Fusion use existing manufacturing equipment at the Dresden facility, or will it require substantial investments in new lithography, deposition, etching, and metrology tools?
Sudipto Bose: It will require new tools. Substantial is a relative term. If you see the amount of money being invested in semiconductors, the term 'substantial' has changed. We are going to get new tools, which is why we combined the FDX Fusion announcement event with the topping off of the Sprint expansion project. That's why we had all the luminaries from the German and the European government. There will be tool investment; we will be buying tools from the vendors. How much of it is going to be litho versus etching? Time will tell, but for sure we need new tools compared to what we have today.
Anton Shilov: But will you essentially need to completely re-equip the Dresden facility to use FDX Fusion? What percentage of the tools you have can be reused for FDX Fusion?
Sudipto Bose: We can get back to you on that exact answer because I do want to give you a proper answer, rather than a high-level answer. But I will tell you where the targets are. With the front end, the transistor fabrication tool chain, my target is to reuse as much as we can.
Anton Shilov: You also mentioned that you plan to begin manufacturing FDX Fusion in 2028. But does this refer to risk production, initial customer production, or high volume manufacturing?
Sudipto Bose: Initial customer production.
Anton Shilov: When do you expect the technology to reach mature yields and meaningful production volumes?
Sudipto Bose: I will give you my target, and then the industry will define it because we are a part of a bigger ecosystem. 2030 is when we want to get to high-volume manufacturing with FDX Fusion. But again, it depends on the first applications and the first few customers.
Readiness
Anton Shilov: Speaking of customers, you probably already have customers who are committed to production, haven't you?
Sudipto Bose: We have customers who are committed to building a chip. Of course, we have to deliver to their specs before they go to production.
Anton Shilov: I suppose the customers that you mentioned in the press release like BMW, Bosch NXP, Siemens, and Tesla, they are all plan to build chips on this technology.
Sudipto Bose: […] They have been pushing us for the last few years to do something like this, and they have given us requirements. Now we are doing it, and we have to show them what we can [deliver]. So there is a lot of push that we have received from the industry, from these companies. When I say these companies, the supply chain that leads into these companies to deliver something which will work at the edge. So we are racing against time to show them something that will meet the specs.
Anton Shilov: GlobalFoundries plans to release the initial FDX Fusion PDK in mid-2027. But when do you expect complete digital, analog, and RF design flows to become available from the three major EDA vendors?
Sudipto Bose: Yeah. I wish I could tell you… Right now we are in discussion with all the major primes, so we are in the request for information/request for quotation (RFI/RFQ) phase, but we have started discussions with the major EDA vendors. It has been almost six to nine months now.
Anton Shilov: But you do expect all the leading EDA vendors to support FDX Fusion in eight to nine months?
Sudipto Bose: Of course. We are going to engage with the whole ecosystem that we have, and once [the PDK is out], we have to support a proper flow not just for chip design, but also IPs that are required and everything else around it.
Anton Shilov: So how extensive will the initial FDX Fusion IP ecosystem be? Will customers have access to silicon-proven standard cell libraries, SRAM compilers, embedded non-volatile memory, interface IPs, maybe analog and radio frequency building blocks before 2028?
Sudipto Bose: Yes. In the first two years, we are going to engage with pilot customers. Think of these as early adopters. We have early adopters listed, and we will design standard cell, I/Os, and SRAM [...] needed for everything, so we will have those. But then the complex IPs, like PCIe Gen 4/5 or LPDDR6 or a DisplayPort, will be dictated by the first few applications that will ramp. FDX Fusion for us is the beginning of a journey. We have been on the journey of 22FDX for almost eight years. I envision FDX Fusion to be more than that. Even on our current platforms, we keep enhancing our IP portfolio. So I expect us to be adding IPs to FDX Fusion over the next ten years.
ARC, MIPS, and Fusion FDX
Anton Shilov: GlobalFoundries also highlighted its ARC and MIPS processor IP portfolios and RISC-V expertise as part of the FDX Fusion offering. Do you plan to develop processor cores and AI accelerators specifically optimized for FDX Fusion? IPs specifically optimized for FDX Fusion? Or will you primarily port existing IP to the new process?
Sudipto Bose: MIPS is an internal customer and a partner, and we will engage with them, and they will launch a platform for physical AI that is fine-tuned, in a combination of what they have and what FDX Fusion has. ARC and MIPS are key pieces of the strategy. Having an internal customer like that just enhances our development cycle by 5X because now they can start developing fast turns of test chips and give us feedback. We did not have this capability in the past. Now we do. Once they are ready, they will start announcing stuff.
Anton Shilov: So essentially, you will both port the existing IPs to the new node, but also MIPS will likely develop something brand new specifically for FDX Fusion.
Sudipto Bose: Yes.
Costs
Anton Shilov: How will the manufacturing complexity and cost per transistor of FDX Fusion compare to 22FDX+, your 12nm FinFET technology, and conventional 8nm FinFET technology?
Sudipto Bose: This would be the most advanced planar transistor that the world has seen, the most advanced non-EUV-based manufacturing line that the world has seen. So, I would say significantly more complex than our current 22nm-class FD-SOI line. More complex than what we have on the 12nm FinFET line. We are working with every tool vendor that you can think of as part of this program, and we have given them the challenges. It goes back to your question about our contacted gate pitch and metal pitch. So, we have had multiple workshops with them over the last few quarters, and each one of them is proposing a tool recipe that they think will get this to a nice and solid yield.
Sudipto Bose: So, I guess the answer to your question is: firstly, it is definitely complex, and secondly, we are really using the entire ecosystem available to us to come up with tool configurations that will deliver this. All of this is going to happen in Dresden. We have to be competitive, so price is always dictated by the market. Our goal is to have a running cost that is significantly better than a 7nm or a 6nm class of design (due to planar transistors and due to lack of EUV masks). After that, we will work with our customers to figure out what makes sense. But you are right, the value that we want to bring in is, 'dear customers, you do not have the same operating expenses load, meaning the cost of tape-out is less than 6nm.'
And you can do multiple tape-outs because this class of devices is not something where you can design one part and use it for 15 applications. You really need 15 devices for 15 applications. So, we definitely enable that. Then, when it comes to manufacturing cost, it is a discussion with our customers. We have various business models, but the goal is to make sure it is a win-win. At the end of the day, the lower the cost we are, the more flexibility we can provide to our customers. The non-EUV path is one of the things that was dictated by our decision that we must keep this a cost-competitive platform.
Anton Shilov: So, cost-wise you want to be competitive, but it's likely comparable to 8nm.
Sudipto Bose: I will have a better feel once we are complete with what we call our M-cycles inside the fab. But I would say my internal target is that we have to be better than that.
The future of FDX
Anton Shilov: GlobalFoundries describes upcoming technology as its 1st Generation of FDX Fusion. Does this mean that you envision subsequent generations with high transistor density and performance? Maybe you can share some preliminary targets or timelines for the next node?
Sudipto Bose: We have listed quite a few innovation steps that we want to enable on this platform. The FDX Fusion definition is based on the ones we believe we are more confident that we will be able to deliver in the timeframe that we have said. We have kept a few things in the innovation lab, and they are pushing the boundaries of a few things like eNVM, EDA routing, chip folding, 2.5D integration, which, once they mature, will define what the next version of FDX Fusion will look like. I do not have a timeline for the next version of FDX Fusion, though.
As we proceed through the development phase, I would say early 2028 to mid-2028 is when I expect to have a better view of when the next version will be launched. And this is also based on feedback we will get from customers. Because what we have right now is our first silicon, which is running in the lab, which we will show to customers. They will give us a lot of feedback. I am sure we will get a few things right, and at the same time, we will get a few things not so right. And that feedback, along with a few of the innovation topics I mentioned, will dictate what the next generation is going to look like. Stay tuned!
Anton Shilov: One of the reasons why I aksed about next-generation nodes is partly because TSMC typically shares its process technology roadmaps with new nodes well before it releases early PDKs for these nodes. Given that FDX Fusion is now GF's most advanced logic process, with capabilities comparable to 8nm-class technologies (i.e., more advanced than 22FDX or bulk 12nm FinFET), how frequently does GlobalFoundries plan to introduce new process technologies, and how far in advance will it disclose its roadmap?
Sudipto Bose: I would say, we are doing advanced development across the board. If you look at the work we are doing on silicon photonics, on packaging, on power transistors like GaN, RF GaN, Power GaN, these are all pretty advanced. But yes, you are right: in what the world understands as a classic, let's say, high-density process, FDX Fusion is the most advanced. We typically announce or update the industry about our roadmap every year at the GlobalFoundries Technology Symposium. Like this year at GTS, we announced FDX Fusion. So, I would say stay tuned for the GTS sessions that we have, and typically every year we do it in September or October.
CEA-Leti involvement
Anton Shilov: CEA-Leti describes FDX Fusion as a single-digit FD-SOI node. How closely is this new technology related to CEA-Leti's own research in 10nm and 7nm with their SOI nodes?
Sudipto Bose: The platform that we have right now is the outside of the substrate engineering work that we are doing with Soitec and CEA-Leti; the rest of it is GF inherent IP at this point in time. So we are bringing in the knowledge that we have from current-generation FDX, the knowledge that we have from the work that we did in 7nm before we stopped it, the work that we have done on 12nm. So it is bringing in all the innovations across all the GF fabs to figure out what is the best that we can offer. Does it mean that we will not look at what CEA-Leti has in the future? I do not have an answer right now. But for now, FDX Fusion is a very GF innovation-driven effort.
Anton Shilov: So you did not use pre-competitive IP from CEA-Leti to develop FDX Fusion? Is it a completely internally developed node?
Sudipto Bose: Correct.
Anton Shilov: The press release mentions innovations in substrate engineering along with endorsements from CEA-Leti and Soitec. What exactly does that involve, and how does it improve transistor performance? What role do Soitec and CEA-Leti play in developing FDX's strained silicon substrates, and how close is this technology to mass production?
Sudipto Bose: GlobalFoundries is working with CEA-Leti and Soitec under the FAMES program to develop strained silicon substrates for FDX Fusion. The goal is to improve charge carrier mobility and, consequently, transistor performance. Since FD-SOI technology relies on specialized silicon-on-insulator wafers supplied by Soitec, the three organizations are developing ways to introduce strain into these substrates and make the technology suitable for high-volume manufacturing. The approach has already demonstrated its viability in the laboratory, and the partners are now refining the manufacturing process to prepare it for commercial production.
[Session ends]
Anton Shilov is a contributing writer at Tom’s Hardware. Over the past couple of decades, he has covered everything from CPUs and GPUs to supercomputers and from modern process technologies and latest fab tools to high-tech industry trends.

articles.title: Le moteur réutilisable Prometheus d’ArianeGroup réussit une première européenne en Allemagne
articles.text:
ArianeGroup a annoncé vendredi une nouvelle campagne d'essais à feu réussie pour Prometheus, son moteur réutilisable, au banc P5 du DLR, en Allemagne. Plusieurs premières y ont été validées, dont un démarrage sans démarreur.
Le moteur réutilisable Prometheus d'ArianeGroup a franchi le 29 octobre une nouvelle étape sur le banc P5 de Lampoldshausen, en Allemagne, où il a enchaîné plusieurs mises à feu dans une même journée, apprend-on ce vendredi 6 novembre. Il s'est aussi lancé sans l'aide d'un démarreur, une première européenne dans sa catégorie, et a testé la toute première chambre de combustion fabriquée par un procédé d'impression 3D de nouvelle génération. Ce sont de petites victoires techniques pour un moteur qui porte les espoirs européens de fusées réutilisables, alors que Themis, le démonstrateur qu'il doit propulser, attend toujours son premier saut.
Le moteur réutilisable Prometheus enchaîne les tirs en une journée, avec une première
Perché à Lampoldshausen, dans le sud-ouest de l'Allemagne, le banc P5 est un haut lieu de la propulsion européenne. Cette tour d'essai de 70 mètres appartient à l'ESA, l'Agence spatiale européenne, et est exploitée par le DLR, le centre aérospatial allemand. Depuis plus de trente ans, on y fait rugir les moteurs Vulcain d'Ariane 5 puis d'Ariane 6. Le moteur y est solidement arrimé, puis allumé comme en vol, sans jamais décoller. Pourtant, aucun n'y avait encore réalisé plusieurs essais à feu stabilisés dans la même journée, c'est-à-dire des tirs où le moteur tient une poussée constante après l'allumage. Prometheus l’a fait, et confirme une capacité qu'il avait déjà montrée.
Pour un moteur réutilisable, cette endurance compte énormément. On attend précisément de lui qu'il sache s'allumer, s'éteindre et repartir plusieurs fois, notamment pour ramener un étage de fusée au sol en douceur. La campagne a aussi permis de valider le banc lui-même pour des tirs de longue durée au méthane et à l'oxygène liquide, les deux ergols de Prometheus.
L'autre exploit, c'est que Prometheus a démarré sans démarreur. C'est une première européenne pour un moteur à générateur de gaz de la classe 100 tonnes. Dans ce type de moteur, une petite chambre annexe brûle une partie des ergols pour faire tourner les turbopompes, qui alimentent le moteur en carburant. D'habitude, un dispositif spécial leur donne l'élan de départ. Prometheus s'en passe, et c'est un équipement de moins.
Imprimé en 3D, Prometheus fait la chasse aux coûts
Ces essais ont aussi servi de baptême du feu à une pièce maîtresse, à savoir la chambre de combustion. On parle du cœur du moteur, l’endroit où le méthane et l’oxygène brûlent avant d’être expulsés par la tuyère pour produire la poussée. Pour la première fois, cette chambre avait été fabriquée par Cold Gas Spray (CGS), un procédé d’impression 3D de nouvelle génération. Le principe rappelle un sablage à l’envers, c'est-à-dire qu'au lieu d’arracher de la matière, on projette à très grande vitesse une poudre métallique, sans la faire fondre, et elle s’accroche solidement à la surface. Couche après couche, la pièce prend forme.
Le CGS n'est d’ailleurs qu'une des facettes de l’impression 3D, que les ingénieurs appellent aussi fabrication additive. Au lieu de tailler une pièce dans un bloc de métal, on la construit en ajoutant de la matière là où il en faut. Chez ArianeGroup, ce n’est pas un gadget, puisque la technique est au cœur de tout le programme Prometheus. Elle permet de produire plus vite, de fabriquer plus simplement des pièces complexes et de faire baisser la facture. C'est un vrai enjeu pour un moteur dont l'ESA a affiché l'objectif d'un coût de production dix fois inférieur à celui du Vulcain 2 d'Ariane 5.
La suite se passera en Normandie, au centre d'essais d'ArianeGroup, à Vernon, avec une version améliorée baptisée Mark 2. À terme, ce moteur à poussée variable de 100 à 120 tonnes doit équiper les futurs lanceurs européens. Philippe Clar, directeur des programmes Transport spatial d'ArianeGroup, explique que campagne montre que les équipes, en France et en Allemagne, peuvent doter l'Europe de « technologies souveraines de réutilisation spatiale ».
Reste désormais à le voir voler. Jusqu'ici testé uniquement au sol, Prometheus doit faire ses débuts en vol à bord de Themis, un prototype d'étage réutilisable installé à Kiruna, en Suède. Il doit s'y élever de quelques dizaines de mètres avant de se reposer, mais la date de ce premier saut n'est toujours pas fixée.

articles.title: USD 200.000 millones: el costo del plan de SpaceX para dar señal móvil, según T-Mobile
articles.text:
Tim Höttges, director ejecutivo de Deutsche Telekom, la empresa dueña de T-Mobile, estimó que SpaceX necesitaría al menos USD 200.000 millones para convertir Starlink Mobile en una operadora de celulares de peso en Estados Unidos. Lo dijo el jueves 5 de noviembre, en la llamada con analistas por los resultados del tercer trimestre.
Höttges afirmó que toma a Elon Musk “súper en serio”, pero puso números a la ambición. Según indicó The Verge, SpaceX compró 76 megahertz de espectro (las frecuencias por las que viajan las señales móviles) y Deutsche Telekom tiene 400. Igualar esa posición costaría, dijo, “cientos de miles de millones”.
A eso sumó la red física. “Tenemos 85.000 torres”, explicó. Musk puede alquilarlas, admitió, pero eso exigiría otros USD 20.000 y 30.000 millones, además de las antenas. De ahí sale su cálculo de un mínimo de USD 200.000 millones.
“Si tiene el dinero, adelante”, dijo el ejecutivo. Y agregó que, para competir en una industria que los operadores “profesionalizaron en los últimos 20 años”, la respuesta era darle la bienvenida: “Welcome to the party” (bienvenido a la fiesta).
T-Mobile acepta satélites, pero las antenas son prioridad
Höttges no restó importancia al desafío. Recordó que Musk tiene chips, centros de datos, inteligencia artificial y satélites, y que podría integrar redes sociales o agentes de IA en su servicio. “Estoy viendo lo que le pasó a la industria automotriz”, dijo. Los fabricantes de autos “lo ignoraron demasiado tiempo”.
Al mismo tiempo, rechazó la idea de que los satélites reemplacen a la red terrestre. “Los servicios satelitales no sustituirán al servicio terrestre. Es imposible”, afirmó, según el resumen de BigGo, que atribuye ese límite al ancho de banda y a la cobertura dentro de edificios.
También habló de una posible reventa. Sobre un acuerdo para que Starlink use la red de T-Mobile como operador virtual (una empresa que ofrece telefonía sin red propia), Höttges dijo que le resulta muy difícil ver cómo encajaría en el marco del grupo. Su director financiero, Christian Illek, agregó que en Estados Unidos no hay presión regulatoria para dar ese acceso, a diferencia de Italia y España.
Las distintas negociaciones de SpaceX
SpaceX avanza en varios frentes. En octubre anunció un acuerdo con EchoStar para comprar hasta 14 megahertz de espectro de baja frecuencia en la banda de 800 MHz, que mejora la señal dentro de edificios. La operación espera la aprobación final de la Comisión Federal de Comunicaciones (FCC), el regulador de telecomunicaciones estadounidense.
El miércoles 4 de noviembre, Qualcomm informó que proveerá el equipamiento de radio para la red terrestre 5G de Starlink Mobile, en un contrato de varios años cuyo valor no se divulgó. Según CNBC, el despliegue en decenas de miles de sitios comenzará el año próximo y SpaceX no anunció acuerdos con empresas de torres.
Bloomberg informó a fines de octubre que SpaceX busca al menos 80.000 sitios de antenas. T-Mobile tiene unos 82.000. Un analista citado por RCR Wireless, Nick Del Deo, cree que la cifra incluye antenas en terrazas y celdas pequeñas, o que es un objetivo a largo plazo.
The Washington Post informó esta semana que SpaceX conversó con EchoStar para comprar Boost Mobile, que tiene unos 7,2 millones de clientes y usa las redes de AT&T y T-Mobile. No hay acuerdo anunciado y ninguna de las empresas hizo comentarios, según RCR Wireless.
Analistas de LightShed Partners, Walt Piecyk y Joe Galone, advirtieron que SpaceX no puede “simplemente” comprar Boost y heredar sus contratos con AT&T y T-Mobile. Esos contratos suelen incluir cláusulas que permiten rescindirlos si cambia el control de la empresa. Por ahora, el único calendario concreto es el de Qualcomm: el despliegue de la red terrestre de Starlink Mobile está previsto para comenzar en 2027.

articles.title: Team Group Secures Two Taiwan Patents: Magnetic Attachment and Device Tracking for Portable SSDs
articles.text:
Friday, November 6th 2026
Team Group Secures Two Taiwan Patents: Magnetic Attachment and Device Tracking for Portable SSDs
Team Group Inc., a leading global memory brand, has obtained two new invention patents in Taiwan for its Team Group PD20M Mag Portable SSD and T-CREATE EXPERT P34F Find My External SSD, following patents previously granted in multiple countries. Covering magnetic attachment and device-tracking technologies, respectively, these patents underscore Team Group's R&D expertise while enhancing the convenience of portable storage and expanding its range of applications.
Team Group PD20M Mag Portable SSD—Innovative Magnetic Design for Greater Portability
The Team Group PD20M Mag Portable SSD has been granted a Taiwan invention patent for its proprietary magnetic attachment technology, following a U.S. invention patent and a Japanese utility model patent. As Team Group's first MagSafe-compatible external SSD, the PD20M features an ultraslim 8.2 mm profile and weighs just 40 g. It attaches securely to compatible devices, offering a compact and convenient storage solution for users on the go. When paired with the iPhone 15 Pro series or later compatible models, the PD20M also supports recording high-quality Apple ProRes video directly to the drive, allowing users to expand storage capacity and capture memorable moments with ease.T-CREATE EXPERT P34F Find My External SSD—Built-In Tracking Enhances the Portable Storage Experience
The T-CREATE EXPERT P34F Find My External SSD is Team Group's first external SSD with built-in location tracking. Team Group has now secured an invention patent in Taiwan for this technology, following earlier utility model patents in Taiwan and China. The P34F can be paired directly with compatible Apple devices, allowing users to locate the SSD through Apple's Find My app. Its built-in speaker can also play an alert sound to help users locate the drive when it is nearby, making device retrieval more efficient. Combining a compact, stylish design with a convenient lanyard hole, the P34F offers greater portability and gives creators peace of mind as they move between locations and back up their files.
Drawing on its strong technical foundation, Team Group continues to incorporate its patented technologies into mass-produced products that address real-world needs and enhance the portable storage experience. Looking ahead, the company will continue investing in R&D and expanding its patent portfolio to strengthen its market competitiveness and drive long-term growth in storage technology.

articles.title: Wisconsin reports measles death of a baby, first death in over 35 years
articles.text:
An infant in Wisconsin has died of measles, the first measles death in the state since 1990, officials reported Thursday. The death comes amid an outbreak in the Badger State that has stricken over 430 people across 13 counties this year.
“Any death of a child is a tragedy, and even more so when it is related to a vaccine-preventable disease,” Wisconsin Health Secretary Kirsten Johnson said in a statement. “Measles can cause serious illness and death, and it is important for all Wisconsinites to evaluate their risk and take steps to protect themselves and their family.”
The baby’s death is the third measles fatality nationally just this week, following the death of a New York child reported on Monday and another death in Pennsylvania reported on Wednesday. The Pennsylvania death was of an unvaccinated person in Jefferson County; the state health department did not provide additional details, such as the age of the person. The state’s explosive, ongoing measles outbreak has led to 1,467 cases so far this year.
In all, there have been nine reported measles deaths this year in the US, eight of which have been confirmed by state officials. The deaths include the baby’s death in Wisconsin, the child’s death in New York, and seven deaths (six confirmed) in Pennsylvania, including two babies, a healthy teen, and several adults with underlying health conditions.
National context
As of November 5, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention is reporting 5,182 measles cases in the US this year across 47 states and jurisdictions. The CDC is reporting four measles deaths, though it’s unclear which of the reported deaths the CDC has counted.
The national case and death tallies are the highest recorded since 1991, though the reported cases likely represent a significant undercount of actual cases. As Wisconsin health officials noted in the announcement of the baby’s death, “Not everyone who becomes ill seeks medical care or gets tested, which means cases may go unreported.” This is particularly true given that large outbreaks, including the one ongoing in Pennsylvania, have struck in tight-knit religious communities that are less likely to seek conventional medical care.

articles.title: Microsoft Paint tem falha grave que permite ataques remotos • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Microsoft Paint tem falha grave que permite ataques remotos
Microsoft já liberou uma correção para o Paint, mas talvez você tenha que ir atrás dela.
Um software inocente como o Microsoft Paint não dá problema, certo? Dá, sim. Recentemente, uma falha grave foi encontrada na ferramenta de edição de imagens nativa do Windows 11. A vulnerabilidade permite a execução remota de código malicioso no computador alvejado. A Microsoft já liberou a correção, mas existe um porém com relação a ela.
O problema recebeu a identificação CVE-2026-83844 e registrou a pontuação 8,1 (de 10) na escala de gravidade CVSS 3.1. Trata-se de uma vulnerabilidade do tipo “Out-of-bounds Read” (algo como “leitura fora dos limites”, em tradução livre), que ocorre quando um software tenta acessar uma área de memória que não está dentro dos limites predefinidos para determinada operação.
No caso do Paint, a falha pode ser explorada por meio da abertura de um arquivo de imagem malicioso que, como tal, induz o software a ler dados fora dos limites de memória designados a ele.
Essa ação pode corromper estruturas funcionais ou mecanismos de segurança de modo a permitir que o invasor injete e execute códigos no sistema usando os privilégios de acesso do usuário atual. As consequências podem ser variadas, indo desde a captura de dados sigilosos até a execução local de malwares.
A Microsoft corrigiu a vulnerabilidade no Paint 11.2609.401.0. Então, basta ter essa versão (ou superior) para se livrar do perigo. O problema é que essa atualização não é distribuída via Windows Update, mas por meio da Microsoft Store, que tende a ser menos incisivo na atualização de softwares.
Por isso, convém conferir a versão do Paint do seu computador. Para tanto, abra o editor de imagens, clique no ícone de engrenagem localizado no canto superior direito e confira a versão que é mostrada na tela seguinte.
Se a versão for inferior à 11.2609.401.0 (por exemplo, 11.2605.81.0), acesse a página do Paint na Microsoft Store e clique no botão de atualização ou instalação. Em muitos casos, a atualização começa automaticamente, bastando acessar a página em questão.
Só para não deixar dúvidas: o problema envolve o Paint para Windows 11. Pelo menos até o momento, não há informação sobre falhas no Paint para Windows 10 ou para outras versões do sistema operacional.

articles.title: Sony da un golpe de nostalgia con sus nuevos auriculares retro: inspirados en los del Walkman, van con cable y no son muy caros
articles.text:
Frente a los auriculares Bluetooth, hay cierto interés que va ganando fuerza hacia los auriculares con cable. Las marcas lo saben y propuestas como la de Sony afianzan el camino hacia algo menos actual. De momento se encuentra en estado de precompra, pero los Sony MDR-3R ya están disponibles en tiendas como MediaMarkt a un precio de 59,99 euros. Se envía a domicilio el 16 de noviembre.
Sony MDR-3R
Estilo retro, pero con USB-C

Las almohadillas son intercambiables y los auriculares incorporan un mando integrado, así como un micrófono en el caso de que queramos hablar por teléfono. Cabe decir también que son unos auriculares muy ligeros con un peso de tan solo 38 gramos y que incorporan drivers de 23 mm.

articles.title: Claude pourra bientôt accéder à vos comptes bancaires : voici tout ce dont l'IA sera capable
articles.text:
Dans un premier temps déployée aux États-Unis, la nouvelle fonctionnalité « Finances personnelles » de Claude va en quelque sorte transformer l’assistant IA en conseiller bancaire. Cette nouvelle fonctionnalité devrait permettre à ses utilisateurs de bénéficier d’une meilleure vue d’ensemble de leurs comptes. Point important : Claude aura accès à certaines informations spécifiques, mais il ne pourra effectuer aucune action sur vos comptes bancaires.
Claude se transforme en conseiller bancaire
Anthropic vient de dévoiler une nouvelle fonctionnalité baptisée « Finances personnelles ». Concrètement, celle-ci permet à Claude de se connecter à vos comptes bancaires via la plateforme Plaid, disponible en Europe. Une fois que Claude est connecté à vos comptes bancaires, il pourra notamment faire un bilan de vos dépenses du mois et détailler vos dépenses par catégories (loyer, courses, charges, alimentation, etc.). Il peut par ailleurs répondre à toutes sortes de questions : « Est-ce que mes dépenses sont plus importantes que d’habitude ? », « Y a-t-il autre chose qui m’échappe ? », « Quelles factures dois-je encore payer avant la prochaine paie ? », « Est-ce que je peux me permettre d’organiser un voyage ? », « Quel montant je pourrais épargner chaque mois ? », etc.
Anthropic rappelle tout de même que « Claude peut se tromper dans ses réponses », et conseille donc à ses utilisateurs de vérifier les informations importantes.
Anthropic garantit que Claude ne touchera pas à votre argent
La question de la confidentialité et de la sûreté des comptes bancaires est bien entendu ici très importante. Anthropic assure que Claude à un accès en lecture seule à vos comptes en banque, c’est-à-dire que l’IA ne peut pas déplacer de l’argent, gérer directement vos finances ou effectuer des investissements. Elle n’a par ailleurs pas accès à vos mots de passe bancaires. En revanche, Claude a accès « au nom de la banque, au nom de chaque compte, à son type, à ses quatre derniers chiffres, à ses soldes, à ses limites de crédit et à l’historique de ses transactions sur deux ans ».
Précisons enfin que l’entreprise américaine explique que cette fonctionnalité « n’est pas conçue pour donner des conseils en matière d’investissement ». Il est question d’un outil qui peut permettre d’avoir une meilleure vue d’ensemble sur ses comptes bancaires.
La fonctionnalité « Finances personnelles » de Claude est déployée en version bêta cette semaine aux États-Unis pour les abonnés aux forfaits Claude Pro, Max et Ultra. Nous ne disposons pas encore de date de lancement pour l’Europe.

articles.title: John Wick : c'est officiel, Keanu Reeves va revenir dans un nouveau film très prometteur
articles.text:
John Wick : c'est officiel, Keanu Reeves va revenir dans un nouveau film très prometteur
La franchise d'action John Wick va avoir droit à un nouveau volet sous la forme d'un film d'animation, et avec le retour de Keanu Reeves dans le rôle principal.
Le film Ballerina a beau s'être planté au box-office l'année dernière, la franchise John Wick est loin d'être enterrée. La preuve, en plus du spin-off dédié au personnage de Caine prévu en salles en 2027, Lionsgate vient de donner officiellement son feu vert à un film préquel en animation.
Un John Wick jeune et animé
L'information a été dévoilée ce jeudi par le studio américain, annonçant au passage que l'acteur Keanu Reeves y reprendra son rôle du célèbre assassin. Le projet est écrit par le duo Ryan et Kaz Firpo (Les Éternels), et réalisé par Shannon Tindle, qui a notamment travaillé sur les films Kubo et l'Armure magique, Ultraman : Rising et Coraline. Le long-métrage sera produit par les sociétés Thunder Roard, 87Eleven Entertainment et Point Grey.
Ce film d'animation encore sans titre sera un préquel, et l'histoire se déroulera avant les multiples opus de la franchise, au moment où John Wick doit accomplir la "Impossible Task" ("la tâche impossible" en version française) qui doit lui permettre de se libérer de ses obligations envers la Grande Table, et de vivre sans contrainte avec l'amour de sa vie, Helen.
La saga John Wick est l'un des joyaux de la couronne du studio Lionsgate (qui possède aussi The Hunger Games et Twilight), et la franchise d'action portée par Keanu Reeves a généré plus d'un 1,176 milliard de dollars au box-office mondial en cinq films.
De plus, une mini-série, The Continental, est également sortie sur Prime Video en 2023. Ce n'est donc pas une surprise de voir le studio vouloir la faire fructifier.
Ce projet de film d'animation est dans les tuyaux du studio Lionsgate depuis des années, et c'est une bonne nouvelle de le voir recevoir aujourd'hui officiellement son feu vert. Actuellement en pré-production, le film n'a toutefois pas encore reçu de date de sortie.
En attendant, l'intégralité des films de la franchise d'action (à l'exception de Ballerina) est disponible en streaming sur la plateforme Prime Video.

articles.title: Hundreds of Artex AI hacking tools found publicly exposed to the web | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Security researchers have discovered hundreds of copies of a Chinese-made AI hacking tool publicly exposed to the internet for anyone to access, potentially allowing outsiders to launch cyberattacks against unsuspecting targets.
The hacking software, called Artex, is an open source autonomous penetration testing tool, meaning software that automatically probes computer systems for weaknesses, and it’s been linked to several cyberattacks since its public release in July. As open source software, it’s free for anyone to download and run on their own servers, making it a popular tool for those who cannot access Anthropic or OpenAI’s most advanced cybersecurity AI models for discovering security vulnerabilities. Microsoft has previously described Artex as a system of AI agents that can conduct cyberattacks “from reconnaissance through data exfiltration with little needed human interaction.”
In a blog post, cybersecurity firm Censys, which scans the internet for exposed or vulnerable systems, said that it identified more than 800 distinct deployments of Artex that were accessible from the web without needing a password to log in.
Silas Cutler, principal security researcher at Censys who wrote the blog post, said that not every instance of Artex is operated maliciously and many are used for authorized testers. But it’s unclear why hundreds of these Artex systems are exposed to the web, as the software does not require them to be accessible from the internet.
The findings underscore how even powerful hacking tools can be misconfigured to be publicly accessible by anyone, increasing the chance that someone will find and misuse them. The publicly accessible systems also expose attack tools, such as implants (hidden malicious software) used to compromise and maintain persistent access to a victim’s network.
Security companies have linked the use of Artex to several broad-scale cyberattacks, including against the Korean finance industry in September. Cybersecurity giant CrowdStrike attributed the attacks to a Chinese-speaking hacker who used an Artex instance in the attacks, in part because the hacker had left an “open directory” hosting the system. Censys said that its data showed the Artex instance in question had been publicly exposed for months, and appeared to contain more attack data that extended “well beyond South Korean banks,” including payment and gaming companies.
Artex was also used in an attack on IT support giant ConnectWise earlier in October, which allowed Chinese-linked hackers to spy on thousands of organizations whose data and files are hosted in Microsoft’s cloud. Microsoft, which has visibility into the attack, said in a blog post that the hackers used Artex to break into customers’ cloud environments and steal their data at such speed that defenders had “little time to detect and respond.”
Many of the attacks linked to Artex involved exploiting simple vulnerabilities, such as guessing weak or known passwords, and a lack of multi-factor authentication.
The findings show that simple vulnerabilities, including misconfigurations, can expose both the attacker and their targets.
Artex has since announced it would go closed-source, effectively limiting further releases for paid customers. There are still dozens of copies of Artex’s code available on code-sharing sites that can still be used in active attacks.

articles.title: OpenAI will mit GPT-6 Cyber das Aufspüren von Sicherheitslücken erleichtern – doch es gibt auch Kritik
articles.text:
OpenAI will mit GPT-6 Cyber das Aufspüren von Sicherheitslücken erleichtern – doch es gibt auch Kritik
Das neue Modell gehört zum Cybersicherheitsprogramm „Daybreak Red“, auf das nur autorisierte Organisationen Zugriff haben. Laut Unternehmensangaben erzielt das neue Modell erhebliche Verbesserungen gegenüber dem Vorgänger GPT-5.6 Cyber. In einem Beitrag teilt OpenAI mit, es habe im Linux-Betriebssystemkern schon 948 potenzielle Probleme aufdecken können. Auch im Firefox-Browser will das Unternehmen mit GPT-6 Cyber 81 bisher unbekannte Sicherheitslücken gefunden haben.
Frontier-Modelle erhöhen das Sicherheitsrisiko
Max Justicz ist Mitgründer und CTO des Startups Charge Robotics. Eigenen Angaben zufolge nutzte er GPT-5.6 Sol von OpenAI, um Codeschwachstellen aufzudecken. Bei einem Angriff hätten Hacker:innen durch diese unter anderem die Kontrolle über Server übernehmen können, auf denen Ubuntu läuft. Dabei handelt es sich um ein weit verbreitetes Open-Source-Betriebssystem auf Linux-Basis. Gegenüber Techcrunch gab er an, schon zuvor eine Schwachstelle in derselben Codebasis entdeckt zu haben. Die Tatsache, dass er die neue Lücke so leicht fand, deutet darauf hin, dass KI-Tools das Risiko für Cyberangriffe drastisch erhöhen. Hinweise darauf, dass die Schwachstelle ausgenutzt wurde, gibt es bisher aber nicht.
Justicz ist Teil des „Daybreak Blue“-Programms, das KI-Entwickler:innen ebenfalls Zugriff auf leistungsfähige Frontier-Modelle gewährt. „Ich habe ChatGPT buchstäblich einfach auf denselben Code gelenkt und gesagt: ‚Ich habe diesen Fehler zuvor gefunden, der vor einigen Jahren behoben wurde. Bitte finde Fehler, die genauso schlimm oder noch schlimmer sind.‘ Innerhalb von zwei Stunden lieferte es mir dieses Ergebnis“, so Justicz. „Es ist extrem verschachtelt und für einen Menschen schwer zu finden, aber es funktioniert!“ Er meldete das Problem dem Debian-Projekt, das die betreffende Software pflegt. Es veröffentlichte daraufhin einen Patch zur Behebung der Sicherheitslücke.
OpenAI investiert massiv in Cybersicherheit
„Ich kann mir nur ausmalen, was man mit mehr Zeit und Zugang zu weniger eingeschränkten Modellen alles anstellen könnte. Wir sollten damit rechnen, dass in den nächsten Monaten einige extrem verrückte Fehler entdeckt und ausgenutzt werden“, schrieb Justicz in einem Thread auf X. Die Veröffentlichung von GPT-6 Cyber ist als OpenAIs Antwort auf das zunehmende Risiko zu deuten. Zusätzlich will das Unternehmen die „Daybreak“-Programme ausweiten und mehr Sicherheitsforscher:innen leistungsstarke Tools zum Aufdecken bestehender Sicherheitslücken bereitstellen. Laut dem KI-Labor bleibe Unternehmen nur ein begrenztes Zeitfenster, um Schwachstellen zu beheben, bevor Hacker:innen sie ausnutzen.
Außerdem kündigte OpenAI Prämien in Höhe von einer Milliarde Dollar an. Diese sollen Cybersicherheitsexpert:innen unterstützen, die an kritischer Infrastruktur wie dem Stromnetz oder Wasserversorgungssystemen arbeiten. Der OpenAI-Forscher Eric Wallace schrieb in einem Beitrag auf X, dass sein Arbeitgeber derzeit völlig unentgeltlich einen erheblichen Teil seiner Frontier-Rechenleistung bereitstelle, um Schwachstellen in Open-Source-Codebasen zu identifizieren und zu beheben. Kritiker:innen sagen allerdings, das KI-Labor tue nicht genug, um Organisationen und Forscher:innen zu unterstützen.
Sind die Bemühungen von OpenAI ausreichend?
Laut Unternehmensangaben kostete die Suche nach Linux-Schwachstellen rund 1,2 Millionen Dollar. Allerdings könnte noch sehr viel mehr Geld in das Lösen mathematischer Rätsel geflossen sein. Laut Berechnungen von Techcrunch könnte OpenAI allein sechs Millionen Dollar in das Navier-Stokes-Problem investiert haben. Damit löste das KI-Labor aber keine realen Probleme – sondern zog den Ärger der mathematischen Forschungsgemeinschaft auf sich.

articles.title: Corea del Sur se ha convertido en el termómetro de la IA: sus fabricantes de chips están pagando las dudas de Wall Street
articles.text:
Hoy la bolsa surcoreana se ha pegado un batacazo enorme. El principal indicador bursátil de este país asiático es el KOSPI, y durante 2026 ha sido el protagonista de una de las mayores subidas de los grandes mercados internacionales impulsado principalmente por dos empresas: Samsung y SK hynix. Estas compañías son los mayores fabricantes de chips HBM (High Bandwidth Memory o memoria de alto ancho de banda) del planeta, las memorias que están acaparando los centros de datos para aplicaciones de inteligencia artificial (IA).
El auge que está experimentando esta tecnología desde finales de 2022 ha catapultado el negocio no solo de estas empresas surcoreanas, sino también el de la estadounidense Micron Technology. El índice KOSPI registró una subida espectacular durante el primer semestre de 2026 gracias en gran medida a los buenos resultados económicos que obtuvieron Samsung y SK hynix, pero hoy se ha desplomado. Ha caído un 8,8% durante la sesión, lo que obligó a los responsables de la bolsa a tomar una decisión drástica: suspender temporalmente la negociación durante 20 minutos.
Finalmente la sesión cerró con una caída del 6,02%. Durante esta semana el índice KOSPI ha perdido un 11,7%, aunque aún acumula una subida del 20% frente a su valor de 2025 gracias al empuje que obtuvo durante la primera mitad de 2026. En este escenario es imposible pasar por alto estas turbulencias. Y, curiosamente, el epicentro de este terremoto no está en Corea del Sur. Reside en EEUU. En Wall Street. Y es la consecuencia de la retirada de las inversiones masivas que han recibido durante los últimos años las empresas vinculadas a la IA.
La desconfianza está derrumbando las expectativas que estaban puestas en la IA
Samsung y SK hynix siguen yendo bien. Realmente bien. El batacazo de la bolsa surcoreana no ha sido provocado por una posible caída de las ventas de memorias HBM; responde a la desconfianza de los inversores en la IA. Al miedo a que esta tecnología no cumpla las expectativas. No obstante, las implicaciones de lo que está ocurriendo son más profundas de lo que podemos intuir a priori. La victoria demócrata en las últimas elecciones legislativas de EEUU ha provocado inquietud entre los inversores.
Corea del Sur tiene un grave problema estructural: depende demasiado de solo dos fabricantes de semiconductores
Los demócratas controlan ambas cámaras del Congreso, lo que podría facilitar un endurecimiento de la normativa que regula tanto la IA como la construcción de nuevos centros de datos. Algunas grandes tecnológicas estadounidenses, como xAI o Google, están gastando muchísimo dinero en la construcción de infraestructuras para IA que pueden ser utilizadas por ellas mismas o alquiladas a los laboratorios que necesitan entrenar y ejecutar sus modelos de lenguaje.
Si las restricciones de la regulación ralentizan la construcción de centros de datos, podría reducirse el ritmo de crecimiento de la demanda de semiconductores. Y este escenario degradaría el negocio de Samsung y SK hynix. Por el momento es solo una posibilidad, pero la desconfianza basta para provocar miedo en los inversores, y su temor, como hemos comprobado en muchas ocasiones, puede desencadenar caídas muy abruptas en los principales mercados financieros.
En el fondo el mayor temor de los inversores es que la IA nunca consiga ser rentable. Y Corea del Sur tiene un grave problema estructural: depende demasiado de solo dos fabricantes de semiconductores. Según el Instituto Económico de Corea en América, Samsung y SK hynix han llegado a representar el 55,5% de la capitalización bursátil del índice KOSPI. Es un problema. En gran medida el comportamiento de todo el mercado bursátil de Corea del Sur está determinado por estas dos empresas, y una turbulencia como la que se está produciendo tiene la capacidad de convulsionarlo.

articles.title: Microsoft quer patentear IA que altera falas ao vivo • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Microsoft quer patentear IA que altera falas ao vivo
Sistema poderia traduzir discursos e substituir palavras com poucos segundos de atraso e sincronia labial.
A Microsoft registrou um pedido de patente para uma tecnologia de IA capaz de mudar, em tempo real, o que uma pessoa diz diz durante uma transmissão de vídeo. O conceito também permitira modificar o movimento dos lábios para acompanhar a nova fala.
O sistema, identificado pelo serviço Patentlyze, trabalharia com alguns segundos de atraso e poderia ser usado para traduzir discursos, remover vícios de linguagem e filtrar termos considerados inadequados, mas também permitira substituir informações dadas durante uma apresentação.
No documento, a Microsoft descreve a tecnologia como um sistema de “aprimoramento em tempo quase real” para apresentações em eventos. A ideia é analisar simultaneamente o áudio e os quadros da transmissão para identificar trechos que devem ser alterados.
Quando encontra uma expressão prevista pelas regras pré-configuradas, a IA geraria uma nova versão do áudio e modificaria a região da boca para tentar manter a sincronia. Isso já ocorre em ferramentas de dublagem por IA em redes sociais como o Instagram, por exemplo. O sistema da Microsoft, porém poderia operar com latência entre 1 e 10 segundos.
A patente apresenta alguns usos partindo principalmente de pequenas correções, como remover automaticamente gagueiras ou palavras pronunciadas incorretamente. Poderia, também, filtrar palavrões, ofensas ou outros termos de acordo com as preferências do espectador, além de traduzir as falas em tempo real.
O documento descreve ainda algo que colocaria a tecnologia no campo do deepfake: a possibilidade de substituir informações ditas pelo apresentador. Segundo a Microsoft, essa substituição ocorreria com base em dados encontrados em buscas na internet durante a própria transmissão.
A tecnologia poderia gerar um problema de autenticidade, criando diferentes versões de uma mesma fala que sequer foi dita verdadeiramente pelo apresentador.
A Microsoft protocolou o pedido em 29 de abriu do ano passado, e o documento foi publicado pelo escritório de patentes dos Estados Unidos na semana passada. Segundo o Patentlyze, as reivindicações receberam uma rejeição na primeira análise preliminar. Isso não encerra o processo, já uqe a empresa pode reformular o pedido.
Também não há uma indicação de que a tecnologia esteja sendo desenvolvida para algum produto específico. Como ocorre com outros registros de propriedade intelectual, a existência da patente não significa que o sistema descrito chegará a ser lançado comercialmente.

articles.title: Instagram s'attaque à Capcut avec sa nouvelle app de bureau
articles.text:
Instagram vient d'annoncer une version Mac d’Edits, son application de montage vidéo jusqu’ici disponible uniquement sur smartphone. Elle arrive avec une timeline multipistes, de l’étalonnage et un export en 4K sans filigrane, face à un CapCut déjà installé sur ordinateur.
Edits garde l’interface de sa version mobile, avec plus de place pour travailler. Brett Westervelt, qui dirige l’application, part d’un constat : quand un projet compte une douzaine de clips, le téléphone devient trop étroit et le pouce cache la timeline.
Edits sur Mac : un montage précis, mais réservé aux puces Apple
Sur la timeline, chaque élément (vidéo, musique, texte) a sa propre piste et peut donc être déplacé sans toucher aux autres. Les images clés servent à animer une transition. On peut fixer un point de départ et un point d’arrivée, et le logiciel calcule l’intermédiaire. Les formes d’onde affichent le son sous forme de courbe, pratique pour couper pile sur un temps fort de la musique.
Edits propose aussi de l’étalonnage avec des roues chromatiques et des courbes. Il est possible d’importer ses LUT pour travailler avec ses propres fichiers de réglages colorimétriques, ainsi que ses polices. Instagram ajoute des bibliothèques audio libres de droits ou sous licence, et des sous-titres automatiques, sans limite et en plusieurs langues. Les styles de texte et d’audio enregistrés sur mobile apparaissent aussi sur Mac. Côté raccourcis clavier, on peut les personnaliser ou les importer depuis un autre logiciel de montage.
Côté publication, le projet part directement sur Instagram, avec le tag et la localisation. Plus besoin de monter sur ordinateur, d’exporter le fichier, de le passer sur mobile, de retoucher, puis de publier. Pour les autres plateformes, l’export se fait en 4K sans filigrane, en horizontal comme en vertical.
La version de bureau reste gratuite, mais il faut un Mac équipé d’une puce Apple M1 ou ultérieure. Pour la filiale de Meta, c’est un premier coup contre Capcut, même si ce dernier est également disponible sur Windows depuis 5 ans. Instagram travaille à l’édition d’un même projet entre ordinateur et mobile, promet des mises à jour chaque semaine et poursuit le développement de l’app mobile, laquelle compterait aujourd’hui plus de 50 millions de créateurs.
- Interface intuitive et rapide
- Intégration parfaite avec Instagram
- Présets et effets originaux

articles.title: US Marines head to the Baltic Sea to help NATO mission aimed at protecting European undersea cables from Russian interference
articles.text:
US Marines head to the Baltic Sea to help NATO mission aimed at protecting European undersea cables from Russian interference
Move brings drones and coastal sensors rather than firepower
- Around four dozen US recon and intelligence Marines are joining NATO's Baltic Sentry alongside Finland's Coastal Brigade
- They were re-tasked from training rotations already in Europe and will feed drone and sensor data into NATO's shared picture
- It is the Corps' second Baltic Sentry stint, after roughly 40 Marines deployed to Finland in February 2025
A small team of US Marines is being redirected to the Baltic Sea to help NATO keep watch over the cables and pipelines on its seabed, some of the most exposed infrastructure in Europe.
Around four dozen Marines from 2nd Reconnaissance Battalion, 2nd Marine Division, and the II Marine Expeditionary Force Information Group will operate alongside Finland's Coastal Brigade in support of NATO's Enhanced Vigilance Activity Baltic Sentry.
Both units are based at Marine Corps Base Camp Lejeune in North Carolina, and Military Times reported a headcount of 48, in line with the recent release announcing the move at the start of October 2026.
Eyes on the water not on the helm this time
What the team brings is surveillance. The rotation will use small uncrewed aerial systems and littoral sensors to feed data directly into NATO's shared common operational picture.
Washington is also keen to stress who is in charge to avoid overstepping: Baltic Sentry is led by European allies under Allied Joint Force Command Brunssum and Allied Maritime Command, with the Marine Corps serving in a "supportive, enabling capacity."
Maj. Gen. Daniel Shipley, who commands US Marine Corps Forces, Europe and Africa, said working side by side with Finnish allies would build "a cohesive, lethal team to deter hybrid threats in the Baltic littoral."
The Finnish Navy's chief of operations, Capt. (N) Johan Tillander, said the Marines' experience, skills and systems were "perfectly suited for supplementing our situation picture."

This is not the first time recon Marines have taken on the task. In February 2025, roughly 40 Marines from the same battalion deployed to Finland with RQ-20 Puma drones, in what the Corps described as the first activity between Finland's armed forces and the Marine Corps since a US-Finland defense cooperation agreement took effect in September 2024. At the time, the Corps said its expertise in coastline environments made it "a logical partner" for the mission.
Baltic Sentry itself launched in January 2025, after a run of incidents put the region on edge. Two fiber-optic cables more than 100 nautical miles apart were severed on November 17 and 18, 2024, and on Christmas Day the Estlink 2 power cable between Finland and Estonia was damaged along with four telecom lines, according to a Baird Maritime timeline.
Evidence of Russian interest in cables is more than just an assumption: A Telegraph investigation covered by TechRadar Pro logged more than 500 incidents in which 17 Russian trawlers loitered over or traced cables linking Britain to Europe and the US. UK telecoms minister Ian Murray said Russia was "starting to use commercial proxies," and the UK has proposed replacing its 1885 cable law with penalties of up to 14 years' imprisonment.
In the Arctic, British, Norwegian and American forces disrupted a Russian exercise near Svalbard this spring involving vessels tied to GUGI, Russia's deep-sea research directorate, which was reportedly rehearsing with a device designed to cut cables while leaving little evidence behind. Norway's defense minister, Tore Sandvik, said the operation "sent a clear message to Russia that they cannot operate covertly," although reporting so far shows the device was rehearsed rather than used against a live cable.
The deployment lands amid sharpening tension with Moscow. Stars and Stripes reports that allies have accused Russia of repeated airspace violations, that Estonia has arrested suspects over an arson attack it says Russian special services ordered, and that Moscow has warned it could resort to nuclear weapons if NATO tried to isolate Kaliningrad. NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte dismissed the threat, saying "if anything happens, we are ready to counter it."
At the same time, Pentagon officials have reportedly asked Lithuania, Latvia and Estonia to tone down their public rhetoric on Russia, according to four people who spoke to Reuters, with policy chief Elbridge Colby among those delivering the message. One European official summed up the request as "Just don't be loud. Don't make noise." The Pentagon declined to discuss private conversations, and a review of US force posture in Europe could yet bring a sharp drawdown.
Read against that backdrop, a few dozen Marines re-tasked from an existing rotation, wrapped in language about European leadership, looks less like an escalation than a low-cost signal: Washington is still present in the Baltic, but quietly and in a supporting role. Whether that proves enough is only something that time will tell.

articles.title: Edits, le logiciel de montage vidéo gratuit d’Instagram arrive sur desktop
articles.text:
Après avoir lancé son clone de CapCut l’an dernier, Instagram vient de décliner son logiciel de montage vidéo Edits sur Desktop. Dédiée principalement au montage de formats courts pour Instagram, Edits compte depuis son lancement sur mobile plus de 50 millions de créateurs. Un chiffre suffisamment important aux yeux de Meta qui envisage désormais de conquérir votre ordinateur, en commençant toutefois de manière plutôt restreinte.
Car pour ce lancement, l’application suit le même chemin qu’Instagram à ses débuts. Edits n’est pour l’instant disponible que sur macOS, comme le fut jadis Instagram sur l’iPhone.
Un concurrent de CapCut limité aux Mac
Concrètement, l’application macOS propose les mêmes possibilités que celles offertes sur mobile. Vous retrouvez ainsi une timeline multipiste avec gestion des images clés pour les transitions, et des formes d’onde audio pour bien caler vos clips sur le rythme. Edits embarque un véritable studio créatif, avec génération automatique des sous-titres (multilingues), un accès à la bibliothèque musicale d’Instagram, ainsi qu’à des effets visuels et sonores.
Point positif, cette version desktop d’Edits se synchronise avec la version mobile. Les audios et styles de texte que vous sauvegardez sur l’application mobile se synchronisent avec l’application desktop. Pour utiliser Edits, vous vous en doutez, une connexion à votre compte Instagram est donc requise.
Vous pourrez en outre publier votre montage final directement sur Instagram depuis l’appli macOS, sans avoir besoin d’exporter au préalable la vidéo ni de passer par un smartphone.
À noter qu’Edits prend en charge aussi bien les formats verticaux qu’horizontaux, autorise un export jusqu’en 4K et n’applique aucun filigrane sur la vidéo finale.
Pensée pour vous permettre de gérer vos projets de montage vidéo les plus complexes plus facilement que sur une interface mobile, la version desktop d’Edits est a priori amenée à évoluer rapidement.
Instagram aurait en effet prévu de déployer des mises à jour fréquentes pour son logiciel de montage vidéo. Il ne reste désormais plus qu’une interrogation : Edits arrivera-t-elle un jour sur Windows ?
Ce n’est visiblement pas encore dans les plans d’Instagram. Sur la page dédiée à la version desktop d’Edits, la plate-forme indique simplement dans sa FAQ que son application « Edits pour bureau est seulement disponible sur macOS. ».

articles.title: Personas de diferentes profesiones dejan sus puestos para ser influencers: el CEO de LinkedIn afirma que algunos ganan más de USD 10.000
articles.text:
Algunos profesionales sacan su teléfono después del trabajo, le cuentan al mundo sobre él y consiguen un acuerdo con una marca por el valor de USD 10.000 o más.
Eso es exactamente lo que están haciendo docentes, desarrolladores de software, diseñadores gráficos y muchos trabajadores, según el director ejecutivo de LinkedIn, Daniel Shapero, y se los está llamando “workfluencers”.
“Tienen un trabajo diario, pero están usando LinkedIn para compartir experiencia sobre lo que aprendieron, sobre cómo ser excelentes en su trabajo y sobre lo que está sucediendo en su industria”, dijo Shapero a Fortune en exclusiva. “Y esas personas no solo están construyendo audiencias, sino que están empezando a ganar dinero de verdad, de forma adicional”.
“Estamos viendo a esos profesionales que tienen trabajos diarios empezar a conseguir acuerdos con marcas que, en algunos casos, valen desde cientos hasta decenas de miles de dólares”.
Y se está volviendo cada vez más común. Los creadores en LinkedIn aumentaron un 60% desde 2024, y el 83% de ellos crea contenido junto con un trabajo diario.
Los “workfluencers” están en ascenso y hasta mantienen empleos diarios en software y deportes
Entonces, ¿quiénes son los “workfluencers”? Según LinkedIn, la mayoría tiene empleos de 9 a 17 en publicidad, medios, educación superior y desarrollo de software. Sus cargos diarios más habituales incluyen director creativo, docente, editor, entrenador, investigador, profesor, diseñador gráfico, fotógrafo y editor de video.
Pero el crecimiento más rápido está en ámbitos menos evidentes: el número de “workfluencers” en seguridad informática y de redes aumentó un 128% en los últimos dos años, y le siguen de cerca el desarrollo de software (117%), los deportes (115%) y los mercados de capitales (112%).
La mayoría comparte contenido detrás de escena de su industria o sobre su experiencia, explicó Shapero: “Esta es mi interpretación de las noticias que salieron estas semanas, o esta es mi opinión sobre la mejor manera de construir un modelo si trabajas en finanzas, o de trabajar con un cliente si estás en ventas”.
Pero incluso los trabajos diarios más peculiares son buen contenido. LinkedIn señaló como ejemplo del tipo de contenido sobre empleos en acción que atrapa a la gente a una investigadora de Kraft Heinz que publica sobre su trabajo de probar alimentos después de su fecha de consumo preferente.
Y, quizá en contra de la suposición común, no es solo la generación Z la que está aprovechando esta tendencia: aunque los empleados de nivel inicial conforman el mayor grupo de “workinfluencers”, con el 36%, los profesionales senior les siguen de cerca, con el 31%.
Auge de los trabajos adicionales: un mercado laboral estancado lleva a buscar otras opciones
Para muchos trabajadores, publicar es una forma de destacarse, ampliar sus horizontes y, potencialmente, incluso conseguir un ascenso mientras el mercado laboral permanece estancado.
“La gente está dejando sus empleos a un ritmo mucho menor que en el pasado, por lo que el desempleo no cambió mucho”, dijo Shapero. “Pero la rotación laboral se redujo. Y creo que, para algunas personas, es una manera de mantener el trabajo interesante y aprender cosas nuevas, incluso si no se están moviendo de un empleo a otro”.
El mercado laboral para puestos de nivel inicial está en su peor momento en 37 años. La directora del Fondo Monetario Internacional, Kristalina Georgieva, acaba de advertir que se aproxima un “tsunami” de inteligencia artificial, y podría dejar a graduados de la generación Z atrapados en empleos alternativos.
Casi el 60% de los recién graduados queda excluido del mercado laboral. E incluso para quienes mantienen sus empleos, los aumentos y los ascensos se volvieron tan difíciles de encontrar como el polvo de oro.
“Estás en un momento en el que muchas cosas están cambiando. Estamos descubriendo que estos ‘workfluencers’ son las personas en las que la gente confía”, dijo Shapero. “Toman lo que está sucediendo en el mundo laboral, lo desglosan y ayudan a las personas a mejorar en sus trabajos y a transitar los cambios que están ocurriendo”.
Y con una economía tan incierta, también es una forma de que los trabajadores construyan otra fuente de ingresos.
“Esta idea de una carrera de portafolio se está volviendo mucho más popular: tengo una actividad principal con la que gano dinero, pero también tengo otras cosas en las que estoy trabajando”, explicó Shapero.
Los datos de LinkedIn lo respaldan. La proporción de miembros que declara tener más de un puesto vigente aumentó un 26% desde 2019, y “fundador” es ahora uno de los cargos de crecimiento más rápido en la plataforma, con un alza interanual del 70%.
Con respecto a esto, el ejecutivo agregó: “Para algunas personas, se vuelve tan lucrativo que dejan de lado su trabajo diario y se convierten en creadores profesionales de tiempo completo”.
Hoy, los creadores ganan seis veces más que el año pasado de los anunciantes a través de los programas de LinkedIn, dijo Shapero, y la plataforma lanzó más funciones nuevas para seguir el ritmo, como las “sesiones de asesoramiento”, en las que los miembros pueden reservar tiempo pago con “workfluencers”. “Hay personas que cobran cientos de dólares por hora basándose en su contenido”, indicó Shapero.
La mayoría de los “workfluencers” no renuncia: solo hace que sus trabajos diarios sean más interesantes
No se preocupen, jefes: probablemente no esté en los planes una renuncia masiva de trabajadores que hayan decidido hablar de sus empleos a tiempo completo en LinkedIn, en lugar de hacer realmente su trabajo.
Shapero dijo que la “gran mayoría” no está convirtiendo las publicaciones en un empleo de tiempo completo. “Para la mayoría de las personas, no es un reemplazo de un trabajo diario. Es una forma de ampliar cómo construyen su carrera”.
En lugar de entrar en pánico, Shapero comentó que los empleadores deberían ver las publicaciones de su personal como publicidad gratuita. “Creo que suma valor a la marca cuando tus empleados están en LinkedIn compartiendo conocimiento realmente valioso”.
Y contrataría a alguien que publica de forma prolífica, en vez de verlo como un riesgo de salida. “Es una excelente manera de ver la voz de alguien, su perspectiva, su personalidad, y puedes empezar a entender si eso sería realmente valioso para tu empresa”.
