articles.title: Yelp Combines Native and Server-Driven UI for Its AI Assistant
articles.text:
Yelp has adopted a hybrid user interface architecture for its AI Assistant, combining native mobile controls with server-driven conversation rendering to support faster interface changes across platforms. The design uses Yelp’s CHAOS framework, short for Content Hosting Architecture with Optimization Strategies, to render conversation content while keeping navigation and message input native.
Yelp Assistant launched on iOS in 2024 to help users create project requests for local service professionals. It has since expanded to answer questions about businesses and support actions such as reservations, appointments, and food orders.
CHAOS supports web, iOS, and Android. In a server-driven UI architecture, the backend defines what the client displays and how it responds to interactions, so interface changes can reach users without requiring a new mobile app release.
Daniel Andrade Groppe, Services Tech Lead at Yelp, highlighted,
Our existing CHAOS framework lacked some of the capabilities the Assistant required, including text input fields and network requests. Extending the framework would have delayed delivery, so we took a hybrid approach: we kept navigation and message input native while using CHAOS to render the conversation area.
Yelp Assistant UI: Native and Server-Driven Components (Source: Yelp Blog Post)
The implementation separates view configuration from conversation data. When a chat starts, the client fetches the CHAOS configuration and initializes a dataset for message events. Subsequent events update the existing view without refetching the configuration. Events represent persistent user and bot messages, temporary typing indicators and quick replies, and links that open destinations. The backend can also send actions to control the interface. For example, when a project request is complete, it can return a message, a link to view matches, and an action that disables chat input. This event-driven design decouples rendering from conversation logic.
Airbnb has documented a related approach through its Ghost Platform, which uses server-defined UI across web and mobile clients. Both approaches let teams update supported presentation without requiring every change to ship in a new client release. Yelp’s implementation applies this model to a conversational interface while retaining native controls and client-side handling for message state and interactions.
Yelp Assistant UI Chat Interaction Flow (Source: Yelp Blog Post)
The client displays submitted messages and a typing indicator, disables input, and sends requests to the backend. On response, it displays the reply and quick replies and re-enables input. Recoverable errors trigger retries, while non-recoverable failures disable input and prompt users to try again later.
Yelp engineers note that the architecture also introduces coordination challenges and engineers needed time to learn both the Assistant and CHAOS, and shared implementations can still behave differently across platforms. Separating view configuration from conversation data enables independent feature development. The architecture also supported reusing the Android Assistant to launch the Biz Ask Anything pilot. According to Yelp, this work laid the groundwork for its next-generation Assistant, which now connects business information with actions users can take.

articles.title: Huawei Watch GT 7 com GPS está 42% mais barato na Amazon • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Huawei Watch GT 7 com GPS está 42% mais barato na Amazon
Watch GT 7 (46 mm) traz GPS com IA mais preciso e tela AMOLED de 3.000 nits; novo smartwatch da Huawei recebe desconto de 42% em oferta da Black November no Pix
O Watch GT 7 de 46 mm está saindo por apenas R$ 1.329 no Pix na Amazon. O novo smartwatch da Huawei, que traz um GPS mais preciso e tela AMOLED de 3.000 nits, recebe desconto de 42% sobre o preço original de R$ 2.299 durante a Black November 2026.
O novo Huawei Watch GT 7 possui um novo modo de GPS multibanda chamado Sunflower, que combina sensores internos e sinais externos para prever rotas e manter a localização precisa em túneis, pontes, viadutos e montanhas.
Sua tela AMOLED de 1,47″ com brilho de até 3.000 nits reproduz imagens com cores excelentes e visibilidade garantida em qualquer lugar. O vidro Cristal de Safira protege o display contra pancadas e arranhões.
O smartwatch suporta mais de 110 modalidades esportivas, incluindo novas como golfe e esqui. Seus sensores oferecem funções de QoL, como monitores do sono, da saúde da mulher e da oxigenação no sangue (SpO2), mas não tem eletrocardiograma (ECG), recurso exclusivo do Watch GT 7 Pro.
Seu corpo em aço inoxidável de 46 mm possui certificação IP69 e resiste a até 5 ATM, suportando assim esportes aquáticos. A bateria de 867 mAh resiste a até 21 dias de uso no modo de economia e 7 dias com o AOD ligado, segundo a fabricante, e suporta carregamento sem fio de 10 W.
Este wearable também pode fazer a diferença em situações de risco: ele é capaz de iniciar uma contagem regressiva caso detecte uma emergência médica e, se o usuário não se recuperar sozinho, pode ligar para números de emergência como 190 (polícia) e 192 (ambulância), desde que esteja pareado a um celular.
O Huawei Watch GT 7 (apenas R$ 1.329 no Pix) traz pulseira mais confortável, conversa com iPhone e Android e suporta Bluetooth 6.0 e NFC.
Durante todo o mês de novembro, a Amazon e outras varejistas trazem cupons e descontos antecipados para a Black Friday do dia 27. Acompanhe o Achados do TB no Telegram ou WhatsApp para ficar de fora da festa.
Aviso de ética: ao clicar em um link de afiliado, o preço não muda para você e recebemos uma comissão.

articles.title: Cómo acceder a las categorías secretas de Netflix desde cualquier dispositivo
articles.text:
Netflix guarda cientos de subgéneros que no aparecen en el menú principal de la plataforma y que solo se pueden desbloquear mediante códigos numéricos asignados a cada categoría. Estos códigos permiten filtrar el catálogo para encontrar desde terror con zombis hasta cine de autor, sin depender del algoritmo de recomendaciones.
El procedimiento para acceder a ellos cambia según el dispositivo que se use: computadora, navegador móvil o aplicaciones de televisores y consolas.
Cómo desbloquear categorías ocultas en Netflix según el dispositivo
El método más directo para acceder a estas categorías funciona en computadoras, Mac o cualquier navegador web, incluido el de un teléfono o una tablet. Consiste en escribir una dirección web específica que incorpora el código de la categoría buscada.
El usuario debe iniciar sesión en su cuenta de Netflix desde el navegador y, en la barra de direcciones, ingresar la estructura https://www.netflix.com/browse/genre/ seguida del número correspondiente al subgénero. Para documentales sobre crímenes, por ejemplo, el código es 9875.
Al presionar Enter, la página filtra de forma automática todo el catálogo disponible bajo esa etiqueta, sin pasos adicionales ni configuraciones previas.
En Smart TV, TV Box, Fire TV, consolas o aplicaciones móviles no existe una barra de direcciones, pero el buscador interno de la aplicación reconoce la mayoría de estos códigos numéricos.
El procedimiento consiste en abrir la app de Netflix, ingresar al ícono de búsqueda y escribir directamente el número en el teclado en pantalla. El código 8711, correspondiente a Terror, es un ejemplo de los que puede tipearse en ese buscador para obtener el listado de títulos de esa categoría.
Cuando el buscador de un televisor no logra procesar algún código en particular, existe una alternativa: abrir el enlace completo en el navegador de un teléfono o computadora, seleccionar el título deseado y agregarlo a la lista personal. De esa forma, el contenido queda sincronizado y disponible de inmediato en la cuenta vinculada al televisor.
Lista de códigos secretos de Netflix por género
Los códigos numéricos están organizados por grandes categorías que a su vez se dividen en subgéneros concretos. Dentro de Acción y Aventura, el código 46576 corresponde a acción y aventuras clásicas, mientras que 10118 agrupa cómics y superhéroes. Las artes marciales se ubican bajo el número 8985 y los wésterns bajo el 7700.
En el rubro de Terror, el código 42023 reúne producciones de terror sobrenatural y el 8646 corresponde a slasher y asesinos en serie. El terror con zombis se identifica con el número 75405, mientras que las producciones de serie B quedan bajo el código 8195.
La categoría de Ciencia Ficción y Fantasía incluye el código 3327 para ciencia ficción con extraterrestres, el 47147 para clásicos del género y el 9744 para películas de fantasía.
Dentro de Comedias, el humor negro se encuentra bajo el código 869, las comedias románticas bajo el 5475, las parodias y sátiras bajo el 4922, y los especiales de stand up o monólogos bajo el 11559.
En Thrillers y Misterio, los thrillers psicológicos corresponden al código 5505, las películas de gánsteres o mafia al 31851, las producciones de espías al 9147 y los misterios al 9994.
Por último, en Cine Internacional y Animación, el código 5685 agrupa películas coreanas, el 2653 corresponde a anime de acción, el 11881 a animación para adultos y el 29764 a cine de autor o producciones de arte y ensayo.
Cómo organiza Netflix sus películas y contenidos
Las películas en Netflix no se ordenan de forma estática o alfabética, sino mediante una interfaz dinámica de filas temáticas impulsada por algoritmos de recomendación e inteligencia artificial.
La plataforma clasifica internamente cada título a través de metadatos exhaustivos (tono, ritmo, temática, actores y miles de microcategorías específicas) y los cruza con tu historial de reproducción, tiempo de visualización, horarios y calificaciones.
A partir de estos datos, el sistema genera una cuadrícula personalizada donde tanto la jerarquía vertical de las filas (como «Tendencias», «Porque viste...» o subgéneros de nicho) como el orden horizontal de cada película se adaptan en tiempo real a tus preferencias, modificando incluso las imágenes de portada para resaltar elementos visuales que capturen mejor tu atención.

articles.title: No more Cybertrucks; Musk moves on from the angular metallic flop
articles.text:
Elon’s Edsel is no more. Last night, Tesla CEO Elon Musk revealed on social media that his car company is ending its failed attempt to wrest control of the American pickup truck market. The Cybertruck will cease production in the middle of 2027, liberating that space in Tesla’s cavernous factory for other uses—more Cybercabs, most likely.
Musk first revealed the Cybertruck in late 2019, back when Tesla was still trading at a theoretically understandable price-to-earning ratio. The pickup’s unusual angular shape owed more to low-res video game models than any concessions to practicality. At the time, Musk made fanciful claims that the truck would use a stainless steel monocoque construction, telling his audience that “the body and bed don’t do anything useful” on a normal truck. While some race cars use carbon-fiber monocoques for strength and lightness, making a pickup truck with a stainless steel monocoque chassis would only make sense if someone had an awful lot of stainless steel lying around and needed something to do with it all.
The truck was supposed to go on sale for less than $40,000, and Tesla made its usual stratospheric sales predictions that (had they been accurate) the bare metal EVs would be as ubiquitous as the Model 3 and Y.

articles.title: Ramp data shows AI spending stalling just as Anthropic nears its IPO | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Companies are using more AI than ever, but they’re not spending more on it.
A new report from Ramp shows AI spending flatlined over late summer even as token volumes rose, a sign that price competition and savvier customers may be capping revenue for OpenAI and Anthropic. According to Ramp’s data, token spend only grew 1.5% across August and September. To compare, in July, it grew 42% from the previous month.
As Anthropic gears up for its IPO, the data suggests investors might be wrong to assume AI companies will keep growing at breakneck speed.
“Almost the entire spend on AI is from venture-backed, high-growth tech companies,” Ramp’s lead economist Ara Kharazian told TechCrunch. “That’s fine as long as AI spend continues to rise, but if it starts to slow down because of something in the market or some other factor, they will all start to slow down simultaneously, and that could lead to other cascading effects.”
Kharazian said he’s already seeing evidence that the top 1% of firms — the most “AI-pilled” — have stuttered slightly in their spend in August and September, coming up just below the $10,000 per-employee they were hitting at their summer peaks. A slowdown among that cohort is “sufficient to slow down revenue entirely, despite the fact that we’re seeing rising volumes,” he said.
Ramp data shows growth in spending among median and top 10%, but it’s not enough to make up the difference. Median firms spend $12-$15 per employee per month, and the top 10% spend $600-$1,000.
“If you look at the use cases today, it’s not necessarily clear they will get up to that $10,000 per employee per month mark that the 1% is at,” Kharazian said. While there’s plenty of demand for AI coding agents in industries like software and finance, “it’s not necessarily true that a doctor’s office or a car dealership will need to spend that much on AI.”
“The era of hypergrowth may be over, and now that we know there may not be as much juice to squeeze out of the top 1%,” he continued.
October data did see a re-acceleration, with token spend up 8.9% from September 23 to October 23, but Kharazian said the headwinds on spend growth are strong.
Kharazian (who has published a series of blogs called “Cracks in the AI Thesis”) said the slowdown isn’t due to a demand problem. Again, AI volumes are up. Instead he points to the competitive nature of the marketplace.
“OpenAI and Anthropic price cuts have…just made it cheaper to use AI,” he said. In September, OpenAI cut API prices in half for GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna. Answering the price war, Anthropic has also made significant reductions to pricing for Fable 5.1 and Opus 5.5 — a decision that the company said in a recent filing slashed revenue growth by about $600 million. Both companies have also been offering enterprise discounts that are intended to lock-in spend, but in reality are hitting their revenue targets.
Kharazian said this dynamic means it has very much become a buyer’s market.
Subsidizing use of expensive technology in order to lock in customers has always been a part of the Big Tech playbook. Just recall how cheap it used to be to take an Uber or Lyft ride, and now that there are few other ride-hail players, the cost of going from A to B has risen significantly. Kharazian says those dynamics don’t work in the AI world because there’s just too much competition.
“Meta and Nvidia are also introducing enterprise offerings with pretty cheap models or open source models,” Kharazian said. He also pointed to the range of other open model companies from China and the United States, as well as a new company called Jev — a lightweight tool for choosing between a few predetermined outputs — that is increasingly among the top performers on Ramp.
“For a lot of AI use cases, you just need a simple Yes/No,” Kharazian said. “So you take your already cheap models, you shift them over to Jev, and now your already cheap stuff gets even cheaper.”
The ability to complete workloads at a much cheaper cost is another factor driving the spending slowdown. That’s partly due to the discounts from AI companies, but also because companies are just getting better at being thrifty.
“As you get really advanced in using AI, you get better at figuring out how to control it,” Kharazian said. “You’re more likely to use defaults that prevent usage of very expensive models for long-running tasks. You’re more likely to impose some budgets on employees. You’re more likely to offload some of the spend from standard and light models to even cheaper light models via routers.”
Notion co-founder Akshay Kothari recently posted internal data that matched Ramp’s insights. As he succinctly put it: “tokens go brrr. costs go ahhh.”
“A lot of the assumptions that we had about the trajectory of AI spend are starting to break down,” Kharazian said. “You can use more AI, but use it for less. That’s great for the customers…but it’s not necessarily great for the model companies. And it does introduce new questions around their revenue trajectories.”
Bloomberg reported Friday that Anthropic’s potential valuation sank from the $2 trillion estimated in early October to just $1.2 to $1.3 trillion. The company is also reportedly expected to receive a high “junk” rating from credit agencies. OpenAI also lowered its proposed valuation to $1.25 trillion from $1.4 trillion and slashed its latest fundraising goals by about $10 billion.
Kharazian says Ramp’s dataset likely informs many investor concerns. There is, however, one potential brightside for spending trajectories, albeit a speculative one.
Much of the thesis for hypergrowth spending is that AI will undoubtedly introduce new use cases that will accelerate things. AI coding emerged just a year and a half ago as the most commercially viable product that has led Anthropic and OpenAI to becoming trillion-dollar companies. The hope among investors is that there will be another revolution that will drive further spend.
Some think personal agents will be the next coding agents. OpenAI, SpaceXAI, and Meta have all released their own personal agents, alongside startups like Instinct. Kharazian is skeptical, though, that personal agents, which are “not as economically productive as coding,” will provide the boost the industry needs for nonstop growth.
“The projection is that there will be new products being introduced that will drive further growth,” Kharazian said. “But based on what we can observe today and the products available and what is commercially advanced, AI spend has started to slow down.”

articles.title: Tesla is winding down Cybertruck production, but Elon Musk insists poor sales aren't the reason
articles.text:
Facepalm: Tesla appears to be killing off the Cybertruck, and according to Elon Musk, the reason isn't that almost nobody is buying them. The CEO says production of the EV will start winding down around the middle of next year to make room for something more important: increased Cybercab production.
Musk's explanation is raising plenty of skepticism. The real reason is more likely that the truck just isn't selling anywhere near as well as Tesla or Musk expected.
 – Elon Musk (@elonmusk) November 6, 2026
Electrek writes that Tesla lumps the Cybertruck into the "other models" segment of its sales reports, along with the Model S, Model X, and now the Semi. A total of 8,295 vehicles in this category were delivered in Q3 2026, down 48% year over year. With Model S and Model X production ending in April, Electrek estimates that 7,000 to 8,000 Cybertrucks were delivered during the quarter.
It's certainly not the first time the controversial EV has reportedly sold in very small numbers. With that estimate implying an annual sales pace of around 30,000 trucks, it's a long way off the 250,000 Musk originally expected Tesla to produce each year.
Cox Automotive offers an even lower US estimate: 4,323 Cybertrucks in Q3, bringing the nine-month total to 11,586.
The warning signs have been there for some time. It was reported last year that Cybertruck sales fell to just 4,306 in Q2 2025, down 50.8% from a year earlier. By October, truckloads were arriving at SpaceX and xAI, giving Tesla a convenient outlet for vehicles that ordinary buyers weren't exactly lining up to purchase.
There have been plenty of problems beyond weak demand, too. Buyers have also had to contend with recalls, including an accelerator pedal cover that could become trapped in the interior trim. The Cybertruck has had 11 US safety recalls as of November 6, 2026, including software fixes delivered over the air. The most recent was in April 2026, covering 173 trucks with 18-inch steel wheels because wheel studs could separate from the hubs
Resale values haven't offered much comfort, either. Last year, trade-in depreciation reached 34% after just one year and 6,000 miles. So much for holding its value.
There is one caveat to the apparent cancellation: Reuters notes that Musk hasn't said whether production will move elsewhere or end altogether. However, Texas is currently the only known Tesla facility equipped to manufacture the truck's specialized components.
For now, Musk is betting on the Cybercab, which has no steering wheel or pedals. Tesla began offering paid rides in Austin in September, though questions over federal safety compliance remain a thorn in the company's side.

articles.title: Marshall Heston 120 ausprobiert: Diese Soundbar hat bei mir zu Hause den Unterschied gemacht
articles.text:
Marshall Heston 120 ausprobiert: Diese Soundbar hat bei mir zu Hause den Unterschied gemacht
Im Hause Engelien bin ich der einzige, der sich über dünnen Sound direkt aus den Lautsprechern des Fernsehers ärgert. Unterhaltung im Film? Lautstärke rauf. Action im Film? Lautstärke schnell wieder runter. So geht der typische Filmabend manchmal vonstatten. Schon mehrfach haben wir deswegen zu Hause Soundbars ausprobiert. Immer mit demselben Ergebnis: Einer freut sich, der Rest hört nach eigenen Angaben “keinen Unterschied”. Die Ausgabe lohnt sich also nicht. Die Marshall Heston 120 hat zum ersten Mal für ein anderes Ergebnis gesorgt.
Die einfache Einrichtung
Doch bevor die Soundbar den ersten Pieps von sich gibt, muss sie zunächst einmal eingerichtet werden. Das geht grundsätzlich ganz einfach, sobald man das Gerät aus dem übergroßen Karton befreit hat. Soundbar vor dem Fernseher platzieren. Stromkabel in die Steckdose und die HDMI-Strippe im Idealfall in den eArc-Eingang (steht für enhanced Audio Return Channel) am TV-Gerät. Der Standard sorgt dafür, dass Tonsignale fast ohne Komprimierung vom Fernseher an die Soundbar weitergegeben werden. Von Vorteil ist das besonders bei Raumklangtechnologien wie Dolby Atmos, die so verlustfrei durchs Wohnzimmer schallen.
Damit von nun an die Heston 120 den Ton im Wohnzimmer angibt, musste ich allerdings einen HDMI-Steckplatz opfern. Mein Fernseher hat nur deren drei und die sind eigentlich mit Spielkonsolen belegt. Zum Glück bietet die Soundbar aber selbst auch noch einen Eingang. Ärgern muss man sich also nicht. Das aber nur am Rande.
Grundsätzlich kann man den Ton direkt an der Soundbar nach Belieben an die eigenen Vorlieben anpassen. Es gibt Voreinstellungen für die Musikwiedergabe, Filme, Stimmen (in Filmen) und einen Nachtmodus, der Explosionen und Stimmen noch etwas mehr angleicht. Die Lautstärke am TV lässt sich dabei bequem mit der Fernbedienung desselben einstellen.
Was bietet die Marshall-App?
Wer es dabei belässt, kann mit der Heston gut leben, verpasst aber einen Großteil der eingebauten Funktionen. Um darauf zuzugreifen, müsst ihr die Marshall-App aus dem App- oder Play-Store herunterladen. Darüber bringt ihr die Heston 120 in euer WLAN – wenn die App mitspielt. Hier zu Hause hat es mehrere Anläufe gebraucht. Ist das erledigt, könnt ihr zunächst einmal die Kalibrierung vornehmen.
Die Soundbar lauscht dann ins Wohnzimmer und spielt einige Probetöne ab, um den Klang an die Gegebenheiten anzupassen. Ähnliche Funktionen bieten andere höherpreisige Modelle ebenfalls. Einen großen Unterschied konnte ich im Vergleich zu den Standardeinstellungen ohne App zwar nicht heraushören, aber ich freue mich auch über jedes bisschen Bass.
Wer mag, kann außerdem mit dem Equalizer in der App herumspielen und den Ton weiter auf eigene Vorlieben abstimmen. Zusätzlich bietet die Anwendung die Möglichkeit, Internetradiostationen wiederzugeben. Die Soundbar unterstützt aber auch die üblichen Standards Spotify Connect, Tidal Connect, Google Cast, Airable und Apples Airplay. Nur Spotify- und Radio-Fans profitieren aber von den Preset-Buttons an der Soundbar. Auf die drei Knöpfe könnt ihr entweder Radiosender oder Playlisten legen. Für andere Dienste sind sie nicht zu gebrauchen. Ohnehin ist die Einrichtung hakelig. In der App ließ sich keine Radiostation auf einem Knopf speichern, das ging nur direkt am Gerät. Wie das geht? Steht im Handbuch. Insgesamt verwundert es nicht, dass die App im App-Store nicht so gut wegkommt (1,8 von fünf Sternen).
Abseits vom Digitalen bietet die Soundbar auch RCA‑Eingänge, über die sich analoge Geräte wie Plattenspieler anschließen lassen. Einen Eingang für Subwoofer gibt es ebenfalls. Einen solchen verkauft Marshall selbst separat. Wer Probleme mit dem WLAN hat, kann die Heston 120 außerdem dank Ethernet-Port direkt an den Router anstöpseln.
Endlich mal guter Filmsound
Doch die wichtige Frage lautet: Wie klingt sie denn nun? Insgesamt 11 Treiber hat Marshall in die Heston 120 eingebaut, darunter zwei Subwoofer. Und die hört man auch. “Er ist schon ein kleiner Bassangaber”, sagt meine Frau über den langgezogenen Lautsprecher. Stimmt schon. Der lässt es gerne dröhnen. Das klingt im Film und Spiel dafür aber auch richtig gut und zieht einen direkt in die Action. Auch die Dialoge klingen klar. Endlich mal richtig guter Filmsound. Zu später Stunde ist aber dann doch eher der Nachtmodus angesagt, wenn man die Nachbarn nicht ärgern will. Ansonsten ist der Sound kristallklar, niemals übertrieben oder zu dünn. Das macht Spaß. Neben Dolby Atmos, das von vielen Streaming-Plattformen zumindest für ausgewählte Titel angeboten wird, unterstützt die Heston 120 auch DTS:X.
Bei der Musikwiedergabe kommen passend zur Marke besonders rockige Stücke gut zur Geltung. In Metallicas Enter Sandman geht es eigentlich um Albträume, das klingt auf der Heston aber traumhaft gut. Rap-Songs wie Empire State of Mind von Jay-Z und Alicia Keys oder X gonna give it to ya von DMX dürften dagegen gerne etwas kräftiger klingen. Insgesamt ist mir die Soundleistung bei Filmen aber wichtiger.
Fazit
Marshalls Heston 120 überzeugt da, wo es darauf ankommt. In Filmen, auch bei Videospielen, auch bei Rockmusik. Das macht schon Spaß. Dauerhaft unter dem Fernseher wird die Soundbar bei mir aber nicht stehen. Sie kostet 999 Euro. Der Preis ist selbst für das Geleistete etwas hoch. Sollte die Soundbar zu Deal-Events wie dem nahenden Black Friday rabattiert werden, ich könnte ins Wanken kommen.

articles.title: Meet the audio glasses using cutting edge tech to provide a natural listening experience
articles.text:
Technology is improving and advancing so fast that it seems like the future we dreamed of is already here.
Take Nuance AudioTM Plus Glasses, for example. These aren’t just any glasses, they are actually used to improve and support hearing.
Using groundbreaking technology, Nuance AudioTM Plus Glasses have paved the way for wearables that are improving lives and healthcare. Want to know how it works? Here’s the 411 on Nuance AudioTM Plus Glasses.
Advanced sound technology for all-day hearing support
Nuance AudioTM Plus Glasses’ integrated advanced sound technology is supported by open-ear speakers that sit just above the ear. They are integrated into the temple arms via extension hinges, which are adjustable within a set range. Once powered, the technology is always on and also uses directional microphones for a natural listening experience.
The device is also compatible with near-prescription lenses, and custom lens options are available to suit the wearer’s vision and listening environment. This eliminates the need for multiple devices and allows the ears to breathe while reducing listening fatigue.
Designed for mild to moderate hearing loss, Nuance supports listening in everyday situations, especially when background noises make conversations harder.
Key features
Breaking the stigma around assistive listening, Nuance AudioTM Plus offers discreet, stylish glasses that seamlessly combine vision and listening support in one frame, building on the distinctive open-ear technology of Nuance AudioTM Glasses with enhanced amplification, improved speech clarity in noisy environments, better own-voice perception, and an extended battery life of approximately 10 hours under average product conditions.*
Directional amplification helps enhance speech clarity through directional microphones and beamforming technology, allowing users to focus on conversations in front of them.
Easy to use and simple to set up and manage through the intuitive Nuance AudioTM App, Nuance AudioTM Plus also features new on-frame controls, including a dedicated power switch and volume buttons conveniently positioned on the temples.
Open-ear comfort comes from lightweight, open-ear speakers integrated into the temples that leave the ears free for long-lasting comfort, while an expanded range of sizes, universal fitting and adjustable nose pads on selected styles help provide a secure and comfortable fit.
It’s an all-in-one solution designed to address both vision and listening assistance needs in one elegant device. Meanwhile, hands-free phone calls allow users to answer and manage voice calls directly from the frames when paired with a compatible iPhone.**
Styles and accessories
Nuance AudioTM Plus is available in three timeless frame styles Square 53, Panthos 48 and Upturn 52 and five colours, Shiny Black, Shiny Burgundy, Deep Blue, Amber, and Olive Green.
The standard package includes a charging pad and USB-C cable to charge Nuance AudioTM Plus.
For those who prefer not to use a device, there is also a remote option, which improves accessibility. When it comes to the lens options, users can decide from transition lenses that adjust to UV and a blue light filter option.
User experience
The glasses are easily manageable from the Nuance AudioTM App, and the glasses also feature on-frame controls for quick access to key functions, while a dedicated remote control is available separately.
With the app, users can control audio modes, where they can switch between two frontal, to focus on face-to-face conversations, and all-around, to amplify all surrounding sounds. Choose the pre-configured amplification settings (A, B, C or D) for a tailored hearing experience, and customize the background noise level with three levels of noise reduction. You can also adjust the volume of amplification on a scale from 1 to 5.
Lenses
Nuance AudioTM Plus can be fitted with any type of optical lens, according to the wearer’s vision needs. The glasses can also be paired with Transitions® lenses, which adapt to changing light conditions to support an integrated hearing and vision experience throughout the day.
In Canada, the recommended retail price will start from $1,149, depending on the lens configuration.
Ready for all-day support without sacrificing comfort or design? Learn more about the first-of-its-kind product, Nuance AudioTM Glasses, online.
*Based on average product condition
**The product, as an MFI certified device, supports voice calls only when used with an iPhone (requires iOS 16 or later)

articles.title: Stranger Things sera de retour dans une nouvelle série préquelle prévue pour 2028
articles.text:
Netflix n’en a pas terminé avec sa série phare. Ce vendredi 6 novembre, jour du Stranger Things Day (la date à laquelle Will Byers disparaît dans la série, en 1983), la plateforme a officialisé l’arrivée d’une nouvelle série dérivée : Other Worlds: A Stranger Things Adventure.
Annoncée dans un communiqué publié sur le site de Netflix, Other Worlds sera une préquelle en prises de vues réelles attendue pour 2028. L’annonce s’accompagne d’un premier teaser, qui reprend déjà les codes de la série principale.
On y aperçoit un vélo abandonné près d’une clôture de barbelés, de nuit, avec une ville au loin. La caméra dévoile ensuite un ciel orageux, où une force mystérieuse semble se réveiller. L’intrigue quitte Hawkins, dans l’Indiana, pour Marion, dans le Nevada, le 19 avril 1955. La série se déroule donc avant la pièce The First Shadow, qui raconte en 1959 la jeunesse d’Henry Creel, le futur Vecna.
Un projet porté par les créateurs de la série originale
Pour donner vie à cette nouvelle histoire, Netflix s’entoure de plusieurs figures bien connues de la franchise. Matt et Ross Duffer sont de retour à la création, aux côtés de Kate Trefry, scénariste de longue date de Stranger Things et autrice de la pièce The First Shadow. Elle sera co-créatrice et showrunneuse de la série.
Le réalisateur britannique Joe Wright, connu pour Orgueil et Préjugés, Reviens-moi et Les Heures sombres, sera derrière la caméra pour les trois premiers épisodes. Shawn Levy, producteur historique de Stranger Things, participera lui aussi au projet en tant que producteur exécutif.
Les frères Duffer décrivent une série qui reste du Stranger Things tout en étant « délicieusement neuve », avec un nouveau décor et de nouveaux héros et méchants. Shawn Levy parle de son côté d’une histoire imprégnée de « l’ADN » de la série originale, mais qui explore une autre époque, avec de nouveaux personnages, de nouveaux thèmes et une nouvelle mythologie.
Le tournage de Other Worlds: A Stranger Things Adventure est prévu au Nouveau-Mexique. Le casting n’est pas encore connu (les frères Duffer indiquent qu’il commence tout juste), et Netflix n’a pas donné de date de sortie précise. Il faudra donc patienter jusqu’en 2028 pour découvrir cette nouvelle histoire. En attendant, les cinq saisons de Stranger Things restent disponibles sur la plateforme.
Other Worlds rejoint ainsi d’autres déclinaisons de la franchise. Netflix diffuse déjà Stranger Things: Tales From ’85, une série d’animation qui suit la bande de Hawkins pendant l’hiver 1985 et dont deux saisons sont disponibles. L’univers a aussi été adapté au théâtre avec Stranger Things: The First Shadow, à l’affiche à Londres jusqu’au 27 décembre et à Broadway jusqu’au 3 janvier 2027.

articles.title: Waze pourrait bientôt afficher les cyclistes équipés d'appareils Garmin
articles.text:
Waze sera-t-il bientôt capable de signaler les cyclistes aux automobilistes ? C’est ce que semblent suggérer des lignes de code récemment trouvées dans l’application Garmin Connect.
Waze s’améliore, lentement mais sûrement. Cet été, l’application s’est dotée d'un mode moto et de plusieurs fonctionnalités boostées à l'IA. Fin septembre, Waze a aussi ajouté des magasins sponsorisés à l’itinéraire de ses utilisateurs. Une nouvelle option prometteuse pourrait également voir le jour bientôt. On vous explique.
Les cyclistes Garmin, bientôt visibles sur Waze ?
L’équipe de Gadget and Wearables a récemment analysé la version 5.31 de l’application Garmin Connect. Elle y a trouvé les mentions suivantes : « Partager votre position avec Waze », « Partager vos trajets avec Waze » et « Partage de position Waze ». Des indices qui laissent penser que Waze pourrait bientôt prévenir les automobilistes de la présence de cyclistes sur leurs trajets.
Cette fonctionnalité, qui devra être activée manuellement par les cyclistes, pourrait s’appuyer sur LiveTrack, un outil déjà inclus dans les appareils Garmin, qui diffuse en direct la position d’un sportif à ses proches. Pour l’instant, Garmin et Waze n’ont pas communiqué sur cette nouveauté. Impossible donc d’en savoir plus sur ce qui est réellement prévu, ni sur les appareils qui prendront en charge cette nouvelle option.
Une bonne idée qui soulève quelques interrogations
Sur le papier, cette nouvelle option, qui sera, hélas, réservée aux propriétaires d'appareils Garmin, a tout d’une bonne idée : le dernier baromètre sur l’insécurité routière de l’Observatoire national interministériel de la sécurité routière, publiés en octobre dernier, montre que « la mortalité à vélo, avec 256 cyclistes décédés sur ces 12 derniers mois, est en hausse de +15 % par rapport aux 12 mois précédents. ».
Dans les faits, la forme que prendra le signalement est cruciale : un surcroît d’alertes pourrait énerver les conducteurs et les pousser à désactiver la détection. Malheureusement, on ne sait pas, à ce jour, comment Waze compte signaler la présence de cyclistes sur son app. L’équipe de Gadgets and Wearables émet toutefois plusieurs hypothèses plausibles : « Waze pourrait afficher une icône de cycliste, un avertissement signalant la présence d'un cycliste, ou une information mise à jour en continu au fur et à mesure que le cycliste se déplace. »
Pour l’heure, impossible de savoir quand cette fonctionnalité sera disponible, ni si elle sera accessible gratuitement. Garmin pourrait, en effet, décider d’en faire une option payante, ce qui serait bien dommage.

articles.title: Northern Arc's diversified debt fund hits first close at over Rs 400 crore
articles.text:
Northern Arc's diversified debt fund hits first close at over Rs 400 Cr
The 15th private credit fund from Northern Arc Investment Managers targets a Rs 1,500 crore corpus and a 16% XIRR, as its India Impact Fund matures after deploying Rs 1,398 crore.
Northern Arc Investment Managers, the asset management arm of Northern Arc Capital, has announced the first close of its Northern Arc Diversified Debt Fund with commitments of more than Rs 400 crore from institutions, family offices, ultra-high-net-worth individuals (UHNIs) and high-net-worth individuals (HNIs).
The fund is the firm's 15th private credit vehicle. It is a sector-agnostic Category II Alternative Investment Fund (AIF) focused on performing private credit, rated AA (SO) by CareEdge Ratings. It targets a corpus of Rs 1,500 crore, with a greenshoe option of Rs 500 crore that could take it to Rs 2,000 crore. The fund has a five-year tenure and targets a 16% XIRR.
The announcement coincides with the maturity of the Northern Arc India Impact Fund, which channelled global capital into financial inclusion opportunities across India. Over its tenure, the fund supported 60 businesses across credit cycles, with gross deployment of over Rs 1,398 crore at the fund level, backed by UHNIs, family offices, and domestic and global institutional investors.
Commenting on the announcements, Ashish Mehrotra, Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer, Northern Arc Capital, said, "The first close of the Northern Arc Diversified Debt Fund reflects continued investor interest in private credit and its evolving role in sophisticated investment portfolios. The maturity of our Northern Arc India Impact Fund further demonstrates our experience in managing private credit investments across credit cycles. Together, these milestones reinforce our focus on disciplined credit selection, portfolio diversification and risk management.”
He added, “Over the past decade, we have built a diversified private credit platform that has deployed over Rs. 16,500 crores across 15 AIFs and two PMS offerings and served more than 1,500 investors across institutional and wealth segments. As private credit becomes an increasingly strategic allocation for investors, we remain focused on connecting capital with businesses across sectors while creating opportunities for risk-adjusted returns."
Since its inception in 2014, Northern Arc Investment Managers has launched 15 funds, of which seven have fully matured, delivering returns at a weighted average XIRR of over 14.5%, in line with targeted returns, without any extension or principal loss to investors, the company said. It has cumulatively distributed over Rs 10,000 crore of principal and coupon since inception.
Separately, Northern Arc Capital reported a 41% year-on-year growth in consolidated profit after tax to Rs 129 crore in Q2 FY27, while net interest income rose 32% to Rs 425 crore. Lending assets under management grew 34% to Rs 19,003 crore, supported by a 64% rise in direct lending AUM to Rs 12,502 crore, which now accounts for 66% of the overall portfolio. Credit costs improved by 11 basis points to 2.66%."

articles.title: Sony donne des nouvelles de la PS6, mais un obstacle de taille se profile
articles.text:
L’air de rien, la PS5 est sortie il y a 6 ans, en novembre 2020. Il est donc temps que la nouvelle génération commence à pointer le bout de son nez. Justement, Lin Tao, directrice financière de Sony, est venue apporter quelques informations concernant la prochaine plateforme de Sony dédiée aux jeux vidéo.
Le développement de la PS6 avance « comme prévu »
Sony vient de dévoiler ses résultats financiers. Lors d’une session de questions-réponses, un journaliste a demandé à Lin Tao, directrice financière de Sony, des nouvelles concernant l’avancement du développement de la PlayStation 6. Lin Tao lui a alors répondu que les travaux de recherche et développement « progressent comme prévu », tout en précisant que le développement lui-même « respecte le calendrier prévu ».
Par ailleurs, Lin Tao indique que Sony compte réaliser « les investissements nécessaires » pour développer sa nouvelle plateforme et accomplir « des progrès significatifs » dans sa préparation. À noter que la directrice financière de Sony n’a pas prononcé explicitement le nom PlayStation 6, mais parle de « prochaine plateforme ». Par ailleurs, elle ne donne aucune indication quant à la date de sortie de cette nouvelle plateforme dédiée aux jeux vidéo.
La PS6 ne risque pas d’arriver de sitôt
Autant dire que Sony ne doit pas être pressé de lancer la PlayStation 6, et ce pour plusieurs raisons. Tout d’abord, la console s’est vendue à ce jour à 97,9 millions d’exemplaires à travers le monde. Sony bénéficie donc d’un parc de joueurs plus que conséquent. Même si les ventes de la console ralentissent progressivement en raison de son ancienneté, celles-ci, et plus particulièrement celles de la PS5 Pro, ont récemment connu un regain important à l’approche de la sortie de GTA 6.
Par ailleurs, Sony bénéficie actuellement d’une position dominante sur le marché, les Xbox Series X et S ne s’étant pas vraiment bien vendues. Il faudra voir si Xbox parviendra à remonter la pente avec sa prochaine console, la Xbox Helix. Mais surtout, la crise mondiale de la mémoire vive risque de limiter les marges de manœuvre de Sony. Il est peu probable que l’entreprise japonaise lance une nouvelle console dans un tel contexte de crise. La PlayStation 6 risque déjà d’être chère, mais un lancement dans les deux prochaines années pourrait faire exploser son prix.
Pour rappel, la PS5 est sortie 6 ans et 11 mois après la PS4. Il est fort probable que nous devions patienter un peu plus longtemps cette fois-ci avant de découvrir la nouvelle génération de consoles Sony.

articles.title: Arturo Pérez Reverte, escritor: "Hay un libro que siempre recomiendo, se llama 'La isla del coral', y otro, 'El señor de las moscas"
articles.text:
Tras su éxito con Alatriste, Arturo Pérez-Reverte ha vuelto al género de aventuras en 'La hipótesis más peligrosa', su última novela recién publicada. Esta vez, el protagonista tiene dieciséis años y se embarca en un velero por el Mediterráneo con un padre al que acaba de conocer.
Qué pueden esperar los jóvenes en una novela de aventuras fue justo lo que le preguntó un estudiante al escritor en una charla de Aprendemos Juntos de BBVA. El escritor dijo que muchos clásicos del género habían perdido a su público, pero que algunos todavía aguantaban bien. "Hay un libro que siempre recomiendo, se llama 'La isla del coral'". "Y otra se llama 'El señor de las moscas'", añadió después de resumir la primera novela.
En 'La isla del coral', de R. M. Ballantyne, tres chicos sobreviven a un naufragio y acaban en una isla del Pacífico. Allí tienen que apañárselas entre los tres. En 'El señor de las moscas', de William Golding, el punto de partida es un accidente de avión. Los únicos supervivientes son un grupo de escolares y, a medida que avanza la historia, la convivencia se vuelve violenta.
En otro momento de la charla, Pérez-Reverte les explicó para qué cree que sirve leer. Si has leído y has visto mundo, les dijo, es más difícil que alguien te venda una versión demasiado fácil de las cosas. "Cuanto más culto eres, cuanto más has mirado, has vivido, has leído, cuanto más te has preocupado de ver el mundo a tu alrededor, eres menos manipulable, menos engañable".
Pérez-Reverte cree que muchos de los libros de aventuras que leía su generación han perdido a su público aunque en la misma charla reconoció a la audiencia que si empezara a escribir de joven, ahora se dedicaría a hacer guiones para videojuegos.
"La aventura siempre ha estado ahí", dijo en la misma charla, aunque ahora cambie el formato de la historia.

articles.title: Los consejeros delegados de las farmacéuticas no se creen que la IA vaya a curar enfermedades: Vertex probó con unas 50 empresas de IA y ninguna logró un fármaco viable
articles.text:
Una de las promesas, quizá la más importante, que han hecho los líderes de algunos de los laboratorios de inteligencia artificial (IA) es que su tecnología contribuirá a la cura de muchas enfermedades. "Creo que la IA podría curar la mayoría de las grandes enfermedades en los próximos cinco a diez años". Estas palabras las escribió Dario Amodei, el director general de Anthropic, el pasado 13 de septiembre.
Demis Hassabis, el consejero delegado de Google DeepMind, defendió en abril de 2025 esta misma premisa: "Podemos curar todas las enfermedades con ayuda de la IA. Quizá dentro de la próxima década. No veo por qué no". Y Sam Altman, el máximo responsable de OpenAI, también ha expresado sus deseos recientemente: "No quiero detener el progreso tecnológico. Quiero esa cura para el cáncer, para el Alzheimer".
Estas declaraciones son muy alentadoras, pero por el momento solo son promesas. A pesar de lo rápido que está avanzando la IA, las expectativas de los líderes de las compañías tecnológicas están todavía muy alejadas de las aportaciones que está realizando al desarrollo de nuevos medicamentos. Esta tecnología está demostrando que es una herramienta muy valiosa en este ámbito, pero está muy lejos de poner en nuestras manos medicamentos eficaces y seguros. Y aún más lejos de curar el cáncer o el Alzheimer.
El experimento de Vertex
Jeff Leiden, el presidente de la empresa farmacéutica Vertex, ha explicado que su laboratorio ha recurrido a aproximadamente 50 compañías de IA para analizar una base de datos con unos 10.000 compuestos farmacológicos. El resultado que ha obtenido ha sido muy decepcionante: ningún modelo de IA logró desarrollar un medicamento viable. Esto no quiere decir en absoluto que esta tecnología no tenga nada que decir en el terreno del desarrollo de nuevos fármacos, pero pone encima de la mesa una realidad inapelable: hoy la IA no puede descubrir nuevos medicamentos por sí sola.
El organismo de los seres humanos es extraordinariamente complejo debido a que intervienen en él miles de procesos biológicos
Además, Leiden ha hecho una reflexión importante: la IA actualmente puede actuar como un copiloto de los investigadores. Puede ayudarlos, pero no puede reemplazarlos. Para desarrollar un nuevo medicamento no basta encontrar una molécula que sea capaz de interactuar con una proteína concreta. El organismo de los seres humanos es extraordinariamente complejo debido a que intervienen en él miles de procesos biológicos. Y entre muchos de ellos existen unas dependencias muy profundas que es difícil identificar y entender.
Los modelos de IA tienen la capacidad gracias, sobre todo, a su habilidad a la hora de identificar patrones, de encontrar posibles dianas terapéuticas, predecir estructuras de proteínas o proponer moléculas prometedoras. Pero de momento ninguno de ellos ha conseguido anticipar con suficiente precisión cómo se comportará un compuesto cuando entre en contacto con un organismo humano. Y este conocimiento es esencial.
Los ensayos preclínicos y las fases de investigación clínica pueden prolongarse durante varios años
Además, hay otra idea que no debemos pasar por alto: el proceso de desarrollo de medicamentos se complica aún más cuando es necesario predecir efectos secundarios e interacciones con los procesos biológicos. Sea como sea, imaginemos que una IA logra desarrollar una molécula muy prometedora que, sobre el papel, no tiene efectos secundarios perniciosos ni desencadena interacciones potencialmente peligrosas con algunos procesos biológicos. Aun así, quedaría un cabo suelto: los ensayos clínicos.
Esta etapa del desarrollo de nuevos medicamentos es fundamental y no puede omitirse por mucho que los modelos de IA predigan que un fármaco funciona correctamente y no es peligroso. Los ensayos preclínicos y las fases de investigación clínica pueden prolongarse durante varios años, por lo que acelerar el descubrimiento de candidatos farmacológicos no implica necesariamente aumentar la proporción de medicamentos que terminan llegando al mercado. La industria farmacéutica está utilizando la IA, sí, pero sus expectativas son mucho más conservadoras que las de los líderes de los laboratorios de IA.

articles.title: GitLab 19.5 Makes Agentic Development a Governed Part of the DevOps Platform
articles.text:
GitLab 19.5, released on October 15, puts agentic software development and governance at the centre of the platform, making its GitLab MCP server generally available while expanding how external AI agents can interact with GitLab.
The release allows MCP-compatible tools such as Claude Code and Cursor to access GitLab's broader tool catalogue and invoke GitLab Duo Agent Platform agents and flows. At the same time, GitLab is adding controls for governing those external agents, giving security teams visibility into which agents are being used, by whom, and against which projects.
The generally available GitLab MCP server provides agents with access to GitLab capabilities through the Model Context Protocol. New tools allow agents to discover groups, inspect individual CI/CD artifact files, and start or monitor GitLab Duo agents and flows. Administrators can also select which MCP toolsets are exposed, reducing unnecessary tools and the context they consume.
Giving an agent every available tool increases both context consumption and the number of actions the model could potentially take. Toolset selection provides a relatively simple form of least-privilege agent design.
GitLab.com also introduces MCP rate limits of 60 requests per minute for Free users and 600 for Premium and Ultimate users, with reconnects and retries counting towards the limit.
One of the more significant additions is the ability to bring Externally Connected Agents into GitLab's AI Governance capabilities.
Previously, the AI Governance Dashboard focused on GitLab Duo Agent Platform agents. GitLab 19.5 allows tools such as Claude Code, Cursor, and Codex to be connected through the GitLab CLI. Once configured, organisations can record qualifying agent sessions, including the user, agent, project, and timing, with activity appearing alongside GitLab's own agents. Audit events can also be streamed to a SIEM.
This is an important step beyond simply providing an MCP endpoint. Connectivity creates capability; governance determines whether that capability can be safely used at organisational scale.
GitLab Duo CLI also gains an auto mode, allowing agents to execute tools without requesting approval for every shell command, Git operation, or MCP call. The feature is disabled by default and can be controlled at instance, group, and project levels, while tools explicitly marked Always Deny remain blocked.
The /goal command is also now generally available, allowing developers to describe an open-ended objective and have GitLab Duo delegate implementation and verification to a governed flow.
Together, these features move GitLab closer to an agent operating model in which developers provide intent while agents execute multiple steps across the development environment.
That makes the governance controls increasingly important: the more autonomous the agent becomes, the less practical it is to rely on a human approving every individual action.
The release also makes GitLab Secrets Manager generally available. Built on OpenBao, it integrates with existing GitLab group and project permissions, scopes secrets to the jobs that require them, and generates audit events for secret operations.
GitLab is also expanding security configuration profiles, allowing organisations to centrally customise settings such as excluded paths, analyzer images and full-history scans for Secret Detection and SAST rather than repeating configuration in every project's CI/CD file.
These changes complement the agent features by strengthening the controls around the repositories, credentials, and pipelines that agents may access.
GitLab's direction increasingly resembles GitHub's strategy of turning coding agents into participants in the software lifecycle, but GitLab is placing particular emphasis on connecting external agents to its existing DevSecOps governance model.
GitHub's ecosystem benefits from the reach of GitHub Copilot and coding agents, while tools such as Cursor and Claude Code focus more heavily on the developer's local environment. GitLab's MCP approach instead attempts to make the DevOps platform itself agent-accessible, including repositories, issues, pipelines, artifacts, and GitLab-native agents.
The competitive question GitLab is looking at is moving beyond which coding assistant generates better code to which platform provides the safest and most useful environment for autonomous agents to perform engineering work.

articles.title: Las computadoras cuánticas podrían descifrar la encriptación bancaria en tan solo tres días, según estudio
articles.text:
Una computadora cuántica con 23.000 cúbits podría romper el cifrado RSA-2048, el estándar que protege cuentas bancarias, sitios web y plataformas de almacenamiento de datos en todo el mundo, en apenas 3,14 días. Así lo determinó un estudio de la firma francesa Alice & Bob, que además proyecta que este escenario podría concretarse antes de que termine la década. Sus resultados, aún no revisados por pares, se encuentran en el repositorio Cryptology ePrint Archive.
RSA-2048 es considerado el máximo estándar de cifrado disponible en la actualidad. Protege la infraestructura digital que sostiene desde redes sociales hasta la banca en línea, y su fortaleza radica en la dificultad de factorizar un módulo de 617 dígitos en dos números primos.
Para una computadora clásica, resolver ese cálculo demandaría recursos económicos tan elevados que superarían cualquier beneficio obtenido al vulnerar el sistema. Esa ecuación cambia por completo cuando se introduce la computación cuántica, que permitiría ejecutar el mismo ataque de forma más rápida y a un costo considerablemente menor.
El algoritmo que amenaza el cifrado actual
La base matemática de esta vulnerabilidad se remonta a 1994, cuando el matemático Peter Shor desarrolló un algoritmo capaz de factorizar los números que sustentan el cifrado RSA-2048.
Su aplicación práctica, sin embargo, depende de contar con una computadora cuántica suficientemente grande y precisa para ejecutarlo. Dado que los cúbits físicos son propensos a errores, cualquier equipo que corra el algoritmo de Shor necesita además un mecanismo de corrección de errores que garantice resultados confiables.
En 2019, investigadores de Google Quantum AI habían calculado que se necesitarían 20 millones de cúbits físicos para quebrar el RSA-2048. En los seis años siguientes, esa cifra cayó a menos de un millón, una reducción que responde tanto a mejoras matemáticas en la eficiencia del algoritmo, perfeccionado durante tres décadas, como a los avances tecnológicos que elevaron el rendimiento lógico de los cúbits.
Los cúbits gato reducen drásticamente la cifra necesaria
Alice & Bob trabaja con una tecnología conocida como cúbits gato (cat qubits), que en 2023 arrojó una primera estimación de 350.000 cúbits necesarios para ejecutar el algoritmo de Shor. Una revisión posterior, con versiones mejoradas de estos cúbits, redujo esa cifra a los 23.000 mencionados, con un tiempo de ejecución de poco más de tres días.
El factor tiempo también resulta determinante en este tipo de proyecciones. Según el estudio, una computadora cuántica equipada con 610.530 cúbits gato podría completar la misma tarea en apenas una hora y media. Aunque ninguna máquina actual alcanza los 23.000 cúbits necesarios, los investigadores de Alice & Bob consideran que se trata de un número relativamente bajo y alcanzable en los próximos años.
El desafío de la infraestructura y las alternativas disponibles
El principal obstáculo para alcanzar esa escala no es solo la cantidad de cúbits, sino la infraestructura adicional que exige un sistema de ese tamaño y la necesidad de que todo el equipo siga cabiendo en un laboratorio de dimensiones razonables. Pese a esa dificultad, los investigadores de la firma francesa estiman que construir una computadora cuántica con esa capacidad será posible dentro de pocos años, lo que dejaría obsoleto al cifrado RSA-2048 tal como se lo conoce hoy.
Frente a este panorama, ya existen estándares de encriptación poscuántica diseñados para resistir ataques de este tipo, aunque todavía no han sido sometidos a pruebas exhaustivas. El estudio de Alice & Bob insta a la comunidad de ciberseguridad a intensificar la evaluación de estos nuevos algoritmos e iniciar la transición de los sistemas actuales hacia ellos antes de que las computadoras cuánticas de esta escala se vuelvan una realidad extendida.

articles.title: Rocket Report: Artemis II literally tore through the atmosphere; New Glenn delay
articles.text:
NASA's Space Launch System rocket lifts off from Kennedy Space Center, Florida, to begin the Artemis II mission to the Moon on April 1, 2026.
Credit:
NASA/Keegan Barber
NASA's Space Launch System rocket lifts off from Kennedy Space Center, Florida, to begin the Artemis II mission to the Moon on April 1, 2026.
Credit:
NASA/Keegan Barber
Welcome to Edition 9.18 of the Rocket Report! Blue Origin packed a lot of news into one afternoon Thursday with the reveal of a new kick stage for the New Glenn rocket, a new rocket engine design, and the minor and widely expected delay for New Glenn’s return-to-flight mission from December until January. The reconstruction of Blue Origin’s wrecked launch pad at Cape Canaveral, Florida, continues apace after a catastrophic explosion nearly six months ago. There’s a lot of pent-up demand from NASA, Amazon, and the Space Force for Blue Origin to get New Glenn back in action.
As always, we welcome reader submissions, and if you don’t want to miss an issue, please subscribe using the box below (the form will not appear on AMP-enabled versions of the site). Each report will include information on small-, medium-, and heavy-lift rockets as well as a quick look ahead at the next three launches on the calendar.
SpaceX vets work on water-fed propulsion. Three brothers who worked at SpaceX in the Falcon 9 era are now building satellites that run on water, a potentially harvestable resource on the Moon and found all over the Solar System, Ars reports. In late 2022, the three Carlisle brothers founded Argo Space to build infrastructure in space. Their vision was not just in-space transportation but also removing the need to use propellants from Earth to move around the heavens. Argo Space’s satellites will use water not only as a propellant, but also as a coolant and radiation shield.
How does this work? … Argo Space flew its first mission in July, but the spacecraft failed after one of its solar arrays didn’t deploy, and there wasn’t enough time to test the propulsion system. Two more missions are on Argo Space’s schedule for 2027 to demonstrate the company’s water-based thrusters. The propulsion system is basically a small rocket that uses hydrogen and oxygen as propellants. However, instead of launching with separate tanks of liquid hydrogen and liquid oxygen, the satellite carries a reservoir of liquid water. In space, the vehicle uses solar power to split water into hydrogen and oxygen gases and burns them to generate thrust.
JAXA backs small satellite launcher. Japanese launcher startup Interstellar Technologies has secured the backing of the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA) for its Zero rocket program, Aviation Week & Space Technology reports. The company said JAXA selected it for its Acceleration of Commercial Rocket Launch Demonstration program under the Space Strategic Fund. The government-funded program supports development and flight demonstrations of private launch companies with grants of up to $76 million per company, with the goal of fostering a growing commercial launch industry in Japan. Interstellar previously raised more than $250 million, with roughly equivalent funds from government and private capital.
Zeroing in … Interstellar is using the money to complete development of its Zero rocket, a two-stage launcher designed to carry up to 1 metric ton (2,200 pounds) of payload to low-Earth orbit. “We have achieved critical technical milestones, including Japan’s first successful firing test of an orbital-class methane engine,” said Satoshi Nakayama, director of the board and president of Interstellar. “We have now reached the stage where we must swiftly turn these proven development results into operational commercial services.” The most recent update from Interstellar indicated a first launch of Zero in 2027.
Rocket Report
Keep up with the latest in space exploration and rocket launches.
Launch demand outpacing supply. A new report from analytics firm Quilty Space confirms that, outside of China, the world faces a significant shortage of rockets over the next five years, Ars reports. The firm estimates that between now and 2030, there will be a shortfall of about 150 launches compared to demand from satellite operators and civil space agencies. If demand from the US military is added in—and SpaceX does not extend the Falcon 9 and Falcon Heavy program to accommodate increased national security needs—the shortage could be doubled.
Worse than we thought … “What we wanted to get at is to understand how severe this launch crisis is and when will it be resolved,” said Caleb Henry, director of research at Quilty Space. “What we learned is that the launch crisis is more severe than we thought and that it will not go away this decade for sure, and it might not abate until sometime late in the 2030s.” Why is this happening? Quilty puts the blame on several factors: the war in Ukraine taking Russian rockets off the Western market; Amazon Leo demand; developmental delays in a new generation of rockets, from New Glenn and Vulcan to Neutron, Terran R, and Nova; and more recently, the retirement of the Falcon 9 as a rocket for commercial service.
China continues launching mega-constellation. Another 18 satellites for China’s SpaceSail Internet network launched Tuesday (Monday, US time) from a spaceport in the country’s northwestern desert. The mission marked the second launch—and first operational flight—of the Kinetica 2 rocket developed by a Chinese startup known as CAS Space. The SpaceSail constellation, also known as Qianfan, now consists of some 275 flat-panel satellites from a series of launches that began in August 2024. The network’s first phase will number 1,296 satellites.
A mini-Falcon Heavy … The Kinetica 2 is an interesting launch vehicle, with three side-by-side boosters arranged in a manner similar to SpaceX’s Falcon Heavy. But the Kinetica 2 is a much smaller rocket, with three kerosene-fueled engines on each booster instead of nine. Its lift performance to low-Earth orbit is about 12 metric tons (26,000 pounds). CAS Space plans to eventually recover and reuse the Kinetica 2 boosters.
India launches strategic navigation satellite. A Geosynchronous Satellite Launch Vehicle (GSLV) rocket launched on October 30 with a satellite to restore India’s regional navigation system, NDTV reports. The NVS-03 satellite is the third spacecraft in India’s second-generation navigation network. Some of the fleet’s older satellites suffered from atomic clock failures, rendering them partially or totally unusable. NVS-03 carries multiple clocks of different designs in an attempt to overcome the system’s reliability problems.
A “naughty boy” … India’s medium-lift GSLV has now launched 20 times since debuting in 2001. The rocket doesn’t fly as often as India’s smaller launcher, the PSLV, and hasn’t always performed well when it has. Six of the 20 flights ended in total or partial failures, but most of the mishaps occurred early in the rocket’s history. GSLV’s track record earned it the title “naughty boy” from Indian space officials. The most recent launch was a different story. The head of India’s space agency, V. Narayanan, declared that the GSLV’s recent flight was the “most precise launch of any rocket in the world.” We’re not sure what metric Narayanan used to make that claim, but the launch was, indeed, a success.
China reveals roadmap to lunar landing. Chinese space officials confirmed that the Asian nation plans to land its astronauts on the Moon within three years, Ars reports. At the Seventh Manned Spaceflight Conference in Beijing, officials, including Wang Xiang, chief designer for the lunar exploration program, laid out the country’s most publicly detailed plans yet for a series of missions leading up to a crewed lunar landing “before 2030.” China’s lunar landings will involve a lunar-orbit rendezvous similar to what NASA did in the 1960s and early 1970s with the Apollo program. However, lacking a rocket as powerful as the Saturn V vehicle, the crew and lunar lander will launch separately to the Moon.
These are the rockets … China’s Long March 10 rocket family will be the workhorse for the country’s initial crew missions to the Moon. The next big test will be the demonstration flight of a Long March 10A rocket, which flies with a single core booster, and China’s new Mengzhou Moon ship to low-Earth orbit in early 2027. The larger Long March 10, with three boosters connected together, will launch China’s Lanyue lunar lander on an uncrewed test flight to the Moon in 2028. The next year, a follow-up mission will involve the concurrent launch of two Long March 10s, one with an uncrewed Mengzhou spacecraft and the other with a Lanyue lander that will dock together in lunar orbit. Then, before 2030, another dual launch of Long March 10s will occur, this time with crew on the Mengzhou spacecraft, leading to the crewed landing mission.
Blue Origin’s big reveals. Blue Origin announced two significant upgrades to its New Glenn rocket on Thursday, reducing the cost of manufacturing the vehicle and expanding its capacity for payload delivery to geostationary orbit and the Moon, Ars reports. With these upgrades, the company aims to eventually position New Glenn to launch more than 1,000 times a year. One of the announcements involved a new engine, called Northstar, that will eventually replace the BE-4 engine that powers the first stage of New Glenn. The other piece of news was that Blue Origin is developing a hydrogen-oxygen third stage for the rocket to give it an extra kick for high-energy missions.
Blue’s Northstar … The Northstar engine is a simplified but more powerful version of the BE-4 engine. It has half the number of parts and 30 percent less mass, and about 65 percent can be 3D-printed, all while providing a thrust increase over the BE-4. Blue Origin believes it can manufacture the engine at 25 percent the cost of a BE-4 engine. The kick stage is somewhat of an engineering marvel in itself. The stage will use a lightweight composite fuel tank, but officials were not sure the structure could contain leak-prone hydrogen at high pressure. The company recently had a breakthrough at Launch Site One in Texas, when it completed its first composite liquid hydrogen tanking test, giving engineers confidence to move forward with the design.
New Glenn won’t return to flight this year. Blue Origin now plans to resume launches of its New Glenn rocket in January, delaying the much-anticipated flight of the vehicle after a destructive launch pad explosion in May, Bloomberg reports. The Jeff Bezos-backed company had been driving to launch New Glenn again before the end of the year in its quest to challenge SpaceX. But Blue Origin Chief Executive Officer Dave Limp told employees on Wednesday that they are now targeting a flight early in 2027.
What’s a month? … The slight delay is unsurprising, and a January launch would still put Blue Origin well head of initial fears of how long it would take to rebuild its launch pad in Florida. New Glenn has a busy launch manifest after the return-to-flight mission, including a crucial launch in the spring of Blue Origin’s Blue Moon Mark 1 lander, an uncrewed precursor to the company’s future human-rated lander for NASA’s Artemis missions.
Artemis II tore through the atmosphere. The launch of NASA’s Artemis II mission in April caused significant disturbances in Earth’s ionosphere that could have triggered temporary, localized errors in GPS positioning, a new study has found, Space.com reports. The study by a team of researchers from National Cheng Kung University in Taiwan analyzed data from high-precision networks of fixed, ground-based GPS receivers. The researchers used the GPS measurements to reconstruct how the passage of the Artemis II mission’s Space Launch System rocket changed the concentrations of free electrons in the upper atmosphere.
Disturbing the peace … The measurements found that the ionospheric disturbances resulting from the Artemis II launch were more significant than any caused by other rocket launches to date. Curiously, they were up to 10 times more intense than those observed following the test launches of SpaceX’s Starship, which is twice as powerful as the SLS based on liftoff thrust.
Next three launches
November 6: Ceres 2 | Unknown Payload | Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center, China | 23:35 UTC
November 7: Falcon 9 | USSF-432 | Vandenberg Space Force Base, California | 00:46 UTC
November 8: Long March 12 | SatNet LEO Group | Wenchang Space Launch Site, China | 20:25 UTC
Stephen Clark is a space reporter at Ars Technica, covering private space companies and the world’s space agencies. Stephen writes about the nexus of technology, science, policy, and business on and off the planet.

articles.title: Nubank demite funcionários após IA reduzir fila de fraudes • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Nubank demite funcionários após IA reduzir fila de fraudes
Automação teria diminuído em 80% as reclamações sobre golpes financeiros. Instituição atribui cortes a uma reestruturação interna.
O Nubank demitiu cerca de 30 funcionários da equipe responsável por investigar denúncias de fraudes financeiras, após automatizar parte das atividades com inteligência artificial. Os desligamentos aconteceram na terça-feira (03/11), em meio a uma reestruturação do setor.
As informações são do jornal Folha de S.Paulo. Segundo funcionários e ex-funcionários, a adoção de IA reduziu em 80% a fila de reclamações sobre golpes financeiros nos últimos seis meses. A empresa atribui os cortes a mudanças internas.
A equipe afetada, chamada internamente de investigations, fazia parte da área de operações contra fraude do Nubank. Entre suas funções estava a análise de contas suspeitas de envolvimento em crimes financeiros. Os cortes atingiram profissionais que investigavam contas laranjas, usadas por criminosos para movimentar dinheiro e dificultar o rastreamento, prática que já foi alvo de operações da Polícia Federal.
Segundo a Folha, as ferramentas de IA começaram a ser utilizadas há cerca de seis meses, inicialmente para analisar casos de menor complexidade. Parte dos funcionários passou a revisar as conclusões produzidas pelos sistemas. Além de identificar possíveis erros, esse trabalho ajudava a aperfeiçoar os modelos de linguagem com exemplos de respostas corrigidas. Com a automação, a fila de reclamações e casos pendentes de análise teria despencado.
Ao Tecnoblog, a instituição afirmou que a “reestruturação de uma parte de uma área administrativa levou ao remanejamento interno de profissionais e ao encerramento de algumas posições”.
O Nubank confirmou ao Tecnoblog que os funcionários afetados receberão um pacote de benefícios, “que inclui salários adicionais por tempo de casa e extensão temporária do plano de saúde”. Antes das demissões, cerca de 40 funcionários da equipe de investigações já haviam sido transferidos para outros setores, segundo a Folha. Os analistas remanescentes devem continuar atuando no combate a fraudes, mas concentrados nos casos mais complexos.
O banco também confirmou que seguirá o “ritmo normal de contratações de acordo com as necessidades de cada unidade de negócio”. Em julho, a diretora do Centro de Excelência em Design, Ellen Kiss, nos afirmou que a empresa não deixaria de contratar por causa da IA.

articles.title: Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake launches to day-one PC emulation and strong reviews
articles.text:
Looking ahead: Despite Nintendo's aggressive efforts, PC users have often been able to play games released for the original Switch through emulation just days after launch. Generative AI coding could help recreate a similar situation with Switch 2 games, although things are still in an early, experimental stage. The latest target is a The Legend of Zelda remake that launched to glowing reviews this week.
The Nintendo Switch 2 remake of arguably the greatest Nintendo 64 game has been dumped and run on a PC emulator within hours of launch. However, users should probably stick with the console version for now.
A recent video from Unreal Gaming PC shows Nintendo's remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time running on the recently launched Lichii emulator. Centro Leaks also shared screenshots of a character model and other assets extracted from a dumped copy of the game, while X user NotRexed claims to have started preliminary work on a PC recompilation.
 – Centro LEAKS (@CentroLeaks) November 4, 2026
However, since the emulator is barely a week old, the game is far from playable. The video demonstration is plagued by visual glitches, and the framerate frequently drops into the 20s on a system equipped with an RTX 4080 and Ryzen 7 9800X3D. For comparison, the Switch 2 version maintains 60fps at dynamic 1440p when docked and dynamic 1080p in handheld mode, with AMD FSR 1 enabled.
Still, the achievement offers another glimpse of the breakneck pace of Nintendo Switch and Switch 2 hacking over the past month. A free, fan-made PC port of the 2019 remake of The Legend of Zelda: Link's Awakening entered public beta in October. Later that month, the first proof of concept for jailbreaking the Switch 2 emerged, and hackers began running Switch games natively on Apple Silicon devices.
 – NotRexed (@NotRexed) November 5, 2026
Enthusiasm for Ocarina of Time is expected to be one of the main drivers of continued development on Lichii and other Switch 2 exploits. The original 1998 release remains Metacritic's highest-rated game of all time, with a 99 Metascore, while the remake debuted with a 96.
The Switch 2 remake earned perfect scores from The Guardian, Eurogamer, GamesRadar, Destructoid, and several other outlets, while IGN, GameSpot, and Forbes awarded it 9/10. Critics say the seminal classic, which helped popularize several conventions of modern 3D gaming, still holds up 28 years later. They also praise its new quality-of-life improvements, with multiple outlets recommending the remake to longtime fans and newcomers alike.
