articles.title: After blocking Muse, Amazon now lets users text Alexa to help them shop | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Amazon is jumping on the currently most popular bandwagon for interacting with AI agents: texting. The company on Friday said it is launching a feature that lets customers chat with its Alexa AI agent over text messages to help them shop, much like you can with AI agents like Muse or Instinct.
The move comes after Amazon blocked Meta’s Muse from querying its site in September. The company is rolling the features out just before the start of the holiday shopping season.
The e-commerce giant said select U.S. customers will get a text asking them to enable the shopping feature. Those with access can text Alexa to shop on Amazon using natural language queries, spanning everything from searching for items, adding them to cart, and purchasing.
The text agent builds on the recent shopping-focused upgrades to Alexa, and so can manage lists, keep tabs on prices, search for items across the web, compare products, and check the status of orders. Users can also share a picture of an item or someone wearing an outfit to search for similar listings on Amazon.
The company said over time, Alexa will learn users’ preferences and suggest items accordingly.
The company said users who don’t get invited to use this feature can sign up to a waitlist. The feature will be rolled out more broadly in the coming weeks.
As the market for consumer-focused AI agents balloons, platforms like Amazon are building their own to tap this new avenue of user interaction. Last month, delivery company DoorDash said that third-party agents had so far only placed hundreds of orders in total on its platform, and that it plans to concentrate on developing its own text-based agent, launched in September, further.

articles.title: JMGO’s fantastic premium projector is flexible, seriously bright and crammed with cutting-edge gaming features — so if you want a 4K projector for a well-lit space, I’d absolutely recommend it
articles.text:
TechRadar Verdict
Extreme brightness and tons of flexibility at a competitive price make the JMGO N3 Ultimate a great option for anyone who doesn’t plan on creating a near-black home theater environment.
Reasons to buy
- + Wonderfully bright and colorful
- + Optical and gimbal make for quick or clear adjustments
- + Ready for fast-paced gaming
- + Competitive value
Reasons to avoid
- - Elevated black levels harm dark scenes
- - Some DLP rainbow effect
- - Motion performance could be better
Why you can trust TechRadar
We spend hours testing every product or service we review, so you can be sure you're buying the best. Find out more about how we test.
JMGO N3 Ultimate: One-minute review
The JMGO N3 Ultimate is the new, top-of-the-line option from JMGO. It brings a lot of what the brand had already been packing into a new design with a motorized gimbal stand and adjustable optics that provide quick or finely controlled setup options.
The JMGO N3 Ultimate's projection can be splendid, thanks to bright RGB lasers that give the projector enough juice to hold up in even well-lit rooms. The N3 Ultimate has vivid color and crisp detail, too. Unfortunately, the brightness isn’t matched by effective dimming to offer better performance in dark scenes, which is perhaps its biggest setback. Its motion could also be smoother without so many artifacts, but it’s not terrible either.
All told, it’s a capable projector that could serve a lot of people well, as long as they’re not seeking out dark, home theater setups where contrast is as important as brightness. At its $2,999 / £2,499 list price, it’s competitively priced compared to the best projectors, but it’s been on sale for much less and becomes all the better a bargain.
JMGO N3 Ultimate Review: Price and release date
- Release date: 2026
- List price: $2,999 / £2,499
The JMGO N3 Ultimate launched in 2026 and is now widely available. It has a $2,999 £2,499 list price, but it has already seen substantial discounts. At the time of writing, it was available for $2,349 / £2,119.
JMGO N3 Ultimate Review: Specs
| Supported screen sizes | 40-300 inches | 
| Optical technology | 3 Laser DLP | 
| Brightness (specified) | 5,800 Lumens | 
| Audio | 2x 12.5-watt speaker | 
| Ports | 1x USB-A, 2x HDMI 2.1 (1x eARC) | 
| Smart TV | Google TV | 
| Dimensions | 12.14 x 9.05 x 10.79 inches / 308.36 x 229.87 x 274.07mm | 
| Weight | 15.32 lb / 6.94kg | 
JMGO N3 Ultimate Review: Design and features
- Built-in Google TV
- Motorized gimbal stand and optical lens adjustments
- 1080p/240Hz VRR mode for gaming
JMGO has been rocking the same design for a few years now, and the JMGO N3 Ultimate does little to shift that. It’s still a fairly compact, two-tone rounded box sitting aloft on a gimbal stand with a rotating base, making it easy to set up and point the projection where you want it.
This go around, JMGO has incorporated small motors for electronic control of the stand. By holding a dedicated button on the remote control and using gyro controls, you can adjust the tilt and rotation of the projector. It’s good for quick adjustment but not for fine tuning.
In an interesting twist, the N3 Ultimate is JMGO’s projector that least needed this technology, as the projector incorporates advanced optics with adjustable zoom and lens shift. The zoom can shift the projector from a 0.88:1 to a 1.7:1 throw ratio, giving it a ton of range. Meanwhile, the lens shift lets it move the projection up or down by 130% or sideways by 53%, so you really just need to point it perpendicular to your wall, and you should have no trouble shifting and squeezing the projection to fit without any keystone correction.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
Those manual controls are how you’ll get the best picture, but the JMGO N3 Ultimate has a host of automated tools that can quickly make adjustments for you, which may be convenient if you’re moving it often. It can analyze the projection area available to it, re-aiming, shrinking, and shifting the picture to fit. I found this using digital keystone even when it really wasn’t called for, though, so I wouldn’t count on it doing the best job.
One additional automatic tool that may be more helpful is the wall color adaptation. This uses the projector's camera and a series of test patterns to tweak colors so they appear better on your wall. You won’t need this if you use a screen, but it worked well on my beige walls.
Since the projector can move quite a bit in operation, it fits its connectors all at the base, rather than the rear of the projection unit itself. This can still get in the way of rotation, but makes vertical tilt a non-issue. The projector doesn’t have a great selection of ports, though, with just two HDMI 2.1 ports, one of which is eARC and probably should be kept for that purpose. There’s also a single USB-A port.
Thankfully, you don’t need to use any of those HDMI ports for basic streaming. The projector has built-in Google TV, and it operates quickly on its 4GB of memory. Annoyingly, it pauses playback while navigating menus sometimes (sometimes it doesn’t), but it’s quite serviceable otherwise. It even gets 64GB of storage, which can be useful if you use lots of apps. Perhaps, more crucially, the projector connects over Wi-Fi 6, giving it faster and more stable connectivity to work with while streaming.
For cinephiles, the JMGO N3 Ultimate supports HDR10 and Dolby Vision. Meanwhile, for gamers the projector can shift from 4K60Hz over to 1080p/240Hz and even brings VRR for smooth, low-latency, responsive gaming. There are some trade-offs though. Enabling VRR hurt clarity no matter if I left the projector at 4K or swapped to 1080p. Even at 1080p, VRR took a small toll on clarity. Fine text exhibited artifacts that looked like chroma subsampling. In games, it wasn’t an issue, but navigating Windows on PC to select games to play, it was a nuisance.
Apart from its gyro controls, the Ultimate's remote is pretty basic. It has the standard Google TV controls and thankfully a pill-shaped volume control that’s easy to feel out in the dark. It includes shortcuts to Prime Video, Netflix, YouTube, and one app of your choice. Google TV Freeplay gets a separate shortcut at the top of the remote. Annoyingly, there’s no mute button for quick silencing and while the remote has motion-activated lighting behind some of its keys, it doesn't behind the shortcut buttons.
Since the JMGO N3 Ultimate is fairly portable, JGMO includes a foam carrying case that can fit it, the remote, and the power adapter all inside. It’s not exceedingly robust or impressive, but it’s not too bulky and should do a better job protecting the hardware than a typical backpack would.
- Design & features score: 4.5 / 5
JMGO N3 Ultimate Review: Picture quality and performance
- Wonderfully bright and colorful
- Black levels could be darker
- Crisp 4K visuals and responsive 1080p gaming
The JMGO N3 Ultimate has brightness in spades, and that’s where it shines best. When it comes to darkness, it can struggle. It fails to sink into darkness where it needs to, and the raised grays are distracting to see, never mind the regularly present letterboxes. Even when scenes aren’t very dark, these shortcomings are clear. Neither Dolby Vision nor adaptive brightness features seem to do the trick.
Thankfully, as soon as more light is called for, the JMGO N3 Ultimate delivers. It pumped out over 5,200 lumens by my measurements, which is plenty for most scenarios and not too far off the rated 5,800 lumens (nor did it require an awful picture setting). Bright scenes are clear and vibrant. Shadows look stronger in contrast to the brightness and the brightness is even enough to give the JMGO N3 Ultimate a solid showing in a modestly lit room. This makes it a great match for casual viewing, news, and bright cartoons. That brightness makes it all the easier to go big without the image getting too dim.
Alongside the brightness, the color of the RGB laser projection is stunning, just as it’s been in other projectors I’ve tested with the tech. When watching Supergirl, the glow of the green sun has plenty of depth, and the red cape glows majestically whenever the sun hits it. When Kara’s laser vision rips through the Brigands, it’s properly dazzling. The world of Pandora in the Avatar series is also lushly presented.
Motion can be hit or miss. By default the projector wants to use unsightly interpolation that presents loads of artifacts and makes the projection feel like anything but high-fidelity. With the MEMC setting dropped to low, it doesn’t look so bad, avoiding distracting soap opera effect and serious artifacts while helping reduce some of the stutter that occurs when it’s disabled entirely.
One area RGB laser projectors have been improving is the DLP rainbow effect. I’m not terribly sensitive to it, but I can usually catch it if I’m looking for it. Lately, I’ve been spotting it less and less on high-end laser projectors, but I can still catch it on the JMGO N3 Ultimate. Thankfully, it’s subtle, and I find it’s largely limited to subtitles
The adjustable optics help ensure a sharp picture from wherever you want to project. Stretched across about an 150-inch section of my wall, 4K looked brilliant in my living room.
Outside of movies, the JMGO N3 Ultimate proves a great option for gaming. You want crisp detail from corner to corner in games, since you never know where something precious is hiding, and the optics help provide this. Latency is satisfyingly low at 4K but sinks to negligible levels at 1080p/240Hz. Mousing around my screen and zipping through levels in Hades 2, I didn’t feel a hint of latency in that mode.
The speakers on the JMGO N3 Ultimate aren’t bad, but they certainly aren’t an adequate match for the projection. They put out decent volume, helping ensure you’ve got enough sound to work with when you want to plop the projector down somewhere and start enjoying right away. They even provide some low-end, helping bump up effects in movies. But the quality of stereo sound won’t be very good unless you’re sitting perfectly in center with the projection.
- Picture quality & performance score: 3.5 / 5
JMGO N3 Ultimate Review: Value
- Can serve multiple purposes well
- Cheaper than many rivals while offering competitive brightness
The JGMO N3 Ultimate is a capable projector and can work well for folks who aren’t committing to a pitch-black home theater where its weaker black levels will steal focus.
At $2,999 / £2,499, it’s still fairly competitive with what’s on the market, but at $2,349 / £2,119, it’s more of a steal. It can compete with large TVs on value while providing the flexibility to enjoy movies and TV in 4K or switch over to 1080p for high-speed gaming. The different realms it can cover all from a single product help boost its value.
- Value score: 4.5 / 5
Should I buy the JMGO N3 Ultimate?
| JMGO N3 Ultimate Scorecard |  |  | 
|---|---|---|
| Attributes | Notes | Rating | 
|---|---|---|
| Design and features | The JMGO N3 Ultimate brings a lot to the table. It’s built for flexibility with adjustable optics and a motorized stand that can make setup quick and easy without sacrificing image quality. It’s well equipped for movies and gaming, and it has built in streaming capabilities and serviceable speakers. It could have more ports and a better remote, though. | 4.5/5 | 
| Picture quality and performance | The JMGO N3 Ultimate delivers on brightness and clarity, making it a joy to watch bright, colorful content with. It can even hold up well in rooms with a lot of ambient lighting. Where it falls short is in its contrast and motion, having distractingly elevated black levels that hurt dark scenes and either slight panning stutter or artifact-laden motion smoothing. | 3.5/5 | 
| Value | With plenty of brightness and versatility at a surprisingly competitive pricing, the JMGO N3 Ultimate offers up a lot of value. | 4.5/5 | 
Buy it if...
You don’t like turning out all the lights
The JMGO N3 Ultimate has brightness to spare, letting it handle dim and even well-lit rooms fairly well. If you don’t like viewing in the dark, this makes it a good match.
You want quick and easy flexibility
The JMGO N3 can work in a lot of different setups and it makes getting it all lined up easy. If you’re always moving your projector around, that can save you a load of time.
You want versatility
The JGMO N3 Ultimate can tackle 4K video, 1080p gaming, precise and careful optical setup, or quick and effortless setup. Its ability to step into different roles can be very convenient if you have a lot of different needs.
Don't buy it if...
You’re looking for OLED performance
Few projectors do a great job with their black levels, and even the best aren’t really on the level with OLEDs. The JMGO N3 Ultimate isn’t even close, with raised black levels that don’t really look great in dark scenes.
You have lots of input sources
With just two HDMI ports, the JMGO N3 Ultimate is a recipe for annoyance if you have a handful of consoles, a Blu-ray player and the like. Heck, it doesn’t even have a 3.5mm jack you can use to free up the eARC port.
You don’t move your projector ever
A big part of the package, and therefore what you pay for, is the flexibility of the gimbal and optics. If you’re not planning to take advantage of them, you can save some money by looking elsewhere.
JMGO N3 Ultimate review: Also consider
| Row 0 - Cell 0 | JMGO N3 Ultimate | Valerion VisionMaster Max | Hisense C2 Ultra | Xgimi Horizon 20 Max | 
| Price | $2,999 / £2,499 | $3,999 / £ 3,799 | $2,999 / £1,799 | $2,999 / £2,599 | 
| Screen sizes supported | 40 to 300 inches | 40 to 300 inches | 65 to 300 inches | 40 to 300 inches | 
| Brightness (specified) | 5,800 lumens | 3,500 lumens | 3,000 lumens | 5,700 ISO lumens | 
| HDR support | HDR10, HLG, Dolby Vision | HDR10+, HLG, Dolby Vision | HDR10+, HLG, Dolby Vision | Dolby Vision, HDR10+, HDR10, HLG, IMAX Enhanced | 
| Optical technology | 3 Laser DLP | 3 Laser DLP | 3 Laser DLP | 3 Laser DLP | 
| Smart TV | Google TV | Google TV | Google TV | n/a | 
| Connections | 2x HDMI 2.1 (1 with eARC), 1x HDMI 2.0 , 1x optical, 1x 3.5mm | 2x HDMI 2.1, 1x HDMI 2.0 (with eARC), 1x optical, 1x 3.5mm | 2x HDMI 2.1 (1x with eARC), 2x USB, optical | 2x HDMI (x1 eARC), 1x USB 3.0, 1x USB 2.0, 1x 3.5mm, 1x optical audio out | 
Valerion VisionMaster Max 
This projector may not be as bright, but it has wonderfully flexible optics, great visual performance and profound black levels that make it a far more worthy home theater projector. It tends to be a bit more expensive, though.
Hisense C2 Ultra
The Hisense C2 Ultra isn’t nearly as bright and doesn’t have the same degree of flexible optics as the JMGO N3 Ultimate. Still, it tends to cost nearly as much. This helps highlight how much the technology has progressed and come down in price in a short time. Read our full Hisense C2 Ultra review.
Xgimi Horizon 20 Max
This model has most of the same capabilities and qualities as the JGMO N3 Ultimate, just in a different package. It had strong contrast in our testing, but it skips the motorized gimbal. If you know you want that dark performance, it’ll probably be the better pick, though you may be best just grabbing whichever is cheapest when you’re shopping since both have frequent discounts. Read our full Xgimi Horizon 20 Max review.
How I tested the JMGO N3 Ultimate
- Tested at home in multiple, real-world viewing conditions
- Presented the display with a variety of media and formats
- I have tested numerous projectors and displays over the last half-decade
I tested the JMGO N3 Ultimate at home, in real-world conditions. This saw it faced with ambient light coming in from numerous windows, in-room lighting, as well as ambient noise that both the projector and speaker systems had to overcome. The projector was tested both against a bare, white wall and an Akia Screens CineWhite screen. It was presented with streamed content, HDR and non-HDR, and console gameplay.
My testing evaluates the projector’s performance with respect to its price and competition from other models I and colleagues at TechRadar have tested.
I have been testing projectors since 2021 and displays for even longer.
- First reviewed: November 2026

articles.title: Führerschein auf dem Handy: Alles zur Einführung des digitalen Nachweises
articles.text:
Digitaler Führerschein: So kommt das Dokument aufs Smartphone
Der digitale Führerschein soll noch in diesem Jahr auf Smartphones verfügbar sein. Das bedeutet, dass Autofahrer:innen in Deutschland ihren Kartenführerschein künftig nicht mehr mitführen müssen, wenn sie den digitalen Nachweis gespeichert haben. Wie das Bundesverkehrsministerium der Frankfurter Allgemeinen Sonntagszeitung mitteilte, ist die Einführung bis Ende November geplant.
So funktioniert der digitale Führerschein
Bei der Digitalisierung hinkt Deutschland im internationalen Vergleich oft hinterher. Das soll sich jetzt sukzessive ändern – und der digitale Führerschein ist der nächste Schritt. Für das Abspeichern des Dokuments ist die i-Kfz-App vorgesehen, die das Kraftfahrtbundesamt zusammen mit der Bundesdruckerei entwickelt hat. Sie steht für Android- und iOS-Geräte schon jetzt kostenlos zur Verfügung. Um Fahrzeugscheine zu hinterlegen, benötigen Nutzer:innen die aktivierte Online-Ausweisfunktion, eine PIN und ein NFC-fähiges Smartphone. Laut Angaben des Kraftfahrtbundesamtes war die App im August 2026 auf mehr als zwei Millionen Mobiltelefonen installiert.
Schon heute können Nutzer:innen ihren Fahrzeugschein in der App digital speichern und bei Verkehrskontrollen vorzeigen. Mit dem digitalen Führerschein kommt ein zweites wichtiges Fahrzeugdokument hinzu. Wer ihn in der App hinterlegt hat, muss die Plastikkarte bei Fahrten innerhalb Deutschlands künftig nicht mehr zwingend mitführen. Auch bei Mietwagen und Carsharing soll der digitale Führerschein den Alltag von Autofahrer:innen erleichtern. Er dient als Ergänzung – ersetzen soll er die klassische Plastikkarte aber nicht. Diese wird unter anderem für Fahrten ins Ausland weiterhin erforderlich sein.
Polizeigewerkschaft begrüßt digitalen Nachweis
Die Gewerkschaft der Polizei (GdP) hatte sich im vergangenen Jahr für die Digitalisierung von Fahrzeug- und Fahrerlaubnisdokumenten ausgesprochen. „Moderne, digitale Nachweise können Verwaltungsprozesse vereinfachen, Ressourcen sparen und den Bürgerinnen und Bürgern den Alltag erleichtern”, erklärte Michael Mertens, stellvertretender Bundesvorsitzender der GdP, in einer Mitteilung der Gewerkschaft.
Kritisch sieht die GdP allerdings die mangelnde Vorbereitung der Polizeibehörden. „Bislang gibt es keine bundeseinheitlichen Schulungen, wie digitale Dokumente geprüft oder rechtssicher dokumentiert werden sollen“, sagte er Ende 2025. „Außerdem müssen digitale Nachweise in Echtzeit gegen offizielle Datenbanken abgeglichen werden können – sonst bleibt die Kontrolle lückenhaft.“ Ob sich diese Lücken inzwischen schließen ließen, bleibt abzuwarten.
Konkretes Datum steht bisher nicht fest
Ein offizielles Datum für die Einführung des digitalen Führerscheins wurde noch nicht genannt. Wer den Nachweis auf seinem Smartphone nutzen möchte, kann sich aber schon jetzt vorbereiten, die App herunterladen und sich online identifizieren. Laut Bundesverkehrsministerium soll der digitale Führerschein Anfang 2027 zusätzlich in der deutschen EUDI-Wallet verfügbar werden. Eine europäische Umsetzung ist ebenfalls geplant, könnte allerdings noch bis 2030 dauern.

articles.title: Assez rapides pour faire Paris-New York en 10 minutes : les sondes Escapade foncent enfin vers Mars
articles.text:
Pour propulser un vaisseau jusqu’à Mars, il ne suffit pas de l’envoyer dans la bonne direction et de le laisser filer en ligne droite. Afin de réaliser des économies de carburant, les satellites qui quittent la Terre vont suivre un parcours sinueux et contre-intuitif qui va leur permettre de gagner de la vitesse progressivement en profitant de la force gravitationnelle des planètes.
C’est comme ça qu’a fonctionné Escapade. Composée de deux sondes jumelles, la mission Escape and Plasma Acceleration and Dynamics Explorers a décollé il y a presque un an, le 13 novembre 2025, à bord de la fusée New Glenn de Blue Origin. Mais à ce moment-là, la Terre et Mars se trouvaient de part et d’autre du Soleil, la pire position pour partir vers la planète rouge. Les deux sondes ont donc décrit une grande boucle en forme de haricot autour du point de Lagrange L2 du système Soleil-Terre, situé à 1,5 million de kilomètres de la Terre, là où se trouvent aussi les télescopes James Webb et Euclid.
Vers Mars à Mach 31
Dans un communiqué publié ce lundi 2 novembre, la Nasa annonce que la Terre et Mars sont enfin bien placées pour que les deux sondes partent vers Mars. Le premier passera ce samedi 7 novembre vers 11 heures (heure de Paris), le second le lundi 9 novembre vers midi. Les deux vaisseaux vont entamer une manœuvre de mécanique orbitale connue sous le nom de TMI, ou en français « injection trans-martienne ».
L’idée est d’attendre que les vaisseaux passent au plus près de la Terre, entre 970 et 1 770 kilomètres d’altitude. C’est là que la gravité terrestre les fait filer le plus vite, et c’est à ce moment qu’un allumage du moteur leur fait gagner le plus de vitesse. Une fois ce point atteint, leurs moteurs s’allumeront pendant environ neuf minutes afin de les propulser vers la planète rouge.
Les vaisseaux vont ainsi gagner plus de 1 600 km/h et passer d’environ 10,1 à 10,8 km/s, de quoi relier Paris à New York en un peu moins de dix minutes. Lancés à environ Mach 31, les deux vaisseaux Escapade suivront pendant dix mois une trajectoire courbe autour du Soleil, corrigée en route par plusieurs manœuvres, avant d’arriver sur Mars les 7 et 9 septembre 2027.
Des jumeaux observateurs de plasma
Une fois là-bas, leur périple ne sera pas terminé. Les deux sondes devront passer plusieurs mois à abaisser et synchroniser leurs orbites, avec une coupure des communications pendant la conjonction solaire de la fin 2027, quand le Soleil se trouvera entre la Terre et Mars. Leurs observations scientifiques ne commenceront qu’à la mi-2028.
Pourquoi ne pas avoir fait partir Escapade lorsque la Terre et Mars étaient bien alignées ? Cette fenêtre de tir ne s’ouvre que quelques semaines tous les 26 mois. Escapade devait partir pendant celle de l’automne 2024, sur le tout premier vol de New Glenn. En septembre 2024, la Nasa a retiré ses sondes de ce vol, car la fusée de Blue Origin ne serait pas prête avant la fermeture de la fenêtre, fin octobre. L’équipe a alors conçu une trajectoire inédite pour partir sur le deuxième vol de la fusée. Ce départ anticipé a aussi permis aux sondes de traverser une région lointaine de la magnétoqueue, la partie du champ magnétique terrestre étirée par le vent solaire, qu’aucun engin n’avait encore explorée directement. L’équipe scientifique doit publier ses résultats prochainement.
Une fois autour de Mars, les deux vaisseaux pourront analyser le plasma de l’environnement martien d’une nouvelle manière. En se suivant sur la même orbite, à quelques minutes d’intervalle, les deux sondes pourront voir comment la structure et la composition de ce plasma changent d’un instant à l’autre. Aucune mission n’avait encore fait voler deux engins coordonnés autour de Mars.

articles.title: Gemini accusé d’avoir aidé une collégienne de 13 ans à planifier son suicide : ses parents attaquent Google
articles.text:
Sur l’ordinateur que son collège de Caroline du Nord lui avait prêté, ChatGPT et Gemini étaient bloqués. Selon la plainte déposée le lundi 2 novembre par ses parents devant un tribunal californien, cette adolescente de 13 ans, appelée Emma dans la procédure, aurait pourtant continué à converser avec l’assistant de Google par le Mode IA du moteur de recherche, que l’établissement ne pouvait pas couper. Environ 3 200 messages rien qu’en février, souvent la nuit, dont une grande partie aurait porté sur son mal-être et sur l’idée de mettre fin à ses jours. Le 17 mars, le logiciel de surveillance de l’école a repéré sur sa machine un document intitulé « Funeral » et alerté les parents, qui ont pu intervenir. La jeune fille n’est pas passée à l’acte.
La plainte, relayée par l’AFP, va plus loin et explique que Gemini aurait « diagnostiqué » chez Emma de graves troubles psychiques. L’assistant IA l’aurait alors poussée à lui faire confiance plutôt qu’à ses parents ou aux conseillers de son collège. Interrogé par l’AFP, un porte-parole de Google assure que l’entreprise examine ces accusations et les prend « très au sérieux », en rappelant que le Mode IA dispose de garde-fous contre l’automutilation et les tentatives de contournement. D’autres ont choisi des dispositifs plus visibles, comme ChatGPT et sa fonction « Contact de confiance », qui peut prévenir un proche en cas de détresse.
Google n’en est pas à sa première procédure de ce type. En mars 2026, la famille de Jonathan Gavalas, un Américain de 36 ans, avait déjà attaqué l’entreprise en accusant Gemini de l’avoir entraîné dans un délire jusqu’au suicide. En janvier, Google et la start-up Character.AI avaient de leur côté accepté de régler à l’amiable plusieurs plaintes de familles d’adolescents, et OpenAI est lui aussi attaqué en justice aux États-Unis pour suicide assisté.
Gemini coupé par défaut, la recherche Google aussi
Le lendemain de la plainte, le 3 novembre, Chris Phillips, vice-président de Google chargé de l’éducation, a publié un billet qui revoit les réglages de quatre produits : l’application Gemini, Gemini Notebook (le nom de NotebookLM dans l’éducation), Gemini dans Classroom et Google Search. Ils seront « entièrement désactivés » pour les comptes élèves, de la maternelle à la fin du lycée, tant qu’un administrateur scolaire ne les aura pas explicitement activés. Google ne fait aucun lien avec la plainte et parle d’une décision prise après avoir écouté écoles, enseignants, chercheurs et décideurs publics. Les sénateurs Richard Blumenthal et Josh Hawley avaient écrit à l’entreprise en octobre pour lui demander pourquoi l’IA était activée par défaut sur les appareils scolaires.
C’est un vrai rétropédalage pour le géant américain, qui mise grandement sur l’éducation. Depuis le 10 août, l’onglet Gemini de Classroom était ouvert aux élèves de tous âges, et activé par défaut dans les établissements qui avaient déjà autorisé Gemini ou Gemini Notebook. Le réglage sera donc inversé, à une date que Google n’a pas encore fixée. Selon le New York Times, le changement interviendrait début 2027 et l’AFP précise qu’il sera déployé dans le monde entier, en commençant par les États-Unis.
La contrepartie fait toutefois déjà polémique, car Google ne prévoit pas de version de son moteur sans IA pour les comptes élèves. Ainsi, une école qui refuse toute IA prive aussi ses élèves de recherche Google. Search et l’IA sont « profondément intégrés », a justifié Chris Phillips auprès du New York Times. Les élèves concernés verront simplement un message de leur établissement indiquant que la recherche n’est pas disponible. À l’inverse, activer Search revient à accepter les AI Overviews et le Mode IA, c’est-à-dire précisément la porte d’entrée pointée par la plainte de la famille d’Emma. Le maire de New York, Zohran Mamdani, accuse Google d’utiliser « son pouvoir de monopole pour imposer l’IA dans nos écoles publiques ». L’entreprise répond sur X que ses annonces donnent aux écoles « plus de choix, pas moins ».
 Google is trying to use its monopoly power to force AI into our public schools.
No corporation should have the power to dictate how we teach our children.
Our public schools exist to serve students, not to grow the profit margins of Big Tech.
https://t.co/jfACMS1Sh2
— Mayor Zohran Kwame Mamdani (@NYCMayor) November 3, 2026
Pour faire passer la pilule, Google met en avant Guided Learning, un mode censé guider l’élève par des questions plutôt que lui livrer la réponse. Il est disponible dans Classroom dans le monde entier depuis le 3 novembre, et sera testé dans la recherche auprès d’écoles américaines dès ce mois-ci.
Et les lycéens français ?
Le billet de Google ne cite aucun pays, et l’entreprise n’a donné aucune date pour la France. La question n’a pourtant rien de théorique chez nous : à cette rentrée, des dizaines de milliers de lycéens d’Île-de-France et des Pays de la Loire ont reçu, ou reçoivent en ce moment, un Asus Chromebook CM14 fourni par leur Région. Reste à savoir si ces nouveaux réglages les concerneront.
Dans tous les cas, ce revirement confirme que sur un ordinateur scolaire, c’est l’administrateur, et non l’élève, qui tient l’interrupteur de l’IA de Google. Encore faut-il qu’il dispose d’un vrai choix, ce que contestent aujourd’hui les détracteurs de l’entreprise.
Si vous ou l’un de vos proches traversez une période difficile, le 3114, numéro national de prévention du suicide, est joignable gratuitement 24 heures sur 24, 7 jours sur 7.

articles.title: Jeff Bezos revela una visión de inteligencia artificial que podría transformar la jornada laboral estadounidense.
articles.text:
Jeff Bezos tiene una visión súper optimista sobre cómo la IA transformará el mercado laboral. Mientras muchas empresas recurren a esta tecnología para automatizar tareas y reducir costes, el fundador de Amazon cree que sus beneficios podrían llegar mucho más lejos, e incluso habla de permitir que algunas personas mantengan económicamente a sus familias trabajando tres días a la semana.
Según sus previsiones, esta posibilidad estaría ligada a un aumento de la productividad. Durante una entrevista concedida a Fox News, Bezos explicó que la inteligencia artificial podría cambiar las necesidades económicas de muchos hogares estadounidenses y, por ejemplo, permitir que algunas familias vivan con un solo sueldo.
Así, su razonamiento se basa en la relación entre producción y esfuerzo de las empresas, ya que podrían conseguir más resultados con menos trabajo y los trabajadores podrían reducir sus jornadas sin perder poder adquisitivo. Por desgracia, Bezos llegó a plantear que contratar personal podría convertirse en un problema si cada vez menos personas necesitaran trabajar tantas horas.
La visión optimista de Bezos contrasta con los despidos de Amazon
Las declaraciones llegan en un momento en el que el impacto de la IA sobre el empleo genera bastante incertidumbre. Durante la entrevista, el periodista Bret Baier recordó que Amazon había eliminado casi 30.000 puestos corporativos desde finales del año anterior, una situación que contrasta con el futuro laboral que describe su fundador.
Bezos respondió que la compañía se encontraba en unas circunstancias particulares al recordar que habían ampliado su plantilla durante la pandemia. Además, aunque el empresario defendió que la inteligencia artificial podría generar aumentos de productividad en la economía global, no explicó cuándo podríamos tener jornadas más cortas o mejores ingresos.
De momento, su propuesta sigue siendo una predicción y no un cambio laboral anunciado por Amazon. La cuestión es si esos avances permitirán realmente trabajar menos o si, por el contrario, servirán para que las empresas produzcan más con menos trabajadores.

articles.title: Fake security tools on GitHub push backdoors and infostealers
articles.text:
Cybersecurity professionals are being targeted with infected security projects on GitHub that deploy a backdoor and information stealer malware.
The campaign started about two years ago and initially targeted crypto wallet users, but recently the threat actor switched focus and published malicious repositories for automating scans, security testing, and log analysis.
Researchers at cybersecurity company Dr. Web found that more than 2,000 Windows systems have been compromised so far.
One malicious repository they found is a fake script advertised as a lightweight solution to parse, clean, and format output from the Fscan network scanner.
Previous lures included blockchain games, bots, and cheat tools, typically targeting blockchain and game enthusiasts.
Dr. Web's investigation found malicious code embedded in Visual Studio project files, Python scripts, and Go source files, hidden behind long stretches of whitespace, an old technique that still proves effective.
In some Visual Studio projects, a pre-build event routine runs the code before compilation, the researchers say.
The infection chain uses PowerShell to retrieve an encrypted download link that fetches a modular Electron-based loader named ‘Microsoft.exe.’
The loader establishes persistence on the infected host, elevates its privileges, disables Windows security and recovery features, and injects the next-stage (malware) into legitimate processes.
Dr. Web describes six evasion techniques in the loader’s Mode3 mode, which is its default operational mode:
- Makes explorer.exe appear to be the malware’s parent process
- Changes a Windows registry value to disable Smart App Control
- Restores original ntdll.dll code from disk to remove hooks added by security software
- Makes direct Windows system calls that are harder for security tools to intercept
- Patches EtwEventWrite in memory to suppress event tracing in the affected process
- Patches AmsiScanBuffer in memory to interfere with antivirus scanning of scripts
If that mode fails to launch, the loader uses Mode2, which adds Microsoft Defender exclusions and uses a PowerShell script to decrypt and inject the payloads into ‘RegAsm.exe.’
The final payloads delivered to the host are the AsyncRAT backdoor, clipper malware that replaces crypto wallet addresses in the clipboard, and an information stealer.
The infostealer collects browser data, VPN settings, FTP client configuration files, gaming account data, and Discord tokens, and exfiltrates the details through a Telegram bot.
According to Dr. Web, the malware also attempts to remove ESET, McAfee, and Malwarebytes antivirus tools from the infected computer, tries to disconnect them from their update servers, and also interferes with Windows backups.
Dr. Web researchers also found a seemingly unfinished component that could help keep the loader running and download it again if it was removed from the host’s disk.
This finding suggests that the threat actor is working to improve the malware with new features. The researchers shared a complete list of indicators of compromise observed in this campaign.

articles.title: Oui, 47 ans après, Sony fait renaître le casque de son tout premier Walkman
articles.text:
Coussinets orange ou bleu, arceau fin et fil toujours présent : Sony remet son casque de 1979 au goût du jour. Prévu en novembre à 70 euros en France, le MDR-3R aura aussi son édition Stranger Things.
Il suffit parfois de deux mousses orange pour reconnaître toute une époque. Présenté le 5 novembre, le MDR-3R fait revivre la famille de casques dont le MDR-3L2 accompagnait le premier Walkman TPS-L2. Le clin d’œil s’étend jusqu’à l’emballage et au mode d’emploi, inspirés de ceux d’origine.
Le look d’hier, la connectique d’aujourd’hui
Ce casque ouvert et supra-auriculaire pèse 38 grammes hors câble. Il est livré avec deux paires de coussinets interchangeables, bleus et orange, et embarque des transducteurs de 23 mm, comme son ancêtre.
La principale évolution se trouve au bout du câble de 1,2 mètre : une prise USB-C remplace le jack 3,5 mm. Aucun adaptateur jack n’est annoncé parmi les accessoires fournis. Le MDR-3R se destine aux smartphones, tablettes et ordinateurs compatibles avec l’audio USB. Il ajoute un microphone et une télécommande pour gérer les appels, la lecture et le volume, sans batterie à recharger ni appairage à effectuer.
Ironie de l’histoire, Sony déconseille de l’utiliser avec un Walkman, sans préciser les modèles concernés ni expliquer pourquoi.
Stranger Things prolonge la nostalgie
L’édition spéciale s’inspire du casque de Max, indissociable de Running Up That Hill de Kate Bush dans la saison 4, et de l’univers du Monde à l’envers. Elle comprend des coussinets rouges et noirs, un logo Stranger Things gravé et un emballage spécifique.
Dans son communiqué, Sony annonce les deux versions pour novembre, sans date plus précise. Il faudra débourser 70 euros pour le modèle standard et 80 euros pour l’édition Stranger Things. De quoi ressortir Kate Bush, même si la cassette restera dans son boîtier.

articles.title: TypeScript 7.1 Beta: Restores the Compiler API and Makes Vue and Svelte First-Class
articles.text:
Microsoft has released TypeScript 7.1 Beta, the first update to the Go-based native compiler that landed as TypeScript 7.0 in July, and the release that finally hands tool authors a programmatic API again. Daniel Rosenwasser announced the beta on 20 October 2026, and the team pointed developers to it on X, inviting feedback ahead of a release candidate and stable build that the iteration plan tentatively places in late November, though the beta itself arrived two weeks behind schedule.
The headline change restores the compiler API that 7.0 dropped. For three months anything that embedded the compiler, from Vue’s Volar to Svelte, Astro, ts-morph and type-aware linting, was stranded on TypeScript 6. Rather than revive the old monolithic module, 7.1 splits it into focused entry points such as typescript/sync, typescript/async, typescript/fs and typescript/ast, paths that previously sat behind an unstable prefix now dropped to signal intent. The client also models incremental edits through reusable snapshots, so an editor can derive new state from an old one without rebuilding the world, and the team says the surface will stay backward compatible across all of 7.x once stable.
Sitting on top of that is the beta’s most discussed feature, content mappers, a supported plugin point that lets a package hand TypeScript a virtual view of a non-standard file such as a .vue or .svelte component, with mappings back to the original so errors point at the right line. Because a mapper runs as a separate process it executes only when you opt in, and the team warns the flag should be treated like any build plugin.
Vue’s language tools are already porting to it: maintainer Johnson Chu has shipped Vue Language Tools v4 alpha on top of content mappers, dropping the separate vue-tsc binary in favour of a @vue/content-mapper that runs inside tsc itself. In a hands-on migration write-up, the Directus admin app, 581 Vue components across 882 TypeScript files saw type checks fall from 14.19 to 3.10 seconds on tsc 7.1 plus the mapper, a 4.6x speedup over vue-tsc 3. The author also flagged that teams adopting the beta would need to run 7.1 in CI alongside an older TypeScript in the editor until Vue tooling stabilises on top of the stable release.
Microsoft’s MUI docs benchmark falls from 22.2 to 11.9 seconds while roughly halving memory, though heavier codebases such as VS Code see closer to 1.2x. An independent test against NestJS put a 353,000 line check at 2.76 seconds on the beta against 4.95 on 7.0 and 12.42 on the old compiler, while flagging a 7.0 memory regression that 7.1 reverses.
On GitHub, Akira Higuchi reported that, in a particular editor workflow, saving a mapper’s watched configuration file could leave types stale until the language server is restarted. The issue remains open.
The language itself gains import attributes in ambient module declarations, TC39 source phase imports for loading WebAssembly, and a stable es2026 target carrying additions like Math.sumPrecise() and Error.isError().
Teams still on TypeScript 5 should move through 6 to 7, and projects using Vue, Svelte or Angular should keep a dual TypeScript 6 and 7 install until their framework tooling ships a 7.1 build. Tool and library authors are urged to port to the new entry points now and to flag missing functions through the API status tracker while gaps can still be filled before stable. The independent numbers are a reminder that the native compiler now sets the bar, with rival type checkers on Hacker News already measuring themselves against tsgo 7.1 beta.
TypeScript is an open-source programming language developed and maintained by Microsoft. It builds on JavaScript by adding optional static typing, catching errors before code runs and making large codebases easier to build and maintain with confidence. Since version 7.0 its compiler has been written in Go rather than in TypeScript itself, a native port that underpins the speed gains in this release, and it remains widely adopted across the frontend and backend ecosystems, with first-class support in frameworks such as React, Angular, Vue and Node.js.

articles.title: OpenAI logra que GPT-6 y Astra diseñen un dispositivo funcional en menos de una semana
articles.text:
Diseñar un objeto físico implica un nivel de exigencia que no admite errores: cada pieza debe encajar, cada circuito debe responder y cualquier desvío de milímetros puede arruinar un proyecto completo. Para medir hasta qué punto la IA puede asumir ese desafío, OpenAI sometió a sus modelos a la tarea de crear un dispositivo electrónico desde cero.
El resultado se conoció a través de una publicación oficial de OpenAI, en la que la compañía detalló cómo GPT-6 y Astra diseñaron en menos de una semana un aparato capaz de comunicarse con Codex, su agente de programación.
El proceso abarcó la carcasa, los componentes internos, la placa de circuito impreso y el software de funcionamiento, aunque la etapa de fabricación mostró que el trabajo de la inteligencia artificial todavía necesita ajustes humanos antes de convertirse en un producto terminado.
Cómo GPT-6 y Astra diseñaron el dispositivo electrónico
El proyecto nació como una iniciativa paralela de dos integrantes de OpenAI, con el propósito de verificar si los modelos podían completar un producto electrónico sin que los humanos intervinieran directamente sobre los diseños generados en el proceso.
GPT-6 definió los requisitos funcionales del dispositivo. Astra, por su parte, asumió la mayor carga técnica: diseñó la apariencia externa, las estructuras internas que sostienen los componentes y la disposición de las conexiones eléctricas.
El modelo también seleccionó las piezas necesarias, organizó la placa de circuito impreso y generó el firmware, el software de bajo nivel que controla el funcionamiento del aparato. A esas tareas se sumaron el desarrollo de la interfaz de usuario y la integración con Codex.
Lo distintivo del experimento es que reunió en un solo proceso disciplinas que suelen requerir equipos especializados diferentes: diseño industrial, ingeniería mecánica, electrónica y programación. Según OpenAI, el diseño completo se concretó en menos de siete días, y un fabricante externo produjo un lote reducido de prototipos en menos de un mes.
Las limitaciones de la IA frente a la fabricación real
Disponer de un diseño terminado no garantizó una fabricación sin contratiempos. Al llegar a la etapa de producción surgieron inconvenientes vinculados con las tolerancias dimensionales, las restricciones propias del fabricante y los detalles necesarios para ensamblar correctamente las piezas.
Astra no había contemplado todas esas condiciones durante el proceso de diseño. Esto obligó a los ingenieros de OpenAI a realizar varias rondas de revisión para adaptar los archivos digitales a las exigencias reales de la industria.
El episodio deja una conclusión concreta: un modelo digital convincente en pantalla no equivale automáticamente a un objeto que pueda producirse a escala industrial. La propia compañía admite que esa brecha continúa siendo uno de los principales obstáculos para automatizar procesos completos de ingeniería.
Como muestra de esa limitación, GPT-6 Astra obtuvo una puntuación media de 0,594 en la evaluación interna BenchCAD 2.0, muy por debajo del 0,875 alcanzado por un modelo más reciente que la empresa todavía no presentó públicamente.
El impacto de la inteligencia artificial en el diseño de hardware
Más allá de este experimento puntual, OpenAI reportó un crecimiento sostenido en el uso de sus modelos aplicados a hardware. Entre febrero y octubre de 2026, el consumo por parte de sus equipos internos de hardware se multiplicó por 23, una cifra calculada a partir del consumo de tokens que, según aclaró la compañía, no equivale de manera directa a un aumento proporcional de productividad.
El avance también se proyecta hacia alianzas externas. OpenAI confirmó que colabora con Chip Ganassi Racing y Mazda en aplicaciones orientadas al diseño de piezas, el estudio de la aerodinámica de vehículos y las simulaciones de ingeniería.
Qué significa este experimento para el futuro de la ingeniería con IA
El experimento de OpenAI no sugiere que los ingenieros dejen de ser necesarios en los procesos de diseño industrial. Muestra, en cambio, que etapas que antes demandaban numerosos pasos manuales pueden resolverse ahora en cuestión de días gracias a modelos como GPT-6 y Astra.
La inteligencia artificial demostró capacidad para generar diseños complejos que terminan convertidos en prototipos reales, pero esos diseños todavía requieren supervisión humana cuando deben enfrentarse a las restricciones físicas y productivas del mundo real.

articles.title: Underdog shows off a 32MB speech model in new demo | TechCrunch
articles.text:
AI companies across the world are racing to make bigger and better models, but the problem is all of them need massive amounts of processing power. On the other end, some researchers and startups are creating smaller models that can run on edge devices, like your phone or computer.
One such startup, Underdog, has released a game built with its new voice model called Woof that’s only 32MB large.
The game features a room with a retro tech theme, a typewriter, and a CRT monitor. There is a desk lamp, which makes a sound when you click its switch. The intro warns users about “intrusive” cloud providers in the town — ostensibly a jab at cloud-based models.
You can interact with the typewriter and music tuner.
You can type anything on the typewriter using your keyboard, and the game will speak it back. You can also rotate the tuner to generate different kinds of music.
All of this works within the browser through Underdog’s speech generation model, which, the company says, can run on most devices without any internet connection. The model has 31 million parameters and is open for everyone to download.
While such a small model likely won’t replace bigger models, it may still be enough to drive local assistant experiences or create personalized podcasts.
This demo comes weeks after Underdog launched Bark, a 167MB speech-to-text model also designed to run on edge devices for transcription and dictation.
Sigil Wen, the founder of Underdog, told TechCrunch that he started building the app because, instead of using notetakers like Granola, he wanted to build his own system with AI models that can run on users’ devices and let them own their data.
“I think we will be able to run most capable models of today on the devices you already own within months. We just want to train the best open models that are American-made, that are open, that are capable and allow people to have private AI,” he said, referring to his manifesto.
In addition to the two voice models mentioned above, Underdog has also released a 27-billion-parameter model that can run on laptops, along with a waitlisted app that the company is positioning as a locally hosted alternative to Muse and Instinct.

articles.title: After AMD's gaming revenue crashes 40%, CEO Lisa Su declares "We are a data center-first company"
articles.text:
A hot potato: Rest in peace, dedicated consumer GPU makers. With Nvidia having long been an AI firm with a passing interest in making prohibitively expensive consumer graphics cards, AMD's boss has confirmed that Team Red now considers itself a "data center-first" company. With the data center segment making up about 63% of AMD's record third-quarter 2026 revenue, it's easy to see why CEOs are moving away from PC gaming to follow the money.
Su made her remarks in an interview with Yahoo Finance's Brian Sozzi, where she presented data centers as central to AMD's identity and growth.
"We are a data center first company, that is our profile and you know, people need more computing to power all these applications," Su said.
In a perfect illustration of the state of the current industry, AMD's Instinct accelerators and Epyc server processors pushed the company's Q3 revenue to a record $13.4 billion, up 97% from a year earlier. Meanwhile, its gaming revenue crashed 40% from a year ago to $773 million, mostly due to AI data centers gobbling up all the memory and other components, hiking the price of graphics cards.
It's all great news for Su, of course. She said that AMD's data center business was going to grow 50% sequentially from Q3 to Q4. "We're looking to double the business, more than double the business as we go into next year," she explained.
Su also addressed the increasing demand for AI hardware from industry giants. "We're a tech company that has a lot of resources and the ability to expand our supply and expand our ability to help our customers," the CEO said. "I want to be the best partner to the largest users of compute in the world."
While there has been plenty of nervousness around the massive spending on AI infrastructure recently, Su said the market can be "a little bit short-sighted" when judging AI spending. Her argument is that companies should invest now to meet demand several years ahead, even if investors question the immediate financial impact.
Su added that AMD is always investing for the long term, which she describes as roughly three to five years ahead. That doesn't sound promising for gaming fans hoping things will change anytime soon.
Rival Nvidia, of course, has gone even further down the AI-first route. In its latest reported quarter (Q2 FY2027), $89.02 billion, or 92.5%, of its revenue came from its data center business. Team Green doesn't even report gaming separately anymore, placing it instead within the broader Edge computing category that brought in $7.5 billion, or 7.5% of its overall revenue.

articles.title: 'Families need reliable electricity': OpenAI pledges to try and provide 'a national effort to support affordable, reliable electricity for families and businesses' living near its data centers
articles.text:
'Families need reliable electricity': OpenAI pledges to try and provide 'a national effort to support affordable, reliable electricity for families and businesses' living near its data centers
Reliable energy and AI?
- OpenAI launches new program to protect residents and businesses near its data centers from power outages
- The Grid Protectors Program is designed to prevent OpenAI campuses from “hogging” all the power
- A new development in Effingham County, Georgia, will pioneer the program
OpenAI wants to protect local communities situated around its data centers from power outages, and has launched a new program intended to deliver both reliability and affordability to nearby residents and businesses.
The Grid Protectors Program is launching with the planned Effingham County, Georgia data center campus, which features an agreement with Georgia Power to make power available in a flexible demand scenario, which should cover demand for around 700,000 households.
OpenAI’s future facilities are designed to be more flexible in how they demand power from the grid, and the Grid Protectors Program viewed as a “starting point” for improved reliability for homes, businesses, and of course data campuses.
Grid Protectors pilot
The Grid Protector Program certainly seems a step in the right direction from OpenAI. It comes against a backdrop of growing concerns over the power requirements of AI data centers and protests over their approval, invariably in locations where residents are resistant.
OpenAI says the pilot site at Effingham County incorporates its agreement with Georgia Power to accommodate “up to 1,000 megawatts of flexible demand response.”
This is intended to ensure local residential and business properties have the power available “to help keep air conditioning running in hundreds of thousands of homes during extreme heat. For scale, that is equivalent to the average electricity demand of roughly 700,000 households.”
OpenAI says this is more than enough to cover the combined households of Washington, D.C., and Boston.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
Financial assurances
By working to offer communities assurances of flexible energy at its new site, OpenAI clearly hopes that its upcoming data centers are recognized as more suited to locations that have recently come under fire.
Perhaps they want to be a part of those communities? The launch announcement adds that its new compute facilities are more flexible than older facilities, and OpenAI is committing itself under the Grid Protectors Program to collaborate with authorities.
“We will work with utilities, regulators and policymakers to develop practical arrangements for the campuses we build in the future,” it announces, “arrangements that reflect local grid needs, help campuses support the grid when it is under pressure, and pay the costs we create. Long-term contracts and financial assurances can protect other customers if a project is delayed, reduced or canceled.”

articles.title: Teilnahme auch ohne eigenes Konto möglich: Whatsapp bekommt eine neue Event-Funktion
articles.text:
Neue Planungsfunktion: Bald kannst du in Whatsapp Events erstellen, teilen und verwalten
Whatsapp führt eine neue Event-Funktion ein. Laut dem Unternehmen soll eine neue Startseite des Messengers die Planung von Veranstaltungen und Treffen ermöglichen. Das Besondere: Nutzer:innen können auch Freund:innen oder Verwandte einladen, die die App selbst nicht nutzen. Die Funktion soll in den kommenden Wochen starten. Ein konkretes Datum steht bisher nicht fest.
Wie funktioniert das neue Event-Feature von Whatsapp?
In Deutschland sind auf privat genutzten Smartphones im Durchschnitt 46 Apps installiert – zusätzlich zu den vorinstallierten Anwendungen. Das geht aus einer Umfrage des Digitalverbandes Bitkom hervor. Whatsapp ist besonders weit verbreitet. Über Generationen hinweg dient der Messenger als Hauptplattform für die alltägliche digitale Kommunikation. Um die App noch nützlicher zu machen, erweitert Meta sie fortlaufend um neue Funktionen. Seit Kurzem testet das Unternehmen etwa einen In-App-Browser, mit dem Nutzer:innen jeden Link direkt im Chat öffnen können. Eine neue Planungsfunktion soll außerdem dabei helfen, den Versand von Nachrichten bis zu zwei Wochen im Voraus festzulegen.
Jetzt plant der Meta-Dienst ein weiteres Feature, das die Planung von Events erleichtern soll. Laut einem kürzlich veröffentlichten Blogbeitrag können Whatsapp-Nutzer:innen dadurch direkt in der App Veranstaltungen erstellen, ein Titelbild festlegen und diese per Link mit anderen teilen – auch mit Personen, die den Messenger selbst nicht verwenden. „Außerdem führen wir eine neue Veranstaltungsübersicht ein, die dir als zentrale Anlaufstelle dient, um individuelle Einladungen zu erstellen und zu versenden sowie Anmeldungen zu verwalten“, heißt es in dem Beitrag weiter. Dort sollen Nutzer:innen auch vergangene und bevorstehende Termine einsehen können.
Whatsapp erweitert den Funktionsumfang
Laut den Entwickler:innen legten sie bei der neuen Funktion großen Wert auf den Datenschutz. Telefonnummern sollen für andere Nutzer:innen, mit denen man selbst nicht verbunden ist, ausgeblendet werden. Und Gäste ohne Whatsapp-Konto können die Adresse einer Veranstaltung erst einsehen, wenn sie ihre Teilnahme bestätigt haben. Auch bei der Event-Funktion schützt die End-to-End-Verschlüsselung Nachrichten und Anrufe, wie die Nutzer:innen es von privaten Chats oder Gruppen gewohnt sind.
Whatsapp verfügt schon seit einiger Zeit über Funktionen zur Veranstaltungsplanung. Das Update weitet die Zielgruppe aus und schließt auch Nutzer:innen mit ein, die selbst nicht auf dem Messenger aktiv sind. Das gilt auch für andere Funktionen. So haben Personen ohne Whatsapp-Konto jetzt beispielsweise auch die Möglichkeit, an Video-Anrufen teilzunehmen. Laut Engadget könnte das Unternehmen dadurch versuchen, stärker mit anderen Diensten zu konkurrieren.

articles.title: How Syd Life AI is turning health data into better quality of life - Disrupt Africa
articles.text:
Lorena Puica had a successful corporate career, but health issues prompted a re-evaluation that led her to launch the AI-enabled wellness monitoring startup Syd Life AI in 2016.
Headquartered in the United Kingdom, with subsidiaries in Japan and the UAE, Syd Life AI measures quality of life and helps both individuals and institutions improve it. The company has been commercially operating since 2022 and is backed by more than a decade of research and development.
“There is no shortage of health data. The hard part is turning it into something a person, or a population, can act on,” Puica told Disrupt Africa.
Puica began her career in strategy consulting and investment banking, where she looked after more than US$200 billion. She holds five degrees across mathematics, finance and economics, and is a CFA charterholder.
“My background has always been deeply rooted in data, research and quantitative analysis,” she said. “My move into entrepreneurship was shaped by my own health challenges. When my health failed, I discovered that much of the evidence that could help me recover already existed, but it was scattered across research and had never been brought together for one person.”
An algorithm for health
She spent three years studying that research, built an algorithm to synthesize it, applied it to her own data, and recovered. She then set two Guinness World Records, running seven marathons on seven continents in seven days.
“That experience made the wider challenge much more tangible. I saw an opportunity to take the analytical skills I had developed throughout my career and apply them to healthcare and life quality, making existing research more useful and actionable for individuals,” Puica said. “The underlying approach remained rooted in data, research, and numbers; what changed was the problem I chose to apply those skills to. Syd is that system, built for everyone.”
At the heart of the platform is Syd’s Life Quality Index, which measures nine dimensions: physical health, emotional health, financial health, purpose, self-awareness, social life, career, brain power, and environment. It analyses more than 2,390 variables per individual. Behind it sits a proprietary 31-billion-parameter Large Quantitative Model, trained on a daily-refreshed corpus of more than 2.7 million peer-reviewed studies and over 14.3 billion person-years of data covering more than 84 risk models.
For individual members, Syd works on their phone as a 24/7 companion, offering personalized, research-backed lifestyle recommendations. Employers, insurers, governments, and partners get an aggregated, anonymized view of where risk is rising, which interventions are likely to have the greatest impact, and the cost and return of acting.
Translating health data
“The gap is translation. Evidence and health data are both abundant. What has been missing is the infrastructure to apply them to a specific person, workforce, or population,” said Puica. “Most AI in health optimizes a single measure, and for a long time health AI meant a chatbot or a wearable. We asked a different question: what does life quality mean for every individual, and how can improvement in it be measured?”
She said consumer mood and sleep apps, employer mental health providers, and population health analytics firms each cover part of the territory, but Syd Life AI works across all three, with every core component built in-house.
“What distinguishes us is the complete cycle: identify where life quality is rising, intervene, then measure whether life quality improved,” she said. “Much of the market stops at prediction, and prediction without intervention is reporting.”
An independent Scientific Advisory Board, chaired by Stanford biomedical informatics pioneer Dr Lawrence Fagan, oversees the company’s work, reviews the evidence base, and signs off on significant model updates before deployment.
Expanding reach
Syd Life AI has now been deployed across 26 countries within roughly three years of launch. Over 12 months, members improve their Life Quality Index by an average of 19 percent, with stress, anxiety and depression down 48 percent on average and productivity up 23 percent.
“The system was validated in a randomized controlled trial across a workforce of 10,000 NHS frontline doctors and nurses,” Puica said. “Participants experienced statistically significant reductions of 16 percent in clinical anxiety, 14 percent in stress and 12 percent in depression, roughly five times the improvement of standard therapy.”
Japan has been a particularly strong market. A government programme in Tokyo’s Shibuya City raised overall life quality by 20.1 percent, while at Takanawa Gateway City, Tokyo’s first smart city district, onboarding completion reached 98 percent against an industry benchmark of 17 percent.
The startup has also already had a taste of the African market. “A global corporate programme ran across 11 countries, including South Africa, and raised overall Life Quality Index scores by 14 percent in three months, against a two per cent threshold the client had set for success,” Puica said. “Across our clients, return on investment ranges from 12 to 25 times, alongside a 15 percent rise in retention and health risk reduced by up to 40 percent.”
Building a global B2B business
Syd Life AI operates a business-to-business and business-to-government model, with employers, health systems, insurers, and governments licensing the platform for their people, and partners offering it under their own brand. Revenue comes from enterprise licensing and strategic partnerships, and the company reached profitability in 2025.
The company was initially funded by Puica, who put in US$2 million of her own capital while the framework was being built. Investors since include the UK Government, the UAE Government’s sovereign wealth fund, and a San Francisco-based VC firm.
The company counts Japan, the US and the UAE as its three anchor markets, but Puica sees clear potential in Africa.
“Africa fits the same model. The continent combines young, mobile-first populations with rising chronic health costs, and health systems under real pressure to act earlier,” she said. “A local partner is what makes entry properly localized there, from the language and the culture to the way trust is earned.”
The challenges of building a global healthcare business
The journey has not been without its challenges.
“Two things were harder than the technology: staying the course while the market caught up, and being taken seriously in countries where nobody knew us,” Puica said. “We were building robust AI for health long before AI was something the market wanted to talk about. There was pressure to ship a simple app that could generate revenue quickly rather than spend years building the foundations. Saying no to that was difficult, but necessary.”
She said trust was the other major hurdle. “Need alone does not open doors in a new market. Japan is the clearest example: there is profound demand, but trust is built slowly. Partnering with Koshida Corporation gave us credibility and reach we could not have built alone. It is the approach I would take into any new region.”
“Being early is a tax you pay in full, up front, for years. You do not budget for the idea; you budget for the wait,” she added.
Puica took part in the Standard Chartered Foundation’s Women in Tech Accelerator last year. The programme, locally implemented by Companies Creating Change (C3) (Dubai, UAE), with support from Village Capital, provided tailored technical assistance, peer learning and a US$5,000 grant.
“What made the biggest difference was the access it opened to Standard Chartered’s leadership and network, and to investors and business leaders at Demo Day,” she said. “The part that stayed with me was the cohort. Every company in it was led by a woman, and the level of innovation in the room was remarkable. You get a network of founders who understand the decisions you are making because they are making them too, and who stay in touch long after the programme ends. I would recommend applying to any founder who would benefit from that.”

articles.title: Construyen el puente para animales más grande del mundo, una obra que busca reconectar hábitats y proteger a pumas aislados
articles.text:
El Wallis Annenberg Wildlife Crossing, un paso elevado para animales que cruza los diez carriles de la autopista US-101 en Agoura Hills, al noroeste de Los Ángeles, está a punto de terminarse. Sus impulsores lo presentan como el mayor paso de fauna de su tipo del mundo, aunque reconociendo que el récord depende de cómo se mida. La idea detrás de todo este proyecto está el poder volver a unir un hábitat que la autopista partió hace décadas, sobre todo para los pumas.
Un puente cubierto de monte. La estructura que salva la autopista mide unos 64 metros de largo, y unos 53 de ancho. Encima se ha extendido tierra con plantas autóctonas, y la web del proyecto explica que lleva muros y otras medidas contra el ruido y la luz de un tráfico de más de 300.000 vehículos al día. De hecho, levantarlo ha obligado a reubicar líneas eléctricas y una conducción de agua, a proteger robles catalogados como patrimoniales y a crear pendientes que conectan con los terrenos protegidos del norte y del sur.
Una factura que no ha parado de crecer. El proyecto arrancó con un presupuesto de 92,6 millones de dólares, unos 82,6 millones de euros al cambio, aunque ya ronda el equivalente a 101,6 millones de euros. Según sus responsables, el encarecimiento se debe a los aranceles, la inflación, los problemas de suministro y el coste de la mano de obra, mientras que las lluvias récord de 2022 y 2023, frenaron la compactación del terreno y retrasaron la apertura prevista para 2025. En cuanto al dinero con el que se paga, combina la financiación pública con donaciones privadas de más de 6.000 donantes, con la filántropa Wallis Annenberg a la cabeza. Sin embargo, el sobrecoste ha hecho que muchos hayan alzado la voz diciendo que es un despilfarro que California no se puede permitir.
Pumas atrapados entre autopistas. ¿Y por qué tanto esfuerzo por un puente para animales? Pues por los pumas de las montañas de Santa Mónica, que llevan décadas encerrados por autopistas y urbanizaciones y han acabado cruzándose entre parientes. Seth Riley, jefe de fauna del Área Recreativa Nacional de las Montañas de Santa Mónica, del Servicio de Parques Nacionales de Estados Unidos (NPS), aseguró que el 41% de los apareamientos documentados desde 2002 se produjo entre parientes cercanos, y algunos ejemplares ya muestran colas torcidas y testículos deformados.
Un estudio de 2016 en el que participó el NPS calculó un 99,7% de probabilidad de extinción en 50 años si la población sigue aislada y la endogamia acaba lastrando su reproducción. La escritora Mary Ellen Hannibal lo resume con una frase que luce la web del proyecto, de la National Wildlife Federation: “La naturaleza no funciona sin conexión”.
El primer visitante, un coyote. El 28 de octubre de 2026, una cámara del NPS fotografió a un coyote trepando por la ladera sur de la estructura, lo que lo convierte en el primer mamífero grande conocido en pisar el paso. Beth Pratt, presidenta del Wildlife Crossing Fund, se emocionó al ver también imágenes de pumas cerca del extremo sur: “Hay muchas cosas mal en el mundo, pero esta la hemos arreglado”, explicó.
Y vendrán más imágenes, porque los biólogos del NPS están instalando cámaras remotas y empezando a implantar unos sensores que registran la temperatura corporal y el ritmo cardíaco, primero en ciervos y después en pumas, para saber si los animales se estresan al pasar por encima de la autopista. Durante las obras ya han visto linces rojos, coyotes, zorros grises, ciervos mulos y pumas utilizando un sendero junto a la estructura.
Si ninguna tormenta invernal retrasa el remate, el paso se abrirá a la fauna el 2 de diciembre de 2026. Sus impulsores quieren que sirva de modelo mundial para la conservación de fauna en las ciudades y que reduzca los atropellos, aunque será difícil de medir porque no hay demasiados debido a que los animales casi nunca intentan cruzar. Sin embargo, los biólogos confían en que los pumas de las colinas de Simi, al norte, acaben cruzando y aportando sangre nueva poco a poco.
Foto | Gobierno de California

articles.title: VeloDB’s Nitin Waghulde on why AI agents break down after the demo
articles.text:
VeloDB
View Brand Publisher
VeloDB’s Nitin Waghulde on why AI agents break down after the demo
At TechSparks 2026, VeloDB’s Regional Director for APAC explained why AI agents that work in pilots struggle in production, and why the fix often lies in the database underneath them.
AI agents tend to look good in a pilot. The scope is narrow, the data is controlled, and the questions are predictable. Production is different, and that gap is where many projects stall.
Gartner predicts that over 40% of agentic AI projects will be cancelled by the end of 2027, due to escalating costs, unclear business value, or inadequate risk controls. For Nitin Waghulde, Regional Director, APAC at VeloDB, a large part of the problem sits below the model, in the data layer.
In a keynote titled ‘AI agents at scale: Surviving beyond the demo’, Nitin explained how AI agents use data differently from people, what they need to work reliably at scale, and how companies are redesigning their data infrastructure to support them.
Nitin started his session with an example. In a traditional system, a business manager who wanted last year’s sales figure would run a ready-made report and get the number in one lookup.
Ask an AI agent why sales dropped over the last three quarters, and the work changes. The agent pulls order records from the ERP and CRM systems, scans support tickets and chats to check whether major customers have escalated problems, and reads sales team reports on territory dynamics. If its reasoning is incomplete, it goes back for more.
“What used to be completed in one simple lookup or one simple query, now you’re taking hundreds of lookups for the same thing,” he said.
AI is now a customer of your data
In the past, people and reports were the main consumers of business data, and systems were built around fixed reports with clear boundaries.
Now, Nitin said, AI has become a new customer of that data, and it behaves very differently.
Agents run around the clock, ask many questions at once, and work in an iterative loop: ask, think, search, and retry until they can answer. Their questions are also unscripted. That puts a heavy, unpredictable load on the data layer.
The challenge grows because business data lives in several places at once: transactional records, chat memory, documents, dashboards and pre-built reports, and vector stores for meaning-based search. An agent has to search all of them and combine the results before it can answer.
Each extra trip to the data adds cost. If the data is stale, the answer is wrong. Nitin compared it to driving with an inaccurate traffic map. And when data comes from many sources, it becomes harder to know where an answer came from, which creates a trust problem.
He likened it to sending someone to five filing cabinets to collect pieces of paper. By the time the person returns from the fifth cabinet, the information from the first may already be out of date.
What production agents need
Nitin outlined four requirements for agents to move from pilot to production.
- Access to every data type: Agents need numbers from structured records, text from documents, and meaning from unstructured sources.
- Scale: A single query may now need to scan petabytes of data, not the few terabytes that systems were once designed for. Also, the platform should support concurrency at scale to support iterative querying for data-hungry agents
- Freshness: Agents can only act correctly on current information. If an agent processing a refund cannot see the latest transaction record, it has to wait. Every change, including updates and deletions, needs to be visible to the agent immediately, without waiting for a nightly batch job.
- A record of every interaction: Every AI interaction leaves a trail. These logs are growing faster than business data itself, and they feed back into decision-making.
VeloDB’s answer is a single engine that handles all of these needs. The company was founded in 2023 by the original creators of Apache Doris, an open-source real-time analytics database that became a top-level Apache Software Foundation project in June 2022. According to VeloDB, Apache Doris has more than 14,000 GitHub stars and 700 contributors, and is used by over 5,000 enterprises worldwide.
To cut down the back-and-forth trips that slow agents down, VeloDB supports hybrid queries. A single query can combine SQL, vector search, and text search, running deterministic and probabilistic searches in parallel. The result is one unified source of truth instead of scattered data.
What it looks like at scale
Nitin shared two examples of companies running this architecture in production.
The first was one of the largest crypto exchanges, with more than 120 million users, which he did not name. The exchange makes transaction data available to AI agents that retail investors can query, for example to see what positions large traders are taking on an asset. He said its agents handle about 33,000 conversations with a tail latency of around 3 milliseconds, running round the clock.
The second was MiniMax, a Chinese AI company that listed on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange in January 2026 and says it serves 212 million users in more than 200 countries. MiniMax rebuilt its logging system on Apache Doris after moving away from Grafana Loki, because logs had become a valuable source of intelligence worth keeping and querying.
Nitin said MiniMax ingests data at 10 Gbps and can query about 10 petabytes in under two seconds, at 70% lower cost. VeloDB has separately reported that the Doris-based system now supports logs across all of MiniMax’s business lines at petabyte scale with over 99.9% availability.
The same challenges apply to early-stage startups building agents, Nitin added. VeloDB works with fintech startups that face the same scaling problems as MiniMax or the crypto exchange, just at an earlier stage.
His closing point was that agents will always ask hundreds of questions, so the infrastructure has to make each one cheap, fast, and current.
For Nitin, scaling AI agents is less about finding a better model and more about giving agents real-time, trustworthy data from a single source. Companies that get the data layer right, he argued, can make decisions faster, reduce costs, and move their agents from pilot to production with confidence.

articles.title: “Il s'agira d'un remplacement complet du système d'exploitation” : Windows 11 27H2 s'annonce massif
articles.text:
Plutôt que Windows 12, Microsoft travaillerait sur Windows 11 27H2, une mise à jour vraiment majeure
Microsoft préparerait le terrain à une vraie grosse mise à jour de Windows 11 en 2027 avec la version 27H2. Une bonne nouvelle pour les performances notamment, mais une mauvaise pour qui attendrait Windows 12.
Microsoft Windows 11 Professionnel
Évoqué et attendu depuis plusieurs années, Windows 12 ne sera visiblement toujours pas pour 2027. D'après des sources du média The Verge, Microsoft plancherait plutôt sur "un swap complet" de Windows 11 avec la future mise à jour 27H2 attendue pour la fin de l'année prochaine.
Il faut dire que si la récente mise à jour 26H2 a partiellement permis à la firme de tenir ses promesses d'améliorations de Windows 11, il reste encore bien du travail à accomplir pour redorer son image et convaincre tout le monde.
Microsoft reste concentré sur Windows 11
Dernièrement, les mises à jour 25H2 et 26H2 n'étaient que des paquets d'activation, venant débloquer graduellement des nouveautés et des améliorations (avec de solides gains de performances à la clé). Mais pour la mouture 27H2, à l'instar de la 24H2 qui venait initier en 2024 un nouveau cycle de développement de trois ans, Microsoft devrait remplacer ou mettre à niveau d'un coup des composants majeurs du système d'exploitation.
C'est pourquoi il est probable que les tests auprès des Insiders commenceront beaucoup plus tôt que d'habitude et n'attendront pas juin 2027. Reste à découvrir ce que contiendra exactement cette mise à jour, mais il est certain que les performances seront toujours un sujet central, puisque le travail d'allégement de Windows 11 est toujours en cours. Reste aussi à savoir si ces nouvelles bases réclameront une mise à jour des réquisitions matérielles, et si cela ouvrira la porte à Windows 12.
Toujours d'après les sources de The Verge, un changement plus mineur devrait accompagner cette future mise à jour majeure de Windows 11 : de nouveaux fonds d'écran. Toujours un peu inspirés du fond d'écran original, ils devraient être dévoilés durant la conférence Microsoft Ignite de novembre, tandis que chaque version de Windows 11 (Famille ou Pro) devrait jouir de variations différentes. Les versions grand public présenteraient également de légères variations axées sur le jeu, la productivité, la création et les performances.
