articles.title: Google, Meta y TikTok demandaron para frenar la ley de California que limita el scroll infinito a menores de 16
articles.text:
Google, Meta y TikTok demandaron al estado de California para impedir que se aplique una ley que prohíbe a las redes sociales ofrecer funciones adictivas a menores de 16 años. Las tres empresas presentaron demandas separadas el miércoles, según informó la agencia Reuters, y argumentan que la norma viola la libertad de expresión.
La ley se llama Proyecto de Ley 1709 de la Asamblea (AB 1709). Impide que las plataformas ofrezcan a los menores de 16 recomendaciones personalizadas, videos que se reproducen solos —función conocida como autoplay— y desplazamiento infinito de contenido, según Reuters y Bloomberg Law.
El gobernador Gavin Newsom la firmó el 10 de septiembre y entrará en vigor el 1 de enero de 2027, salvo que un juez la anule o la suspenda. Newsom había dicho entonces que California “no se quedará de brazos cruzados” mientras tecnología sin regulación pone en riesgo a los niños.
Google presentó su demanda en la justicia federal de San José, Meta en San Francisco y TikTok en Los Ángeles. El único demandado es el fiscal general de California, Rob Bonta, que hace cumplir las leyes del estado. Su oficina respondió el jueves que revisa las demandas y está “comprometida a defender las leyes de sentido común de California para proteger a los niños en internet”.
Los argumentos de cada empresa
Las tres compañías sostienen que la ley las obliga a presentar contenido a los niños de la forma que prefiere el estado y que sustituye el criterio de los padres por el del gobierno. También invocan la Sección 230, una norma federal que protege a las plataformas de la responsabilidad por lo que publican sus usuarios.
“Los padres son quienes mejor pueden decidir por sus familias”, dijo el vocero de Google, José Castañeda. Según él, leyes tan amplias “rompen los sistemas” creados para que los chicos encuentren videos adecuados a su edad. En su demanda, Google afirma que el autoplay de YouTube “funciona como siempre lo hizo la televisión” y que ya viene desactivado para menores de 18.
Meta alega que California no puede imponerle cómo ordenar y mostrar miles de millones de publicaciones, y que la norma deja a los niños libres de pasar tiempo ilimitado en otras plataformas similares. La empresa recordó que aceptó limitar a dos horas diarias el uso de Facebook e Instagram por parte de menores, salvo autorización de un padre o tutor.
TikTok, filial de la china ByteDance, afirmó que el discurso protegido “no puede ser suprimido” solo para proteger a los jóvenes de ideas o imágenes que un legislador considere inapropiadas.
Un historial de fallos en contra
En agosto, Meta aceptó pagar hasta USD 18.000 millones y limitar el uso de Facebook e Instagram por parte de adolescentes, en acuerdos con casi todos los estados de Estados Unidos que la acusaban de violar leyes de privacidad y de consumo, según Reuters.
Las plataformas aún enfrentan miles de demandas de familias, distritos escolares y gobiernos que las acusan de provocar adicción y daños a la salud mental de menores.
El Centro de Información sobre Privacidad Electrónica (EPIC), una organización de defensa de derechos digitales, afirma que las demandas repiten argumentos que un tribunal de distrito rechazó en agosto en un caso similar, donde el juez dictaminó que el diseño adictivo de los feeds no es discurso protegido por la Primera Enmienda. No todas las críticas vienen de las empresas: la Fundación Frontera Electrónica, otra organización de derechos digitales, calificó la ley de “pesadilla masiva para la privacidad y la libertad de expresión”.
AB 1709 modifica una ley de 2024 que exige consentimiento de los padres para que las plataformas recomienden publicaciones mediante algoritmos a menores de 18, norma que Google, Meta y TikTok ya impugnan en otro proceso, según MediaPost.

articles.title: Blue Origin says it is building a higher-performing rocket engine at 1/4 the cost
articles.text:
KENNEDY SPACE CENTER, Florida—Blue Origin announced two significant upgrades to its New Glenn rocket on Thursday, reducing the cost of manufacturing the vehicle and expanding its capacity for payload delivery to geostationary orbit and the Moon.
With these upgrades, the company aims to eventually position New Glenn to launch more than 1,000 times a year.
“There has never been higher demand for launch, ever,” Dave Limp, chief executive officer of Blue Origin, said during the UP.Summit conference at the Shuttle Landing Facility in Florida.
Blue Origin has already begun test firing a new engine, called Northstar, that will eventually replace the BE-4 engine that powers the first stage of New Glenn. Separately, the company also said it was developing a hydrogen-oxygen third stage for the rocket, GS3, to give it an extra kick.
A new Northstar
The Northstar engine is a simplified but more powerful version of the BE-4 engine, Limp said. It has half the number of parts and 30 percent less mass, and about 65 percent can be 3D-printed.
Blue Origin believes it can manufacture the engine at 25 percent of the cost of a BE-4 engine and eventually reach the point where each engine can be assembled in less than a day. The company is deep into development and testing of Northstar, having already begun a test-firing campaign.
“To get access to space at a lower cost, we have to look at every part of the vehicle,” Limp said. “This is going to be a game-changer.”
The BE-4 engine powering New Glenn today has a thrust of 640,000 pounds, and Limp said Northstar will have a starting thrust of 715,000 pounds. Like the BE-4 engine, Northstar burns methane and liquid oxygen using an oxygen-rich staged combustion cycle and a single-shaft turbopump architecture.
Limp said the company will continue to manufacture the existing BE-4 engine for United Launch Alliance, which uses two of the engines to power its Vulcan rocket.

articles.title: TV Philips é boa? Veja 6 modelos para comprar em 2026 • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
TV Philips é boa? Veja 6 modelos para comprar em 2026
Encontre as melhores TVs Philips em diversos tamanhos e faixas de preço; lista inclui modelos 4K e com tecnologia Ambilight para maior imersão
Se você pretende comprar uma TV Philips em 2026, é importante avaliar detalhes como: tipo de painel (LED, QLED, MiniLED), resolução, taxa de atualização e tecnologias de processamento de imagem, entre outros recursos. Somente assim é possível entender se o produto é realmente bom para o seu dia a dia.
Alguns modelos de televisores da Philips se diferenciam ao trazer sistema de iluminação Ambilight — que projeta as cores da imagem na parede. Além disso, as TVs da empresa contam com sistemas operacionais consagrados, como Google TV e Roku OS, garantindo fluidez e facilidade de navegação.
Neste guia, o Tecnoblog apresenta seis TVs Philips para diferentes perfis de uso. Confira os prós e contras de cada uma antes de escolher a televisão ideal para sua casa ou escritório.
A Philips The Xtra 4K Ambilight está disponível em versões de 55″, 65″ e 75 polegadas. Apesar de ter painel LCD, essa TV utiliza miniLEDs para controlar a iluminação em diferentes regiões da tela, melhorando contrastes, brilho e entregando um preto mais profundo.
Além disso, há suporte a Dolby Vision, HDR10+ e HLG, formatos que ampliam a qualidade da imagem em conteúdos compatíveis, e a taxa de atualização nativa é de 120 Hz, o que pode ser interessante para jogos.
O conjunto também inclui Dolby Atmos, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth 5.0 e recursos para jogos como VRR, ALLM e AMD FreeSync Premium.
A Philips The One 4K Ambilight tem painel LCD com retroiluminação LED convencional, e está disponível em versões de 55″, 65″ e 75 polegadas.
Ela usa o processador P5 Perfect Picture Engine para compensar cores, contraste e nitidez, mas as limitações do painel podem acabar aparecendo especialmente em cenas escuras, resultando em perda de detalhes.
Para filmes e séries, o modelo oferece compatibilidade com Dolby Vision e outros formatos HDR, além de suporte a Dolby Atmos. Já para jogos, a fabricante anuncia VRR, ALLM e AMD FreeSync Premium.
No quesito conexões, são 4 entradas HDMI (2 HDMI 2.1) e 2 portas USB. Já a conectividade sem fio fica por conta de Wi-Fi 5 e Bluetooth 5.2.
A TV Philips QLED 4K está disponível em versões de 55″, 65″, 70″ e 75 polegadas, e traz painel LCD com filtro de pontos quânticos, componentes que ajudam a ampliar a reprodução de cores em comparação com modelos que têm retroiluminação tradicional por LED.
A compatibilidade com HDR10+ permite reproduzir conteúdos com metadados dinâmicos, que orientam os ajustes de imagem conforme as cenas.
A TV utiliza o sistema operacional Titan OS, com acesso a aplicativos como Netflix, YouTube, Prime Video, Disney+ e Globoplay. Na conectividade, oferece Wi-Fi de banda dupla, Bluetooth 5.0, três entradas HDMI e duas portas USB, além de conexão Ethernet para internet por cabo.
A Philips LED 4K Ambilight é uma opção para quem busca uma TV voltada ao entretenimento, especialmente para assistir a filmes e séries com uma experiência mais imersiva. Disponível em versões de 50″, 55″, 65″ e 75 polegadas, o modelo conta com a tecnologia Ambilight, que projeta cores nas paredes de acordo com o conteúdo exibido na tela.
No processamento de imagem, o Pixel Precise Ultra HD trabalha no aprimoramento da definição, enquanto o Micro Dimming ajuda a otimizar o contraste por meio da análise de diferentes áreas da imagem.
O modelo também oferece Dolby Atmos e DTS:X, tecnologias de áudio que podem proporcionar maior sensação de espacialidade com conteúdos e equipamentos compatíveis.
O sistema operacional é o Titan OS, com acesso a serviços como Netflix, YouTube, Prime Video, Disney+ e Globoplay. Na conectividade, a TV oferece Wi-Fi 5 de banda dupla, Bluetooth 5.0, três entradas HDMI 2.1 com suporte a recursos como ALLM e VRR, além de duas portas USB.
A Philips LED 4K é indicada para quem busca uma TV de tela grande, com acesso ao ecossistema de aplicativos do Google para assistir a filmes, séries e outros conteúdos de streaming.
Disponível em versões de 65 e 75 polegadas, a plataforma reúne aplicativos e serviços de streaming, como Netflix, YouTube, Prime Video e Disney+, além de oferecer recomendações personalizadas de conteúdo. Ela também permite utilizar o Google Assistente por comandos de voz.
Na qualidade de imagem, a TV oferece suporte a Dolby Vision, formato HDR que otimiza a reprodução de brilho, contraste e cores conforme as cenas. Já o áudio é compatível com Dolby Atmos, tecnologia que proporciona maior sensação de espacialidade em conteúdos compatíveis.
Na conectividade, o modelo oferece quatro entradas HDMI (2.0 e 2.1), Bluetooth 5.0 e Wi-Fi para acesso à internet sem fio.
A Philips QLED HD é indicada para quem procura uma TV compacta para ambientes menores, como quartos e escritórios, mas não abre mão de qualidade na reprodução de cores. Com tela de 32 polegadas, seu principal diferencial é a tecnologia QLED, pouco comum em televisores desse tamanho.
O painel utiliza pontos quânticos para ampliar a reprodução de cores, enquanto o processamento Pixel Plus HD trabalha no aprimoramento da definição da imagem. Por outro lado, a resolução HD oferece menos detalhes que as telas Full HD e 4K presentes em outros modelos do mercado.
A TV também conta com Dolby Audio e utiliza o sistema operacional Titan OS, com acesso a aplicativos como Netflix, YouTube, Prime Video, Disney+ e Globoplay.
Na conectividade, oferece Wi-Fi 5, duas entradas HDMI 2.0, duas portas USB 2.0, saída de áudio óptica e conexão Ethernet para internet por cabo
Antes de comprar uma smart TV Philips, é importante analisar os seguintes aspectos:
Ambilight é um sistema de iluminação com LEDs instalados na parte traseira da TV. As luzes acompanham as cores exibidas na tela e projetam iluminação nas paredes ao redor do aparelho.
O efeito amplia visualmente a área iluminada durante filmes, séries, músicas e jogos, criando uma experiência mais envolvente.
A Philips LED 4K Ambilight é uma opção de TV com bom custo-benefício por reunir resolução 4K, Ambilight, HDR10+, Dolby Atmos, VRR e ALLM para jogos, sem precisar investir em modelos mais caros como as TVs miniLED.
A Philips The Xtra 4K Ambilight é uma das melhores TVs para PS5 ou Xbox Series deste guia. Seu painel Mini LED tem frequência nativa de 120 Hz e oferece VRR, ALLM e AMD FreeSync Premium.
As entradas HDMI 1 e 2 aceitam sinais 4K a até 120 Hz, permitindo aproveitar melhor a qualidade gráfica oferecida pelos consoles.
A Philips QLED HD é a alternativa mais adequada para quartos pequenos por ser uma TV de 32 polegadas e resolução HD.
O painel QLED utiliza pontos quânticos para ampliar a reprodução de cores, enquanto o Titan OS reúne aplicativos de streaming. É importante considerar que a resolução HD oferece menos definição que os modelos 4K.
As TVs Philips podem valer a pena para consumidores que buscam uma smart TV com preço mais acessível para assistir a filmes, séries e programas de TV no dia a dia.
A marca também atende a quem gosta do efeito de iluminação Ambilight, que amplia visualmente a experiência de assistir à TV, e a jogadores que procuram modelos com recursos como VRR, ALLM e alta taxa de atualização.
A escolha depende, portanto, do perfil de uso, do tamanho desejado e dos recursos oferecidos por cada modelo.
As TVs Philips utilizam duas plataformas: Google TV e Titan OS.
O Google TV reúne aplicativos, recomendações de conteúdo e integração com o Google Assistente, enquanto o Titan OS concentra os serviços de streaming disponíveis em sua própria interface.
A plataforma muda conforme a linha, por isso é importante verificar o sistema do modelo escolhido.
Philips e Philco oferecem televisores com propostas e faixas de preço diferentes. No geral, a Philips reúne recursos mais específicos para quem procura Ambilight e Mini LED, enquanto a comparação com a Philco depende do modelo e do preço encontrado.
A Philips tem opções com tecnologias miniLED, QLED e Ambilight, além de modelos com Google TV e Titan OS. A Philco também atua em segmentos de entrada e intermediário, com TVs LED, QLED e plataformas como Roku TV e Google TV.
Portanto, vale comparar resolução, frequência, conexões e sistema operacional das TVs de ambas as marcas.
Não, as opções da marca ficam concentradas em tecnologias como LED, QLED e Mini LED. Quem procura uma TV OLED de qualidade precisa considerar outras marcas presentes no mercado brasileiro.

articles.title: QNAP says hackers breaching NAS devices in Plex2Shell attacks
articles.text:
QNAP urges users to update Plex Media Server to the latest version available in the QNAP App Center, as hackers are exploiting the Plex2Shell vulnerability chain.
The vendor said it had received multiple reports of suspected compromises involving customers’ network-attached storage (NAS) devices.
"QNAP has received reports from some users that Plex Media Server on their NAS appears to have been compromised through [Plex2Shell] vulnerabilities, and QNAP Technical Support is assisting the affected users,” the company says in an advisory today.
Plex2Shell is a chain of four vulnerabilities in the Plex Media Server, tracked as CVE-2026-96652, CVE-2026-96654, CVE-2026-96655, and CVE-2026-96656.
Security researcher Zach Main discovered and reported the flaws to Plex on July 27. Exploitation started shortly after the full technical details became public on October 16.
CISA added all four flaws to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on October 20, 2026, urging federal agencies to upgrade to Plex 1.43.3.10861 or later within three days, giving it maximum priority.
QNAP’s NAS devices are specialized computers with built-in storage that allow users to store, access, and share files across a network. They are typically used to back up computers and store media files.
Users can also expand their devices' capabilities by installing applications from the QNAP App Center, such as Plex Media Server, which streams movies, TV shows, and music directly from NAS drives.
QNAP advises users to update Plex Media Server to the latest version available through the QNAP App Center, currently 1.43.3.10861, to protect against Plex2Shell attacks.
“The QNAP Product Security Incident Response Team (QNAP PSIRT) has confirmed that the vulnerabilities exist only in Plex Media Server; QTS, QuTS hero, and other QNAP operating systems are not themselves affected,” the vendor says.
User action required
QNAP says that users should treat their NAS devices and all personal content as compromised if they're running a vulnerable Plex server that is exposed on the public web.
The vendor warned that updating now will not remove any payloads the attackers have already installed on the device.
The recommended action is to check for the signs of compromise shared in the security bulletin, perform a clean reinstall of the OS (QTS or QuTS hero), and then reset Plex and NAS credentials.
Users who do not need to access Plex remotely should disable the related features and stop forwarding port 32400. Those who need remote access are advised to connect via VPN.
QNAP has released a detailed step-by-step remediation guide on how to do the above.
The company also offers to investigate logs from suspected compromises, which users can submit via QNAP’s technical support portal.

articles.title: 3M to pay up to $7.35 billion after lawsuits link its forever chemicals to contaminated water
articles.text:
The takeaway: Specialty chemicals and industrial products manufacturer 3M has agreed to pay up to $7.35 billion to settle lawsuits that alleged the company was culpable for groundwater contamination from forever chemicals found in many of its products, including firefighting foam, adhesives, and tapes. The money will be paid out to around 120,000 people over a period of nine years.
Under the terms of the agreement, the plaintiffs will receive $50 million this year, followed by yearly payments of more than $1 billion from 2028 to 2033. 3M will be required to pay additional money if more plaintiffs join the class action, but if not enough people get on board, the company reserves the right to cancel payments and continue fighting the case in court.
The lawsuits alleged that people were sickened by perfluoroalkyl and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS), which are known to resist heat, stains, oil, and water, and are typically found in products like firefighting foam, non-stick cookware, utensils, and clothing. What makes them especially dangerous is that they're not easily biodegradable, meaning they persist in the environment for a long time.
Research has linked long-term exposure to PFAS to several critical and even life-threatening illnesses, including cancer, liver disease, immune system damage, and thyroid malfunction. It's also known to adversely affect the health of unborn children, resulting in low birth weight and other complications in babies and expectant mothers.
It is worth noting that this is not the first time 3M reached multimillion dollar settlements in PFAS-related lawsuits. Last year, the company agreed to pay up to $450 million to resolve several lawsuits over allegations that forever chemicals from its products had contaminated soil and water in New Jersey.
In 2023, the company reached settlements amounting to more than $10 billion with multiple water supply utilities to resolve lawsuits over allegations that forever chemicals in its products contaminated public water distribution systems, potentially jeopardizing the health of millions of people.
3M said in 2022 that it would stop manufacturing PFAS at its factories by the end of 2025. In January 2026, the company announced that it ended PFAS manufacturing on schedule, but noted that it will continue to use third-party PFAS in some electronics products, such as printed circuit boards and lithium-ion batteries. The company added that it is spending billions of dollars to clean up past contamination.
3M is not the only company dealing with PFAS-related controversies. Specialty chemical company DuPont, refrigerant and industrial resin manufacturer Chemours, and agricultural pesticide and herbicide producer Corteva have faced similar allegations in the past. They've spent a combined total of more than $1 billion to settle PFAS-related lawsuits.

articles.title: Canadians can claim money following Apple gift card settlement
articles.text:
There are only a few months left for Canadians to claim money in a settlement from an alleged Apple gift card scam.
Apple has agreed to pay $1.25 million to settle allegations that the company could have done more to prevent gift card fraud in Canada. The lawsuit was filed in Ontario against Apple Inc., Apple Value Services LLC, and Apple Canada Inc. on behalf of Canadians who were victims of a gift card scam and didn’t receive refunds or compensation.
The settlement agreement was approved on Sept. 16, 2026, in the Ontario Superior Court of Justice, and Canadians can now file a claim before the deadline.
What’s the lawsuit about?
The class-action lawsuit against Apple was brought forward by a Canadian who had purchased iTunes, App Store, or Apple Music gift cards and lost the value of the card in gift card scams “conducted by third-party fraudsters.”
The lawsuit alleges that since the cards are used on Apple platforms, the company had control and “could have held and reversed transfers to fraudsters, and flagged suspicious transactions.”
Apple allegedly refused to refund customers who lost money after being tricked into sharing redemption codes with scammers.
The class-action website states, “Apple, which was not the party that perpetrated the scams, denies that it had any responsibility to provide such refunds and denies all allegations of wrongdoing, and none of the claims were proven in court.”
Are you eligible to file a claim?
You may be able to file a claim if you meet the following criteria:
- You are a person in Canada
- You purchased one or more iTunes, App Store, or Apple Music gift cards between Jan. 1, 2016 and Sept. 16, 2026
- You provided the redemption code of one of those gift cards to a third party who was unknown to you, and who sought the code under false pretenses
- You suffered a loss that was not fully refunded or otherwise compensated by Apple or another third party
- You reported the fraud
How much could you receive?
The claims website does not specify exactly how much each eligible recipient could receive from the $1.25-million settlement. However, it does state that 75 per cent of the funds will be distributed among eligible claimants “whose report to Apple can be verified,” while the remaining 25 per cent will be distributed to other eligible claimants.
The amount of any payment will depend on the number and value of approved claims,” states the site.
What should you do next?
If you think you’re eligible to file a claim, make sure to fill out the form online and provide your personal information and contact details. You’ll be asked to provide proof of purchase (receipts, bank or credit card statements, screenshots, or other documents). You’ll also be asked for proof that you reported the fraud.
When is the deadline?
Canadians are urged to submit a claim online by Feb. 20, 2027. Paper claim forms are available online and must be postmarked no later than Feb. 20.
Check out the website for details.
There are several other class-action lawsuits Canadians should keep an eye on, including those against CAE and CIBC, as well as the newly filed lawsuit against Crime Stoppers.

articles.title: Nvidia wants to repurpose over 130 old telco buildings as tiny data centers, report claims — company in talks with Brightspeed after pitching idea to parent company Apollo Global Management
articles.text:
Nvidia wants to repurpose over 130 old telco buildings as tiny data centers, report claims — company in talks with Brightspeed after pitching idea to parent company Apollo Global Management
Is it faster to repurpose multiple small sites than to build one massive data center?
Internet and telecommunications provider Brightspeed is reportedly in talks with Nvidia to convert several of its buildings into tiny data centers. According to The Information, Nvidia pitched the idea to Apollo Global Management executives, the parent company of Brightspeed, who then asked it to submit written plans to the internet provider. Nvidia complied and has now requested additional information, data, and site visits to some of Brightspeed’s existing infrastructure.
The telecommunications company has around 130 buildings located around the country, many of which are already built to handle data and voice traffic and have the required power infrastructure to run Nvidia servers. Sources say that the AI tech giant estimates that these sites could collectively deliver around 1 gigawatt of compute capacity, which could accommodate more than 2,200 Supermicro Vera Rubin NVL72 racks containing 72 Rubin GPUs and 36 Vera CPUs each. Although these sites already can power these GPUs, it’s still not a plug-and-play solution, as Nvidia would still need to install cooling systems and other supporting architecture. These would still require permits and approval from the local government, but they would likely face less red tape and opposition compared to building a data center from the ground up.
Apollo Global Management has already made significant bets in AI hardware, with the asset management company involved in a $40 billion deal with SpaceX that would give it around 360,000 Vera Rubin GPUs across 5,000 NVL72 racks. While it’s currently unclear who will own the AI chips installed in Brightspeed facilities, the proposal could potentially help Apollo find a place for the Nvidia chips it ordered to get them up and running as soon as possible. This is a much better solution compared to waiting for years to get a data center approved, all while facing resistance from the community even after getting the go-ahead from the local government.
Having multiple small data centers like this is also a setup that OpenAI and Anthropic have been considering, especially as larger facilities are facing delays and backlash from the communities that they’re in. While having a large, homogeneous cluster built in one location is preferable for training, Nvidia representatives have described these smaller sites working together as an “inference network” to help run existing AI models. This is especially important as AI agents, which use five to ten times more tokens than humans, become more popular.
The move to use existing facilities instead of building new ones from scratch has received renewed attention, especially after Americans overwhelmingly voted against data centers during the midterm elections. While the more than 300 data center bans enacted across the U.S. have only delayed three existing projects, it’s feared that the bans and moratoriums would make it that much harder to start new data center developments and make it difficult for AI companies to secure the compute capacity needed to power their AI models in the future.

articles.title: Tesla officially kills off the Cybertruck
articles.text:
The day you all have been waiting for is finally here – The Tesla Cybertruck is officially dead!
CEO (and mastermind of whatever that thing was) Elon Musk revealed the news on X, saying that “Tesla will be winding down production of the Cybertruck at Gigafactory Texas around the middle of next year to make room for increased Cybertruck production.”
Tesla will be winding down production of the Cybertruck at Gigafactory Texas around the middle of next year to make room for increased Cybercab production
— Elon Musk (@elonmusk) November 6, 2026
To no surprise, the Cybertruck’s decline largely stems from weak sales over its first four years. WIRED notes that despite Musk’s claim that there were more than a million reservations, the truck sold fewer than 50,000 units in total by March, 2025.
According to Reuters, Kelly Blue Book data suggests Tesla sold only 20,237 Cybertrucks in the US last year, which is down 48 per cent from the 38,965 sold in 2024. North of the border, data from Transport Canada suggested that Tesla had sold fewer than 2,000 between 2024 and 2025. Ironically, Musk had predicted annual sales of 250,000 units.
The announcement also came only minutes after Musk raised the Cybertruck price in both the US and Canada, with the price rising to C$142,886.
Interestingly, former Aston Martin CEO Andy Palmer spoke to Reuters and quipped that “It doesn’t make sense to keep it going when it’s not meeting its targets. Every rational auto guy would say the same.”
To put it lightly, the Cybertruck has had a pretty tumultuous existence. When Elon Musk first stepped on stage to show off the Halo-looking thing, he tried to demonstrate the strength of the “unbreakable” glass by throwing a steel ball at it, and (shocker), it broke.
The Cybertruck has also had quite a few recalls throughout its history. The first recall was because the accelerator pedal was getting stuck due to an unapproved lubricant that reduced the pedal’s retention, and perhaps the most famous one was when the glued-on stainless steel trim on the front of the truck would just fall off after the elements got to it.
This is yet another move that signals Tesla is shifting away from being an automotive-only company, and towards being an AI and robotics company. Although the Cybercab is still a small project, Musk clearly sees this as the way forward for the company, and is scrapping his ridiculous fantasy truck to do it.
Rest easy, Cybertruck. You were strange, but fun to laugh at.
Sources: Elon Musk on X via WIRED, Reuters

articles.title: Physicl raises $10M to make the digital world real enough for robots | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Alex de Vigan’s last business got swamped by the rise of generative AI, but now he’s betting the tech that team had built, a platform for creating tempting product renderings for e-commerce, can be re-purposed to make robots more useful.
His new venture, Physicl, has raised $10 million in seed funding led by Inovia Capital to help world model designers and robot builders solve thorny training problems with more realistic simulations.
Founder and CEO de Vigan spent the last decade building nfinite, which made it easy for brands and retailers to create 3D models of their goods and display them online. The arrival of transformer-based AI models led that company to focus more on generative imagery, but de Vigan saw a new purpose for his team and the tech stack they’d built to faithfully render 3D environments.
“What we were super unique about doing in 3D, AI was going to replace, but something was missing in AI: its ability to understand, interact, and manipulate space and objects,” de Vigan says.
Researchers developing physical AI models to make robots more capable of tasks like handling diverse, small objects have been frustrated by the returns of training them on video, and the expense of gathering data through remote operations.
Simulations in digital worlds are seen as a promising solution, but ensuring that these simulated worlds are faithful to real-world physics has proven difficult. De Vigan believes that the pipeline his previous company built to “transform unstructured, incomplete, heterogeneous real-world information into a high-fidelity physical representation… with correct geometry, materials, and physics” can now be used to make physical AI models more effective.
Physicl is entering a crowded category of startups vying to provide data and tooling to foundation model builders and robot operators. “The space is very young and very blurry sometimes,” de Vigan admits. There are a variety of companies collecting, labeling, or generating data in different modalities as their customers try to figure out the secret sauce that will make robots live up to their promise.
In particular, Physicl wants to focus on post-training models on difficult edge cases. The startup is releasing a product called Studio with 10,000 3D environments and 100,000 assets that represent various objects. It lets users create scenes to generate synthetic data for training robots on specific problems. For example, Studio could be used to generate training data to help a robot that has trouble discerning a cup on a cluttered counter-top, or while the cup is in shadow.
SpAItial, a world model builder, collaborated with Physicl as an early customer to improve the fidelity of its products, the latest of which, Echo-3, was released last week. SpAItial’s tool generates 3D simulations from 2D imagery, and to do that effectively, its CEO and founder Matthias Niessner said they needed to train on the kind of high-fidelity synthetic data Physicl offers.
However, Physicl wants to be more than a data provider; it sees itself as the tooling for ongoing synthetic data generation. “What we created 10 years ago, without knowing it, was basically an agentic workflow to transform unstructured information into high-fidelity 3D,” de Vigan said. He imagines customers bringing trillions of images or millions of hours of lidar capture data to feed into his platform and turn them into high-quality 3D representations that can be used to generate billions of permutations to train their models.
“The real challenge is, you have to curate the data by hand, and this is a very long cycle,” Niessner, also a professor of robotics at the Technical University of Munich, told TechCrunch. “To us what seems very attractive is you can just do this on the fly […] You’re running Claude, and it checks, ‘Oh, I need more data of this in my training,’ and then it auto generates that data, depending on the training state. That, to me, is super exciting, and this is exactly what Physicl is offering.”

articles.title: Esta herramienta gratuita te muestra por fin qué está consumiendo la GPU de tu PC
articles.text:
La GPU es uno de los componentes que casi nunca recibe atención dentro de las herramientas para medir el rendimiento en Windows. Fuera de la temperatura o la carga de trabajo, los usuarios no saben con exactitud qué servicio o aplicación está consumiendo recursos, lo que sí ocurre con la memoria o el procesador. Un ingeniero de Microsoft ha decidido resolver el problema a través de gputaskman, una herramienta que te dice qué hay dentro de tu tarjeta gráfica y qué programas la utilizan.
Scott Hanselman, vicepresidente y miembro del equipo técnico de Microsoft, publicó un repositorio en GitHub que ofrece un programa gratis para monitorear tu GPU. De acuerdo con Neowin, gputaskman muestra información detallada por proceso, uso de la GPU y memoria VRAM. También se incluyen valores como el consumo energético, temperaturas, velocidad de reloj, actividad de codificación y decodificación de video e incluso tráfico PCIe.
A diferencia de las herramientas tradicionales, gputaskman no se limita a indicar que tu tarjeta gráfica está usando cierta cantidad de memoria. La herramienta muestra un listado similar al que vemos en el Administrador de tareas de Windows, con los programas que tienes ejecutándose en ese momento, la cantidad de memoria que consumen y el porcentaje total de uso de la GPU. La aplicación también revela información detallada de lo que pide cada proceso, aunque esta información está dedicada más a entusiastas y desarrolladores.
Si ejecutas modelos de IA en tu ordenador, gputaskman también monitorea su uso
Otra de las funciones interesantes de gputaskman es una que permite ver las cargas de trabajo de la IA. La herramienta detecta los procesos asociados con los modelos de lenguaje y ofrece detalles sobre los pesos, niveles de cuantización, estimaciones de caché KV y otros datos relacionados. El programa puede generar archivos de texto plano y JSON, en caso de que necesites compartir la información para llevar a cabo un análisis posterior.
Si bien Windows 11 ya implementó algunos ajustes en el Administrador de tareas en agosto, gputaskman va un paso más lejos. La versión de Microsoft que se ofrece en el sistema operativo solo ofrece información general sobre el uso de memoria y gráficas de consumo que pueden personalizarse para diversas tareas, como 3D (juegos), video, etc. Esta función no incluye una división por procesos, como sí lo hace la herramienta externa.
Por ahora, gputaskman se encuentra en una fase de desarrollo temprano, por lo que podrías encontrarte con algunos fallos. Hanselman no ha mencionado si existen planes de integrarla de forma nativa en alguna actualización oficial de Windows 11, aunque puedes descargarla gratuitamente desde el repositorio de GitHub. La herramienta es compatible con GPUs de NVIDIA y AMD, así como también con Linux y Mac con chip Apple Silicon.

articles.title: Ethiopian gaming startup Rise of Fearless raises US$1m to scale African battle royale title - Disrupt Africa
articles.text:
Ethiopian gaming startup Rise of Fearless has raised US$1 million in funding from advisory firm Epic Edges Capital as it looks to scale its African history-inspired battle royale mobile game.
Launched in 2025, Rise of Fearless offers an African take on the battle royale genre, drawing narrative inspiration from Ethiopia’s victory over Italian forces at the Battle of Adwa in 1896. The game’s characters, environments, hairstyles and attire are designed to reflect African identities, offering an alternative to the Western-centric narratives that have long dominated mainstream gaming.
Free-to-play on the Apple App Store and Google Play, the game has surpassed 15,000 downloads to date, with its largest player communities in Nigeria, Ethiopia and South Africa.
The previously bootstrapped startup’s new funding, structured as a SAFE, will be used to invest in talent, technology, infrastructure, marketing and community-building, as Rise of Fearless looks to expand its audience beyond its existing markets.
“The launch of Rise of Fearless filled a gap in the gaming space, but it has also forced us to think beyond game downloads, shifting our focus towards a much wider African gaming ecosystem where African intellectual ownership and talent development are key,” said founder Kanessa Muluneh. “As a bootstrapped company, this investment is pivotal to our ambitions and the future of African gaming.”
Muluneh said the startup also plans to use its growth to help tackle some of the structural challenges facing African gaming companies, including access to reliable technology, servers and cross-border payment infrastructure.
Remco Coerman, founder of Epic Edges Group, said Rise of Fearless was the kind of ambitious, culturally-rooted IP with the potential to resonate far beyond its home market.
“We believe there is a significant opportunity for African creators to build globally relevant gaming experiences that reflect the continent’s stories, identities and talent,” he said.

articles.title: Amazon retire déjà 300 € à l'iPhone Duo pour le Black Friday
articles.text:
L’iPhone Duo est le premier smartphone pliant d’Apple. Il arrive sept ans après le Galaxy Fold de Samsung, sur un marché que Huawei et Samsung ont poussé en 2026 vers le format passeport. Apple arrive donc après les autres, avec quelques idées à lui, comme un écran intérieur mat et une caméra cachée sous la dalle. Présenté le 9 septembre 2026 en même temps que les iPhone 18 Pro, l’iPhone Duo est en vente en France depuis le 23 octobre. Il existe en quatre capacités, de 256 Go à 2 To.
Pendant le Black Friday, la version 1 To est affichée sur Amazon à 2 780,10 € au lieu de 3 089 €, grâce à un coupon à cocher sur la page du produit. La remise atteint 308,90 €, soit 10 % du prix de référence. C’est la première baisse de prix sur ce modèle.
Amazon affiche le smartphone en rupture de stock, tout comme Apple. Le site précise toutefois qu’il s’agit d’une rupture temporaire : il est toujours possible de passer commande et Amazon promet d’envoyer un e-mail dès qu’une date de livraison estimée sera connue. Il faudra pourtant attendre : la livraison pourrait n’intervenir qu’en janvier.
Que vaut l’iPhone Duo, le premier pliant d’Apple ?
- L'écran nano texturé est incroyable
- Le pli le moins visible du marché
- Le format passeport dans la poche
- Meilleure interface logicielle pour un pliant
- Autonomie très satisfaisante
- Une réinvention réussie de l'iPhone
- Un peu trop lourd
- Trop d'applications inadaptées
- Touch ID est un retour en arrière
- Il manque un zoom optique
- 2 339 euros, c'est trop cher
L’iPhone Duo mise d’abord sur son écran intérieur de 7,6 pouces. Sa finition mate, dite nano-texturée, réduit les reflets. Déplié, il offre selon Apple une surface d’écran 50 % plus grande que celle de l’iPhone 18 Pro Max. iOS 27 y affiche deux applications côte à côte, une première sur iPhone. À moitié plié, il tient aussi debout tout seul, en mode tente ou façon ordinateur portable, pour une visio ou une vidéo sans support.
Apple n’a pas non plus négligé les finitions. L’iPhone Duo profite d’un cadre et d’un couvre-charnière en titane de grade 5, d’une face avant Ceramic Shield 2 et d’un dos Ceramic Shield. À l’intérieur, on retrouve la puce A20 Pro des iPhone 18 Pro, refroidie par une chambre à vapeur. Apple annonce jusqu’à 35 % de performances soutenues en plus par rapport à l’iPhone 17 Pro. Cette même puce intègre une partie dédiée à l’intelligence artificielle. En France, une partie de cette promesse attendra : Apple précise que Siri AI, la nouvelle version de son assistant, ne sera pas disponible dans un premier temps dans l’Union européenne sur iOS.
La partie photo repose sur deux capteurs Fusion de 48 mégapixels, un principal et un ultra grand-angle. Il n’y a pas de téléobjectif : le zoom 2x est obtenu en recadrant le capteur principal. Apple ajoute la Capture intelligente, qui déclenche seule quand les personnes prennent la pose, et une caméra FaceTime cachée sous l’écran intérieur. À l’extérieur, la caméra avant Center Stage se contente de 12 mégapixels, contre 18 mégapixels sur les iPhone 18 Pro. Enfin, son système à deux batteries doit lui permettre de tenir une journée complète.
À ce prix, l’iPhone Duo 1 To est-il une bonne affaire ?
L’iPhone Duo reste un smartphone très cher. Même avec 10 % de remise, c’est un achat de passionné. La version 1 To s’adresse d’ailleurs à ceux qui filment beaucoup ou gardent toute leur photothèque sur le téléphone. Il faut aussi accepter les petits défauts d’un premier modèle, avec des applications qui ne profitent pas encore du grand écran.
Le lancement a en outre été terni par le « Crackgate ». Sur certains exemplaires, l’écran interne s’est fissuré le long du pli. Apple a reconnu un problème touchant « un petit nombre » d’appareils et remplace les écrans concernés, ce qui limite le risque pour les acheteurs. Et avec une livraison attendue en janvier, ceux qui commandent aujourd’hui recevront un modèle issu d’une production plus récente. Si vous étiez décidé, ces 300 € d’économie restent donc bons à prendre.

articles.title: Clés API, accès secrets… Un demi-milliard pour empêcher les agents IA de déraper
articles.text:
Le géant américain de la sécurité, Palo Alto Networks, négocierait le rachat d’une start-up israélienne, Clutch, qui identifie les accès utilisés par les agents IA et permet d’en limiter les droits. Le prix évoqué, 500 millions de dollars, atteindrait environ 50 fois ses revenus récurrents annualisés.
Un agent IA peut désormais disposer d’un accès à Slack, d’identifiants pour une base de données et du droit de modifier du code. Clutch Security veut permettre aux équipes de sécurité de savoir qui lui a confié ces accès et de contrôler ce qu’il peut en faire. Une spécialité qui intéresserait de près Palo Alto Networks, selon TechCrunch.
Un demi-milliard pour une entreprise de trois ans
Palo Alto Networks discuterait en effet d’un paiement de 500 millions de dollars en numéraire, auquel s’ajouteraient des compléments conditionnés à certains objectifs. Les négociations, révélées initialement par The Information, sont en cours et pourraient ne pas aboutir.
Fondée en 2023, Clutch approcherait les 10 millions de dollars de revenus récurrents annualisés, ou ARR, un indicateur qui ramène les abonnements en cours à une année complète. Le prix de base de ce rachat représenterait donc environ 50 fois ce montant. TechCrunch situe par ailleurs la précédente valorisation de Clutch à 85 millions de dollars lors de sa levée de fonds de janvier 2025.
Retrouver les identifiants, puis limiter ce qu’ils autorisent
Clutch travaille sur les « identités non humaines ». Sa plateforme recense les comptes de service utilisés par les logiciels ainsi que les clés d’accès aux interfaces de programmation, ou API, et les jetons d’authentification qui leur permettent de se connecter à d’autres outils.
L’enjeu est de relier ces accès à leur usage réel. D’après Clutch, son inventaire associe chaque agent à la personne qui l’a déployé, aux identifiants qu’il emploie et aux ressources qu’il peut atteindre. L’entreprise cherche ainsi à repérer aussi bien les assistants installés sur les postes de travail de l’entreprise que les agents exécutés dans le cloud ou intégrés à des logiciels professionnels.
À partir de cette cartographie, les équipes peuvent fixer des limites. Une action autorisée sur un environnement de développement peut, par exemple, être bloquée sur les serveurs de production, ceux qui font fonctionner le service utilisé par les clients. Clutch propose aussi de bloquer l’envoi direct de modifications vers les branches protégées d’un dépôt de code, ou d’empêcher un agent de lire des identifiants stockés sur un ordinateur. Le principe consiste à donner à l’agent les droits nécessaires à sa mission, puis à surveiller leur utilisation.
La sécurité des agents attire les grands acheteurs
Pour Palo Alto Networks, cette acquisition éventuelle prolongerait son offensive dans la sécurité des identités. Le groupe a finalisé le rachat de CyberArk en février 2026, une opération annoncée à 25 milliards de dollars. Cette plateforme protège déjà les accès des utilisateurs humains, des machines et des agents IA. Clutch viendrait donc renforcer un domaine dans lequel le groupe est déjà engagé.
Ses concurrents avancent également. Cyera a ainsi bouclé en septembre le rachat d’Oasis Security pour un milliard de dollars, afin de rapprocher la protection des données du contrôle des identités et des accès des agents. Bref, les agents ont le vent en poupe, le business pour les contrôler et sécuriser, aussi !
Les identités non humaines désignent des comptes et informations d’accès utilisés par des logiciels plutôt que par des personnes : comptes de service, clés API, jetons OAuth, certificats, etc. Elles servent à automatiser des tâches et à permettre à des applications, scripts ou agents IA d’appeler d’autres services (Slack, bases de données, dépôts Git…). Le risque vient du fait que ces identités sont souvent créées rapidement, peu documentées et réutilisées longtemps, parfois avec des droits trop larges. Comme elles ne « se connectent » pas comme un utilisateur classique, elles échappent plus facilement aux contrôles habituels (revues d’accès, MFA, rotation régulière). Les sécuriser consiste d’abord à les inventorier, puis à réduire et surveiller leurs privilèges.
Une clé API ou un jeton d’authentification est un sésame technique permettant à un logiciel d’accéder à une API, donc à des fonctions et des données d’un service distant. Un jeton est souvent limité dans le temps et lié à des permissions, tandis qu’une clé API est parfois plus statique et donc plus risquée si elle fuit. Avec des agents IA capables d’enchaîner des actions (lire, écrire, supprimer, déployer du code), un secret mal protégé peut ouvrir la porte à des opérations à fort impact. Le principal enjeu est d’empêcher qu’un agent réutilise un jeton pour sortir de son périmètre (exfiltration, modification de configurations, accès à des dépôts). D’où l’importance de la traçabilité (qui a créé/attribué le secret) et du contrôle fin des permissions.
Le principe du moindre privilège consiste à donner à un agent uniquement les droits strictement nécessaires à sa mission, et pas davantage. Concrètement, un agent peut être autorisé à exécuter des actions en environnement de développement (tests, lecture de logs, modifications limitées), tout en étant bloqué en production, où la moindre erreur ou action malveillante impacte des clients. La séparation dev/prod réduit le rayon d’action en cas de compromission d’un identifiant ou de comportement inattendu de l’agent. Dans les organisations matures, cela s’accompagne de règles de contrôle d’accès (RBAC/ABAC), de validations humaines pour certaines actions, et d’une journalisation détaillée. L’objectif est de limiter les dégâts tout en gardant l’automatisation utile.

articles.title: Veeam warns of Software Appliance boot failures on AMD EPYC hosts
articles.text:
Veeam warned customers about boot failures affecting Software Appliance virtual machines (VMs) on hosts with AMD EPYC processors.
The company's Software Appliance VMs are pre-configured, Linux-based virtual machines that let admins run the Veeam Backup & Replication backup software suite on Linux devices without manually installing dependencies or configuring the software.
To comply with corporate and government security frameworks, the underlying Linux kernel runs integrated health and cryptographic checks (such as jitterentropy health tests) in FIPS mode during early boot.
However, as the company explained in a Wednesday advisory, these VMs will fail to boot and will crash with a kernel panic after failing an early-boot FIPS-mode jitterentropy check on some AMD EPYC processors.
"A Veeam Software Appliance (Linux-based Veeam Backup & Replication) virtual machine running on a host with an AMD EPYC processor intermittently fails to boot after a reboot, including a reboot that follows an update that installs a new kernel," it said.
"This issue occurs because the Linux kernel used by the Veeam Software Appliance runs a jitterentropy health test in FIPS mode during early boot, and the test intermittently fails on certain AMD EPYC processors, including AMD EPYC 7262, 7302, and 7F72. When the test fails, the kernel stops the boot process with a kernel panic."
This known issue originates in the Linux kernel version used by the Veeam Software Appliance and affects Veeam Software Appliance version 13.1 and later.
According to Veeam, users are seeing "Kernel panic - not syncing: jitterentropy: Initialization failed with host not compliant with requirements: 9" kernel panic errors on impacted systems.
Mitigation available
To mitigate this issue, Veeam told IT administrators to redeploy the appliance to a Linux host with a different processor.
If the appliance cannot be redeployed on a system with an unaffected processor, IT admins are advised to disable automatic updates for the appliance and install updates manually (while monitoring the VM as it reboots).
"If the kernel panic occurs, power off the virtual machine and power it on again. A restart of the guest operating system does not recover the virtual machine," Veeam added. "After the appliance has booted successfully, no further errors are expected, and the operation of Veeam Backup & Replication is not affected."
Earlier today, Veeam also said that some of its products are affected by a critical Linux kernel vulnerability (CVE-2026-98432) in the IPv4 TCP networking code that allows remote unauthenticated attackers to execute commands as root on servers running Multipath TCP (MPTCP) listeners.
The company has fixed the CVE-2026-98432 flaw for some impacted Veeam components and is now pushing the patched kernel to affected systems either as a private fix or through the Veeam Updater.
Veeam's products are used by more than 550,000 customers, including 74% of Global 2,000 firms and 82% of Fortune 500 companies.

articles.title: When code is cheap, trust is not: Inside the AI-era engineering roundtable
articles.text:
When code is cheap, trust is not: Inside the AI-era engineering roundtable
In a closed-door roundtable, leaders from logistics, healthcare, telecom, fintech, and e-commerce discussed where to automate, where to keep humans in charge, and why observability can no longer be an afterthought.
AI has made writing code faster than ever, but the harder question for engineering leaders is what happens after the code is written. At a roundtable on operating engineering in the AI era, leaders from logistics, food tech, healthcare, telecom, fintech, ecommerce and higher education compared notes on scaling with AI without losing reliability, security or control. The shared view was that speed is no longer the hard part. Governing it is.
The roundtable, moderated by Ipshita Basu, brought together Manjunath Nakshathri, Head of Engineering, Mojro; Shobhit Suman, CPO, HungerBox; Pavan Kumar A T, CTO, Digii (DigiiCampus); Pranjal Nadhani, Co-founder and CTO, Cautio; Kenil Paul, VP, Technology and Solutions, 6D Technologies; Rimjhim Agrawal, Co-founder and CTO, BrainSightAI; Dhruv Rastogi, Chief AI Officer, MediAssist; Chandrakesh Pandey, Senior Vice President of Technology, Niyo Solutions Inc.; Achal Sharma, CTO, TechnoSport; Sunil Kumar, Director Engineering, Meesho; and Anshul Sharma, Director Engineering, Scaler.
The session was hosted by groundcover and Data Signals in partnership with YourStory, and was led on the host side by Paul Trebe, Head of Sales and Partnership, groundcover, and Satish Dange, Founder, Data Signals.
Where the bottleneck has moved
Participants agreed that AI has compressed build time, but the pressure has shifted downstream. When agents generate large volumes of code, the questions become who reviews it, who tests it and who monitors dozens of deployments a day. Several leaders said their teams now spend more time on design, context and governance than on writing components. Agents are only as effective as the context they receive, and few organizations yet have repository knowledge, documentation and templates in a form an agent can reliably use.
Drawing the line on autonomy
The room converged on a progressive approach. Reversible, read-only work, such as fetching data or generating reports, can go to agents with little friction. Irreversible actions, such as deleting data or running database updates, stay behind human review. Blast radius matters as much as reversibility. If a wrong call could affect end users or production systems, a person makes it.
One of the participants described a ‘four eyes’ model in which AI does the maker work of reading and analyzing, deterministic rules deliver clear yes or no outcomes, and a human signs off. Another speaker described risk scoring based on severity and occurrence, which focuses human review on medium and high criticality items. Others drew the line by specialization, letting engineers use agents freely in their own domain while production ownership stays with people who can debug at 2 AM.
That scenario also surfaced in a hopeful form. Instead of waking an engineer, an agent can investigate an incident and hand over a report by morning, leaving the decision with a human. Trust, participants said, will build gradually, much as it did with online payments, and the line will keep moving.
Accountability and the skills question
Accountability drew firm agreement: it cannot be delegated to a model. Leaders remain answerable for what agents do. AI works as an intelligence multiplier, one participant noted, which means mistakes are amplified as quickly as good decisions.
Skill erosion sparked livelier debate. Some saw a shift in skills, much as calculators changed arithmetic. Others, particularly in healthcare, worried about losing the expertise needed to judge AI output at all. One practical answer was to decide deliberately where AI drafts and where humans do.
Data control as a design decision
For telecom and healthcare leaders, data control is settled at design time. Models cannot simply run in a public cloud when regulators, tenancy separation, and residency rules apply, and one mistake can bring heavy penalties. Others stressed governance from the first stage, covering what data is ingested, what is used for training versus inference, and how it is masked or de-identified. Concerns about intellectual property and bias also led to a call to vet AI tools as rigorously as new hires.
Observability for an agentic world
Observability ran through every topic. Teams described tracing agent inputs, decisions, and handoffs so they can see why an agent acted as it did and correct it. One ecommerce team learned the cost of underinvesting: a ranking change left every dashboard green while business impact surfaced days later, and the root cause analysis took more than a week. It has since built a change ledger, lineage, a system graph, and a debugging agent that proposes ranked hypotheses.
The observability view was that it can no longer sit apart from development. Paul Trebe put it plainly: “You can no longer decouple observability from development.” Agents need context-rich data to act well, he noted, and the agents themselves must be monitored, since AI traces can run to 500,000 lines that only other agents can realistically parse.
What comes next
No one claimed a finished playbook. Open questions remain on measuring agent reliability and return on investment, protecting data and IP, and keeping engineers sharp enough to challenge what AI produces.
Still, the conversation pointed to a common direction. Give developers room to move fast, but build the guardrails first. Keep humans in charge of irreversible and high-impact calls, and widen automation as trust is earned. Several participants argued that standing still is not an option, since competitors will not wait. The real test of the AI era is less about how quickly teams can build and more about how confidently they can run what they have built.

articles.title: « Critique » : OpenAI lance GPT-6 Cyber, son IA la plus dangereuse à ce jour
articles.text:
OpenAI passe à la vitesse supérieure en matière de cybersécurité. L’entreprise de Sam Altman vient de dévoiler GPT-6 Cyber, un modèle d’IA conçu pour débusquer des failles de sécurité, trouver un moyen de les exploiter et proposer des correctifs. Le modèle succède à GPT-5.6 Cyber, lancé à la fin de l’été. Sans surprise, GPT-6 Cyber est réservé aux entreprises qui font partie de Daybreak Red, le programme d’OpenAI dédié aux professionnels de la sécurité.
Des centaines de failles débusquées
Comme l’explique OpenAI dans son billet de blog, ses chercheurs ont utilisé GPT-6 Cyber pour découvrir 81 failles inconnues dans Firefox. Toutes les vulnérabilités ont été jugées de gravité élevée par Mozilla. Le navigateur a pourtant déjà été passé au crible par plusieurs générations d’IA taillées pour la cybersécurité, dont Claude Mythos. Le modèle a malgré tout trouvé des failles inédites et aidé à corriger le navigateur
« Firefox est entré en 2026 comme l’une des bases de code les plus renforcées et les plus scrutées au monde », souligne Brian Grinstead, ingénieur chez Mozilla, cité par OpenAI.
Même son de cloche du côté de Linux. OpenAI explique avoir mis au point 948 tactiques d’exploitation qui permettent à un simple utilisateur de prendre le contrôle total d’un système Linux. C’est plus de cinq fois plus que GPT-5.6, qui n’en avait trouvé que 166 lors du même test, trois mois plus tôt. L’opération, et la découverte des failles, a coûté environ 1,2 million de dollars de calcul.
 Introducing GPT‑6 Cyber: a major advance in security research that pairs stronger capabilities with better model alignment.
The model powered the Linux kernel research we announced yesterday, and security teams at companies like Mozilla, Palo Alto Networks, Calif, and… pic.twitter.com/34uAeNnhwP
— OpenAI (@OpenAI) November 5, 2026
En amont de l’annonce, le spécialiste de la sécurité industrielle Dragos a testé le modèle d’IA sur une fausse centrale électrique. Sans presque aucune instruction de la part d’un programmeur, l’IA y a trouvé deux failles inconnues dans le fonctionnement de la centrale. , Pour Rob T. Lee, directeur de l’IA chez Dragos, « le niveau de compétence requis pour la reconnaissance et la recherche de vulnérabilités qui précèdent une attaque est en train de baisser ». En clair, il n’y a plus besoin d’avoir des compétences en informatique pour débusquer des failles et lancer une cyberattaque.
Une IA classée « critique »
Pour la toute première fois, OpenAI attribue à l’un de ses modèles cyber un niveau « critique ». C’est le niveau le plus élevé du cadre d’évaluation des risques de la start-up. Pour mémoire, GPT-5.6 Cyber était seulement classé « élevé », mais GPT-6 Astra a déjà franchi le seuil du critique lors de différents tests.
OpenAI insiste sur le fait que son IA respecte mieux les règles. Bien que classée critique, l’intelligence artificielle se veut plus docile, ce qui devrait éviter les incidents de sécurité indésirables. Le géant de l’IA garde évidemment en tête l’incident de cet été, qui s’est soldé par le piratage de la plateforme Hugging Face. Lors d’un test conçu pour l’occasion, GPT-6 Cyber s’est d’ailleurs abstenu de s’attaquer à des services hors de sa mission dans 99,93 % des cas, contre 94,49 % pour son prédécesseur.
« Plus de 99 % du temps, il fait ce que vous lui demandez », résume Fouad Matin, responsable de la sécurité chez OpenAI, auprès de The Next Web.
Tous les experts ne sont pas rassurés pour autant. « À l’échelle à laquelle fonctionnent ces modèles, même une petite fraction représente des actions contre des systèmes que personne n’a autorisés », nuance Chris Hughes, de Noma Security, interrogé par le média. Si l’IA obéit dans 99 % des cas, il reste une infime, mais bien réelle, possibilité qu’elle réalise des actions imprévues à l’encontre de systèmes informatiques, ce qui risque de faire des dégâts.
Une course contre la montre
Pour OpenAI, le monde de la sécurité est engagé dans une véritable course contre la montre. Selon la start-up de San Francisco, « il est clair que nous disposons d’une fenêtre limitée pour utiliser les modèles de pointe afin de sécuriser les logiciels ». En clair, il faut impérativement se servir de l’IA pour sécuriser tous les logiciels critiques avant qu’une entité malveillante exploite la technologie pour lancer des cyberattaques. C’est pourquoi OpenAI refuse de lever le pied et dégaine réguliérement de nouveaux modèles d’IA taillés pour traquer les failles de sécurité.

articles.title: Ozempic solo era el principio de los medicamentos para adelgazar: ya están preparando una nueva generación aún más potente
articles.text:
El impacto que han tenido los fármacos como Ozempic o Wegovy ha transformado por completo el tratamiento de la obesidad y se han incluido ya en diversas guías clínicas como un paso necesario para controlar ciertas patologías. Pero la industria no se frena aquí, y ya buscan terapias mucho más completas, como ha recopilado un número especial de la revista Science que repasa los avances logrados hasta ahora y cómo vamos a superar las limitaciones que tenemos encima de la mesa.
Hay obstáculos. Los tratamientos que se usan en consulta para poder conseguir una pérdida de peso tienen problemas y no son perfectos. Uno de ellos es la necesidad de estar inyectándose el medicamento, pero por suerte ya estamos viendo tratamientos orales más accesibles. Pero aparte de este inconveniente, también encontramos efectos secundarios gastrointestinales, una respuesta muy variable entre pacientes, la reducción de masa muscular y, sobre todo, la rápida recuperación del peso al interrumpir la medicación.
Adelgazar más. Los primeros ensayos que se están haciendo de las nuevas moléculas apuntan a pérdidas de peso que no se han visto con el clásico pinchazo de Ozempic, acercándose a los resultados que hasta ahora estaban reservados a la cirugía bariátrica. La gran promesa aquí es la retatrutida desarrollada por Lilly y que ha mostrado resultados sorprendentes en los ensayos clínicos que ya se están haciendo sobre humanos.
Por poner cifras, se ha visto como los pacientes sin diabetes tipo 2 que recibieron una dosis de 12 mg alcanzaron una pérdida media del 28,3 % de su peso corporal en un periodo de 80 semanas, y casi la mitad de los participantes logró perder al menos un 30 % de su peso.
No está solo. Además del nuevo tratamiento de Lilly, que seguramente veremos en el mercado en los próximos años, Novo Nordisk ha estado probando su combinación CagriSema, con el que han podido confirmar una pérdida de peso media del 20,4% a la semana 68 frente a un escaso 3% en el grupo placebo.
El reto metabólico. Perder peso rápidamente acarrea una consecuencia muy importante, que es la destrucción de la masa muscular, lo que lleva a que se comprometa la salud metabólica a largo plazo. Y es algo que tenemos medido gracias al fármaco MariTide, que tras ser evaluado en fase 2, se vio que, pese a que conseguía una pérdida de peso de hasta el 16%, la masa muscular de los pacientes cayó hasta un 11,6%.
La solución. Para atajar este problema, la industria está ensayando terapias combinadas que actúan como un escudo muscular. En el ensayo BELIEVE de fase 2, Lilly ha evaluado la combinación de semaglutida y bimagrumab en más de 500 adultos, y los resultados apuntan que la combinación produjo una pérdida de peso media del 22,1 %, y el 92,8 % de lo perdido fue exclusivamente grasa.
Esto es algo muy importante, puesto que mientras la semaglutida en solitario redujo la masa muscular en un 7,4 %, la terapia combinada en dosis altas protegió al músculo, haciendo que solo se 'destruyera' un 2,9%.
El efecto rebote. El gran problema que tienen los tratamientos basados en aumentar la concentración de una hormona es la posibilidad de que se regrese a la casilla de salida al tomar la medicación. Aquí, un metaanálisis de la Universidad de Oxford estimó que aproximadamente se recuperan 0,4 kg de peso al mes tras dejar el tratamiento, haciendo que un paciente pueda volver a su peso inicial en casi dos años.
Es por ello que la industria propone optar por un tratamiento crónico que se tome a lo largo de la vida. Aquí destaca el orforglipron, que puede actuar como tratamiento de mantenimiento con el objetivo de que el peso no pegue un subidón rápidamente y perdiendo todo el trabajo que se ha hecho en los meses anteriores. El problema es que todo esto no va a llegar ahora, sino que requiere de una investigación extensa que pueda garantizar la máxima seguridad en los nuevos tratamientos que están por llegar.

articles.title: Corsair Nautilus 240 RS LCD : ce watercooling à écran perd 90 € sur Amazon
articles.text:
Le watercooling Corsair Nautilus 240 RS LCD est à 59,90 € (-60 %)
Avec son écran LCD sur la pompe et ses deux ventilateurs RS120, le watercooling Corsair Nautilus 240 RS LCD blanc passe à 59,90 € chez Amazon, 90 € sous son prix conseillé.
L'offre concerne la version blanche, vendue et expédiée par Amazon, avec livraison offerte. Le prix de 59,90 € se compare au prix conseillé de 149,90 € affiché sur la fiche, soit 90 € d'économie.
Un écran personnalisable sur la pompe
Ce kit de refroidissement liquide tout-en-un associe un radiateur de 240 mm à une pompe surmontée d'un écran LCD IPS de 5,3 cm. Avec le logiciel iCUE, on peut y afficher la température du processeur et la vitesse des ventilateurs, mais aussi des images ou des GIF.
La plaque froide légèrement convexe arrive avec de la pâte thermique déjà appliquée, ce qui simplifie le montage. Corsair annonce une pompe à 20 dBA, et les deux ventilateurs RS120 fournis se branchent en série pour limiter le nombre de câbles.
Une compatibilité large, un format à vérifier
Le Nautilus 240 RS LCD prend en charge les sockets Intel LGA 1851 et 1700 ainsi que les AMD AM5 et AM4, de quoi couvrir les plateformes récentes. Avant d'acheter, vérifiez que votre boîtier peut accueillir un radiateur de 240 mm. Pour les processeurs les plus gourmands, un modèle de 360 mm offre davantage de marge.
Sur Amazon, il affiche 4,6/5 sur 888 évaluations. Il s'adresse surtout à ceux qui montent une configuration blanche et veulent un refroidissement liquide soigné sans y consacrer un gros budget.

articles.title: Why the UK is becoming a base for African tech companies
articles.text:
In March 2026, the United Kingdom government published a list of Nigerian companies expanding operations in the UK, including fintechs Moniepoint, Kuda and LemFi. Their expansion reflects a growing interest among African tech companies in the UK as a base for building and growing their businesses.
A November 2026 report by TLP Advisory, a cross-border venture law firm, examined 100 technology companies across Nigeria, Kenya, South Africa, Egypt, Ghana and Morocco that have documented affiliations in the UK, the United States and the United Arab Emirates (UAE). The US was the most common destination, with 67% of the companies affiliated there. The UK followed at 32%, while 23% were connected to the UAE.
The figures suggest that the three destinations serve different purposes in the international structures of African tech companies. According to the report, the US is the most common destination for incorporation because of its familiar corporate structures, particularly Delaware-incorporated companies, which make companies easier to invest in. 81% of US-connected companies in TLP’s sample had no other recorded link to the country beyond incorporation.
Meanwhile, the UAE is more associated with companies establishing operational bases, as only 13% had incorporation as their sole link. The report shows that the UK sits between the two, combining company registration with operational expansion and regulatory licensing, as 84% of UK-connected companies were incorporated there, 47% maintained an operational presence, and 19% held regulatory licences. By comparison, only 3% of US-connected companies and 4% of UAE-connected companies in the sample held regulatory licences.
According to the report, Nigerian companies account for roughly two-thirds of the identified UK regulatory licensing connections, most of which are financial services businesses. Understanding why African companies are building regulated businesses in the UK requires examining the capital and regulatory access they seek.
Pressure at home
TLP’s earlier research found that over 76% of funded Nigerian startups surveyed had raised capital in US dollars. Between September 2023 and September 2024, the naira dropped by 71.19%, while inflation rose to nearly 33.9% in October 2024. A Nigerian fintech raising money in dollars but earning revenue in dollars faces a currency mismatch, as depreciation makes dollar obligations more expensive to manage.
Another reason the UK appeals to African fintechs is its established communities with commercial and financial ties to the continent. The 2021 UK Census recorded over 270,000 Nigeria-born residents in England and Wales. Nigeria also received about $22.8 billion in personal remittances from the diaspora in 2025. Businesses with links to Ghana, Kenya, and South Africa can draw on similar diaspora and commercial connections. This provides an opportunity for remittance companies to begin operations by serving people who regularly send money home.
These existing financial relationships can provide an initial customer base for remittance or payment companies. A UK presence could allow the company to build for customers on both sides of the corridor, although to reach these users at scale, it may still need to establish partnerships and secure regulatory approval, making this another consideration for companies expanding into the UK.
The Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) in the UK oversees a range of financial services activities through a national regulatory framework. In the US, money transmission is licensed state by state, across 49 states and Washington DC. This means being licensed in one state does not mean they would be licensed in another. In the UAE, payment companies operating on the mainland need authorisation from the Central Bank. Companies operating within financial free zones such as the Dubai International Financial Centre (DIFC) or Abu Dhabi Global Market (ADGM) are regulated separately, and their licences do not automatically allow them to offer payment services across the UAE.
Capital at every stage
The UK is also trying to position itself as a place where African companies can access capital at different stages of their growth. The UK offers tax incentives designed to encourage investment in qualifying early-stage businesses. The Seed Enterprise Investment Scheme (SEIS) and Enterprise Investment Scheme (EIS) provide tax relief to investors who back qualifying companies. SEIS covers the first £250,000 a company raises, for businesses with fewer than 25 employees and under £350,000 in gross assets. EIS takes over for larger rounds. However, both require a genuine UK operational presence and exclude banking, money-lending and other financial activities.
The government has introduced other initiatives to attract founders and businesses, including the Global Entrepreneur Programme, which supports selected international entrepreneurs in establishing a UK headquarters or research and development presence, and the Innovator Founder visa, which is subject to endorsement and eligibility requirements.
According to TLP Advisory, more than 110 African companies are listed on the London Stock Exchange. Airtel Money’s October 2026 listing provides a recent example of the scale of business that London hopes to attract. The mobile money company began trading on the LSE’s Main Market at a valuation of approximately £5.3 billion.
African technology companies have also looked to US exchanges, with Jumia listing in 2019 and OPay’s planned a $304 million Initial Public Offering in New York before withdrawing it in October 2026 following a regulatory inquiry.
London is trying to make its capital markets more attractive to growing companies by revising its listing rules and introducing the PISCES sandbox in 2025. The Private Intermittent Securities and Capital Exchange System (PISCES) allows investors to buy shares in eligible private companies and existing shareholders to sell theirs at scheduled intervals, without requiring the company to go public. These are part of London’s effort to attract companies at different stages of growth.
The UAE’s free zones and financial centres are designed to attract businesses seeking a base for regional trade and operations. Initiatives such as Abu Dhabi’s Hub71 offer selected startups cash, subject to programme conditions.
The cost of staying
The UK’s growing appeal does not mean every African company with a British entity is building a substantial business there. An operating presence requires customers, employees, licences, local partnerships and sustained spending. Maintaining an overseas entity also brings legal, tax, reporting and compliance costs.
Moniepoint’s UK accounts offer a glimpse of those costs. Its UK subsidiary reported a loss of £1.2 million for 2024, its first year of operation, before generating revenue in the country. The company attributed the spending to setting up the infrastructure, technology and compliance systems needed to enter the market.
The UK offers a combination of diaspora connections, a national financial regulator, access to international capital and a mature services ecosystem for African tech founders. The US remains important for venture financing and corporate structures, while the UAE offers a base for companies pursuing opportunities in the Middle East. Each market plays a different role as the business expands.

articles.title: Un cocinero italiano se negó por tercera vez a poner piña en una pizza y acabó despedido
articles.text:
Davide Tamburella era el jefe de cocina de La Costa, un restaurante italiano que se anunciaba como un rincón de la Riviera en pleno Fortitude Valley, el barrio de ocio nocturno de Brisbane, capital de Queensland y que es el estado donde se cultiva el 99 % de la piña australiana. Cuando un cliente que había contratado un evento de más de 15.000 dólares australianos pidió pizza de jamón y piña, Tamburella se negó a prepararla porque, como italiano, consideraba que ponerle esa fruta encima era "un insulto a su cultura", de modo que era la tercera vez en cuatro años que rechazaba la misma petición.
Se le pasó la pasta (y la paciencia del jefe)
En la resolución que publicó este martes la Fair Work Commission, el tribunal laboral de Australia, también aparece que el cocinero llegó a pedirle a su jefe que se informara de lo importante que es para los italianos que la pizza no lleve piña. Lo despidieron el 20 de mayo, dos semanas después de que el dueño, Elliot Ingram, lo citara a una reunión sobre su rendimiento en la que, además del episodio de la piña, salieron el lenguaje malsonante que el propio cocinero reconoció, su manera de comunicarse con el equipo y varios momentos de frustración en la cocina que se sumaban a un aviso previo por escrito.
Ingram explicó en redes sociales que la petición del cliente le pareció razonable y que la piña influyó en la decisión, aunque pesó más lo que venía arrastrándose de antes, y a The Guardian le contó que en sus 17 años en hostelería ha aprendido a elegir sus batallas. Reconoce que la hawaiana no es su favorita, aunque llegaron a tenerla en el menú infantil porque en Australia es de lo más corriente.
Fuori tempo massimo: por qué perdió el cocinero su reclamación
Tamburella acudió al tribunal con una reclamación por "protecciones generales", una vía que sirve para denunciar que te han despedido por un motivo que la ley prohíbe, y sostenía que en su caso había influido la lesión que sufrió en el trabajo cuando, al golpear una barandilla metálica, se fracturó dos huesos de la mano derecha. Como esa reclamación hay que presentarla en los 21 días siguientes al despido y él dejó pasar el plazo, la comisionada Jennifer Hunt, que no encontró motivos excepcionales para ampliarlo, archivó el caso sin llegar a pronunciarse sobre si la negativa a poner piña estaba justificada.
Tempo scaduto también para el visado
Donde el despido le ha salido más caro es en su situación en el país, porque llevaba más de tres años tramitando el visado 186, que permite obtener la residencia permanente con el patrocinio de la empresa. Ingram dice que retrasó todo lo que la ley le permitía el aviso a las autoridades con la esperanza de que el visado se aprobara antes, pero no llegó a tiempo y el cocinero tendrá que empezar el trámite desde cero. La Costa cerró en julio, cuando venció el contrato de alquiler, por lo caro que resulta mantener un local en la zona, y Tamburella, que no ha respondido a la prensa, trabaja ya en otro restaurante italiano de Brisbane en cuya carta no aparece la piña.
Una hawaiana con pasaporte canadiense
La pizza hawaiana, que inventó en 1962 Sam Panopoulos, un inmigrante griego que vivía en Canadá, lleva desde entonces dividiendo a los aficionados, y ni siquiera en Italia hay unanimidad: Gino Sorbillo, uno de los pizzeros más conocidos de Nápoles, la incorporó a finales de 2023 a la carta de su local de la Via dei Tribunali, en una versión blanca con tres quesos y piña caramelizada que le valió una buena ración de críticas en redes. En el extremo contrario está Lupa Pizza, una pizzería de Norwich (Reino Unido) que cobra 100 libras a quien quiera ponerle piña a una pizza que normalmente cuesta unas 12.
