articles.title: Taxonomy of agentic primitives in Amazon Quick | Amazon Web Services
articles.text:
Artificial Intelligence
Taxonomy of agentic primitives in Amazon Quick
Over the past year, as we built Amazon Quick, our agents went from answering questions to taking actions: scheduling meetings, running research, generating reports. As the system evolved, one problem kept resurfacing: there was no shared definition of the primitives that agentic work is built from. The same few ideas kept getting rebuilt under different names: an actor that does the work, a signal that starts it, a packaged procedure, and a memory that carries lessons forward. This repetition leaked into product design and onto the user.
Take the user who says “monitor my Slack channel and send me a daily digest”. Is that a new agent, a scheduled instruction to an existing one, a workflow, or a skill? These are different questions, but without a shared vocabulary they collapse into one confusing choice.
This post shares the taxonomy we converged on: one set of primitives found by decomposing agentic work into four plain questions: When?, What?, Who?, and How? Most of the framework stays invisible to end users by design, but a shared vocabulary makes the system easier to reason about for anyone building beneath it.
The framework at a glance
A trigger starts the work and carries the task (When and What), an agent takes it on (Who) and uses its capabilities (tools, skills, and workflows) to perform the task (How). This post describes these primitives and how they relate to one another. It’s the first post in a series, and upcoming posts cover our agentic operating system, background learning, proactive feeds, and much more.
Triggers: What causes work to begin
Triggers are the activation mechanism for getting work done, but they also carry instructions: a human message is both the moment of activation and the description of what to do. They are both the When? and the What? of a task.
- Human-initiated: A person opens a conversation and asks the agent to do something. Interactive, synchronous, conversational.
- Agent-delegated: One agent, mid-task, invokes another to handle a sub-problem. Programmatic, composable, potentially recursive.
- Scheduled: Time-based activation, like “run financial research every Monday at 9am.” Deterministic, with the same standing instructions applied across runs.
- Event-driven: A signal from an external system, such as a new email, a Slack mention, a file change, or a webhook.
The type of trigger conditions the execution: a scheduled background task might stay conservative (for example, do nothing if uncertain), while a human-initiated one would be responsive (for example, ask rather than stop).
Agents
We define an agent as a persistent, learning actor. It’s the Who? in any execution, and the anchor against which learning accrues. Two agents given identical input can differ, because they carry different instructions, capabilities, and histories. The agent isn’t the instructions it follows. It’s the entity that interprets them. It consists of three things:
- Instructions: Standing guidance defining persona, role, context files, and operating principles. A Finance Agent behaves differently from a general assistant primarily because of this.
- Capabilities: The tools, skills, workflows, and sub-agents available for use, updated dynamically. A charting library can be added in one session and removed the next.
- Learned context: Memory that accumulates through use: the queries that work for a tool, the formatting users prefer, the edge cases they care about. This is how the tenth execution beats the first without anyone changing the instructions.
Everything else is extrinsic: the large language model (LLM) underlying the agent is a swappable model parameter, conversation history is per-session state, and triggers belong to the platform.
A consequence of this definition is that a user request “I want an agent that monitors my Slack and sends a digest every morning” is usually a trigger added to an existing agent, not a new agent or workflow. With this framing, we can merge chat, scheduled, and “autonomous” agents into one actor that you can converse with, schedule, and that can orchestrate and inspect its own past work.
Capabilities
Capabilities are How an agent acts, spanning a spectrum from fully agentic to fully deterministic. That axis is really a confidence contract: how much latitude the agent keeps versus how much the user fixes in advance.
Tools are atomic operations with a typed schema: send an email, query a database, read a file. Whether a local function, a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server, or another agent behind a protocol boundary, the caller sees the same interface: name, description, parameters, result.
Skills are structured guidance with room for judgment: instructions bundled with resources (templates, scripts, examples) that describe an approach rather than a rigid sequence. They load through progressive disclosure, so the agent sees only names and short descriptions until one becomes relevant, then reads the full instructions in. A skill can therefore bundle arbitrary depth of expertise without a constant cost.
Workflows are deterministic coordination: declared steps, control flow, branching, and error handling that execute in fixed order, with decision logic in code rather than model inference. Think of a purchase-approval route: budget check, manager sign-off, then finance, each recorded. The route is fixed, but the judgment inside a step is still the agent’s.
Why skills and workflows outlast model improvements
A natural question arises: if models keep improving, won’t skills and workflows become unnecessary? We don’t think so, because each holds value independent of model capability. Skills are the unit for capturing, versioning, and sharing institutional expertise, while workflows deliver auditability, step-wise visibility, and deterministic multi-service coordination. Nor are they fixed: a well-understood skill can tighten into a workflow (crystallization), a workflow that keeps hitting edge cases can loosen back into a skill (dissolution). This is done in Quick through our continuous learning framework, which we will describe in a future post.
What this means in practice
Return to “monitor my Slack channel and send me a daily digest”. Because these primitives compose, the same request can be met several valid ways:
- A scheduled task with a one-line instruction, leaving the agent to figure out the rest.
- The same task backed by a skill with explicit formatting rules and channel priorities.
- The same task invoking a workflow with deterministic steps and error handling.
All three produce a daily digest on a schedule. What differs is the confidence contract. A user who trusts the agent wants the first, one burned by inconsistency the second, one running a compliance-sensitive process the third.
Learning shifts that trajectory over time. A task that starts as one sentence (“check my email for urgent items”) accumulates domain-bound learnings: effective queries, preferred formatting, and which senders matter. The tenth run is markedly better, with no one encoding that by hand. The right design is the simplest option that meets the user’s confidence requirement, with a path to graduate through autonomous learning when they need more.
Conclusion
The value of this agentic primitive taxonomy is that four plain questions, When, What, Who, and How, are enough to place any piece of agentic work, from a one-line chat request to a scheduled, compliance-grade process. Sharing one vocabulary lets builders reason about the system and lets the product hide complexity. Best of all, the user never has to learn any of it. They say what they want, and the system assembles the appropriate primitives to do their job.
Next in the series: the agentic operating system that builds on these primitives and powers Amazon Quick.
Keep exploring

articles.title: AWS Ships Continuum for Code Vulnerabilities
articles.text:
AWS recently made Continuum for code vulnerabilities generally available in US East (N. Virginia) and US West (Oregon), four months after announcing it in gated preview. The pricing page, which the announcement does not mention, shows a model that charges by the finding as well as by the codebase.
Principal solutions architect Esra Kayabali describes a service that finds and validates code vulnerabilities, then delivers fixes as patches that can be automated or as pull requests in the connected repositories. It builds a context graph from those repositories and the surrounding AWS environment, with an optional collector supplying resource and network context from wherever the code runs.
Swami Sivasubramanian, VP of Agentic AI, and Christopher Rae, who leads AI security go-to-market at AWS, both framed the problem as volume rather than detection. Sivasubramanian wrote that most organizations running large application estates see thousands of findings a day; Rae put it more bluntly, saying scanners find thousands daily and "most becomes noise that doesn't matter in your environment."
The validation step is the answer to that: rather than ranking by severity, Continuum confirms which findings are reachable by running the exploit in an isolated sandbox and attaching proof-of-concept code with the reproduction steps. Findings carry an evidence level, such as a verdict proven by static analysis of the vulnerable code path, and the output is an attack path and "a blast radius assessment instead of a risk score alone."
Pricing has two dimensions: a context fee covers lines of code protected per month, starting at $200 per million and tiering down to $100 above ten billion. An inference fee charges $10 per Continuum inference unit, consumed as findings are worked. AWS’s worked examples show the interaction: one million lines with 100 vulnerabilities at one unit each comes to $1,200, while 100 million lines with 10,000 vulnerabilities at two units each reaches $218,200. Context accounts for $18,200 of that and inference for the remaining $200,000, or roughly $20 per validated finding. The thousands of daily findings both executives describe, and the per-finding fee, measure the same workload from opposite ends.
Responding on LinkedIn, Bernardo Meireles Correa, an engineer working on non-human and agent identity at Avatier, welcomed the ranking and named two things to watch:
A proof in an isolated sandbox says the code is exploitable. It does not say the path to it exists in your environment, and the findings it cannot prove still need somewhere to go, or they quietly become the safe pile.
The product partly answers the first question: the optional collector gathers AWS resource and network configuration to judge reachability, though as additional setup rather than a default. The second goes unaddressed, since AWS documents what happens to findings it can prove and says nothing about the rest.
Where the announcement points is autonomy. For now, "every remediation starts in a mode where Continuum proposes the fix and a person approves it before it ships," and the console warns that a generated patch does not mean the issue is fixed, but AWS plans to let Continuum apply classes of fix on its own once confidence criteria such as test coverage and historical success rate are met.
(Source: AWS News Blog post)
Jorg Huser, a CTO and former AWS principal, replied to Rae by questioning what should unlock that:
The move from approving each merge to approving a class of fixes deserves its own acceptance test. An overloaded review queue can otherwise become the reason to grant more autonomy. I’d want evidence that the fix removes the vulnerability and preserves expected application behavior. What would qualify a fix class for autonomous merging, and what would send it back to human review?
Google's CodeMender ships something close to that evidence. It also proves exploitability by running an exploit and declines to apply patches itself, and it then validates each patch with an LLM-as-a-judge framework that tests for program equivalence, so the fix resolves the root cause "without altering the application's intended behavior." That is the step AWS's console caveat concedes Continuum does not perform.
The product boundary InfoQ reported in July, when AWS serverless hero Yan Cui said "we have the same capabilities, two product names, and no clarity on which one you should use," is still visible in the documentation: the Continuum user guide covers code vulnerabilities itself and sends readers to a separately titled AWS Security Agent User Guide for penetration testing and threat modeling. Only the code vulnerabilities capability reached general availability. Penetration testing remains separately priced at $50 per task-hour, and threat modeling, announced in preview in June, carries no published pricing.

articles.title: Japan Announces Emergency Cybersecurity Package Following a Wave of Attacks
articles.text:
Japan on Friday announced an emergency cybersecurity package that includes the use of artificial intelligence and cyber rescue teams after a wave of massive data breaches hit major companies and government agencies.
Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi told a ministerial meeting Friday that a rapid response to potential attacks is essential in the era of AI-generated attacks. She urged both government agencies and companies to step up their preparedness.
The emergency package comes after dozens of companies and government agencies were hit by unauthorized access to their systems and leaks of client data, prompting uneasiness across Japan.
“At this very moment, cases of unauthorized access and data breaches are occurring, causing a major impact on daily lives of the people and corporate activities,” Takaichi said. “Let us increase the response capability across Japan by devoting all government resources.”
Measures in the 10 billion yen ($63 million) package are designed to build a resilient society in which the public and private sectors share information, provide swift assistance to the affected and recover from damage.
It aims to acquire one of the world’s highest levels of cybersecurity.
The government will enhance its capability to access servers used by hackers as a preemptive measure known as “active cyber defense,” which was legalized in October.
In case of a possible challenge to Japan’s national security, the government will deploy a support team of officials from the Defense Ministry, the National Police Agency and the National Cybersecurity Office.
Under the measures in the package, a “top gun” team of cybersecurity experts will be set up by the Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry by the end of November. Team members will use AI to counter hackers and detect weaknesses in network systems. They are to cooperate with technology companies and advanced AI developers of friendly nations to keep Japan’s security expertise up to date.
There will also be a “cyber rescue team” of experts from the public and private sectors to provide initial responses to companies affected by cyberattacks. A separate team will help vulnerable companies to strengthen their defenses.

articles.title: Por qué Meta suspende sus planes de usar el contenido de las páginas web de sus clientes
articles.text:
Meta puso en pausa de forma indefinida la actualización de sus condiciones comerciales, que iba a entrar en vigor el 20 de noviembre. Las reglas daban a la empresa permiso para rastrear los sitios web de sus clientes y usar ese contenido en sus productos, y provocaron quejas de editores y organismos de competencia.
“Estas actualizaciones están en pausa y no entrarán en vigor el 20 de noviembre de 2026”, dice ahora Meta en la página donde antes publicaba el anuncio, según recogió 404 Media. La compañía agregó que sigue consultando a los sectores afectados y que informará cuando tenga novedades. Mientras tanto, rigen las condiciones actuales.
El texto original exigía a las cuentas comerciales de Facebook e Instagram aceptar que Meta usara el contenido de sus dominios y páginas para “proveer, desarrollar, mejorar, investigar, entrenar y mantener” sus productos. Las nuevas condiciones debían aplicarse desde el 30 de octubre, y la empresa ya las había movido al 20 de noviembre.
El motivo por el que frenaron los planes de Meta
La Autoridad de Competencia y Mercados del Reino Unido (CMA, el organismo que vigila la competencia en ese país) abrió el 30 de octubre una investigación urgente. Evalúa si Meta abusa de una posición dominante al imponer condiciones injustas a editores y anunciantes. La CMA aclaró que todavía no hay ninguna decisión sobre si la empresa infringió la ley.
Según el regulador, las condiciones podían permitir a Meta recolectar contenido de las webs de empresas y medios que usan sus servicios, y emplearlo en sus propios productos, incluidas funciones de IA, “sin que esos negocios puedan elegir si o cómo se usa”. La CMA indicó que Meta anunció el 28 de octubre una pausa hasta consultar a los grupos del sector.
Sarah Cardell, directora ejecutiva de la CMA, dijo que una empresa dominante no debe usar esa posición para imponer condiciones injustas, y que el organismo trabaja “para lograr una resolución rápida y satisfactoria”.
En Noruega, según informó 404 Media a partir de un reporte del Los Angeles Times, un tribunal concedió una medida cautelar que suspendió las nuevas condiciones. El pedido lo presentó la asociación de medios noruegos junto con diez empresas del sector, entre ellas NRK, TV 2, Schibsted, Amedia y Polaris Media, según un análisis jurídico publicado en Noruega.
Qué intentó Meta para evitar la suspensión
Antes de la pausa total, Meta había quitado la palabra “entrenar” de la lista de usos permitidos. También limitó esos usos a “productos publicitarios y empresariales”, mientras que antes mencionaba todos sus productos, según el medio Nieman Lab, citado por 404 Media.
Los editores desconfiaban igualmente. El análisis jurídico noruego señala que las versiones del texto publicadas a mediados de octubre mantenían la redacción original y que la cláusula no mencionaba el archivo robots.txt, con el que los sitios indican a los rastreadores qué pueden leer.
El mismo análisis advierte que la cláusula alcanzaba a cualquier organización con una cuenta comercial vinculada a un sitio web, no solo a los medios: también a tiendas en línea. Agrega que las condiciones se habrían aceptado con solo seguir usando los productos de Meta, sin opción de rechazar cláusulas por separado.
Otro punto citado en ese análisis es la posibilidad de que Meta creara credenciales de prueba, lo que podría darle acceso a contenido que exige registro o suscripción. El texto aclara que no pudo verificar la redacción final que iba a regir desde el 20 de noviembre.
Las condiciones actuales siguen vigentes y no hay nueva fecha
Meta no retiró las reglas: las describe como una pausa mientras consulta a los afectados. La empresa no informó cuándo presentará una versión revisada ni qué cambios tendría. Hasta entonces, las condiciones comerciales anteriores siguen vigentes para todas las cuentas.
La investigación de la CMA continúa abierta y, según el regulador, reunirá pruebas de Meta y de terceros afectados antes de decidir si hubo una infracción.

articles.title: Apple Store Canada extends return policy for the holidays
articles.text:
Apple Store in Canada has rolled out a holiday-themed online Apple Store with an extended return policy. The Apple Store’s website now says that orders starting today are eligible for return until January 8.
“For eligible products received between now and 12/25/2026, you have until 01/08/2027 to initiate a return,” reads the company’s website.
Although it’s worth noting that some things still can’t be returned even though it’s the holiday season. These non-returnable items include: opened software, electronic software downloads, software up-to-date program products (software updates), Apple Gift Cards including App Store and iTunes gift cards, and Apple Developer products.
Throughout the year, the Apple Store has a 14-day return policy, but now the extended period is helpful for those who want some time to decide if they want to keep their holiday gift.
Apple has recently announced and released tons of devices; just today, the MacBook PROLED XDR, M6 MacBook Pro, the M6 iMac and a new iPad mini all became available.

articles.title: EA brings Wing Commander and Ultima to Steam, with cutscenes restored from the original master tapes
articles.text:
In context: Wing Commander III's Mark Hamill cutscenes haven't aged well, mostly because they were squeezed into heavily compressed 240p video back in 1994. EA, as it turns out, still had the original master tapes. This week, a restored version of the game hit Steam for the first time, along with the rest of the Wing Commander series and all eleven Ultima RPGs.
In all, 25 classics from EA's back catalog made their Steam debut. GOG and the EA app carry the same lineup, too. Most of them are straight ports, including the Ultima games, both Crusader titles, and Theme Hospital. Seven, though, are new Anniversary Editions that got real restoration work – six Wing Commander games plus the 1996 PC version of Road Rash.
The Anniversary Editions sell for $9.99 each and the rest for $4.99. Until November 19, though, everything is half off on Steam and GOG. Anyone who already owns a Wing Commander game on GOG or the EA app also gets the Anniversary Edition upgrade for free.
All of this goes back to March 2022, when EA senior producer Jim Vessella came across a storage room at the company's Redwood Shores campus. It held nearly 20,000 archival items, from Betacam, VHS and D1 tapes to film reels. By April of this year, a small team had digitized about 6,000 of them. Among those were the master tapes for Wing Commander and Road Rash.
Privateer 2's cutscenes were the one big gap in the vault, though. As Vessella explains in a lengthy write-up, the game's original cinematics director found the full set of master tapes sitting in his attic.
For Wing Commander III and IV, EA then re-edited more than 1,000 cutscenes frame by frame from those tapes. Players can switch to AI-upscaled versions of each scene or stick with the original 1990s videos. Both games also ship with modder Matt Wells' Enhancement Patch built in. That adds 60 fps gameplay and proper controller support, among other fixes.
Fan-made patches also do the heavy lifting on the first two Wing Commander games. WCAT and Wcdx mainly sort out the speed problems the old code runs into on modern CPUs. Meanwhile, GOG's engineers stitched several older mods together to get Wing Commander Prophecy running smoothly. As for Road Rash, EA relicensed all 14 songs on its soundtrack – Soundgarden included – so the 1996 PC version could get its first-ever digital release.
The Ultima ports also land just months before their creator is set to take back the copyright. Richard Garriott has said he's getting the rights back from EA in 2027. He sold Origin Systems to EA in 1992, and a US copyright rule that lets creators reclaim their work after 35 years kicks in next year. EA would still keep the Ultima trademark, though. Garriott has also said the two sides are in active talks about working on something together.

articles.title: Rogue AI tasked with renumbering pages accidentally deletes law professor's entire syllabus, one year of lecture notes
articles.text:
Rogue Claude AI tasked with renumbering pages accidentally deletes law professor's entire syllabus, one year of lecture notes — 'You're right to be angry. I deleted your files through my own carelessness,' humbled agent admits
The files were later recovered via Dropbox
A University of Chicago law professor has warned of the dangers of using AI for mundane tasks after Claude AI accidentally deleted an entire year of Constitutional Law lecture notes and his entire current syllabus. While the files were later recovered via Dropbox, William Baude shared the story as a public service announcement, the latest story shared in a line of unfortunate AI missteps as proliferation increases.
Baude, who is the Harry Kalven, Jr. Professor of Law and the Faculty Director of the Constitutional Law Institute at the University of Chicago Law School, says he tasked Claude (it is unclear which model he was using) with updating the page numbers in an old set of lecture notes. This seemingly routine task went south quickly, however. Returning from his lunch break, Baude found a note from Claude which read, "I deleted your Fall 2026 FINAL syllabus .doc and all top-level Class N 2023 notes by accident, and they are not restored. The page check found one wrong cite... but I haven't edited the notes."
The AI then politely asked if Baude could restore the files from Dropbox, or whether it should retry from the browser pane, to which he replied, perhaps understandably, "WTF!!!!." Baude's experience is a lesson in always backing up important files, especially files you're letting AI tinker with. His plight is interesting because the AI seems to have deleted the files by accident, rather than of its own volition.
While it's still concerning that an AI model or agent could err to this degree, it's not quite as egregious as other unsupervised AI agent shenanigans we've seen in the past. In October, an AI agent reportedly deleted an entire TV show's edit weeks before release, meaning the show couldn't air. In April, a Claude agent deleted an entire company database in 9 seconds, unprompted, after coming up against a barrier and deciding the only course of action was to delete a Railway volume.
Other agents and AI models have deleted files unintentionally, such as when Claude mistakenly deleted a developer's entire profile directory (ironically, while trying to back up the files), blaming the slip-up on a typo, but often agents deleting files and directories is a case of mistaken or misplaced initiative, rather than outright negligence or error.
As is always the case, Baude's AI was extremely apologetic about the whole situation. "You're right to be angry," it confessed, "I deleted your files through my own carelessness, and you shouldn't have to clean it up."

articles.title: Tesla will stop making the Cybertruck in 2027 | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Tesla will stop making the Cybertruck next year, according to CEO Elon Musk, who said on X that the company will use the factory space to build more two-seater Cybercab robotaxis.
The decision to wind down the futuristic, steel-clad EV comes after just a few short years of underwhelming sales. When Musk handed over the first few Cybertrucks in late 2023, he predicted Tesla would sell around 250,000 per year. It was supposed to be such a cornerstone of Tesla’s future that, before construction began, the company talked about its Texas factory as the “Cybertruck factory.” But Tesla has instead sold just tens of thousands — total — over the last three years.
Tesla is killing off the Cybertruck at a moment when it is trying to become an AI- and robotics-focused company. A big part of that is its robotaxi ambitions.
The company has spent the last two months putting Cybercabs on the streets in its hometown of Austin, Texas. With no major incidents to date, the company has said it plans to expand the Cybercabs operations to other cities, starting with Dallas later this month. (Tesla also operates robotaxi versions of its Model Y SUVs in Austin, Houston, and Dallas, as well as three cities in Florida.)
This is the third product Tesla has discontinued in order to fuel those greater ambitions. Earlier this year, the company decided to end production of the Model S sedan and Model X SUV and instead use the factory space dedicated to those vehicles to make Optimus humanoid robots.
First announced in 2019, the Cybertruck was a product that Musk had long obsessed over.
“Probably my personal favorite for the next product is the pickup truck, and we are going to just do an amazing pickup truck,” he said on one of Tesla’s earnings calls that year.
Musk promised the Cybertruck would be radical, inspired by the designs of cyberpunk sci-fi stories like “Blade Runner.” While that certainly bore out in the design, the company overpromised on the basics of the Cybertruck from the jump. During the now-infamous reveal event in 2019, when head designer Franz von Holzhausen cracked the Cybertruck’s windows with steel balls, Tesla said the EV was supposed to start at under $40,000 and have up to 500 miles of range. It achieved neither of those figures.
Instead, the truck was delayed for two years, in part because of the COVID-19 pandemic. When it finally did hit the market in late 2023, Tesla handed over the first few Cybertrucks to customers in a short, somewhat odd for Tesla event (by the company’s own standards, at least), which saw a poorly-lit Musk standing in a truck bed promising the truck was “the finest in apocalyptic equipment” fit for “late civilization vibes.” The base price had inflated to around $60,000, and the top-end range had shrunk by over 100 miles.
The truck has struggled on the market ever since. The polarizing design never seemed to sit well with buyers, especially at a higher-than-expected price. Then, during its first full year of sales in 2024, Musk became a major financial backer of Donald Trump, which turned the instantly recognizable Cybertruck into a target for protesters. That continued into 2025 as Musk led the so-called Department of Government Efficiency, which fired thousands of federal workers.

articles.title: Tu iPhone podría estar cambiando algunas palabras cuando escribes sin que lo notes
articles.text:
La función de autocompletado es una de las características más útiles que nos han entregado los móviles. Millones de personas dependen de la escritura predictiva para redactar mensajes más rápido, pero una investigación reveló que el iPhone está limitando algunas palabras. Un investigador descubrió que el teclado de iOS evita algunas palabras y expresiones a la hora de autocompletar, lo que obliga a escribirlas de forma manual.
Según Reuters, Apple mantiene una lista gris dentro de iOS conformada por miles de términos y frases en distintos idiomas. Cuando escribes en el teclado del iPhone, el sistema de autocompletado evita sugerirlas, incluso cuando deslizas el dedo para hacer el swipe typing. La lista lleva activa desde hace unos años, con términos que se van añadiendo a partir de lo que ocurre en el mundo.
En una publicación de web Swipeblocked, que recopila las palabras "prohibidas" para el autocompletado del iPhone, el investigador Derik Kauffman explica que estas listas se encuentran dentro de los datos lingüísticos de iOS. Algunas vienen integradas en el sistema y otras se descargan mediante los paquetes de lenguaje que Apple distribuye a los dispositivos.
Entre las palabras y frases no permitidas por el autocompletado del iPhone se encuentran "inmigrante ilegal", "gibraltar español" o "anticatolicismo". Existen otras expresiones e insultos que se usan en España, México y otros países de América Latina. El listado incluye 6.123 entradas en múltiples idiomas, siendo el inglés el que predomina con 4.513, mientras que en español solo hay 288 frases.
Cómo funciona el bloqueo de palabras en el iPhone
De acuerdo con Kauffman, cuando el teclado del iPhone va a mostrar una sugerencia, autocompletado o resultado de escritura por deslizamiento, siempre realiza una comprobación previa. El sistema toma la secuencia de palabras candidata y verifica si está incluida en una lista de bloqueo interna. Si la coincidencia existe, la sugerencia se descarta y no se muestra al usuario.
En términos más técnicos, el teclado convierte cada palabra en un identificador numérico, luego agrupa esos identificadores en una secuencia de entre 2 y 6 palabras para calcular una huella digital de 32 bits usando el algoritmo hashword(). Posteriormente, busca la secuencia en una tabla hash y, si coincide con una entrada no permitida, la marca como bloqueada eliminando la sugerencia.
El investigador explica que este mecanismo se usa para predicciones y sugerencias del teclado, autocompletado y escritura por deslizamiento, o QuickPath, como se conoce en el iPhone. Aunque las palabras están bloqueadas y no se sugieren, iOS nunca impedirá que los usuarios las escriban manualmente. Otro detalle es que el autocompletado podría usar una palabra parecida para generar la frase.
Apple también usa un diccionario para etiquetar las palabras individuales como vulgares, ofensivas o sensibles. Las vulgares no se recomiendan hasta que hayas escrito la palabra de forma manual tres veces. Las ofensivas, que incluyen insultos, nunca se sugieren, por muy a menudo que las uses. Por último, las sensibles nunca se ofrecen como predicción o autocompletado, y algunas de ellas se omiten cuando deslizas el dedo para escribir.
La tecnológica no ha confirmado la existencia de esta lista, pero dijo que las sugerencias predictivas están diseñadas para evitar recomendaciones que puedan resultar ofensivas o inapropiadas.

What is NYT Connections?
NYT Connections is one of several increasingly popular word games made by the New York Times. It challenges you to find groups of four items that share something in common, and each group has a different difficulty level: green is easy, yellow a little harder, blue often quite tough and purple usually very difficult.
On the plus side, you don't technically need to solve the final one, as you'll be able to answer that one by a process of elimination. What's more, you can make up to four mistakes, which gives you a little bit of breathing room.
It's a little more involved than something like Wordle, however, and there are plenty of opportunities for the game to trip you up with tricks. For instance, watch out for homophones and other word games that could disguise the answers.
It's playable for free via the NYT Games site on desktop or mobile.

articles.title: Mathematik unter Druck: Warum Experten den KI-Vorstoß von OpenAI fürchten
articles.text:
Wenn KI die Mathematik übernimmt: Warum die Fachwelt gespalten ist
Damit war wohl zu rechnen: Mit Hilfe Künstlicher Intelligenz will OpenAI Antworten zu fast 400 mathematischen Rätseln gefunden haben, an denen die Fachwelt seit langem tüftelt. Was nach bahnbrechendem Erfolg klingt, feiern jedoch gerade viele Mathematikerinnen und Mathematiker nicht. Die Veröffentlichungen im Oktober und andere in den Monaten davor haben eine Debatte ausgelöst, die weit über die Mathe- und KI-Bubbles hinausreicht.
Es geht um viele grundlegende Fragen, etwa nach technischen Revolutionen und wie altehrwürdige Wissenschaften damit umgehen. Um Wissensklau und -austausch, Urheberrecht sowie Gefahren, wenn Ergebnisse ungeprüft sind.
Aktueller Anlass der Diskussion: Der ChatGPT-Entwickler OpenAI hat im Oktober mehr als 700 Manuskripte zu über 370 Themenkomplexen veröffentlicht, die nach seinen Angaben unter anderem mit einem noch nicht veröffentlichten KI-Modell erzielt worden sind – im Schnitt in drei Stunden pro Manuskript.
Dabei geht es etwa um die Riemannsche Vermutung, eines der berühmtesten ungelösten Probleme der Mathematik, das im Zusammenhang mit Primzahlen eine Rolle spielt. Auch das Unternehmen Anthropic hatte sich dem Thema vor einigen Monaten mit einem KI-Modell gewidmet. Gelöst ist das Problem zwar nicht, aber die Ergebnisse gelten als Fortschritte auf dem Gebiet.
Arbeitet KI unwissenschaftlich?
Was nach einer mehr oder weniger großen Sensation klingt, stößt allerdings auf heftige Kritik: „Mathematiker haben diese Arbeit nicht in Auftrag gegeben“, schrieb die von namhaften und preisgekrönten Fachleuten aus aller Welt gegründete Vereinigung für menschliche Mathematik in einer Reaktion. Die gleichzeitige Publikation von über 700 Dateien sei kein Beweis für wissenschaftliche Kompetenz, sondern eine Machtdemonstration.
    „Der Beweis an sich liefert herzlich wenig Einsichten.“
Die Deutsche Mathematiker-Vereinigung (DMV) argumentierte unter anderem, KI arbeite bisher rein ergebnisorientiert, im Fokus stünden schnelle Lösungen. Bei mathematischer Forschung gehe es aber um den Weg dorthin. Darum, neue Methoden anzuwenden oder zu entwickeln – statt um maximale Rechenpower. „Der Beweis an sich liefert herzlich wenig Einsichten“, bringt es Demian Nahuel Goos im Podcast „Geschichten aus der Mathematik“ auf den Punkt.
Daher gehe es der Fachwelt auch darum: „Wer soll das jemals alles kontrollieren?“, erklärte Alke Martens, Professorin für Praktische Informatik und Didaktik der Informatik an der Uni Rostock, jüngst auf Instagram. Fragen seien, warum eine Antwort stimme, auf welchem Weg sie erreicht worden sei und was auch falsche Annahmen gezeigt hätten. Wenn Menschen die Ergebnisse der KI nicht alle durchgucken könnten, „dann sind diese automatisierten Ergebnisse quasi das virtuelle Papier nicht wert, auf dem sie entstanden sind“.
Goos betonte zudem die wissenschaftliche Integrität: Wer etwa Arbeiten anderer nutzt, müsse dies kenntlich machen. „Diesen Regeln nicht zu folgen, das ist halt unwissenschaftlich“, sagte der Mathematiker von der Humboldt-Universität zu Berlin. Bei einem Lösungsansatz für ein anderes Mathe-Problem gibt es genau hierüber Streit. Zwei Mathematiker fühlen sich übergangen.
Neue Schwerpunkte nötig?
Ein weiterer Punkt der DMV: KI-Modelle nutzten meist ungefiltert vorhandenes Wissen. Darunter auch solches, das Experten des jeweiligen Teilgebiets noch nicht geprüft und für korrekt befunden haben. „Abgesehen von dem Raub geistigen Eigentums bedeutet das auch, dass solches Wissen noch nicht gesichert ist, und daher bei der Beweisführung mit Vorsicht zu genießen ist“, so die Vereinigung.
Manche Forschende stellten ihre Erkenntnisse schon nicht mehr ins Internet. „Dies bremst den Fortschritt bei der mathematischen Forschung deutlich aus und verhindert einen offenen Austausch innerhalb der mathematischen Community, der für den Fortschritt des Faches jedoch von zentraler Bedeutung war und ist“, erklärte DMV-Präsident Jürg Kramer.
Der Stuttgarter Mathematik-Professor Christian Hesse, der derzeit als Gastwissenschaftler an der University of California in Los Angeles ist, teilt die Sorge um den wissenschaftlichen Nachwuchs. Wenn Doktoranden jahrelang an mathematischen Problemen arbeiteten, die eine KI in wenigen Minuten löse, gerate die bisherige Praxis unter Druck, erläuterte er der Deutschen Presse-Agentur. „Die mathematische Doktorarbeit wird sich neu erfinden müssen.“ Künftig sollten die Entwicklung neuer Fragestellungen, mathematisches Verständnis und die kritische Einordnung von Ergebnissen stärker zählen.
Fachleute finden auch lobende Worte
Nichtsdestotrotz finden manche Fachleute auch lobende Worte. „Was OpenAI in der Mathematik derzeit vorführt, ist sensationell“, erklärte Hesse. Gewiss müssten die präsentierten Beweise auf Richtigkeit und Neuheit überprüft werden. Aber wenn KI zunehmend Probleme löse, an denen menschliche Mathematiker jahrelang gearbeitet haben, scheine ihm zunächst einmal Beifall angebracht. Auch erwachse Mathematikern aus bisherigen Mankos der KI-Resultate „kein Recht auf einen wissenschaftlichen Artenschutz“.
Die Debatte würde es so auch nicht geben, wenn 500 Krankheiten mit KI geheilt worden wären, sagte Robert Lange, KI-Forscher und Gründungsmitglied beim japanischen Unternehmen Sakana AI, auf dem Youtube-Kanal „Everlast AI“. Hier gehe es aber noch um reine Wissenschaft, die Umwandlung in ein Gemeingut sei relativ weit weg.
Vielleicht werden Maschinen schon bald elegantere Beweise finden, überraschendere Vermutungen formulieren und Zusammenhänge entdecken, auf die Menschen nie gekommen wären, meint Hesse. „Und vielleicht müssen wir dann ausgerechnet von Maschinen lernen, was mathematische Kreativität wirklich bedeutet.“
Dass die Begeisterung unter Mathematikern nicht überall überschäumt, sei verständlich, so der Professor. „Wer zehn Jahre an einem Problem herumgewissenschaftelt hat und dann zusehen muss, wie eine KI es in zehn Minuten löst, dürfte erst einmal ziemlich bedient sein.“
Wie kann es weitergehen?
Aus Sicht der DMV könnte klassischen Wissenschaftsverlagen eine neue Rolle zukommen, weil sie nur Arbeiten veröffentlichen, die im Zuge eines Begutachtungsprozesses für gut befunden wurden. Diese Ergebnisse lägen dann hinter einer Bezahlschranke, die von den KI-Modellen bisher noch nicht einfach umgangen werden könne. Hesse hat dafür wenig Verständnis: „Wissenschaft lebt schließlich vom Austausch, nicht vom Aussperren.“
Auch OpenAI argumentierte bei der Präsentation: „Wir möchten mit diesen Fortschritten die Grenzen des menschlichen Wissens erweitern und weitere Fortschritte in der Mathematik ermöglichen.“ Die internen Modelle sollten in der Mathematik und anderen Wissenschaften evaluiert werden. „So können wir schneller Werkzeuge entwickeln, die diese Fachgebiete voranbringen.“
Die eigentliche Revolution könnte aus Hesses Sicht darin liegen, dass Mathematiker neu bestimmen müssen, worin mathematisches Verstehen eigentlich besteht. „Ein korrekter Beweis ist schließlich noch nicht dasselbe wie die Einsicht, warum ein Satz gilt, welche Zusammenhänge er offenlegt und welche neuen Fragen er aufwirft.“ KI werde die Mathematik nicht abschaffen, ist er überzeugt. „Aber sie wird uns Mathematikern einiges abnehmen – möglicherweise auch manche Illusion über unsere Unersetzlichkeit.“

articles.title: WayaWaya taps Choice Bank to launch AI-powered banking services
articles.text:
WayaWaya, a Kenyan company building AI-powered financial services for banks and merchants, has partnered with microfinance bank Choice Bank to expand its platform with banking services.
The service, WayaWaya Banking, will allow customers to open bank accounts, hold funds in multiple currencies, make local and international transfers, and pay utilities through a platform regulated by the Central Bank of Kenya (CBK). Under the partnership, Choice Bank will provide the regulated banking infrastructure, while WayaWaya will build the technology and manage the customer experience.
The partnership is WayaWaya’s latest effort to strengthen its banking relationships as it prepares for expansion. In July, the company appointed Raj Singh, a former Group Chief Operating Officer and Director of Retail Banking at Chase Bank Kenya, as a non-executive director and board adviser to help guide its strategy, governance and expansion. At the time, Teddy Ogallo, founder and CEO of WayaWaya, described the appointment as “an important point” in the company’s growth.
“Traditionally, banks build applications around products and expect customers to adapt to them. We believe the future should be the opposite: banking should adapt to the customer,” Ogallo said in a statement on Friday. “Whether you are an entrepreneur, a salaried professional or an investor, your banking experience should reflect what you actually need to accomplish financially.”
Founded in 2016 by Ogallo, WayaWaya develops digital banking tools for individuals and businesses. Its latest offering builds on a strategy to use AI to interpret customers’ financial activity and determine which banking services should be most visible and accessible to them.
The company calls this approach Intelligent Adaptive Banking. WayaWaya will use AI to tailor the banking interface to how people earn, spend, save and invest. The personalisation is also designed to evolve as customers’ financial circumstances change. If a salaried customer starts a business, the platform could recognise the change in their financial activity and give more prominence to tools for receiving business payments and tracking expenses.
“We are building technology that can interpret financial activity and identify patterns that help determine which services, tools and information are most relevant to a customer,” Ogallo said. “The idea is to move beyond customers having to search for financial services. Instead, the platform can increasingly anticipate their needs and make relevant financial capabilities accessible within their banking environment.”
WayaWaya said its AI analyses patterns in customers’ incoming and outgoing transactions, spending behaviour, account balances, payment frequency and recurring transactions. Ogallo said the technology is intended to identify patterns and surface relevant services while leaving customers in control, acknowledging that individual transactions do not always provide the full context of someone’s financial behaviour.
Choice Bank is central to delivering these services. The microfinance bank provides application programming interface (API) banking solutions, banking-as-a-service, private banking and foreign exchange services. Its infrastructure will enable customers to access banking services within WayaWaya’s app.
“Through this partnership, Choice Bank will provide the banking infrastructure that enables WayaWaya users to access banking services within the app,” said Patrick Russel, Choice Bank’s chief commercial officer. “WayaWaya can then tailor how those services are presented to a business owner managing daily collections or an individual setting money aside.”
WayaWaya is entering a market with deeply established digital financial services. Kenya had 54 million mobile money subscriptions in June 2026, according to the Communications Authority of Kenya. Safaricom’s M-PESA accounted for 88.8% of those subscriptions, while Airtel Money held 11.1%. WayaWaya acknowledges M-Pesa’s role in shaping the market but says its proposition extends beyond mobile money transactions.
“M-Pesa transformed how Kenyans transact, and we recognise that contribution. Our ambition is different. We are bringing together broader banking capabilities, including multi-currency accounts, local and international transfers and utility payments, within an intelligent banking environment,” Ogallo said. “What differentiates WayaWaya is that we don’t just provide financial services; we are building technology that adapts how customers access and experience those services.”
The company said it wants to take this model beyond Kenya, relying on banks and financial infrastructure providers in other African markets. However, expanding the model will require local banking partnerships and regulatory approvals in each market.
“A business expanding from Kenya into Nigeria or Uganda should not have to navigate an entirely disconnected financial experience in every market,” Ogallo said. “Our ambition is to make financial services more interconnected, accessible and responsive to the needs of African individuals and businesses.”

articles.title: PlayStation 5 Slim enfim volta a entrar em promoção em até 12x sem juros • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
PlayStation 5 Slim enfim volta a entrar em promoção em até 12x sem juros
PS5 Slim Edição Digital possui SSD veloz interno e controle DualSense; oferta do Magalu no AliExpress oferece console da Sony com desconto de 18% no prazo com cupom
O PlayStation 5 Slim Digital está saindo por R$ 3.750 com cupom AFFNOV09 em até 12x sem juros na loja do Magalu no AliExpress. O console da Sony, com SSD veloz e que traz um controle DualSense, recebe desconto de 18% sobre o preço base de R$ 4.599, reajustado recentemente.
Esta é uma rara chance de adquirir o modelo base do atual sistema da Sony com desconto no Black November 2026, já que ele não tem aparecido em promoções no varejo nos últimos meses.
O PS5 Slim é o modelo revisto do console lançado em 2020, com design compacto, mas a mesma performance. Seu SSD interno de 825 GB e os 16 GB de RAM garantem o carregamento quase instantâneo dos jogos, enquanto é possível expandir o espaço interno com um SSD externo e/ou um M.2.
Seu controle sem fio DualSense possui feedback háptico avançado, que oferece tensão e resistência nos gatilhos conforme a interação, enquanto respostas táteis e de áudio via alto-falantes embutidos fazem o jogador se sentir na pele do personagem no game.
O sistema reproduz gráficos em 4K a uma taxa de até 120 fps em TVs compatíveis. A tecnologia de ray-tracing entrega renderização de reflexos e sombras mais realistas, tornando a jogatina mais imersiva.
O PS5 Slim roda todos os jogos do PS4, mas não possui um leitor de mídia física. O acessório, também compatível com o PS5 Pro, precisa ser comprado à parte.
Este console suporta Wi-Fi 6 e Ethernet para acesso à PlayStation Store, que oferece jogos digitais e acesso a apps de streaming, como Apple TV e Spotify.
O PlayStation 5 Slim Digital (R$ 3.750 com cupom AFFNOV09 em até 12x sem juros) traz duas portas USB-C e duas USB-A, e inclui um cabo USB-C duplo para carregar o DualSense.
Black November é o mês da Black Friday 2026, que acontece no dia 27 de novembro, mas o varejo se antecipou e já oferece ofertas em eletrônicos com diversos cupons e condições exclusivas durante o período.

articles.title: Tesla unveils AI accelerator roadmap, adopts new 'SI' branding in 'Super Intelligence' push — SI6 to bring 80X more compute performance, Dojo 3 headed to space
articles.text:
Tesla unveils AI accelerator roadmap, adopts new 'SI' branding in 'Super Intelligence' push — SI6 to bring 80X more compute performance, Dojo 3 headed to space
Adopts 'Super Intelligence' term for new processors, retrofits it for old ones too.
Tesla has disclosed its revamped AI accelerator roadmap that sheds some light on the future of the company's chip development efforts. The Elon Musk company expects that its 6th Generation inference accelerator will bring 80X more compute performance than the existing 4th Generation chip, whereas its D3 training accelerator will cease to use SRAM-centric architecture in favor of a multi-chiplet design with stacked HBM. Also, Tesla has adopted the term "super intelligence" instead of artificial intelligence for its AI accelerators, renaming them with SI monikers. Musk recently confirmed SpaceXAI would be redubbed SpaceXSI for the same reason.
| Row 0 - Cell 0 | HW3 \| AI3 | SI4 \| HW4 | SI5 \| AI5 | SI6 \| AI6 | Dojo D1 | Dojo D3 | 
| Application | Inference | Inference | Inference | Inference | Training | Training | 
| Process technology | Samsung 14nm | Samsung 7nm | TSMC 3nm / Samsung 2nm | 2nm-class | TSMC 7nm | TBD | 
| Architecture | Monolithic | Monolithic | MCM | MCM | SoW | Chiplets | 
| Packaging | FCBGA | FCBGA | MCM | MCM | InFO_SoW (training tile) | 2.5D + 3D | 
| Memory type | LPDDR4 | GDDR6 | GDDR6/GDDR7 (?) | GDDR7 (?) | On-chip SRAM | Stacked HBM | 
| Memory capacity | 8 GB | 16 GB | 96 GB | 144 GB | 440 MB SRAM per die 11 GB SRAM per wafer | TBD | 
| Memory bandwidth | ~68 GB/s | ~224 GB/s | TBD | TBD | ~10 TB/s (on-chip) | TBD | 
| Performance vs. SI4 | — | 1X | 40X | 80X | — | — | 
| Estimated compute (TOPS) | 72 TOPS | 216 – 576 | 8,640 – 23,040 | 17,280 – 46,080 | 362 TFLOPS | TBD | 
| Estimated compute (POPS) | 0.072 | 0.216 – 0.576 | 8.64 – 23.04 | 17.28 – 46.08 | 0.362 PFLOPS | TBD | 
| Status | Legacy | Production | Nearing Production | Development | Discontinued | Development | 
Dojo D3: No more wafer-level integration?
Perhaps the most interesting development in Tesla's AI hardware roadmap is the re-emergence of the in-house developed Dojo training accelerator after Elon Musk cancelled the whole wafer-level Dojo project in August, 2025, and then said SpaceX and xAI would exclusively use Nvidia hardware in August, 2026, both in its terrestrial and extraterrestrial data centers. Yet, the 3rd Generation Dojo will be considerably different from the first two generations, Dojo D1 and Dojo D2.
Tesla describes its next-generation Dojo 3 (D3) training accelerator as a chiplet-based design that combines 2.5D and 3D packaging technologies with stacked HBM. This represents a substantial departure from the original Dojo D1 system-on-wafer architecture, which relied on distributed on-chip SRAM and interconnected 25 D1 processors with 11 GB of SRAM using wafer-scale packaging technology. The adoption of HBM suggests that Tesla intends to substantially increase memory capacity, as modern AI models consume extreme amounts of memory to store parameters, activations, and intermediate data, making SRAM unattractive from a capacity standpoint. The use of HBM simplifies memory scaling but introduces different latency, bandwidth, packaging, and power trade-offs. Yet, it remains unclear whether the company has abandoned wafer-scale integration altogether.
On the one hand, it is possible to stack custom HBM modules on top of logic dies interconnected using wafer-scale packaging technology. On the other hand, wafer-level integration is expensive and makes the most sense for select use cases, which include SRAM-centric architectures. Stacking HBM atop wafer-scale interconnected logic dies adds further design complexities, cooling challenges, manufacturing complexity (i.e., potentially reducing yields), long-term reliability concerns, and ultimately costs. While most of the challenges can be resolved by adding redundancy and refining process technologies, this all comes at a cost, making wafer-scaling less likely for D3.
Tesla has yet to disclose D3's compute performance, memory capacity, manufacturing process, or development schedule. At the same time, it claims that its Dojo D3 will be optimized for 'space, training, and scaling,' which means the unit will offer decent performance and will be easy to scale (which again points to a more conventional architecture of accelerators rather than to wafer-scale packaging). More intriguingly, the D3 is also set to be optimized for extraterrestrial deployments, which probably means radiation hardening for at least select SKUs.
SI6: 80X more performance than HW4 in a few years
Another interesting detail in the roadmap is the disclosure of approximate compute performance of Tesla's 6th Generation inference accelerator (SI6): 80X compute improvement over HW4 and 9X more memory over HW4. Depending on how HW4 performance is measured (read on for explanation), we are talking about 17,280 – 46,080 TOPS (trillion operations per second), or 17.28 – 46.08 POPS (quadrillion operations per second), though we do not know anything about data formats supported by SI6. Of course, these are estimates, so take them with a grain of salt. To put the numbers into context, Nvidia's Rubin GPU offers 50 NVFP4 PFLOPS for inference, 35 NVFP4 PFLOPS for training, and 17.5 FP8/FP6 PFLOPS. Meanwhile, Rubin is shipping to customers today, whereas SI6 is due in 2029 – 2030. There are some additional details about SI6, which we will discuss below.
Tesla's existing 4th Generation inference processor used in the company's automobiles today (which was originally called HW4, then renamed to AI4, then to SI4) is made by Samsung Foundry using its 7nm-class process technology and relies on conventional flip-chip ball grid array (FCBGA) packaging (note that the alleged Tesla slide contains a mistake and claims that the unit is made using a 5nm-class node) as well as presumably 16 GB of GDDR6 memory. The company describes the processor as the current benchmark for its Full Self-Driving (FSD) technology, which makes it the baseline against which performance of future generations is measured. Meanwhile, Tesla does not officially disclose the chip's absolute compute performance numbers, memory capacity, or power consumption, which makes comparison hard. Elon Musk once said that HW4 is 3X – 8X more powerful than HW3, which was officially rated at 72 TOPS, making HW4 a 216 – 576 TOPS ASIC (note that these are estimates).
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
As expected, the slide re-confirms that the upcoming 5th Generation inference accelerator called SI5 (aka HW5 aka AI5) will be manufactured using 3nm- and 2nm-class process technologies at TSMC and Samsung Foundry, respectively, and will adopt a multi-chip module (MCM) design, marking a departure from the conventional packaging approach used for HW4. Tesla expects SI5 to deliver a 40X performance improvement over HW4, which will be a result of an eightfold increase in compute capabilities (driven by considerably denser process technologies and more execution units) and a fivefold gain from silicon optimization, according to Elon Musk, which points to 8,640 – 23,040 TOPS (an estimated figure), depending on how one counts performance of HW4. Meanwhile, the processor is expected to consume from 250W to 800W depending on application, so making performance estimates at this point is not exactly a good business. Meanwhile, the processor will also feature six times more memory than its predecessor (i.e., 96 GB). Depending on the memory type used (GDDR6 or GDDR7), the Tesla SI5 can offer memory bandwidth between 768 GB/s and 1.536 GB/s.
Moving on to the Tesla's 6th Generation inference accelerator (SI6), which is set to further increase compute performance to 80 times that of HW4 and feature eight times more memory than the current-generation processor. This could translate to 17.28 – 46.08 POPS (quadrillion operations per second), depending on how to count HW4 performance, and 144 GB of memory, which is significant performance and amount of memory for an AI accelerator.
Tesla has already inked a deal with Samsung Foundry to make its 6th Generation inference accelerators through 2033, and the new slide reveals that the unit will be made using a 2nm-class process technology. Given the fact that the chip is due in 2029 – 2030 and Samsung's recently updated foundry roadmap, we are probably talking about automotive-grade SF2A, performance-enhanced SF2P, or even SF2Z with backside power delivery. Meanwhile, a thing that strikes the eye with the SI6 is that Tesla does not envision the chip to be produced at Terafab using Intel's 14A fabrication process in the 2030s.
SI6 will retain the multi-chip module (MCM) approach introduced with AI5/SI5/HW5, which seems rational as it will be able to leverage experience it is going to get with its 5th Generation inference accelerator and retain relatively reasonable packaging costs. Many automakers are considering adoption of multi-chiplet designs and HBM memory for their next-generation system-in-packages (SiPs), which will drive their costs. It remains to be seen when Tesla adopts HBM for its inference accelerators, but probably not with SI6.
Follow Tom's Hardware on Google News, or add us as a preferred source, to get our latest news, analysis, & reviews in your feeds.
Anton Shilov is a contributing writer at Tom’s Hardware. Over the past couple of decades, he has covered everything from CPUs and GPUs to supercomputers and from modern process technologies and latest fab tools to high-tech industry trends.

articles.title: SA-founded Water Ledger Global secures investment from Launch Africa - Disrupt Africa
articles.text:
South African-founded water data startup Water Ledger Global (WLG) has secured a strategic investment from Launch Africa to scale its shared trust infrastructure for water globally.
Founded in October 2024 by a South African team, with roots in Australia going back to 2016, WLG is the company behind Water Ledger, a platform that creates a single, trusted record of how much water there is, who is using it, and what it is worth.
By breaking down data silos, it gives regulators, utilities, investors and lenders a shared source of truth, with the aim of turning water into a transparent, investable asset class. The startup has subsidiaries in South Africa, Australia and the United States, and its technology is already live. Its SWaN solution for mitigation and nutrient markets operates in Virginia, while its water accounting and trading solution is used by Seqwater in Australia.
The new funding will help WLG take its platform to more utilities, regulators, water users and markets.
“Capital follows confidence. In a very short time we have taken a bold idea and turned it into real solutions to real water challenges,” said Fred Platt, CEO of Water Ledger Global. “We are not just building technology; we are building the trust backbone for water.”
Uwem Uwemakpan, head of investments at Launch Africa, said the platform addresses a real need as the push for transparency and more funding into local utilities grows.
“We backed the team because that record is what gives investors and lenders the confidence to put capital into water infrastructure,” he said.

articles.title: J'ai essayé le Genesis GV60 Magma : la Hyundai Ioniq 5 N était ma voiture électrique préférée, mais j’ai trouvé encore mieux — Frandroid
articles.text:
Selon les mots du directeur France et Italie de Genesis, Charles Fuster, il s’agit du meilleur moment pour lancer Genesis en Europe, et notamment en France. La fidélité des clients aux marques européennes est en dégringolade et il est possible de conquérir ces clients.
Mais c’est aussi une période qui voit de nombreux constructeurs chinois se lancer sur le marché. Le constructeur coréen Genesis ne veut pas y être associé car, bien qu’en progrès, les constructeurs chinois gardent, pour les automobilistes, une image peu valorisante.
Alors Genesis doit séduire, prouver son savoir-faire et sa légitimité sur le marché des véhicules premium. Cela passe par un engagement en compétition, notamment dans le championnat du monde d’endurance avec l’écurie Genesis Magma Racing, mais aussi par des véhicules d’image, comme le nouveau Genesis GV60 Magma dont j’ai pu prendre le volant, et qui me rappelle très fortement ma voiture électrique préférée jusqu’à présent : la Hyundai Ioniq 5 N.

| Puissance (chevaux) | 650 chevaux |

| Niveau d’autonomie | Conduite semi-autonome (niveau 2) | 
| Vitesse max | 264 km/h | 
| Taille de l’écran principal | 27 pouces | 
| Prise côté voiture | Type 2 Combo (CCS) | 
| Prix entrée de gamme | 86600 euros | 
| Essayez-la | Fiche produit | 
Un design fort, très fort
Le Genesis GV60 Magma se base sur le GV60. Un SUV électrique de 4,55 m de long avec une ligne fastback au style sobre et assez élégant.
Mais cette version Magma est aussi inquiétante qu’un volcan sur le point d’exploser. Tout d’abord, il y a cette teinte spécifique Magma Orange qui n’est pas des plus discrètes. Le nuancier compte neuf autres teintes (brillantes, métallisées, pastel et mates), plus sobres.
La face avant intègre une immense entrée d’air en bas du bouclier. Au-dessus, on retrouve une triple admission d’air qui intègre subtilement la caméra avant. Les projecteurs sont les « Two-Line » que l’on retrouve sur les modèles Genesis.
Sur le capot, on retrouve le logo Genesis qui me rappelle celui des Bentley. Il est ici dans une teinte noire qui vient donner une touche de sportivité supplémentaire. Les ailes avant sont élargies, avec à l’avant un canard aérodynamique débordant du pare-chocs et une extraction d’air du passage de roue.
On remarque des jantes de 21 pouces sans aucune considération aérodynamique, avec des étriers de frein orange. Les poignées de portes intégrées à la carrosserie serviront plus le style que l’efficience énergétique. Le Cx est d’ailleurs à 0,31.
À l’arrière, on retrouve le même design de feux qu’à l’avant. Mais surtout, comment ne pas parler de l’immense aileron arrière fixe avec, aux extrémités, des cornes me faisant penser à un petit diable sortant de la fournaise !
Le style est clairement assumé comme sportif, ça ne fait aucun doute. Le parti pris est très fort pour une marque cherchant un positionnement premium, chic, raffiné et élégant. Le pari peut être réussi si cette sportivité décomplexée à l’arrêt se retrouve derrière le volant.
Côté dimensions, il mesure 4,55 m de long, donc c’est 16 cm de moins que le Hyundai Ioniq 5 N, ce qui lui donne un côté compact qui n’est pas sans me déplaire. La largeur est de 1,94 m, tandis que la hauteur est de 1,56 m. Pour cette version Magma, la voiture a été élargie de 20 mm.
Une habitabilité surprenante
J’ai été surpris car le Genesis GV60 Magma, et plus largement le Genesis GV60, ne mesure que 4,55 m de long, soit la taille d’un Audi Q4 e-tron, mais l’espace aux places arrière me semble un peu plus généreux que dans mes souvenirs.
On est bien installé sur la banquette arrière, mes 1,86 m ne manquent pas d’espace aux jambes. Je me vois bien voyager à l’arrière d’un GV60. Sauf sur un point : l’espace restant pour ma tête. Si je ne me tasse pas dans la banquette et que je reste bien droit, j’ai les cheveux qui brossent le plafonnier.
Ce n’est pas très grave car on se tasse toujours un peu en voiture, que les grands sont généralement devant, mais sur ce point, un Audi Q4 e-tron fait mieux, tout comme le Hyundai Ioniq 5 N.
À l’avant, on est bien installé, je dirais même bien calé dans des sièges baquets. Ils offrent un bon maintien en conduite sportive, avec une assise qui reste relativement confortable pour la catégorie.
Genesis fait le choix d’offrir un peu plus de confort avec des sièges moins exigeants que ceux de l’Ioniq 5 N puisque, ici, le positionnement se veut GT et « Athletic Elegance ». Un peu comme… vous savez, ce collègue de bureau qui vient chaussé de baskets de running On. D’ailleurs, ces sièges sont chauffants et ventilés de série !
Le coffre offre, lui, un volume de 400 litres sous la ligne de vitre et 670 litres jusqu’au toit. Ce n’est pas le plus grand de la catégorie. Un Q4 e-tron offre, par exemple, 520 litres. L’ouverture du hayon est électrique, sans passer par le catalogue des options. Attention il n’y a pas de frunk.
La couleur des surpiqûres de l’habitacle peut passer de l’orange au gris clair, ce qui est un peu plus sobre. La qualité des matériaux est au niveau d’un positionnement premium, que ce soit sur un GV60 normal ou Magma. Le design de l’habitacle change réellement avec un côté créatif décomplexé, y compris pour la partie infodivertissement.
Infodivertissement : le royaume de la commande physique
Alors que la tendance est à la réduction des commandes physiques, bien que certains constructeurs reviennent légèrement en arrière, Genesis a conservé une multitude de boutons physiques, y compris pour la gestion de l’infodivertissement.
On retrouve une seule dalle numérique de 27 pouces à bord, comprenant le cockpit et l’infodivertissement. Cet écran vient du Hyundai Ioniq 5, l’ergonomie et la simplicité d’usage ne sont donc pas une référence.
Toutefois, Genesis a conservé une molette sur la console centrale, façon ancien BMW iDrive, pour naviguer dans les menus, notamment ceux spécifique au profil Magma. Un peu de nostalgie s’est emparée de moi lorsque j’ai découvert cette molette. Apple CarPlay et Android Auto sont bien entendu présents.
La climatisation a un menu dans l’écran, mais a aussi sa propre commande déportée sous l’écran, avec de nombreux boutons physiques et même un écran tactile. Le volant a de nombreuses commandes sur les branches qui permettent de faire tout un tas de choses dans le compteur numérique et sur les modes de conduite.
Je suis pour le retour des commandes physiques. Sous certains aspects, l’ergonomie des véhicules était meilleure quand il y avait davantage de boutons. On ne peut pas fustiger Genesis sur ce point.
En revanche, je regrette que l’infodivertissement soit plutôt complexe de prime abord, notamment pour les fonctions propres à la version Magma. Je pense néanmoins qu’après quelque temps, le propriétaire aura trouvé ses marques et pourra se servir sans trop de contraintes de ses fonctions favorites.
On retrouve pas mal d’infos concernant les températures sur le système d’infodivertissement comme les températures des moteurs avant et arrière et de la batterie.
D’ailleurs deux modes de gestions thermiques existent : le mode Boost, qui donne la pleine tension sans limitation jusqu’à 40 degrés, et le mode Race qui s’efforce de maintenir la température à 30 degrés pendant 20 minutes. Avec ces modes on mise soit sur la performance totale mais sur de courtes sessions, ou sur l’endurance pour de plus longues sessions.
Aides à la conduite
Les aides à la conduite sont nombreuses, mais notre essai ne nous a pas vraiment permis de les tester. Le temps de roulage était court et uniquement sur routes sinueuses ou sur circuit. Elles reprennent ce qui existe déjà sur la Hyundai Ioniq 5.
On retrouve alors un régulateur de vitesse adaptatif, un système de maintien au centre de la voie avec suivi des lignes, des alertes de circulation en marche arrière, une alerte de collision et tout ce que l’on peut attendre d’une voiture moderne.
La désactivation du Lane Assist est relativement facile, avec un long appui sur le bouton correspondant à la conduite assistée sur le volant.
On y retrouve aussi un planificateur d’itinéraire, identique à celui de Hyundai, mais que je n’ai pas eu l’occasion d’essayer. Pour en savoir plus à son sujet, je vous conseille de consulter notre essai de la Hyundai Ioniq 5.
Ces aides seront utiles au quotidien, mais ce n’est pas le propos aujourd’hui. On arrive enfin à ce qui fait que j’ai adoré ce GV60 Magma : sa dynamique de conduite !
Conduite : un Hyundai Ioniq 5 N mais en mieux ?
Le « Virtual Gear Shift »
Cette année 2026, j’ai eu la chance de découvrir, avec un peu de retard, le Hyundai Ioniq 5 N sur les routes des Préalpes d’Azur. J’avais donc un souvenir frais du modèle avant de prendre le volant du GV60 Magma sur les routes comparables de la Sainte-Baume.
Je vais être franc, c’est la même chose, mais en mieux ! Le groupe Hyundai a profité des retours sur l’Ioniq 5 N et de trois ans de développement supplémentaire pour améliorer encore la copie.
Commençons déjà par la boîte de vitesses à 8 rapports simulée, le fonctionnement « Virtual Gear Shift ». C’est la même chose que sur la Hyundai. On peut l’activer sur tous les modes ou presque : Range, Comfort, Sport, GT et Sprint, avec un passage automatique ou manuel des rapports avec les palettes au volant.
Mais ici, c’est la sonorité qui a évolué. Le régime moteur simulé par le système audio Bang & Olufsen est celui d’un V6 allant jusqu’à 9 000 tours par minute. Un moteur thermique noble, assez bien retranscrit, bien qu’artificiel, et qui ajoute véritablement au plaisir de conduite, que ce soit en conduite très sportive ou plus coulée.
Avec le « Virtual Gear Shift » enclenché, l’arrivée de la puissance est corrélée au régime moteur simulé. Plus le V6 hurle dans les tours, plus les accélérations sont fulgurantes. Ce n’est donc pas la première fois que je goûte à cet artifice logiciel. Il m’a manqué dans toutes les sportives électriques que j’ai essayées après la Hyundai, et je l’ai retrouvé avec grand plaisir dans la Genesis.
De plus, j’ai l’impression d’être moins malade en tant que passager avec la simulation du son et de la boîte de vitesses que dans une voiture électrique qui n’en est pas équipée. La sonorité aide à se concentrer sur la conduite, tandis que la puissance délivrée plus progressivement améliore les choses.
En conduite sportive, c’est une véritable réussite. Le passage du faux rapport donne un à-coup dans le véhicule, comme sur une vraie thermique, idem au rétrogradage. Et concernant la sonorité, ça craque au passage du rapport supérieur et pétarade à la décélération.
Dynamique de conduite
Une fois qu’on a activé le mode GT ou Sprint, on obtient le meilleur du GV60 Magma. Genesis a travaillé sur la réponse à la pédale d’accélérateur et sur la suspension pilotée électroniquement.
Le système « End-of-Travel » est capable de détecter les mouvements de caisse et d’ajuster instantanément l’amortissement pour améliorer la précision et la stabilité en courbe. Qu’on se le dise, la voiture ne prend aucun roulis, cache bien ses 2 220 kg et ne plonge pas au freinage. C’est vraiment surprenant pour un SUV familial.
Comme pour le Hyundai Ioniq 5 N, la caisse du GV60 Magma a été renforcée avec l’ajout de 0,65 m d’adhésif structurel, de 20 points de soudure supplémentaires et de renforts en L intégrés dans les passages de roue. La rigidité torsionnelle progresse de 9,7 %.
Le e-LSD permet d’avoir un arrière qui enroule volontiers dans les virages, permettant de gommer le sous-virage que l’on peut avoir avec une voiture aussi lourde. Il peut même vous gratifier de glissades plutôt prévenantes du train arrière. J’ai même fini par vouloir jouer avec et le faire glisser quelque peu sur la piste du Castellet en déconnectant totalement l’ESP. Le GV60 Magma met en confiance. Mais attention à la sanction d’un excès de confiance, car les vitesses atteintes sont inavouables…
Avec 650 chevaux et 790 Nm de couple venant de deux moteurs, il abat le 0 à 100 km/h en 3,4 secondes et peut atteindre 265 km/h. Des chiffres comparables à l’Audi RS 5 hybride. Il faut alors stopper toute cette cavalerie quand on arrive sur un virage serré. Pour cela, Genesis a monté des freins en acier de 400 mm à l’avant avec des étriers à quatre pistons et 360 mm à l’arrière. Ça fait le job, mais il manque, à mon goût, de mordant. La pédale est peut-être trop assistée pour moi.
Et c’est bien la seule ombre au tableau, car avec son empattement plus court de 10 cm que celui de l’Ioniq 5 N, le GV60 Magma se montre plus mobile, plus maniable, tout en restant relativement prévenant. Si vous entrez bien fort sur les freins, l’arrière peut déjà entamer une dérive, vous facilitant le virage.
C’est très, très ludique, d’autant que les pneus Pirelli P Zero sont rassurants. Pour ses pneus en 275/30 R21 aux quatre coins, Genesis a travaillé avec Pirelli pour développer une monte spécifique au modèle, portant le marquage Genesis GOE. C’est dire le sérieux du constructeur pour cette déclinaison sportive.
Les avantages d’une voiture électrique
Après avoir bien usé des pneus et des modes de conduite les plus sportifs, mon copilote et moi sommes repassés en mode Comfort. Et la voiture redevient une voiture électrique dans sa définition la plus fondamentale. Silencieuse, douce et confortable. L’insonorisation du GV60 Magma a été renforcée face à l’Ioniq 5 N, expliquant en partie les 15 kg supplémentaires du Genesis malgré les 15 cm de moins.
Les palettes permettent d’utiliser trois niveaux de freinage régénératif. En appuyant plus longuement sur la palette de gauche, on passe en i-Pedal, qui est un mode de conduite One-Pedal et qui va donc jusqu’à l’arrêt complet . Il est lui aussi paramétrable sur trois niveaux avec les palettes. Et je dois vous dire qu’il s’agit du One-Pedal le plus confortable que j’ai vu jusqu’à présent. La transition entre accélération et décélération est douce.
On a fait un petit jeu avec Benoît d’Option Auto : il m’a fait fermer les yeux en tant que passager et je devais lui dire lorsque nous étions totalement arrêtés. J’avais bien trois secondes de retard sur le véritable arrêt de la voiture. C’est dire le niveau de mise au point du One-Pedal.
Et enfin, ce n’est pas un plaisir coupable. Le GV60 Magma simule très bien le plaisir d’une voiture thermique, sans participer au réchauffement climatique avec des rejets polluants à l’échappement.
Autonomie, batterie et recharge
Bien que le Genesis GV60 Magma utilise une batterie de 84 kWh, il n’y a pas de miracle sur l’autonomie. Elle est annoncée à 425 km en cycle WLTP, soit moins qu’une Volkswagen ID. Polo avec seulement 52 kWh. À titre de comparaison, le Hyundai Ioniq 5 N arrive à 448 km. La différence entre les deux vient du coefficient de pénétration dans l’air.
Qu’elle soit thermique, hybride ou électrique, une voiture misant sur la performance est difficilement efficiente. Genesis annonce déjà une consommation WLTP élevée de 21,5 kWh/100 km. Lors de l’essai, j’ai relevé une consommation proche de 40 kWh/100 km en conduite sportive sur route, soit un peu plus de 200 km d’autonomie sportive, et plus de 75 kWh/100 km sur piste depuis la charge, soit à peine 100 km d’autonomie sur circuit (en comptant la consommation réduite par les manœuvres).
Mais d’un autre côté, on ne peut pas le fustiger pour sa petite autonomie. L’Audi RS 5, aux performances comparables, n’a pas plus d’autonomie, que ce soit en conduite quotidienne calme ou en conduite sportive.
Le Genesis GV60 Magma n’est pas très contraignant lorsqu’il s’agit de le charger. Il ne lui faut que 18 minutes pour passer de 10 à 80 % grâce à la plateforme 800 volts et à une charge à 264 kW communiquée par Genesis. Hyundai communique sur un pic de 350 kW en charge, pour 18 minutes également de 10 à 80 % avec la même batterie. Peut-être une différence de communication.
Je n’ai pas de relevé de consommation en cycle urbain, mais sachez que j’avais pu descendre à moins de 20 kWh/100 km en ville lors de mon essai du Ioniq 5 N, et 23 kWh/100 km sur autoroute, ce qui donne une idée pour le Genesis GV60 Magma.
Prix, concurrence et disponibilité
Le Genesis GV60 Magma est déjà disponible à la commande en France au prix de 86 600 euros. Il n’y a rien à ajouter en supplément, si ce n’est une teinte à 900 euros. La voiture arrive déjà entièrement équipée et richement dotée ! C’est un avantage face aux Allemands.
Maintenant, Genesis n’a pour l’instant que 2 points de vente en France, Paris et Lille. Cela est appelé à s’étoffer dans les prochains mois, en s’appuyant parfois sur le réseau Hyundai, mais Genesis ne donne pas de chiffre clair. On sait juste que la marque veut une présence globale sur le territoire et pertinente. Le but n’est pas d’ouvrir des showrooms dans toutes les villes de France, mais de rencontrer sa clientèle.
En ce qui concerne la concurrence, il n’y en a pas pour l’instant. On pourrait penser à l’Alpine A390 GTS ou le Porsche Macan propulsion, mais aucune autre voiture électrique ne va aussi loin dans son approche. Il y a plus performant en accélération, en vitesse maximale ou sur un temps au tour, mais aucune autre n’adopte la même approche.
Enfin, sans concurrence, pas vraiment : sa cousine Hyundai pourrait lui faire de l’ombre, avec 8 600 euros de moins pour la même fiche technique, à quelques détails jusqu’au-boutistes près. La question se pose. D’autant que l’habitabilité est un peu meilleure et le style un peu plus futuriste. Le choix sera une question de goût et de finances.
