articles.title: How Satin Group’s Sankalp plans to empower India’s next wave of founders
articles.text:
How Satin Group’s Sankalp plans to empower India’s next wave of founders
University incubators play an important role in nurturing early-stage ideas, but Sankalp aims to go further by helping entrepreneurs bridge the gap between developing a concept and preparing it for the market.
India’s startup ecosystem is witnessing a growing wave of innovation in climate action and sustainability. From students developing affordable technology solutions for micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) to early-stage entrepreneurs tackling circular economy challenges, the ideas are promising. But turning a climate-focused idea into a scalable business requires more than passion. Founders need access to capital, industry networks and structured mentorship to translate their vision into viable enterprises.
Recognising these gaps, Satin Group, based in Gurugram, Haryana, launched Sankalp this September. It is a platform designed to nurture sustainability-focused ideas from students and early-stage entrepreneurs. In an exclusive interaction with YourStory, Pramod Marar, CEO of Satin FinServ Limited, discussed the thinking behind the initiative, the importance of non-financial support alongside funding, and the role financial institutions can play in scaling climate innovation.
Sankalp operates through two distinct tracks: student-led business ideas and early-stage startups. The student track encourages college students to develop technology-driven solutions to climate and environmental challenges. The startup track focuses on young businesses working in areas such as clean mobility, circular economy, waste management, and sustainable supply chains. Sankalp winners stand a chance to win Rs 32 lakh, with Rs 10 lakh for students and Rs 22 lakh for startups.
Applications for the first cohort closed on October 4. Sankalp says the response has been encouraging, with more than 17,000 registrations and over 1,000 teams taking part. Student innovators, it adds, showed a notable interest in technology-led solutions for climate challenges.
“We were pleasantly surprised to see a strong focus among students on creating technology-led solutions in the climate space,” Marar said.
The genesis of Sankalp
Marar brings more than two decades of experience across banking, microfinance, and sustainability-focused entrepreneurship. Having started his own venture early in his career, he experienced firsthand the challenges faced by entrepreneurs seeking initial funding, particularly those from salaried or service-sector families without access to financial backing.
“Startup wasn’t a cool term at that time; it wasn’t even a term that existed. I come from a middle-class service background family. There was a lot of moral support, but there was no financial support. That’s when I realised how difficult it was to access early-stage capital,” Marar recalled.
While founders may have the passion and business acumen to develop an idea, scaling it requires a broader support system. Capital is only one part of the equation; access to expertise, networks and institutional support can be equally important.
“Most startup founders are very passionate about their ideas and have the acumen to scale them. But scaling requires a lot of elements beyond capital. That’s why we started Sankalp — to help build the ecosystem around sustainability and climate innovation,” Marar said.
Satin Group, which was founded in 1990, comprises three non-banking financial companies (NBFCs) focused on microfinance, housing finance, and corporate and SME lending. Its broader ecosystem also includes Satin Growth Alternatives, a debt fund, and Satin Technologies, its technology arm. This combination of financial and technological capabilities provides the group with multiple avenues to support emerging sustainability-focused businesses.
University incubators play an important role in nurturing early-stage ideas, but Sankalp aims to go further by helping entrepreneurs bridge the gap between developing a concept and preparing it for the market.
“I wouldn’t call it a scaled-down version because we actually try to go beyond the conventional model of incubation. We want to understand whether we can support founders through experienced mentorship, both at an individual level and through institutions, as well as through debt and equity,” Marar said.
With applications closed, Sankalp has moved from a wide pool of ideas to a tighter evaluation. KPMG is the programme’s assessment partner. It is independently evaluating every application against a predefined framework, helping with shortlisting and identifying the most promising ventures. Satin says this keeps the selection objective and based only on merit.
Thirty teams have made it to the virtual jury round, where they will present to a panel of practitioners, venture capital (VC) fund managers and lenders. The shortlisted ventures cover climate tech, circular economy, clean energy, sustainable cities, waste management, water management and sustainable agriculture.
According to Satin, what stood out was not just the range of ideas but the depth applicants showed in their chosen areas. Judges will look at the strength of the idea, innovation, feasibility, scalability and potential for meaningful impact.
Based on the jury’s assessments, select finalists will go on to the in-person Grand Finale, where they will present before a jury and industry leaders for final evaluation and recognition.
The jury rounds are also meant to open doors beyond the prize money. Both the virtual round and the Grand Finale will have representatives from VC funds, incubation centres and institutional investors, who can evaluate the ideas and explore funding possibilities. Satin has also signed formal arrangements with certain incubation centres to offer institutional mentoring to the selected founders. In addition, Satin Growth Alternatives, the group’s Category II alternative investment fund (AIF), will look at the ideas from an investment angle.
Satin is careful about what this means for funding. At this stage, it says, Sankalp is not an announced debt-and-equity programme. Any financing would be considered case by case, depending on the business model, stage of development, funding needs and suitability, with the aim of finding viable opportunities and exploring ways to support their growth.
For Satin, the programme fits in its wider ambition to help build a more sustainable and climate-resilient economy. Financing remains central to its business, the company says, but Sankalp gives it a chance to engage with emerging innovators and understand how climate-focused business models are evolving, along with the opportunities and challenges in the space. It also helps Satin spot solutions that may, over time, match its own financing capabilities.
The group has already been building towards this. Satin Finserv set up its Sustainable & Emerging Businesses (SEB) vertical in August 2025 to offer financing to sustainability-oriented and emerging enterprises, with a streamlined process and dedicated relationship support. In the last 12 months, it has disbursed loans of roughly Rs 400 crore to businesses focused on sustainability, either as users or providers of sustainability-focused solutions.
Sankalp complements that effort, Satin says, by helping it discover promising entrepreneurs and innovations.
Why Sankalp matters for India’s green transition
India’s transition towards a low-carbon economy will require more than technological breakthroughs. It will also depend on whether promising innovations can secure funding, find customers, and scale sustainably. Financial institutions, established businesses, and entrepreneurs all have a role to play in building this ecosystem.
Sankalp seeks to bring these stakeholders together, combining access to finance with mentorship and industry connections. Its approach reflects the idea that supporting climate innovation should extend beyond funding a promising idea or awarding a one-time prize.
“Rather than just waiting for institutions to put their money on the table, can financial institutions come together to create a platform that helps founders go beyond simply raising capital?” Marar said.
By seeking to connect entrepreneurs with financing, expertise, and potential commercial partners, Sankalp aims to create a longer-term support system for sustainability-focused businesses.""

articles.title: MacBook Neo 2 : Apple verrait les choses en grand pour éviter une nouvelle rupture de stock
articles.text:
Nous le savons, le MacBook Neo a connu un succès pour le moins retentissant. En l’espace de trois semaines après sa sortie, ce sont pas moins de 1,1 million d’unités qui ont été expédiées, et la demande n’a ensuite pas vraiment faibli. Il aura fallu un certain temps pour que les stocks parviennent à suivre la demande. L’entreprise à la pomme semble avoir retenu certaines leçons de cet épisode triomphal et elle ne compte pas réitérer la même erreur pour la seconde génération de son MacBook Neo.
Apple veut éviter une nouvelle rupture de stock pour son prochain MacBook Neo
Même si Apple ne l’a pas encore confirmé, il semble maintenant acté qu’un nouveau MacBook Neo est en préparation. L’information provient d’ailleurs du toujours très bien informé Mark Gurman, journaliste chez Bloomberg, qui précise que la sortie de l’appareil aurait lieu « pour le premier semestre de l’année prochaine ». En réalité, Apple a tout intérêt à miser sur ce Mac dont la première génération s’est vendue à plus de 8 millions d’exemplaires à travers le monde.
Mais l’entreprise à la pomme prévoirait un stock au lancement bien plus important. En effet, selon le célèbre leaker Lanzuk, la production du MacBook Neo de seconde génération serait doublée par rapport à celle de la première génération. Du moins, lors de son lancement. Apple prévoirait ainsi de produire 16 millions d’unités rien que pour le premier semestre 2027. À titre de comparaison, le MacBook Neo de première génération avait été produit à 8 millions d’exemplaires pour son lancement.
Qu’attendre du MacBook Neo de seconde génération ?
Autant le dire tout de suite, Apple n’a communiqué aucune information à ce sujet. En revanche, Mark Gurman est venu rapporter quelques informations : le prochain MacBook Neo serait doté de 12 Go de RAM et d’une puce A19 Pro, soit celle que l’on retrouve dans les iPhone 17 Pro, Pro Max et Air. Pour rappel, le MacBook Neo de première génération intègre 8 Go de mémoire vive et une puce d’iPhone 16 Pro, l’entreprise à la pomme ayant pris l’habitude de recycler certaines des puces qu’elle produit. À noter également que des rumeurs annoncent de nouveaux coloris, ce qui serait logique pour ce type de produit.
Il reste maintenant la question épineuse du prix. Le succès du MacBook de première génération tient en partie au prix attractif qu’il avait affiché lors de son lancement : 699 euros. En juin dernier, l’appareil avait déjà connu une hausse de tarif de 100 euros. Par conséquent, qu’en sera-t-il d’un MacBook Neo de deuxième génération, doté de davantage de mémoire vive et d’une puce plus performante ? Un modèle vendu à plus de 1 000 euros ne risquerait-il pas de dénaturer ce qui a fait en partie le succès de son prédécesseur ? Une chose est sûre : la crise mondiale de la mémoire ne risque pas de s’estomper de sitôt.

articles.title: Quelles sont les meilleures cafetières Create ?
articles.text:
Quelles sont les meilleures cafetières Create ?
Les cafetières Create se déclinent en plusieurs technologies, de la machine super-automatique avec broyeur intégré aux modèles expresso semi-automatiques, en passant par les machines compatibles avec plusieurs formats de café. Le choix dépend principalement des habitudes de préparation, du niveau de contrôle recherché et des contraintes d’entretien. Voici quatre modèles à examiner selon ces différents critères.
Les meilleures cafetières Create
Create THERA MATIC : une machine automatique avec broyeur intégré
La THERA MATIC est une cafetière super-automatique équipée d’un moulin intégré et d’une buse vapeur. Elle permet de préparer du café à partir de grains et d’envisager différentes boissons, notamment des préparations à base de lait. Son fonctionnement automatisé la distingue des modèles qui demandent davantage de manipulations à chaque utilisation.
Prix : 249,95 € sur la boutique officielle Create.
Points forts
- Moulin à café intégré.
- Fonctionnement super-automatique.
- Buse vapeur pour les préparations lactées.
- Pression annoncée de 20 bars.
Points faibles
- Le moulin nécessite un entretien régulier.
- Les opérations de nettoyage peuvent demander une certaine attention.
Verdict
La THERA MATIC s’adresse aux amateurs qui souhaitent utiliser du café en grains sans effectuer toutes les étapes de préparation manuellement. Son moulin intégré constitue son principal attribut, tandis que la buse vapeur permet d’élargir les possibilités de boissons. En contrepartie, une machine équipée d’un broyeur demande un entretien régulier pour limiter l’accumulation de résidus. Ce modèle conviendra surtout aux personnes qui préparent fréquemment du café et souhaitent réunir plusieurs fonctions dans un seul appareil.
Create THERA CLASSIC ADVANCE : un expresso semi-automatique avec buse vapeur
La THERA CLASSIC ADVANCE adopte un fonctionnement semi-automatique. Elle s’adresse aux utilisateurs qui souhaitent conserver une part de contrôle dans la préparation de leur expresso. Sa buse vapeur permet également d’envisager des boissons lactées, selon les gestes et les réglages utilisés.
Prix : 259,95 € sur la boutique officielle Create (prix de référence : 299,95 €).
Points forts
- Fonctionnement semi-automatique.
- Buse vapeur intégrée.
- Préparation adaptée aux amateurs d’expresso.
- Possibilité de réaliser des boissons à base de lait.
Points faibles
- La préparation nécessite une intervention de l’utilisateur.
- La régularité du résultat dépend notamment du dosage et des manipulations.
Verdict
La THERA CLASSIC ADVANCE convient aux personnes qui préfèrent participer à la préparation de leur café plutôt que de confier l’ensemble du processus à une machine entièrement automatique. Sa buse vapeur élargit les possibilités, notamment pour les boissons lactées. Son fonctionnement semi-automatique implique toutefois de maîtriser plusieurs manipulations. Elle s’adresse donc davantage aux utilisateurs prêts à consacrer du temps à la préparation et à l’entretien de leur cafetière.
Create THERA STUDIO : une machine compatible avec plusieurs formats de café
La THERA STUDIO se distingue par sa polyvalence. Cette machine permet de préparer du café avec des capsules Nespresso, des capsules Dolce Gusto ou du café moulu grâce à trois adaptateurs interchangeables. Elle offre ainsi plusieurs possibilités de préparation dans un même appareil.
Pour comparer les différents modèles et découvrir d’autres cafetières Create, il est utile de tenir compte des formats de café compatibles, des caractéristiques techniques et des contraintes d’utilisation.
Prix : 89,95 € sur la boutique officielle Create (prix de référence : 99,95 €).
Caractéristiques principales
- Type : machine multi-capsules et café moulu.
- Compatibilité : Nespresso, Dolce Gusto et café moulu.
- Adaptateurs : trois modèles interchangeables.
- Pression annoncée : 19 bars.
- Puissance : 1 450 W.
- Capacité du réservoir : 600 ml.
Points forts
- Compatibilité avec deux systèmes de capsules.
- Utilisation possible de café moulu.
- Trois adaptateurs interchangeables.
- Plusieurs possibilités de préparation dans une seule machine.
Points faibles
- Le changement de format nécessite de remplacer l’adaptateur approprié.
- Le réservoir de 600 ml peut demander des remplissages réguliers en cas d’utilisation fréquente.
Verdict
La THERA STUDIO s’adresse aux utilisateurs qui souhaitent alterner entre différents formats de café sans multiplier les appareils. Sa compatibilité avec les capsules Nespresso, les capsules Dolce Gusto et le café moulu constitue son principal intérêt. Cette polyvalence suppose néanmoins de sélectionner l’adaptateur correspondant à chaque préparation. Son réservoir de 600 ml devra également être pris en compte selon la fréquence d’utilisation. Elle peut convenir aux foyers qui privilégient la variété des consommables et la flexibilité d’utilisation.
Les achats malins
Create THERA RETRO : une cafetière expresso semi-automatique au style rétro
La THERA RETRO associe une préparation expresso semi-automatique à un design rétro. Elle s’adresse aux personnes qui accordent de l’importance à l’apparence de leur équipement de cuisine, tout en souhaitant utiliser une cafetière destinée à la préparation d’expresso.
Prix : 109,95 € sur la boutique officielle Create (prix de référence : 129,95 €).
Points forts
- Design inspiré des appareils rétro.
- Fonctionnement semi-automatique.
- Préparation orientée vers l’expresso.
- Un style distinctif pour le plan de travail.
Points faibles
- La préparation demande une intervention manuelle.
- Pas de moulin intégré : la machine fonctionne avec du café moulu ou des dosettes ESE.
Verdict
La THERA RETRO s’adresse aux amateurs d’expresso qui recherchent également une cafetière design. Son apparence rétro constitue son principal élément distinctif, tandis que son fonctionnement semi-automatique laisse à l’utilisateur une part importante dans la préparation. Comme pour les autres modèles de cette catégorie, les manipulations nécessaires doivent être prises en compte avant l’achat. Elle dispose néanmoins d’une buse vapeur orientable pour les boissons lactées, d’un réservoir amovible de 1,25 litre et d’un indicateur de pression et de température.
Comment choisir parmi les cafetières Create ?
Le choix d’une cafetière dépend avant tout du type de café consommé et du temps que l’on souhaite consacrer à sa préparation. La THERA MATIC privilégie l’automatisation grâce à son moulin intégré. La THERA CLASSIC ADVANCE propose une approche semi-automatique avec buse vapeur, tandis que la THERA STUDIO mise sur la compatibilité avec plusieurs formats de café.
La THERA RETRO se distingue pour sa part par son esthétique rétro et son fonctionnement semi-automatique. Ces différences permettent de comparer les modèles selon des critères pratiques plutôt que sur la seule apparence.
Avant de choisir un appareil, il convient de tenir compte de la capacité du réservoir, des accessoires, des opérations d’entretien et des consommables nécessaires. Les prix publics et les caractéristiques détaillées doivent être vérifiés au moment de l’achat. Des informations complémentaires sur les appareils et les autres produits sont disponibles sur le site officiel de Create.

articles.title: McDonald's demandó por una herramienta de IA que recomienda precios a los franquiciados en EE. UU.
articles.text:
McDonald’s se enfrenta a una demanda en Estados Unidos por una herramienta de IA que lleva años utilizando para recomendar los precios de sus productos. Al parecer, el sistema analiza información sobre las ventas de cada establecimiento, su ubicación y los precios de la competencia, y tras eso calcula cuánto debería costar cada artículo del menú.
Sin embargo, un consumidor de Illinois considera que esta tecnología podría estar facilitando la coordinación de precios entre restaurantes que deberían competir de manera independiente aunque pertenecen a la misma cadena. La demanda, presentada el 2 de octubre por Michael Thomas, sostiene que McDonald’s utiliza datos comerciales que normalmente no compartirían unos franquiciados con otros, incluidos los resultados de ventas de cada local.
Según recoge Reuters, el denunciante acusa a la empresa de aprovechar esa información para recomendar precios que podrían reducir la competencia y, al mismo tiempo, encarecer los productos. Thomas, que suele comprar una hamburguesa con queso, patatas y un refresco, comenzó a cuestionarse el funcionamiento del sistema al toparse con diferencias de precios entre restaurantes cercanos.
McDonald’s asegura que la IA no decide los precios de sus restaurantes
La compañía ha rechazado las acusaciones y asegura que sus herramientas solo ofrecen recomendaciones que los franquiciados pueden aceptar o ignorar. En un comunicado publicado en su web, McDonald’s insiste en que no utiliza precios dinámicos y que la IA tampoco modifica de manera automática lo que paga cada cliente.
En este escenario, la empresa recuerda que cerca del 95 % de sus 14.000 restaurantes estadounidenses están gestionados por franquiciados, o lo que es lo mismo, responsables de establecer sus propias tarifas. El problema (según los demandantes) es que McDonald’s tendría suficiente influencia sobre esos establecimientos como para presionarlos a seguir las recomendaciones del sistema, y una investigación previa de Reuters ya había señalado que algunos franquiciados percibían esa presión. Sea como fuere, la compañía rechazó dicha interpretación.
Así, la demanda solicita que el procedimiento pueda representar a otros consumidores afectados y reclama una indemnización, pero todavía no existe una resolución judicial que determine si la herramienta ha servido realmente para coordinar precios.

articles.title: El SEPE dará el subsidio por desempleo a quien gane menos de 964 euros brutos al mes en 2027
articles.text:
El SEPE (Servicio Publico de Empleo Estatal) concederá subsidios por desempleo a partir de 2027 a los trabajadores que puedan demostrar unos ingresos inferiores a 964 euros brutos al mes. Es algo que lleva vigente varios años, aunque las cifras varían, pues el nuevo tope es una consecuencia administrativa de la decisión del Gobierno de elevar el Salario Mínimo Interprofesional (SMI) un 5,3 % el próximo año. Te contamos los detalles.
Sube el SMI, sube el tope del subsidio. La mayoría de los subsidios por desempleo en España condicionados a los ingresos exigen que los solicitantes tengan unos ingresos no superiores al 75 % del SMI, excluyendo la parte proporcional de las dos pagas extraordinarias anuales. El SMI se sitúa actualmente en 1.221 euros brutos al mes en 14 pagas, lo que fija el tope en 915,75 euros, según las cifras publicadas por el propio SEPE.
El borrador del Ministerio de Trabajo sitúa el SMI de 2027 en 1.286 euros, es decir, 18.004 euros al año, tal como cuenta El País. El 75% de esa cantidad es lo que equivale a esos 964,50 euros. Por tanto, el umbral aumenta en casi 50 euros al mes.
Lo básico. La condición está recogida en el artículo 275 de la Ley General de la Seguridad Social. El SEPE la comprueba cuando alguien solicita un subsidio por primera vez y de nuevo cada vez que se prorroga o se reanuda. Para ello, tiene en cuenta los ingresos del mes natural anterior a cada una de esas fechas.
Qué cuenta como ingresos. De acuerdo con la ley, se computan los ingresos por alquiler, los rendimientos del trabajo por cuenta propia, los intereses bancarios, las pensiones, las pensiones alimenticias y otras prestaciones públicas o privadas, así como ciertas ganancias de capital y rendimientos del patrimonio. Los salarios se computan por su importe bruto, incluida la parte proporcional de las pagas extraordinarias.
Entre líneas. Las personas que salen ganando son aquellas cuyos ingresos habrían estado justo por encima del límite de 2026 y justo por debajo del de 2027, así que realmente son poquitas. Superar el test de ingresos tampoco garantiza obtener el subsidio, ya que los solicitantes deben seguir cumpliendo los demás requisitos de cada modalidad. Entre ellos se encuentran:
- Haber agotado la prestación contributiva por desempleo.
- Ser mayor de 52 años.
- Haber cotizado menos de 360 días.
Algunos subsidios también permiten volver a solicitarlo más adelante si se cumple el requisito de ingresos tras haberse denegado la solicitud previamente. Así que para esas personas puede haber una segunda oportunidad.
Lo que no cambia. Los subsidios se calculan a partir del IPREM (Indicador Público de Renta de Efectos Múltiples), en lugar del salario mínimo, y tal como señala Noticias Trabajo, el IPREM permanece congelado en 600 euros al mes desde 2023. A menos que el Gobierno lo actualice, el subsidio para mayores de 52 años se mantendría en 480 euros en 2027. El SMI te dice si puedes solicitar el subsidio, y el IPREM, cuánto se percibe.
Y ahora qué. La cifra aún no es definitiva, pues tal y como comparte El País, el borrador está abierto a consulta pública hasta el 16 de noviembre. El Gobierno podría aprobarlo en el Consejo de Ministros el 17 de noviembre, o el 24 de noviembre a más tardar, antes de las elecciones generales del 29 de noviembre. El Ministerio de Trabajo quiere que el incremento quede zanjado antes de los comicios, para que no dependa de un gobierno en funciones ni del siguiente. El salario mínimo se fija por decreto, por lo que no necesita la aprobación del Parlamento.
Las patronales CEOE y Cepyme quieren que la decisión se posponga hasta después de las elecciones, y los sindicatos CCOO y UGT, que solicitaron una subida del 7 %, no han respaldado la del 5,3 %.

articles.title: How Greenlight Financial built an autonomous SOC solution on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore | Amazon Web Services
articles.text:
Artificial Intelligence
How Greenlight Financial built an autonomous SOC solution on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
Greenlight Financial resolves more than 90 percent of up to 4,000 security and risk cases each month without human intervention. Greenlight’s Luna uses Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, infrastructure for building, connecting, and optimizing agents at scale. Specifically, Greenlight uses AgentCore runtime, a capability of Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, to host Luna’s agent code. It uses AgentCore memory, a capability of Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, to support its tiered multi-agent system. This avoids the need to build and operate these capabilities in-house. Luna triages dark web breach-card alerts, identity anomalies, and financial-risk events in seconds.
This post explains how Greenlight Financial built an autonomous security operations center (SOC) solution on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. We cover its multi-tiered supervisor architecture, more than 30 specialized agents, episodic memory for continuous learning, and expansion from SOC use cases into financial risk triage. We share production metrics, infrastructure decisions, and patterns for building autonomous security operations in regulated industries.
What Greenlight needed to solve
Greenlight Financial provides financial products for families: debit cards, savings tools, and connected devices such as the Family Hub and Pet Tracker. The company processes sensitive financial data at scale under the same regulatory requirements as major banks.
Greenlight’s SOC receives 3,000–4,000 security and risk alerts per month from four primary vectors:
- Dark web breach cards – Card Network and internal threat intel flag Greenlight customer cards found on the dark web.
- Identity and access anomalies – Unusual login patterns, privilege escalations, and policy violations across Identity Provider (IdP) and internal systems.
- Infrastructure alerts – Signals from Signals from EDR (Endpoint Detection and Response), SIEM (Security Information and Event Management), Asset Inventory, and other observability tools.
- Financial risk events – Suspicious transaction patterns, compliance triggers, and fraud indicators from card processing systems.
Each alert demands cross-referencing multiple data sources before an analyst can render a verdict. A single dark web breach card notification requires checking whether the card is active, deduplicating against prior notifications, reviewing customer session data, and checking open support tickets. This workflow takes a human analyst 15-30 minutes per case. At 4,000 cases per month, that math breaks.
Greenlight needed a system that could:
- Triage and resolve routine cases autonomously at machine speed.
- Escalate complex cases with full context to human analysts.
- Learn from resolution patterns to improve accuracy over time.
- Operate within financial services compliance guardrails.
Architecture: Tiered multi-agent system on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
Greenlight built Luna as a hierarchical multi-agent system on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. The architecture follows a tiered supervisor pattern that mirrors how human SOC teams operate. L1 handles volume, and L2 handles complexity.
Tier 1 supervisor: High-volume triage
Tier 1 supervisor uses an advanced language model available through Amazon Bedrock running on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore runtime within an Amazon Virtual Private Cloud (Amazon VPC). The runtime uses private subnets and direct code deployment through a ZIP file and Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3). It handles initial triage of incoming cases by orchestrating more than 30 specialized agents:
| Domain | What the agent does | 
| Identity and Access | Checks login history, MFA status, session anomalies | 
| Endpoint Detection | Pulls endpoint alerts, process trees, IOC matches | 
| Observability | Correlates infrastructure metrics with alert timing | 
| Asset Inventory | Maps affected assets, ownership, exposure surface | 
| Data Analytics | Queries historical patterns and baseline deviations | 
| Payment Processing | Verifies card status, transaction history, account state | 
| Customer Experience | Reviews customer session behavior around incident time | 
| Customer Support | Checks related open tickets, prior complaints | 
| Code and Repositories | Traces code changes correlated with alerts | 
| Project Tracking | Links incidents to recent deployments or known issues | 
| Threat Intelligence | Enriches IOCs with external threat context | 
| Automation (SOAR) | Executes approved remediation playbooks | 
The Tier 1 supervisor receives cases through two paths: Amazon API Gateway, which exposes the Luna Queue API and a Model Context Protocol (MCP) endpoint, and Tines SOAR for automated alert ingestion. It determines which specialized agents to invoke based on alert type, synthesizes their findings, and renders a verdict. The median triage time for routine cases is single-digit seconds.
Tier 2 supervisor: Deep-dive investigation
Cases that exceed Tier 1’s confidence threshold escalate to a Tier 2 supervisor using an advanced foundation model on Amazon Bedrock with extended reasoning capabilities. This agent handles the 10 percent of cases that require multi-step reasoning:
- Re-investigates escalated cases with deeper cross-source correlation.
- Invokes specialized agents through boto3 with expanded context windows.
- Chains reasoning across 3–5 data sources to establish causality.
- Produces detailed investigation reports with evidence chains for human review.
The Tier 2 supervisor runs on a scheduled basis, using Amazon EventBridge rate triggers and Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) queue completions to batch-process escalated cases, and on demand for urgent Tier 1-escalated cases.
Entry points for different personas
Different teams engage Luna in different ways, so the application exposes three entry points. These range from fully automated alert ingestion to interactive, on-demand investigation. Each entry point maps to a persona and how their work arrives:
- Tines SOAR – Primary volume driver. Automated alert ingestion feeds cases directly into Tier 1.
- Security, Risk, and ProdOps engineers – Direct API access for ad-hoc investigation requests.
- Claude Desktop extension – Chat-based interface for on-call engineers. An engineer opens the extension, describes what they want investigated, and Luna executes a deep-dive with full tool access.
Memory and learning: How Luna gets smarter over time
The memory layer is built on AgentCore memory. This layer is what separates Luna from a stateless triage tool. It supports pattern recognition, deduplication, and continuous accuracy improvement.
Episodic memory (30-day rolling window)
Stores recent events and resolution outcomes. When a new alert arrives, Luna checks: “Have I seen this pattern in the last 30 days? What was the verdict? Is this a known behavior that I should allowlist?”
Concrete example: A Greenlight infrastructure role generates a specific access pattern every Tuesday at 3 AM for scheduled maintenance. Without memory, Luna would flag this every week. With episodic memory, Luna learned after the first resolution that this pattern is expected and auto-allowlists it.
Long-term memory
Persists semantic preferences and resolution templates beyond the 30-day window:
- “This access pattern is expected because that’s the role’s purpose.”
- Greenlight’s historical case data shows “Cards from this specific dark web source have a 73 percent false-positive rate – prioritize deduplication.”
- Resolution templates for recurring case types that encode institutional knowledge.
Case-learnings pipeline
A dedicated pipeline feeds resolution outcomes back into the system:
- Ingestion – An AWS Lambda function captures every case resolution from Tines events.
- Learnings + Dedup – DynamoDB stores resolution patterns and deduplicates similar cases. When Luna resolves a case the same way three times, it records that as a confirmed pattern.
- Digest – A Lambda function processes new learnings into actionable context that supervisors consume at inference time.
- Feedback loop – Resolution learnings feed back into Tier 1, improving first-pass accuracy incrementally.
This pipeline drove Luna’s autonomous resolution rate from 83 percent (Tier 1 only) to more than 90 percent (Tier 1, Tier 2, and learnings).
Expanding from SOC into financial risk triage
Greenlight expanded Luna into financial risk assessment within two months of the SOC deployment. The architectural changes were minimal: new specialized agents and a risk-domain supervisor layered onto the existing infrastructure.
Dark web breach card workflow
When a Greenlight customer card appears on the dark web, Luna executes this workflow autonomously:
- Ingest – Threat intel providers (Mastercard, internal feeds) report compromised card numbers.
- Verify – Luna queries Galileo: Does this card belong to Greenlight? Is it currently active? What’s the recent transaction history?
- Deduplicate – DynamoDB check: Is this a repeat notification? Has this card already been remediated? Multiple providers often report the same breach.
- Cross-reference – Query Mixpanel for customer session anomalies, Zendesk for related tickets, and internal fraud scoring.
- Assess and act – Determine risk levels. Low risk: log and monitor. Medium risk: flag for review. High risk: escalate to human analysts with full evidence chain.
Greenlight receives hundreds of breach card notifications daily. Luna processes each in seconds. A human analyst doing the same work, logging into Galileo, checking DynamoDB, opening Mixpanel, searching Zendesk, takes 15-30 minutes per card.
Results
The following table tracks Greenlight’s security operations on the metrics that matter most to the SOC. It compares three stages: manual triage before Luna, Tier 1 automation, and the full Tier 1 and Tier 2 system.
| Metric | Before Luna | With Tier 1 | With Tier 1 and Tier 2 | 
| Autonomous resolution rate | 0% (all manual) | 83% | More than 90% | 
| Cases processed per month | 3,000-4,000 | 3,000-4,000 | 3,000-4,000 | 
| Median time-to-triage (routine) | 15-30 minutes | Seconds | Seconds | 
| Human analyst escalations | 100% of cases | 17% | <10% | 
| Cost avoidance | Baseline | Significant | Equivalent of multiple full-time employees | 
| Risk reduction | Baseline | Faster detection | Consistent 24/7 quality | 
Estimated analyst time avoided:
Based on Greenlight’s case volume and manual handling-time measurements, processing 4,000 cases at 15–30 minutes each would require approximately 1,000–2,000 analyst hours per month. Greenlight reports that Luna autonomously resolves more than 90 percent of these cases, avoiding an estimated 900–1,800 hours of routine manual work each month. Analysts can focus instead on cases that require human judgment.
The risk reduction comes from two factors: speed (seconds compared to minutes reduces the exposure window) and consistency (Luna applies the same triage logic at 3 AM on Saturday that it does at 10 AM on Tuesday, with no fatigue and no shortcuts).
Five lessons from building Luna
Building Luna and expanding it from security operations into financial risk surfaced five lessons for teams building multi-agent systems in regulated environments:
1. Start with a bounded domain, then expand horizontally
Greenlight started with security triage because the success criteria were clear: resolve the case correctly or escalate. After the pattern proved reliable at 83 percent resolution, expanding financial risk required adding new specialized agents and a risk-domain supervisor, not rebuilding the architecture.
2. Mirror your human team structure
The Tier 1/Tier 2 pattern maps directly to how SOC teams already operate. L1 analysts handle volume with playbooks. L2 analysts handle the complex cases with investigation skills. This made trust-building with the security team faster. They understood the model intuitively because it matched their own escalation logic.
3. Memory compounds in value
The episodic and long-term memory layer is what moved Luna from 83 percent to more than 90 percent. Each resolved case teaches Luna something: a new allowlisted pattern, a confirmed false positive source, a resolution template. After 6 months of operation, Luna has accumulated institutional knowledge that would take a new human analyst months to build.
4. Triage first, action later
In a regulated environment, Greenlight designed Luna to triage and recommend, not to take autonomous remediation actions without explicit policy approval. The risk expansion follows the same principle. Luna provides evidence supporting its recommendation. In this human-in-the-loop model, a human analyst or an approved automated policy authorizes and executes remediation. This separation satisfied Greenlight’s compliance requirements and built trust with the risk team.
5. Share specialized agents across domains
When Greenlight expanded into financial risk, they reused existing specialized agents (Datadog, Zendesk, Mixpanel) and added domain-specific ones (Galileo, fraud scoring). The same agent that checks Zendesk tickets for security cases also checks them for risk cases. This reduces maintenance overhead and helps keep consistency across domains.
Infrastructure stack
Luna runs entirely on managed AWS services. Amazon Bedrock AgentCore is the orchestration runtime, and the rest of the stack handles scheduling, messaging, state, secrets, and integration. The following table lists each service and its role in the infrastructure:
| Service | Role | 
| Amazon Bedrock AgentCore | Multi-agent orchestration runtime. VPC deployment, private subnets, direct code through ZIP and S3 | 
| Amazon EventBridge | Scheduled rate-based triggers for Tier 2 deep-dive triage cycles | 
| Amazon SNS | Queue completions and notification routing between tiers | 
| Amazon DynamoDB | Learnings storage, case deduplication, resolution pattern persistence | 
| Amazon S3 | Agent packages and Terraform state management | 
| Amazon CloudWatch Logs | 30-day retention for audit trails and compliance evidence | 
| AWS Secrets Manager | External API credentials | 
| AWS Lambda | Ingestion, resolution post-processing, kickoff, and digest functions | 
| Amazon API Gateway | Luna Queue API and MCP endpoint for external integrations | 
What Greenlight is building next
Building on the security and risk foundation, Greenlight is extending Luna’s multi-agent pattern into new operational domains and tooling:
- Full risk domain coverage – Autonomous triage for financial and business risk cases (in progress, launched about one month ago).
- Product operations – Exploring AWS DevOps Agent for incident investigation, root-cause analysis, and mitigation guidance. Greenlight is also evaluating how Luna’s existing agents could support operational investigations where their capabilities overlap.
- Custom operational workflows – Exploring AWS DevOps Agent custom agents, skills, and Model Context Protocol integrations for repeatable operational workflows and access to Greenlight’s internal tools.
- AWS DevOps Agent and skills – Combining the UI and skills framework of AWS DevOps Agent for script execution workflows (90-second execution time limit).
- Well-Architected reviews – Exploring Model Context Protocol servers for automated infrastructure assessments against AWS best practices.
Conclusion
According to Greenlight’s production measurements, Luna autonomously resolves more than 90 percent of the company’s security and risk cases and processes up to 4,000 cases each month. Cases requiring additional judgment are escalated to human analysts. This human-in-the-loop approach allows Greenlight to automate routine triage while retaining control over remediation decisions.
Teams in other regulated industries can apply the same approach by starting with a bounded use case, defining clear escalation criteria, and adding specialized agents and memory as the system matures. After the initial pattern proves reliable, teams can extend it to related operational domains.
To learn more, visit the Amazon Bedrock AgentCore product page and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore documentation.

articles.title: À 503,17 km/h sur une route publique, la Yangwang U9 Xtreme de BYD devient la voiture la plus rapide du monde
articles.text:
503,17 km/h. Voici le nouveau record du monde de vitesse pour une voiture de route et il est signé BYD, enfin Yangwang, la marque haut de gamme du constructeur chinois. Le bolide utilisé est l’hypercar électrique homologuée pour la route U9 Xtreme, qui développe la « bagatelle » de 3 019 chevaux, plus du double des 1 287 chevaux de la U9 de série, pilotée par l’Allemand Marc Basseng.
Selon le communiqué de BYD publié ce vendredi 6 novembre, cette performance permet de décrocher deux records du monde Guinness : celui de la voiture de série la plus rapide lors d’un essai dans un seul sens de circulation, toutes motorisations confondues, et celui de la voiture électrique de série la plus rapide.
Un record effectué sur une route publique fermée à la circulation
La Yangwang U9 Xtreme bat ainsi son propre record réalisé en septembre 2025 qui était de 496,22 km/h. Cette prouesse avait été obtenue sur le circuit de Papenburg, en Allemagne. À l’époque, elle dépassait l’indétrônable Bugatti Chiron Super Sport 300+ et ses 490,48 km/h atteint en août 2019, sur piste également.
Cette fois, les 503,17 km/h ont été atteints sur une route publique, fermée à la circulation pour l’occasion. Pour revoir un record dans de telles conditions, il faut remonter au mois de novembre 2017 lorsque Koenigsegg avait atteint 457,49 km/h (447,19 km/h dans les deux sens) sur une route fermée près de Pahrump, dans le Nevada aux États-Unis.
Pour le record de BYD, la route retenue est la E11 dans la région d’Al Dhafra, à Abu Dhabi. Dans un tel environnement, les précautions sont de mise, car « « contrairement à un circuit d’essai dédié, une voie publique présente des contraintes spécifiques, qui rendent la précision, la stabilité et la confiance dans le véhicule plus essentielles que jamais. À ces vitesses extrêmes, chaque détail compte » », explique le pilote.
Au total, un tronçon de 10 kilomètres a été fermé à la circulation, dans lequel se dessine une ligne droite de 7 kilomètres. En raison de la proximité avec le désert et de la circulation quotidienne, la chaussée a dû être balayée avant la tentative, puis chaque mètre du parcours « « a fait l’objet d’une inspection minutieuse afin de retirer toute particule métallique résiduelle provenant des brosses de nettoyage » », raconte BYD.
Il ne fallait pas revivre l’impressionnant crash survenu en Chine quelques jours plus tôt, lors d’essais préliminaires à ce record. À environ 360 km/h, une Yangwang U9 Xtreme était sortie de sa trajectoire, percutant de plein fouet la barrière. Miraculeusement, le pilote chinois de BYD s’était extirpé lui-même, sans blessures.
Le 31 octobre, deux premières tentatives ont plafonné à 490 km/h. Pendant la nuit, les ingénieurs de la marque ont modifié l’angle de l’aileron arrière, l’amortissement et la pression des pneus, ce qui a permis d’atteindre les 503,17 km/h le lendemain. BYD n’a pas annoncé de tentative dans les deux sens de circulation, la mesure retenue par Koenigsegg en 2017 pour son record à 447,19 km/h de moyenne. Toutefois, il ne faudrait pas que cela donne des idées aux 30 futurs propriétaires de la U9 Xtreme.

articles.title: NASA-Mission Artemis 2: Physikalische Schockwelle stört GPS auf der Erde
articles.text:
Artemis 2: Warum die NASA-Rakete GPS-Signale auf der Erde stört
Am 1. April 2026 startete mit Artemis 2 die erste bemannte Mondmission seit 1972. Eine Trägerrakete des Space Launch Systems (SLS) beförderte in Cape Canaveral das Orion-Raumschiff mit vier Astronaut:innen an Bord in den Weltraum.
Trägerrakete brachte Ionosphäre der Erde durcheinander
Wie nun eine Studie zeigt, hatte die Mission verblüffende Konsequenzen. Die Manöver der Rakete veränderten demnach die Ionosphäre der Erde. Dies störte wiederum GPS-Signale.
Hinter der Studie steckt ein Forschungsteams der National Cheng Kung University in Taiwan und des NASA Goddard Space Flight Center. Sie ist in der Zeitschrift Geophysical Research Letters erschienen.
Schockwelle durch Raketenstart
Laut der Studie registrierten bodengestützte GPS-Systeme bei drei Manövern Veränderungen der Elektronendichte in der Ionosphäre. Dabei handelt es sich um den elektrisch geladener Bereich der oberen Erdatmosphäre. Er erstreckt sich in einer Höhe zwischen 60 bis 1000 Kilometern über der Erdoberfläche.
Die erste Irritation der Ionosphäre passierte beim Take-off der Rakete, der Schockwellen und Gravitationswellen auslöste. Dadurch entstand buchstäblich ein Loch in der Ionosphäre, das allerdings nur kurz Bestand hatte.
5000 Kilometer langes Loch in Ionosphäre
Gut zwei Stunden nach dem Start folgte das Manöver zur Anhebung des Apogäum, also des am weitesten von der Erde entfernten Punktes in der Umlaufbahn. Dabei wird ein Raketentriebwerk am erdnächsten Punkt gezündet, durch den Schub erhöht sich die Geschwindigkeit.
Diese Zündung erzeugte wiederum Schockwellen und ein Loch in der Ionosphäre über Nordamerika. Es hatte laut der Studie eine Länge von rund 5000 Kilometern.
Zum ersten Mal drei Störungen über derselben Region
Gut einen Tag nach dem Take-off leitete die Rakete das Manöver zur Einleitung der translunaren Flugbahn ein. Auch hier entstand über Nordamerika ein Loch, das allerdings zu schwächeren ionosphärischen Störungen führte.
Laut der Studie hat mit Artemis 2 zum ersten Mal eine einzelne Mission während drei Manövern Störungen über derselben Region hervorgerufen.
Veränderung von Elektronendichte irritiert GPS
Das Problem an der Sache ist nun: Die Veränderungen der Konzentration von Elektronen in der Ionosphäre haben ganz konkrete Folgen auf der Erde. Sie stören nämlich den Empfang von GPS-Signalen.
Empfangsgeräte von GPS-Signalen auf der Erde bestimmen ihre Position, indem sie ständig ihre Entfernung zu GPS-Satelliten messen. Wenn sich die Dichte von freien Elektronen in der oberen Atmosphäre ändert, kommen die Signale früher oder langsamer als gewöhnlich an. Dies kann nicht nur bei Raketenmanövern, sondern auch bei Sonnenstürmen passieren.
Gefahr für selbstfahrende Autos und Drohnen
Die Störungen können zu ungenauen Messungen führen. Mit gefährlichen Konsequenzen. „Ein Positionsfehler von nur wenigen Metern reicht aus, um ein autonom fahrendes Auto zum Spurwechsel zu veranlassen“, sagte Studienautor Charles Lin zu dem Portal Space.com.
Laut Lin könnten die GPS-Aussetzer auch Folgen für die Positionsbestimmung von Drohnen haben. Ob es wegen Artemis 2 zu Unfällen kam, ist nicht bekannt. Für zukünftige Missionen könnte die Forschung aber wichtige Erkenntnisse liefern.
Gravitationswellen? Geht’s noch? Wisst ihr überhaupt was das ist ?

articles.title: Claude peut désormais analyser les dépenses des utilisateurs grâce à son nouvel outil de finance personnelle
articles.text:
Anthopic a déployé « Personal Finance », une nouvelle fonctionnalité qui permet à Claude d’analyser les comptes bancaires des utilisateurs.
Alors que son entrée en Bourse approche, Anthropic multiplie les annonces. La société a lancé Smart Reports, une option qui permet aux patrons de surveiller le travail de leurs équipes. Elle a aussi bridé Claude afin de l’empêcher de recopier des jeux vidéo existants. Anthropic s’intéresse désormais au compte bancaire de ses utilisateurs. Du moins, un peu plus que d’habitude.
Un assistant de poche spécialisé en finance
Le domaine des finances personnelles intéresse de plus en plus les géants de l’IA : OpenAI a ouvert le bal en mai dernier en proposant des conseils budgétaires à ses utilisateurs et Anthropic vient à son tour de sauter le pas. La société a, en effet, annoncé hier l’arrivée de la fonction « Personal Finance » sur Claude.
Cette option disponible en version bêta permet aux utilisateurs qui le souhaitent de relier leurs comptes et cartes au chatbot via le service Plaid, puis de poser des questions en langage naturel comme « Où est passé mon argent ce mois-ci ? », « Que me reste-t-il avant mon jour de paye ? », « Quelle somme puis-je mettre de côté ce mois-ci ? » ou encore « Puis-je me permettre de partir en voyage ? ».
Selon la firme, l’outil serait capable de détecter les prélèvements en double, les frais inattendus ou les factures dont le montant a évolué. Il peut aussi aider à calculer des intérêts ou à décrypter le jargon financier. Via « Personal Finance », Claude peut également générer des graphiques, des échéanciers et des tableaux sur mesure qu’il est possible d’éditer par la suite.
- Excellente compréhension des consignes complexes
- Très bon niveau en rédaction
- Analyse de longs documents efficace
Un accès encadré aux comptes bancaires des utilisateurs
Bien sûr, confier ses relevés bancaires à un chatbot ne va pas de soi. Anthropic se veut rassurant et explique que Claude n’a jamais accès à votre mot de passe bancaire. L’entreprise explique également que « pour les comptes que vous choisissez de connecter (et uniquement ceux-là), Claude a accès au nom de la banque, au nom de chaque compte, à son type, à ses quatre derniers chiffres, aux soldes et aux limites de crédit, ainsi qu’à l’historique des transactions remontant jusqu’à deux ans. »
D’autres garde-fous sont également prévus : Claude ne peut ni déplacer, ni gérer ni investir de l’argent et les échanges avec le chatbot ne servent pas à entraîner les modèles de la firme. Il est également possible de déconnecter son compte à tout moment. Bien sûr, Claude peut se tromper et il est vivement conseillé de vérifier l’exactitude de ses dires : « demandez quelles opérations correspondent à un montant donné et vérifiez les chiffres importants auprès de votre banque », explique notamment Anthropic. Pour un outil censé aider à gérer des finances, l’aveu ferait presque sourire.
La fonctionnalité « Personal Finance » est réservée aux abonnés Pro, Max et Ultra qui résident aux États-Unis. Aucune date de déploiement n’a, pour l’instant, été communiquée pour la France et le reste du monde. En attendant, Anthropic a d’ores et déjà des plans pour l’avenir : la société invite les banques, gestionnaires de patrimoine et sociétés de service financier qui le souhaitent à collaborer avec ses équipes.

articles.title: Massive wants to help small businesses turn Google searches into customers
articles.text:
For four years, Segun Olaiya worked in local search engine optimisation (SEO) in the United States, helping large operations, including AT&T and businesses in San Diego and Texas, improve their visibility in online searches.
But he observed that marketing technology largely catered to organisations with multiple locations, leaving smaller businesses overlooked.
“Most of this kind of industry, which is marketing technology, is usually focused around big organisations that have multiple locations across cities and states that want to be as visible as possible. But small businesses are not always really paid attention to,” Olaiya told TechCabal in an interview.
He began helping small business owners manually optimise their Google Business Profiles. Some reported receiving more calls from customers who found them through organic search rather than paid advertisements. “They were like, ‘Oh, now I get more calls,’” he recalled.
“Maybe I can actually just make this into a proper thing and then automate it,” Olaiya said.
That idea led to Massive in 2026, an AI-powered local SEO platform that helps businesses like restaurants, clinics, salons and home-service providers improve their visibility on Google. It combines automated optimisation with human account managers who monitor search rankings and review business profiles.
Why being on Google is not enough
Being listed on Google does not guarantee a business will appear prominently when potential customers search for its services. Google says local search results are mainly based on three factors: relevance, distance, and prominence.
Relevance measures how closely a business profile matches a search; distance considers how far the business is from the person searching. Prominence reflects how well-known it is online, including through customer reviews and links from other websites.
Olaiya says businesses can improve their visibility by ensuring their Google Business Profiles accurately describe their services, keeping their business information consistent across online platforms, and encouraging customers to leave reviews.
For many Nigerian microenterprises, establishing an online presence remains a challenge. A 2024 Research ICT Africa report, based on a survey of 718 Nigerian microenterprises, found that only 13% used the internet for business activities. Just 0.3% had their own websites, while 6.7% had a social media presence. The report also found that 37% lacked the digital skills to use the internet productively for their businesses.
Yet online search can be an important source of customers. A study commissioned by Google and conducted by Public First found that, on average, businesses surveyed in Nigeria reported that around 11% to 20% of their new customers found them through Google Search. The survey covered 140 business leaders from small, medium, and large online businesses.
For business owners already occupied with running their operations, keeping their online profiles competitive adds another responsibility. Olaiya says Google’s frequent changes to its local search priorities make it difficult for businesses to know what to update or improve.
“Typically, the problem is that Google usually changes the rules. More often than not, they usually change what they really care about,” he said.
He said many business owners lack the time to keep up with these changes and work out how to improve their visibility, so some outsource the task to specialists to focus on running their businesses.
He believes this makes services like Massive more appealing to businesses that would rather focus on their daily operations.
How Massive manages local search for businesses
Massive’s process begins with a free visibility scan on its website, TryMassive.ai. Business owners enter their business name and a search term potential customers might use, such as “barber near me.” The platform then generates a map showing where the business appears in Google Maps search results across the surrounding area.
Olaiya said the scan simulates searches from 49 points around a business by default, showing how its ranking changes depending on where a potential customer is searching.
He said the system uses Google data to estimate what someone searching from each location would see.
“The Massive system goes and simulates that search across, by default, 49 points in the city,” he said. “We simulate it as if somebody physically went to that physical location and then opened their phones and they search for that keyword.”
Businesses looking to assess a wider area can increase the number of points to 81 or 100. Massive also calculates an average ranking across the locations, giving business owners an overview of their visibility in the area.
Those who want to improve their rankings can subscribe to the platform and book a 30-minute call with a member of Massive’s team. During the call, an account manager reviews their existing results and business profile, discusses their goals and explains the changes Massive recommends. Olaiya describes the arrangement as a “done-for-you experience”, adding that “we literally do everything for you”.
The platform uses AI to analyse business profiles and identify areas for improvement. It reviews a business’s existing description and recommends changes that could help Google better understand its services and the customers it wants to reach.
“Once a business is imported to Massive, the system itself automatically reviews the existing description and then recommends the proper description,” Olaiya said.
Massive also checks for inconsistencies in a business’s online information, such as differences between the descriptions on its website and social media pages. For businesses without websites, Olaiya said the platform can automatically generate one using their business information and update it as changes are made. It also recommends changes to ensure that the business presents consistent information across its online platforms.
Some tasks run automatically without requiring the business owner or an account manager to intervene. When a customer leaves a Google review, Massive analyses it, considers the business’s services and communication style, and drafts a response. Olaiya said the system can then publish the response directly on Google without the business owner having to log in and reply.
However, account managers remain involved in reviewing recommendations and handling issues that require human judgement. Olaiya said some businesses upload images or other content that Google may not accept. When the system flags such material, an account manager can contact the business owner, explain the problem, and advise them on what to change.
“We believe that a person should talk to another person instead of us just running a system that AI is talking to the person,” he said.
Massive runs visibility scans every two weeks to track changes in a business’s rankings. If rankings do not improve after two weeks, Olaiya said the team changes its strategy. Subsequent scans can also reveal declines, allowing the team to identify changes that may have affected a business’s position and reverse them where necessary.
Olaiya said that after three to four months of optimisation, once a business’s profile is stable, the system becomes largely autonomous and continues monitoring its visibility with less direct intervention from the team.
Who Massive is building for
Massive targets businesses whose customers need to find them in a particular location. Olaiya identified four main categories.
The first is businesses with physical outlets, including restaurants, gyms, salons, spas, and law firms. The second is service-area businesses, such as electricians and lawn-care companies, which travel to customers rather than operate from a fixed location. The third is multi-location businesses that want customers searching for their services to find the outlet closest to them. The fourth is new businesses entering an established market and trying to attract local customers alongside existing competitors.
Olaiya said businesses in less populated areas could have an advantage because they face fewer competitors and can serve a wider area.
“For places that are not very dense, the businesses there who happen to find Massive, for example, are at a good advantage because they have fewer competitors and they can cover even a bigger area,” he said.
However, not every business needs local SEO. Olaiya said Massive is not designed for online-only businesses, software companies, newsrooms or blogs whose customers do not need to find a physical location or service provider nearby.
Massive earns revenue through monthly and annual subscriptions. Its website lists the service at ₦18,000 ($13.37) a month per business location, or ₦216,000 ($160.47) for a year. The subscription includes profile optimisation, weekly Google Business Profile updates, review management, map-rank tracking and a dedicated account manager. Businesses can also try the full service free for 14 days before subscribing. Olaiya said the company has more than 20 active customers.
Olaiya said many small businesses rely on social media to reach customers without fully exploring how Google Search can help them attract new ones. He
sees educating business owners about local SEO as an important part of growing Massive’s customer base.
“One of the things that can drive the product is to educate business owners to say, ‘ You need this,” he said. “We are currently bootstrapping, and it is quite limiting how far we can go in terms of reaching out to the business owners. But we are on it.”
Building Massive’s next phase
Massive is entering a market with established international platforms offering similar local SEO and location-marketing services. Olaiya identified Polish platform Localo, San Diego-based SOCi, a]nd New York-headquartered Yext as competitors.
He said Massive is cheaper than competitors outside Africa, which he believes allows it to serve African businesses and small businesses in other markets. Massive’s published monthly price is lower than Localo’s $49 Single Business plan, which falls to $39 per month with annual billing.
However, the two platforms offer different service models. Localo provides software tools for businesses to manage their own Google Business Profiles. Massive offers a done-for-you service with an account manager. SOCi and Yext do not display comparable prices on their enterprise pricing pages, instead directing prospective customers to request customised information or a demo.
However, the company still has to convince business owners that local search visibility is worth paying for and expand its reach beyond its current customer base. Olaiya said he wants Massive to demonstrate its value through the business decisions customers make after improving their visibility.
“Over the next year, I need to have at least 100 businesses who can attest to the fact that Massive has helped them expand their businesses,” he said.
For him, that would mean more than businesses appearing higher in Google Maps results. He wants customers to use the visibility insights to make decisions such as opening another outlet or moving into a new area. He said such expansion would show that Massive had made a significant impact on their businesses.

articles.title: US Agencies Urge Organizations to Harden Refrigeration Controllers
articles.text:
The US government is urging healthcare, chemical, food, and transportation organizations to harden their industrial refrigeration and cold chain monitoring systems.
Over the past weeks, threat actors have been hacking monitoring systems to tamper with fridges and freezers in supermarkets and blood banks across Europe, causing millions in losses.
Hundreds of supermarkets were hit on October 11, when the attackers turned the temperatures in fridges to 50 degrees Celsius (122 degrees Fahrenheit) and set freezers to defrost, spoiling food and, in some cases, causing fires.
A second wave of attacks hit more than 100 supermarkets and a blood bank this week, but only supermarkets suffered losses. Quick action from staff prevented the compromise of blood products and samples, the French Blood Establishment (EFS) said.
Russian hacktivist groups such as Noname057(16) and Z-Pentest Alliance reportedly claimed hacking Danfoss, leading to speculation that they mounted the supermarket attacks. However, nothing has been confirmed, and Iranian hacktivists or state-sponsored hackers may also be responsible, BBC notes.
CISA, the FBI, HHS, USDA, and DoT say they “are aware of malicious cyber actors targeting electronic temperature controllers and commercial refrigeration controllers in retail grocery and cold storage facilities.”
“The actors may exploit vulnerabilities or weaknesses in unpatched or internet-accessible controllers to remotely alter settings and force units into continuous heating and defrost cycles, which can cause widespread inventory loss and equipment hazards,” the agencies note (PDF).
Hackers may exploit authentication bypasses, code injection, and weak configurations to access the management systems and tamper with refrigerator and cold storage systems’ temperature or cause denial-of-view conditions, the agencies say.
According to internet intelligence firm Censys, out of 6,695 internet-exposed refrigeration controllers identified on October 9, only 3,124 (or 47%) remain accessible from the web as of November 5.
The company’s analysis covers the widely used Copeland/Dixell XWEB and Danfoss StoreView controllers: XWEB exposure dropped 35% (3,708 to 2,420), while StoreView dropped 76% (3,004 to 708).
Per the US government’s recommendations, taking the control systems off the internet is the best action organizations can take to prevent attacks. If web access is necessary, these systems should be protected by a firewall or edge device.
Organizations should also isolate OT devices, restrict access to trusted identities, enforce strong password policies and phishing-resistant multifactor authentication, keep systems updated, maintain backups offsite, and enable logging and monitoring.

articles.title: Edera's Object Capability Bounded Authority Promises to Isolate Credentials From AI Agent Workloads
articles.text:
Promising to secure autonomous AI agent workloads, Edera has launched Object Capability Bounded Authority, a security model that isolates autonomous AI workloads and Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers from sensitive credentials. Led by Edera co-founder and distinguished engineer Ariadne Conill, known for her contributions to low-level open-source security, the technology tackles one of modern enterprise architecture's most urgent challenges by enforcing granular object capabilities directly at the hypervisor level, keeping AI agents strictly contained without handing them standard access credentials. The Object Capability Bounded Authority is a security model that isolates autonomous AI workloads and MCPl servers from sensitive credentials while enforcing granular access controls.
As organisations increasingly deploy autonomous coding agents and external tool integrations into production, they routinely expose sensitive API tokens, cloud keys, and administrative access credentials directly to execution environments that remain vulnerable to prompt injection and supply chain manipulation.
Bounded Authority's core architecture decouples the operational authority needed to perform a task from the underlying credentials required to execute it. Traditional container security relies heavily on boundary isolation combined with static secrets injected into environment variables or configuration files. If an LLM-driven agent is compromised, attackers can typically extract those tokens and pivot laterally across internal systems. Edera proposes addressing this with hypervisor-enforced object capabilities that restrict an agent to narrowly defined actions without placing secrets inside the workload itself. For instance, an AI coding assistant can be authorised to modify a single GitHub repository without a personal access token, ensuring any compromise remains strictly bounded to that context.
To achieve this granular isolation, several runtime components are integrated into its Agent Runtime framework. Credential-free API access is handled by capcurl, routing authorised requests through an isolated broker while keeping the underlying authentication material hidden from the agent. Similarly, capsudo manages scoped command execution, allowing workloads to run specific privileged commands without acquiring standing administrative privileges or root access. Workload identity is cryptographically verified using SPIFFE and SPIRE integrations, establishing mutual TLS connections and service identities without relying on long-lived static secrets.
These architectural mechanisms extend directly to Model Context Protocol servers, which frequently act as high-value targets by bridging large language models with enterprise tools and databases. By defining explicit object capabilities at the infrastructure layer, security teams can restrict an MCP server to specific external resources and commands, preventing unchecked access even if the host model behaves unexpectedly or encounters a prompt injection vulnerability. This approach complements hardware-enforced runtime isolation by shrinking the blast radius of potential compromises from environment-wide access down to discrete, task-specific actions.
Engineering teams evaluating autonomous agents often spend significant development effort building custom credential-handling middleware and ad hoc permission proxies. The Bounded Authority promises to shift this enforcement mechanism into the hypervisor and runtime layers, standardising how enterprise systems provision authority to non-deterministic software. Initial functionality, focused on scoped command execution and workload identity, was released, with credential-brokered API access and deep orchestrator integrations to follow as part of the broader Project Lunchbox initiative.

articles.title: Nintendo’s latest Zelda remake already circulating online as a Switch 2 ROM — OpenAI-assisted software jailbreak, new game dumper let pirates share game for free, immediately following release
articles.text:
Nintendo’s latest Zelda remake already circulating online as a Switch 2 ROM — OpenAI-assisted software jailbreak, new game dumper let pirates share game for free, immediately following release
Nintendo's new Zelda remake has barely launched, but hackers have already found a way to extract its game files and circulate copies online
Nintendo’s remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time has reportedly been dumped the same day it launched on the Switch 2. The game launched today, but ONE jailbreak says copies of the original 1.0.0 release and its 1.1.1 update are already circulating outside Nintendo's official distribution channels. The update reportedly weighs 23 GB.
The leak is not entirely surprising. Physical copies had already started turning up at buyers' homes several days before the release date. Footage of the game was already appearing online by Nov. 1. Those early cartridges gave hackers access to the remake before most players could get their hands on it, with some gamers sharing videos of themselves playing the game on social media. 
However, the game still remains far from playable on PC, with emulators struggling to render its graphics correctly. Some users encountered washed-out visuals or black screens, while others saw terrain bleeding through objects or could not get past the title screen.
Notably, the game is identified by title ID 0400486024DEC000, with its report naming two tools involved in extracting the files: ‘ns2jb and OunceCake’. The first is a software jailbreak developed by security researcher Sammy ‘pepsipu’ Hajhamid.
Last month, Hajhamid explained how he managed to get code running on Nintendo's latest console without installing a modchip, and also described what the exploit does: "This lets us run homebrew, reverse engineer and mod Switch 2 games, back up save files off the Switch, and access most of the Switch 2’s peripherals through MMIO. To my knowledge, it’s the first such exploit for the Switch 2."
That opens up several possibilities for homebrew developers and researchers as well as pirates, but ns2jb has limitations. It is a tethered jailbreak, meaning it has to be activated again after the console restarts. The exploit also does not provide unrestricted kernel access. The same extraction method has reportedly been used with two other games: Deltarune Chapters 1-4 and Mario Kart World.
This is not the first time hackers have found a way into Nintendo's hardware. Just a day after Switch 2 went on sale in June 2025, an exploit that allowed hackers to run custom code on the system popped up, although it did not provide root access or a full jailbreak. Cartridge-based backups have also caused headaches. In August this year, we reported that Nintendo had targeted more than 400 GitHub repositories, with 401 repos removed following seven Digital Millennium Copyright Act (DMCA) notices. Several Yuzu forks were among the affected projects.
Nintendo has not publicly commented on the Ocarina of Time dump or the nsj2b exploit yet. However, SmileBASIC 4, the application used to launch the jailbreak, has disappeared from the Nintendo eShop following the exploit’s disclosure.

Newton Gitonga is a tech journalist covering gadgets, PC hardware, AI, data centers, and the wider tech industry. His interest in technology started early, taking apart things around the house to see how they worked, often to his dad’s frustration. His curiosity sometimes got the better of him, including a few failed attempts to fix laptops, one of them a gifted Dell XPS. He has previously written for Notebookcheck, ZyCrypto, CoinCentral, and Crypto News Flash.
