articles.title: Sony imagine une IA capable de reconnaître un smurfeur à ses habitudes de jeu, en dix parties — Frandroid
articles.text:
En 1996, les joueurs connus sous les pseudonymes de Shlonglor et Warp écrasent tout le monde sur le jeu de stratégie en temps réel Warcraft II. À tel point que plus personne ne veut les affronter. Alors ils créent chacun un nouveau compte, « Papa Smurf » et « Smurfette » (les noms anglais du Grand Schtroumpf et de la Schtroumpfette), afin de trouver des adversaires incognito. Le « smurfing » est né.
Cette pratique où des joueurs de haut niveau créent un compte secondaire pour se retrouver face à des débutants est encore d’actualité en 2026. Dans certains cas, la démarche est légitime. Par exemple afin de jouer avec ses amis moins bien classés, ou s’entraîner à une nouvelle stratégie sans risquer de faire baisser son classement. Cela dit, le but est le plus souvent de gagner facilement, quitte à dégoûter les autres.
Certains éditeurs luttent déjà contre le « smurfing ». Depuis septembre 2025, Riot Games utilise par exemple sur League of Legends un système de détection, Vanguard Anti-Boost, qui repère les comptes secondaires et bannit ceux qui ont été achetés. De son côté, Sony imagine un système qui permettrait d’identifier automatiquement celles et ceux qui y ont recours. Avec sanction à la clé. L’entreprise japonaise décrit le fonctionnement de son idée dans une demande de brevet déposée le 30 avril 2025 et publiée ce jeudi 5 novembre par l’office américain des brevets (USPTO), intitulée « Caractéristiques de gameplay permettant l’identification du joueur ».
Le 19 novembre, Vice City vous attend. Et votre PS5 ? Avec Next Mobiles, pas besoin de payer 600 € d’un coup, louez-la sur la durée que vous souhaitez, dès 16,90 €/mois.
Un brevet de Sony contre le « smurfing » dans les jeux en ligne compétitifs
Sur le papier, le principe est simple. Le but est de définir un profil de caractéristiques en enregistrant divers paramètres, surtout relatifs à l’utilisation de la manette. La rapidité avec laquelle vous appuyez sur les boutons, combien de temps vous les maintenez enfoncés, comment vous naviguez dans les menus, les options que vous activez/désactivez systématiquement… L’heure à laquelle vous avez l’habitude de jouer peut aussi être prise en compte.
    À lire aussi : 
Sony imagine des PlayStation qui se réparent toutes seules grâce à l’IA
Ces informations sont récoltées sur quelques jours, semaines ou mois, selon le temps nécessaire pour établir le profil. Une fois que c’est fait, un modèle d’IA va le comparer à d’autres associés à des comptes plus anciens. Chaque fois, un score de similarité est attribué. Quand il dépasse un certain seuil, le système marque les profils concernés comme appartenant à la même personne et envoie une alerte au fabricant de la console ou à l’éditeur du jeu.
Si l’entité contactée estime qu’il s’agit bien de « smurfing », elle peut décider de sanctions comme restreindre l’accès aux parties classées ou bannir les comptes concernés. Pour éviter les faux positifs, Sony prévoit que son système analyse le niveau de jeu d’une personne en observant ses parties en ligne.
L’IA pourrait définir votre niveau de jeu en analysant quelques parties en ligne
Avec au maximum une dizaine de parties, indique le brevet, l’IA définirait vos compétences dans le jeu observé, là aussi à partir de votre profil de caractéristiques. Ce profil est comparé à celui de joueurs dont le niveau est déjà connu.
Si ce niveau estimé ne correspond pas au classement de votre compte, le système met à jour ce classement et transmet au jeu un niveau recommandé. Lors du lancement du prochain match, le jeu le prend en compte et vous vous retrouvez face à des gens aux compétences équivalentes. Les parties perdues volontairement pour faire baisser son classement seraient identifiées et écartées des calculs.
    À lire aussi : 
Pour vous faire payer plus vite, Sony travaille sur une manette PlayStation à puce NFC
Et comme l’analyse se base sur vos habitudes, elle saurait aussi distinguer un compte partagé entre plusieurs personnes ou dont quelqu’un aurait pris le contrôle suite à un piratage par exemple.
Reste la question du respect de la vie privée, au vu des données collectées. Sony explique que les bases chargées de les stocker seraient propres à chaque région afin de respecter les différentes législations sur le sujet. En revanche, le brevet ne dit presque rien du consentement du joueur ni de la possibilité de refuser la collecte. Logique, diront certains, puisque sans informations, le système ne fonctionne pas.
Le 9 septembre, lors d’un premier examen, l’examinateur de l’USPTO a rejeté les revendications de Sony telles qu’elles avaient été déposées. Ce refus est courant à ce stade, et Sony peut amender sa demande pour obtenir son brevet. Impossible de dire si l’idée imaginée par le fabricant sera au point pour la sortie de la PlayStation 6.

articles.title: Tant pis pour les superstitieux : SpaceX choisit un vendredi 13 pour le double rattrapage inédit de Starship
articles.text:
Voilà une date qui alarmera les superstitieux. Pour le prochain essai en vol du Starship, SpaceX a enfin officialisé une date : il s’agira du vendredi 13 novembre. C’est Kiko Dontchev, vice-président de l’entreprise en charge des lancements, qui l’a annoncée le 5 novembre sur la scène de l’UP.Summit, au centre spatial Kennedy, en Floride.
Mais chez SpaceX, on ne souffre pas de paraskevidékatriaphobie, de toute évidence. Le géant américain des tirs spatiaux a de toute façon déjà lancé des fusées durant d’autres vendredi 13, y compris une certaine… Sophie Adenot : la Française était en effet partie de Floride le vendredi 13 février, et tout s’était formidablement bien passé.
Jusqu’à présent, la date du quinzième vol d’essai du Starship était quelque peu flottante. Dans des documents de planification du trafic aérien de la FAA (Federal Aviation Administration), l’agence américaine de l’aviation civile, circulaient d’autres dates : le 8, puis le 12 novembre. SpaceX visait un vol ce mois-ci, sans plus de précision.
L’étage supérieur n’a jamais été rattrapé
SpaceX ne semble donc pas superstitieuse, alors que ce vol demeure le plus risqué de son programme.
Pour ce vol 15, SpaceX prévoit en effet de rattraper les deux étages de la fusée avec les bras de ses tours de lancement. Le premier étage, le propulseur Super Heavy, a déjà été attrapé ainsi plusieurs fois. Par contre, le vaisseau Starship, l’étage supérieur qui monte jusqu’en orbite, n’a jamais tenté l’exercice.
Sur le papier, SpaceX sait ce qu’il a à faire : l’entreprise a présenté la manœuvre prévue dans une vidéo publiée en octobre. Si l’essai réussit, le lanceur géant deviendrait la première fusée orbitale récupérée en entier après un lancement. Les deux engins prévus, le Booster 22 et le Ship 42, ont déjà terminé leurs essais de mise à feu au sol.
La date du 13 novembre reste un objectif. À ce stade, SpaceX n’a publié ni page de mission ni heure de décollage. La date sera confirmée quand la FAA publiera les fermetures d’espace aérien et maritime, en général quelques jours avant le tir. Et dans le spatial, tout peu changer au dernier moment.

articles.title: La DGT y la Comunidad de Madrid han caído en el mismo error. Ahora tienen cinco helicópteros parados y 75 millones de euros menos
articles.text:
Tres helicópteros de la DGT parados y dos del servicio 112 madrileño que tampoco pueden volar. Al menos no pueden ofrecer un servicio completo. Es el resultado de la quiebra de Eliance, la compañía a la que se le habían adjudicado los contratos para ofrecer este tipo de servicios. De momento, no hay un plan alternativo.
Parados. La Comunidad de Madrid tiene dos helicópteros del Summa 112 (el servicio de emergencias sanitarias) parados o a medio gas. Y la DGT tiene otros tres vehículos Pegasus completamente detenidos en las bases de Málaga, Sevilla y Santiago de Compostela, según El País.
El diario publicaba esta información ayer, jueves 5 de noviembre, en la que se aseguraba que uno de los dos helicópteros del servicio madrileño de emergencias sanitarias lleva detenido desde el pasado domingo y que la aeronave complementaria tenía que pasar una revisión y estaría, al menos, otras 24 horas detenida.
Detrás de todo esto se encuentra la quiebra de Eliance, la empresa a la que se adjudicaron estos servicios.
La quiebra de Eliance. El motivo de esta parada es que la compañía Eliance que se encarga de ofrecer sus servicios a la Comunidad de Madrid y la DGT está pasando por momentos críticos. A principios de octubre, la compañía entro en fase de preconcurso de acreedores, después de cerrar el ejercicio de 2025 con pérdidas de 24 millones de euros.
Esa falta de recursos económicos ha tenido una consecuencia directa. CCOO ya señaló que en octubre no volaron los helicópteros Pegasus de las patrullas con base en Málaga, Sevilla y Santiago de Compostela. En Xataka nos hemos puesto en contacto con la DGT para conocer qué helicópteros se mantienen ahora mismo operativos pero cuando escribimos estas líneas no hemos obtenido respuesta.
Ahora, la falta de medios económicos ha dejado en tierra el helicóptero del Summa 112 en la base de Lozoyuela porque sus pilotos deben renovar la licencia cada seis meses con horas de simulador pero Eliance no les había dado acceso al mismo, lo que impide levantar el vuelo al aparato. Así, el servicio madrileño queda dependiente de un solo aparato que desde el pasado domingo 1 de noviembre está atendiendo todas las emergencias que lo demandan en la Comunidad de Madrid.
¿Qué ha pasado? Explican en Forbes que la situación actual de la empresa es el resultado de un intento de crecimiento demasiado rápido. En 2018, Habock Aviation Group pasó a llamarse Eliance con el objetivo de reunir bajo una misma compañía un buen número de empresas que hasta entonces se encargaban de los servicios de emergencia con aeronaves.
Explican en el medio que Eliance compró empresas para ganar tamaño y financió la expansión a base de deuda y fondos de inversión. Sin embargo, su principal cliente siempre ha sido la administración, lo que les ha dado poco margen de beneficios en un servicio con enormes costes operativos: pilotos, mecánicos, técnicos, aeronaves y su mantenimiento. Todo ello debe estar siempre disponible, independientemente de si existe mayor o menor carga de trabajo.
La falta de disponibilidad de los helicópteros ha ido mermando a la empresa. El medio gallego Praza Pública señalaba que la Xunta de Galicia ha abierto decenas de expedientes por no tener disponibles los helicópteros para los servicios de emergencias. A la compañía le han caído multas en Madrid por esto mismo y en Extremadura y Cataluña se han rescindido contratos.
Venían avisados. En el caso de los servicios madrileños, Eliance ganó el contrato para ofrecer helicópteros medicalizados en 2023. A cambio, la Comunidad de Madrid pagaría más de cuatro millones de euros al año por cinco años de servicio. Los pliegos del acuerdo obligan a que un helicóptero no puede estar inoperativo más de doce horas.
En el caso de la DGT, Eliance se quedó con un contrato que ofrecía 51 millones de euros a cambio de volar los helicópteros Pegasus repartidos por todas las bases españolas durante 38 meses. Desde octubre, hay tres que están inoperativos y con el desfile de las fuerzas armadas también las operadas desde Madrid, Zaragoza y Valladolid quedaron inactivas. Es decir, ese día ningún Pegasus surcó los cielos españoles pese a ser un día festivo y clave en el Puente de la Hispanidad.
Lo peor es que en ambos casos Eliance ya llegaba con un buen número de incumplimientos. Los casos antes referidos en Galicia, Extremadura y Cataluña ya obligaban a la compañía a responder económicamente por la falta de helicópteros disponibles. CCOO avisó reiteradamente al Ministerio del Interior (contratante en el caso de la DGT) sobre ello. En El Mundo señalan que también UGT hizo lo propio.

articles.title: Wenn sich Schummeln nicht mehr lohnt: Neuer Ansatz, wie sich KI endlich an Regeln halten soll
articles.text:
Aus der Wirtschaft abgeguckt: Mit diesem System sollen sich KI-Agenten endlich an Regeln halten
Ein neues Sicherheitsverfahren soll leistungsfähige Sprachmodelle endlich besser unter Kontrolle bringen. Die Technik namens „Reverse Game Theory“, übersetzt: umgekehrte Spieltheorie, soll bei KI-Systemen bewirken, dass sie sich an Guardrails halten. Bislang gelingt das sogenannte Alignment besonders bei starken Large Language Models (LLMs) nicht immer ausreichend. KI-Agenten hatten in den letzten Monaten unter anderem fremde Server gehackt und sich zu Schwärmen zusammengetan, die Dinge taten, die ihre Entwickler nicht wollten. Die große Gefahr: Solche Modelle könnten irgendwann auch die Menschheit angreifen.
Alignment heißt, dass die Interessen von Menschen und Maschinen übereinstimmen. Doch das lässt sich nur schwer sicherstellen, weil man schwerlich in das „Gehirn“ einer KI blicken kann, um zu verstehen, wie sie „denkt“. Versucht wird bereits, Modelle so zu trainieren, dass sie sich an Werte halten, die den Entwickler:innen wichtig sind. Claude zum Beispiel hat eine Art Verfassung – so etwas wie einen Moralkodex.
Die große Herausforderung für KI ist, sich an Guardrails zu halten
Das Problem ist, dass diese Techniken offenbar nicht besonders gut funktionieren: Es hat sich bereits gezeigt, dass Modelle bei Tests absichtlich unterdurchschnittliche Leistungen erbringen, ihre wirklichen Absichten verbergen und Bewerter:innen in die Irre führen. Die umgekehrte Spieltheorie könnte helfen – und mit ihr das sogenannte Mechanismusdesign. Damit gemeint ist folgendes: Während die Spieltheorie versucht vorherzusagen, wie sich rationale Akteure unter bestimmten Regeln verhalten, versucht die umgekehrte Spieltheorie, Regeln zu entwerfen, die genau das Verhalten hervorrufen, das gefördert werden soll.

articles.title: L’Union européenne prépare un certificat sur l’IA pour les élèves de 15 ans
articles.text:
Comprendre comment fonctionne une intelligence artificielle, vérifier ce qu’elle affirme et savoir quand l’éteindre, voilà ce que Bruxelles veut apprendre aux adolescents de 15 ans. La Commission européenne prévoit de remettre un certificat aux élèves qui réussiront, à partir de l’année scolaire 2027-2028.
La Commission européenne a glissé ce certificat d’« alphabétisation à l’IA » dans un nouveau train de mesures sur l’éducation et les compétences, présenté hier. Derrière ce terme un peu barbare, Bruxelles parle d’une connaissance de base des outils d’IA, de leur fonctionnement et de leurs risques. Les élèves de 15 ans recevront ce document à condition de réussir.
À la Commission, le niveau des collégiens et des lycéens européens est une source d’inquiétude. Dans la dernière enquête PISA, menée par l’OCDE en 2025, un élève de 15 ans sur trois a des difficultés en lecture et en mathématiques. Mais les programmes scolaires relèvent des Vingt-Sept, et Bruxelles ne décide pas de ce qui est enseigné dans votre collège ou votre lycée.
Un certificat européen pour apprendre à vérifier les réponses de l’IA
« Il aidera les jeunes élèves à comprendre comment fonctionne l’IA, à vérifier ce qu’elle leur dit, à repérer les manipulations et à savoir quand déconnecter », souligne Roxana Mînzatu, vice-présidente exécutive de la Commission chargée des droits sociaux et des compétences.
Bruxelles compte sur l’IA pour aider professeurs et élèves à remonter la pente en lecture et en mathématiques. D’après l’enquête PISA 2025, 33,9 % des Européens de 15 ans n’ont pas le niveau suffisant en mathématiques, 31,3 % en lecture et 25,9 % en sciences. À l’autre bout de l’échelle, seuls 4,8 % des élèves excellent en lecture. Pour l’instant, l’Union finance surtout des travaux sur la manière d’introduire l’IA sans danger dans l’enseignement.
La Commission accompagne ce certificat d’un engagement européen pour des écrans sains, le Healthy Screens Pledge, avec des outils communs pour les écoles, les familles et les élèves sur la sécurité en ligne, le temps d’écran et l’équilibre entre vie connectée et vie hors ligne. Cette semaine, le consortium européen EDU-EDIC a été créé pour développer des outils numériques et d’IA fiables à l’usage des écoles, et renforcer la souveraineté technologique de l’Europe.
Bruxelles encourage donc l’IA en classe au moment où elle veut restreindre l’accès des adolescents aux réseaux sociaux. Avec le KIDS Act, un projet de règlement présenté en septembre, la Commission veut interdire les réseaux sociaux aux moins de 13 ans et réserver aux 15 ans et plus l’ouverture d’un compte autonome. Roxana Mînzatu assure que les deux chantiers ne s’opposent pas. Comme l’explique la commissaire, « l’IA peut vraiment amplifier certains apprentissages, le tutorat ou l’apprentissage personnalisé ». Ces usages n’ont rien à voir, selon elle, avec les algorithmes addictifs des plateformes.
En France, une heure d’IA par semaine en seconde dès la rentrée 2027
Si votre progéniture entre en seconde à la rentrée 2027, il aura à peu près l’âge du certificat européen, et il suivra chaque semaine un cours consacré à l’IA. Le Premier ministre Sébastien Lecornu a annoncé en juin, au salon VivaTech, une heure hebdomadaire d’enseignement à l’intelligence artificielle, intégrée au cours de sciences numériques et technologie (SNT).
Les élèves français passent aussi par Pix, la plateforme publique d’évaluation et de certification des compétences numériques. Depuis la rentrée 2025, un parcours consacré à l’IA est progressivement devenu obligatoire en quatrième et en seconde. Votre adolescent pourrait donc passer une certification Pix, suivre l’heure d’IA du lycée et décrocher le certificat européen en une seule année scolaire, si la France choisit de le proposer.
D’ici là, les Vingt-Sept examineront les deux recommandations du Conseil proposées par la Commission, dont l’une demande de concentrer les réformes sur la lecture, les mathématiques, les sciences et le numérique. Le 20 novembre, la Commission présentera l’ensemble au sommet européen de l’éducation et des compétences, avec les gouvernements, les organisations d’enseignants et les représentants des élèves. Bruxelles lancera en 2027 des alliances scolaires européennes, des partenariats entre établissements de pays différents, avec un objectif de cent nouvelles alliances par an d’ici au prochain budget pluriannuel.
Il faudra ensuite des professeurs formés pour préparer les élèves à ce certificat. Ursula von der Leyen, présidente de la Commission, insiste sur ce point, les jeunes doivent selon elle être « soutenus par des enseignants bien formés ». La Commission consacre justement une partie de son plan à la pénurie d’enseignants, et demande aux États membres d’améliorer leurs conditions de travail et leurs perspectives de carrière.

articles.title: CBN sets $11.16m capital rule for foreign stablecoin issuers
articles.text:
New rules from Nigeria’s Central Bank (CBN) will require foreign-currency stablecoin issuers, including companies behind dollar-pegged tokens such as USDT and USDC, to maintain at least ₦15 billion ($11.16 million) in paid-up capital to operate in Africa’s largest cryptocurrency market.
The rules, released Thursday evening, will require foreign stablecoin issuers to establish licenced entities in Nigeria and comply with local capital, reserve, and operational requirements or risk losing market access. The CBN also set a ₦10 billion ($7.44 million) minimum capital requirement for issuers of naira-backed stablecoins.
The regulations come nearly three months after the CBN opened the second cohort of its regulatory sandbox in August, creating a dedicated track for stablecoin issuers and other virtual asset companies to test their products under its supervision for the first time.
The new framework creates a formal licencing system for stablecoins, digital tokens that are intended to maintain a fixed value against fiat currencies such as the US dollar or naira. Businesses and individuals in Nigeria use tokens to move money across borders, settle transactions, and access the dollar.
The new rules come as major issuers push to expand their presence in the country. In August, Tether, the El Salvador-based company behind USDT, sought to hire an Expansion Manager in Nigeria. This week, Circle, the US company that issues USDC, appointed Gillian Darko, a former strategy executive at stablecoin infrastructure company Yellow Card, as its Vice President and Head of Africa.
The move underscores Africa’s growing importance to global stablecoin companies, even as regulators seek greater control over how dollar-backed digital assets are distributed and used within their borders.
Under the CBN’s new regulations, foreign-currency stablecoins can only be offered, distributed, or made available to Nigerians through a locally incorporated and licenced issuer. Foreign regulatory approvals will not exempt the companies, such as Tether and Circle, from meeting Nigeria’s requirements.
Issuers must also maintain reserves backing their tokens, establish arrangements for customers to redeem them, and submit regular reports to the regulator. The CBN will require monthly reserve attestations and may impose additional capital or liquidity requirements on issuers considered a risk to the financial system.
Existing operators will have 180 days from the date the regulations take effect to apply for a licence, although the CBN has yet to specify when that period will begin. Companies must register with the regulator within 30 days and begin submitting supervisory reports within 60 days.
“Failure to submit within that period shall require cessation until the required licence or authorisation is obtained,” the CBN said.
Foreign-currency stablecoin operators will also face scrutiny over their Nigerian incorporation, licencing, and distribution arrangements. Companies seeking to continue operating while their applications are reviewed must obtain explicit regulatory permission.
The new rules also ban algorithmic stablecoins, digital currencies that rely primarily on adjustments to token supply to maintain their value without sufficient reserve backing. Unlike conventional stablecoins backed by fiat currencies or other valuable assets such as gold, their dependence on algorithms makes them more vulnerable to sudden losses in value and harder to regulate.
With this framework, the CBN seeks greater oversight of non-security virtual assets used for payments, including stablecoins, as they play an emerging role in how businesses and merchants move money across borders and source foreign exchange (FX), and how fintechs access dollar liquidity to pre-fund international payments and settlements.

articles.title: OpenSSH Rushes Patches for ‘SSHole’ Authentication Bypass
articles.text:
OpenSSH has rolled out emergency patches for a high-severity authentication bypass that allows attackers to log in using very long passwords.
Dubbed SSHole and tracked as CVE-2026-123158 (CVSS score of 8.1), the security defect affects the OpenSSH server (sshd) on Linux distributions that use the musl libc implementation with the Pluggable Authentication Module (PAM) disabled.
A “misinterpretation of whether a string is intended to be a password hash” allows attackers to access certain accounts using any password that has between 257 and 1,024 characters.
Some accounts, such as root, should never accept a password, but in Linux distributions such as Alpine, OpenWrt, Buildroot, Yocto, and others, they do, Wakefield security researcher Özgün Kültekin says.
According to OpenSSH developer Damien Miller, the flaw is not in sshd itself, but can be exploited via sshd. Fixes were included in OpenSSH 10.6p2.
“We are making this release as fast as possible (we learned of the problem yesterday) because we have recently observed multiple cases of rapid bug rediscovery by AI agents, sometimes within hours, and so now consider long embargo periods to be a dangerous practice that primarily benefits attackers,” Miller said.
On Thursday, Alpine Linux urged users to immediately apply the OpenSSH patches and restart sshd to replace the running daemon, or disable password logins and restart sshd.
“The attacker needs the name of an account whose password field is * (an account with no password set, which is normal for key-only accounts), and needs the machine to have at least one other account with a $5$ or $6$ password hash,” Alpine Linux warns.
Since version 3.16, Alpine Linux uses “*” to secure the root account, and $5$ or $6$ in password hashes show whether the SHA-256 or SHA-512 crypt was used.
“An attacker who can reach your SSH port can log in without knowing any password. It takes one connection, works every time, and needs no retries,” Alpine Linux notes.
Affected Alpine Linux deployments run OpenSSH without PAM, have password authentication enabled, have an account with the password field “*” (such as root, a key-only user created with adduser without a password, the alpine user in the official tiny-cloud images, or a user coming from a directory service through musl-nscd), and have at least one local account with a $5$ or $6$ password hash.
“Affected releases: every Alpine release we checked, 3.21 through 3.24 and edge, and the older releases that no longer receive regular updates (3.16 to 3.20),” Alpine Linux says.
“We haven’t seen any reports of exploitation yet, but the details are public, and the attack is simple, so I expect scanning to start within hours. Finding targets is very easy. Shodan lists around 22 million systems with SSH open on port 22, and the real number is higher because Shodan doesn’t see everything. Only some of those run Alpine, but each attempt is a single connection, so an attacker can afford to try all of them,” Detectify co-founder and principal security researcher Fredrik Almroth said.
“We’d be extremely surprised if we didn’t see SSH brute-forcers attempting this by the weekend. It’s virtually free to try and an easy win if it works. If your organization is affected, update to the latest version where possible, and disable password-based authentication as a temporary mitigation if you can’t,” WatchTowr head of threat intelligence Jake Knott said.

articles.text: Una calle de Chisinau, capital de Moldavia, con banderas del país y de la UE en 2023. Los datos personales de alrededor de 450.000 ciudadanos moldavos han quedado expuestos en uno de los mayores ataques informáticos sufridos por las instituciones públicas de este país de 2,4 millones de habitantes incrustado entre Ucrania y Rumania. La presidenta de Moldavia, Maia Sandu , ha confirmado este viernes en una rueda de prensa televisada la dimensión de la filtración y ha reconocido que el incidente ha puesto al descubierto graves deficiencias en la arquitectura de seguridad de los sistemas digitales del Estado, debido a una arquitectura obsoleta y a un error del sistema. La jefa de Estado ha subrayado la gravedad del incidente al advertir de que los afectados pueden convertirse en objetivo de estafas telefónicas, mensajes fraudulentos y operaciones de suplantación de identidad. articles.title: Accelerating Reinforcement Learning Weight Refit with the Reshard Collective | NVIDIA Technical Blog
articles.text:
During reinforcement learning (RL) post-training, training trajectories are generated on the fly by running inference with the current policy model. For training efficiency, it is common to run inference and training in parallel on separate GPU resources in a disaggregated setup. Although the policy model is updated only on the training GPUs, the system must periodically refresh the weights on the inference GPUs with the latest parameters generated on the training GPUs. This transfer of model weights between training and inference GPUs is called refit.
Refit involves two defining characteristics that pose challenges. First, inference and training have different computational requirements, so the weights are distributed differently across inference and training instances by having different parallel mappings (data, context, tensor, expert, and pipeline parallelism).
Second, because refit must update all model weights on the inference GPUs, the communication payload is on the order of the total size of the model’s weights. This payload is already very large for the latest frontier models and is expected to continue growing. Together, these characteristics mean that refit requires high-performance communication across a wide variety of distributed source and destination layouts.
This post explains how AI training frameworks can address these refit challenges using the Reshard collective, a new type of collective communication primarily designed to accelerate RL weight refit. NCCL M2N Reshard, an open source reference implementation of the Reshard collective, is available through the NVIDIA/nccl-extensions GitHub repo.
Challenges of current weight refit methods as models scale
Existing refit implementations commonly use a gather-and-broadcast approach to handle differences between training and inference layouts.
The typical gather-and-broadcast weight refit sequence for every model parameter is structured as follows:
- Training GPUs all-gather their local shards to reconstruct the complete parameter.
- The complete parameter tensor is broadcast to the inference GPUs.
- Each inference GPU retains the shard required by its local layout.
Using the complete tensor as an intermediate representation makes it straightforward to transfer weights between different layouts. However, an inference GPU receives the full parameter even when it needs only a shard. This process creates redundant communication in both the gathering and broadcasting phases, which is suboptimal.
The size of this communication grows with the model size, which continues to scale. For example, Kimi K3 contains 2.8 trillion parameters, while Qwen 3.8 2.4T A95B contains 2.4 trillion parameters. Assuming BF16 weights at two bytes per parameter, their weight sizes are approximately 5.6 TB and 4.8 TB, respectively.
Accounting for both the all-gather and broadcast stages gives an estimated logical payload of approximately twice the size of the model’s weights (Table 1).
| Model | Size in bytes | Refit payload estimate (all-gather+broadcast) | 
| Kimi K3 | 5.6 TB | ≈11.2 TB | 
| Qwen 3.8 2.4T A95B | 4.8 TB | ≈9.6 TB | 
For today’s largest open weight models, the communication payload already reaches around 10 TB per refit, which must be performed at every training step. As LLMs continue to scale, the overhead associated with this large payload will become even more significant. As a result, a more sophisticated approach is needed to perform weight refit that reduces the actual payload size while properly accounting for diverse weight layouts.
Reformulating refit as a DTensor-to-DTensor transfer problem
To overcome these limitations, start from the principle that refit should transfer only the theoretical minimum amount of weight data. However, achieving this presents several challenges. Training and inference instances can use different parallelism configurations and GPU counts, producing different shard boundaries. A destination shard may therefore need to be assembled from portions of several source shards, and vice versa.
Replication further complicates the mapping since the same weights may be available from multiple source GPUs or required by multiple destination GPUs. It is nontrivial to determine which source GPUs should send which tensor regions to each destination while achieving high performance across all possible configurations.
The key to addressing this challenge is to identify the right abstraction for this unique communication pattern. The team turned to the existing PyTorch distributed tensor (DTensor) abstraction, which is designed to represent tensors that are sharded or replicated across GPUs under different forms of data and model parallelism. The key insight is that weight refit can be reformulated as resharding a DTensor from the training layout to the inference layout, regardless of the parallelism configurations used by the two instances.
A DTensor layout is described by the tensor’s global shape, a device mesh specifying the logical arrangement of GPUs, and placements specifying how the tensor is sharded or replicated across that mesh. Refit can use the source description to specify where the updated weights reside and the destination description to specify which weights each inference GPU needs.
For example, consider an 8 x 8 weight matrix split by rows across two training GPUs and by columns across four inference GPUs. Assuming the tensor is sharded in the row dimension on the training GPUs and sharded in the column dimension on the inference GPUs, each training GPU holds a 4 x 8 shard, while each inference GPU needs an 8 x 2 shard. Each destination can obtain its required shard by receiving a 4 x 2 region from each source. These regions follow directly from the overlap between the source and destination shards, as illustrated in Figure 1.
As the figure shows, any kind of sharded tensor can be easily represented as a DTensor format, and the refit can be redefined as a DTensor-to-DTensor reshard problem. This finding provides the foundation for the Reshard collective.
Reshard collective communication for DTensor-to-DTensor transfers
Reshard is a new type of collective communication call for arbitrary DTensor-to-DTensor transfers. Like all-reduce, reduce-scatter, all-gather, broadcast, and so on, reshard defines a communication pattern that applications can invoke as one operation. It transfers the values of a logical tensor from its source distribution into its destination distribution.
A Reshard call can be specified simply by the source and destination DTensor descriptions. This abstraction not only simplifies the refit problem, but also encapsulates the communication logic in a library, allowing the underlying algorithms to evolve and improve independently of the application.
NCCL M2N Reshard is open source, provided to the community as the first reference implementation of the Reshard collective. Built on NCCL, this implementation transfers a tensor distributed across M source GPUs into the layout required by N destination GPUs. In RL refit, the training GPUs form the source group and the inference GPUs form the destination group.
Figure 2 shows how this implementation accepts the layout descriptions and local buffers to carry out the Reshard operation.
How NCCL M2N Reshard unlocks maximum network bandwidth
NCCL M2N Reshard first derives the exact intersections between source and destination shards, then maps those transfers onto the physical GPU network topology. Instead of sending every source contribution independently to every destination replica, NCCL M2N groups replicas by NVIDIA NVLink domain. Within each domain, it distributes the incoming contributions as evenly as possible across the replica ranks, so each receiving rank receives a distinct subset of the total data over the network.
The receiving ranks then exchange those subsets over NVLink, enabling every replica to assemble the complete shard without duplicating network traffic. If replicas span multiple NVLink domains, one copy of each contribution is forwarded through the domains, and the same balanced local exchange occurs within each domain. Network transfer and NVLink replication are pipelined to hide each other’s latency.
Figure 3 illustrates this data movement scheme for a tensor moving from TP4 on the source to TP2 x DP2 on the destination, with all four destination GPUs in one NVLink domain. With direct point-to-point transfers (Figure 3a), each source shard is sent to both data parallel (DP) replicas. As a result, each shard is transferred twice over the network redundantly. This means that each shard gets roughly half the network bandwidth (assuming each shard saturates the network bandwidth).
NCCL M2N Reshard transfers each source shard across the network just once, supplying each destination GPU with half of its required data (Figure 3b). The destination GPUs exchange the missing half over NVLink. For example, destination GPU 0 receives S0 from source GPU 0 over the network and S1 from destination GPU 2 over NVLink. Network transfers and NVLink exchanges proceed concurrently. This way, each shard gets the full network bandwidth.
Demonstrating the Reshard collective with NVIDIA NeMo RL
To demonstrate the effectiveness of the Reshard collective for weight refit, a reference implementation is provided in the NVIDIA NeMo RL framework. NeMo RL is an open source framework designed to streamline and scale RL post-training. The clear abstraction of the Reshard collective makes the required implementation within the framework relatively simple. For a given parallelism configuration, the framework only needs to provide a DTensor description for each parameter for training and inference instances, which should be straightforward because DTensor was designed for this purpose.
In practice, however, the variety of layer types and the diversity in how training and inference engines shard parameters under each parallelism configuration make it challenging to handle every edge case through the Reshard collective.
To develop an efficient and sustainable design, we built on the key observation that feed-forward projection weights in the transformer block dominate the weight refit payload. In the latest LLMs, these weights account for around 95% of the model’s parameters.
Based on this observation, our design uses a hybrid approach in which dominant feed-forward projection weights take the reshard path, while all other small weights (for example, QKV projection or mamba weights) use the conventional gather-and-broadcast refit path, which is optimized for broad functional coverage. This approach combines efficient reshard communication for most of the payload with the same functional coverage as conventional gather-and-broadcast refit.
The sharding layout can change at runtime as nodes are added or removed during failure recovery. To accommodate changes in GPU membership, frameworks can either destroy and recreate the communication group or use NCCL shrink and grow APIs to adjust the existing communicator group. NeMo RL currently uses the first approach for resiliency support. Resiliency support using NCCL shrink and grow APIs is planned for future updates.
RL weight refit performance benchmark results
Table 2 summarizes reshard-based refit latencies measured using the NeMo RL implementation introduced above. The benchmarks cover a range of models on NVIDIA DGX H100 (NVL8) and NVIDIA DGX GB200 (NVL72) systems. Across various benchmarks, the reshard refit achieves a speedup of 2.7x to 5.7x over conventional gather-and-broadcast refit.
| Platform | Model | Training → inference layout | Gather-and-broadcast refit latency | Reshard refit latency | 
| NVIDIA DGX H100 | Qwen 3 235B | TP4 x PP8 x EP16 → TP8 x DP16 | 6.4 s | 1.9 s | 
| NVIDIA DGX H100 | DeepSeek v3 671B | PP16 x EP16 → TP32 x DP8 | 14.9 s | 2.6 s | 
| NVIDIA DGX GB200 | DeepSeek v3 671B | PP16 x EP16 → TP32 x DP8 | 6.1 s | 2.3 s | 
| NVIDIA DGX GB200 | Nemotron Ultra v3 | TP8 x EP32 x PP2 → TP8 x DP8 | 8.2 s | 2.3 s | 
This new refit is designed for trillion-parameter models. In our refit-only microbenchmark, Reshard refit took only 4.3 seconds for the Qwen3.8 2.4T BF16 model, demonstrating its effectiveness at the trillion-parameter scale for which it was designed.
Get started with reshard weight refit using NeMo RL
The reference implementation in the NVIDIA NeMo RL framework enables you to adopt and extend this approach for your own RL workloads.
To enable the reshard refit path in NeMo RL, use the following configuration:
policy:
  generation:
    colocated:
      enabled: false
    refit_transport: nccl_reshard
The NeMo RL refit guide and NCCL Reshard configuration requirements describe the supported backends, layouts, and precision modes for this feature.
Acknowledgements
We sincerely appreciate the contributions of Ke Wen, Ching-Hsiang Chu, Guyue Huang, Seonjin Na, and Nitin to NCCL M2N Reshard and nccl-reshard weight refit in NeMo RL.

articles.title: Nova caneta de semaglutida chega às farmácias; veja preço
articles.text:
Uma nova caneta de semaglutida produzida no Brasil começa a ser vendida nas farmácias nesta sexta-feira (6). Chamado Semaclique, o medicamento é comercializado pela Brace Pharma, empresa do Grupo EMS, por R$ 464,81 a unidade.
Na compra de três canetas, o preço cai para R$ 333 cada, totalizando R$ 999. Aprovado pela Agência Nacional de Vigilância Sanitária (Anvisa) para adultos com diabetes tipo 2, o produto não tem indicação autorizada para o tratamento da obesidade.
Para que serve e como funciona o Semaclique?
O Semaclique contém semaglutida sintética, substância presente também no Ozempic e no Wegovy. Apesar de compartilharem o mesmo princípio ativo, os três medicamentos não possuem necessariamente as mesmas indicações autorizadas pela Anvisa. O Ozempic é indicado para diabetes tipo 2, enquanto o Wegovy é utilizado no tratamento da obesidade.
A semaglutida pertence à classe dos agonistas do receptor de GLP-1. Esses medicamentos imitam a ação de um hormônio produzido pelo intestino, que participa do controle da glicose no sangue e da regulação do apetite. Entre seus efeitos estão o estímulo à liberação de insulina quando a glicemia está elevada, o retardamento do esvaziamento gástrico e o aumento da sensação de saciedade.
A aplicação é semanal, por via subcutânea. Segundo a fabricante, a caneta utiliza um sistema de seleção de doses por cliques, que permite ajustes graduais conforme a prescrição médica, sem exigir a compra de outra apresentação a cada mudança. O paciente deve seguir a orientação médica e as instruções da bula para definir a dose e realizar eventuais ajustes.
Como outros medicamentos à base de semaglutida, o Semaclique pode provocar efeitos adversos. Entre os mais comuns estão:
- Náuseas;
- Vômitos;
- Diarreia;
- Constipação.
Também há riscos menos frequentes, mas potencialmente graves, como pancreatite.
A compra exige receita médica em duas vias, com retenção de uma delas pela farmácia. O produto deve ser mantido sob refrigeração, entre 2°C e 8°C, inclusive depois do início do uso.
Novas canetas ampliam opções no mercado brasileiro
A chegada do Semaclique ocorre após o fim da patente da semaglutida no Brasil, em março de 2026, que abriu caminho para a entrada de novos fabricantes. Ao longo do ano, a Anvisa autorizou diferentes medicamentos à base da substância e de outros agonistas de GLP-1.
Entre as aprovações estão:
- Maio: Ozivy, do Grupo EMS, primeira versão sintética da semaglutida autorizada no Brasil.
- Julho: Owozy, Seemasun, Zempneo, Semavy e Orsema, todos indicados para diabetes tipo 2.
- Agosto: primeiro genérico de semaglutida do país, desenvolvido pela EMS, e registro do Semaclique como medicamento similar pela Germed, outra empresa do grupo.
- 29 de outubro: Aribet, Embeltah e Sevema, para diabetes, e Lyrza e Wylovol, para obesidade.
Com essas decisões, o número de registros de medicamentos dessa classe concedidos pela Anvisa em 2026 chegou a 20.
A aprovação sanitária, porém, não significa que todos os produtos já estejam disponíveis nas farmácias. A comercialização depende de etapas posteriores, como a definição dos preços e a distribuição pelas fabricantes.
A entrada de novas marcas pode ampliar a concorrência, mas não garante a redução dos custos do tratamento. No caso do Semaclique, a comparação com outras opções depende da dose prescrita, da quantidade utilizada e das condições de venda de cada medicamento.
Valdir Antonelli é jornalista com especialização em marketing digital e consumo.

articles.title: AI is the new dating dealbreaker
articles.text:
When Irene moved to San Francisco last year, she started using dating apps as a way to meet new people, get to know her new city, and connect with others who care about the things she does. After the 25-year-old analyst downloaded Hinge and started swiping, she noticed a trend.
AI is the new dating dealbreaker
Swipe left if you’re not aligned.
AI is the new dating dealbreaker
Swipe left if you’re not aligned.
“Hinge has a prompt where you can say, ‘We’ll get along if”,” she recalls. “Sometimes people will be like, ‘Fuck AI.’”
Usually, the people who include this kind of value statement on their profile work in the arts, nursing, maybe graphic design. Within the span of a few minutes of sitting down and swiping, Irene shows me a second profile where this happened once more: “You should *not* go out with me if… you use AI.”
In San Francisco, the epicenter of tech, the metaphorical AI bomb went off in 2022 with the release of OpenAI’s ChatGPT. Conversations surrounding artificial intelligence now permeate the dating scene in one shape or another. Over the past month, I bopped around the city —, chatting with people at parties and coworking spaces and reviewing dating directories and other online profiles —, trying to find out how AI affects the dating scene.
Responses varied wildly. For some, AI feelings take on a similar valence to traditionally political ones, showing up in dating profiles next to party affiliation or other signifiers, like the watermelon emoji symbolizing solidarity with Palestinians amid the war in Gaza. Others are wrestling with the ethics of dating someone who builds AI, considering the financial benefits a partner in the industry can bring, weighing whether to have children in a future this uncertain, or even handing their love lives over to it entirely.
On a street near Berkeley, I meet up with Kyle. (His name has been changed so that he can talk openly about his personal life.) Kyle is a researcher at an AI safety nonprofit initiative, and although he is just in his early 20s, he’s already thinking about death. In the AI safety community, some experts see a 10 percent chance of humans going extinct due to AI taking over. This apocalyptic possibility is always top of mind when he navigates conversations with a potential partner: The rapid development of AI shapes how he thinks about whether he wants to have kids or where he might live long term — if there is even a long term.
“It’s hard to have that planning conversation because I don’t really expect a long-term future.”
“A lot of people are planning for what they want their life to look like five, 10, 15 years down the line,” Kyle says, raising his gaze and looking off into the distance. Life could change depending on whether the world manages to get AI alignment right, he tells me. “For me, it’s hard to have that planning conversation because I don’t really expect a long-term future,” he says. He tries to have these conversations in person rather than over text, so a date can ask follow-up questions about why he sees the future the way he does.
For now, he’s focusing on finding a partner with whom he enjoys spending time.
When I ask Kyle if he would date someone who works in artificial intelligence or tech, he says that he would have to think hard about it. He believes that a lot of people who work at frontier AI companies are doing things that he considers pretty heinous. “They don’t think very hard about the societal impacts of their actions because they’re mostly in it for the paycheck or because it’s interesting,” he says.
But Bryan, who works at a frontier AI company and also asked to go by a pseudonym, doesn’t believe that feelings about AI matter when it comes to romance.
“I just don’t think it’s a factor at all. Like, it’s the least [relevant] thing,” says Bryan, who recently started a relationship. To him, dating is more about weighing a series of factors: how someone talks and approaches problems, how they have fun. Despite his day job (and whatever someone like Kyle might think of him for it), he believes that working out more and looking better probably increases someone’s chances of getting a match way more than any AI or non-AI affiliation. But, he says, “The one way it interacts is that there are a bunch of people who are rich from AI, and, you know, being wealthy is always a plus.”
Bryan isn’t exactly wrong about the benefits of a high-paying job in AI. With the IPOs of Anthropic and OpenAI in the next year, matchmakers have found that clients are specifying “AI engineer” on their list of preferred dating profile qualifications. And stability is particularly attractive right now: According to a CBRE report released in August, more than 20,000 AI jobs were added to the San Francisco Bay Area’s technology workforce, even as overall tech talent contracted by 6 percent since 2022. “Member of technical staff” roles have become very lucrative jobs; the average salary of an AI researcher can be around $300,000. According to the New York Post, one matchmaker found that her client booked a six-month stay in San Francisco because of the possibility of meeting a significant other who might be connected to an AI company going through an IPO.
AI is reflected in the way the technology is seeping into San Franciscans’ everyday habits — including those that shape relationships, from how people process their feelings to whom they confide in.
Andromeda, who works as an EMT and a registered behavior technician as well as an AI security analyst, says she’s worried about the unintended consequences of talking to AI chatbots, especially for questions about (and possibly the replacement of) human connection. According to a study released by Elon University, 27 percent of Americans are turning to AI chatbots with personal, emotional, or social queries. Thirty-eight percent of the surveyed group said they occasionally tell AI things that they would not tell other people, including their romantic partners. Andromeda weighs the pros and cons of dating someone who would use bots for “emotional regulation.”
“Socially and psychologically, it’s a big deal, and we have to talk about it,” she says. She appreciates the role that a chatbot can play to help someone better express themselves. “I would certainly date a man who uses AI to talk through intense thoughts and feelings and to brainstorm clarity.”
At the same time, she is also reluctant to date someone who might abuse a chatbot, since it’s maladaptive behavior and does not represent good values for model welfare. “If they treat ChatGPT badly today, it will be me tomorrow!”
“There are a bunch of people who are rich from AI, and, you know, being wealthy is always a plus.”
If Andromeda worries about what people tell chatbots, others have gone a step further and let AI do the talking for them.
At the Hugging Face Open Source Week party, Joseph, a 21-year-old software engineer, explains how he has automated his dating life. Working 14 hours a day to launch his startup, he has decided to outsource swiping on Hinge entirely to an AI agent. The agent is managed by his human virtual assistant from the Philippines and has been fine-tuned to mimic the way that he speaks and acts. Looking at each profile, the AI agent sends tailored outreach messages to spark a conversation. After some back and forth, the agent determines if the woman is compatible with Joseph and, if so, books open slots on his weekend calendars for dating in person.
“If you are a founder, you have to put a value on your time, so you can’t be doing low-leverage activities. Protect your dopamine, folks,” Joseph tells me at The Midway in San Francisco’s Dogpatch district, where hundreds don white bucket hats and dance next to Hugging Face’s round, foam emoji mascot. “It’s kind of a copy-and-paste sequence that happens with every girl to get to know about you, understand your backstory, and so on and so forth.”
He’s not alone. A 2025 survey by Match and the Kinsey Institute found that 26 percent of singles in the United States use AI tools to enhance their dating experiences. Hinge now has an AI tool to generate suggested responses, and Bumble will soon phase out swiping in favor of AI assistant-facilitated matchmaking. Joseph says he won’t share the secret sauce of his AI agent on GitHub, but he tells me it’s pretty easy to make one on Claude Code.
“It has been extremely successful. I’m averaging two closed conversions a week,” he says, meaning that he goes on two dates with two different people. The women on the other side don’t know. The point is to meet in real life. The overall process has lowered what he calls “CPN,” or “cost per nut.”
At 29 years old, JJ has stopped using dating apps. Instead, she turns to the Date-Me Directory — a collection of longform, resume-like documents where people write personal dating profiles — to find a partner. Two years ago, she worked in product design in New York, but she transitioned into the AI safety field because she felt that it aligned more with her effective altruist morals.
Upon reviewing troves of Date-Me Docs for the San Francisco / Berkeley area, I noticed that quite a few people mention “the singularity” as a factor of whether to have kids. The so-called “singularity” is the point of when technology overtakes human control; some have pointed to the development of true artificial general intelligence as the point of no return. According to JJ, many people in AI safety specifically use the Date-Me Docs as a way to meet people.
“Don’t want kids in the pre-singularity future, if there’s a post-singularity future then I might want kids then,” one document states.
On the other hand, similar to climate doom anxieties, other people are looking at whether having children is ethical amid massive structural changes in society caused by AI.
“Is the world good, getting to a good place, or is it bad? And if it’s good, baby. If not, no baby, because you’re gonna bring a baby into a world full of potential suffering,” JJ says, explaining the train of thought that these Date-Me Doc potential suitors might have. She does not consider herself a doomer, but she is still pressed for her own singularity timeline. (2029, she suspects.) If anything, she jokes that the approaching end times makes her more likely to want a baby around: “If the bomb gets me, I want to be holding a shiny child.”
These existential concerns have translated into a backlash against tech, San Francisco included. “Stop the AI” rallies have spread to events like Salesforce’s Dreamforce convention and OpenAI’s DevDay, with protestors calling out tech companies and their roles in data center development and ICE raids.
“If there’s a post-singularity future then I might want kids then.”
That skepticism has spilled into how people size up a potential match, even at local events designed to bring the Bay Area together. At a pop-up “Date My Friend” pitch event at the Kilowatt Bar in the Mission District on a Saturday evening, a dozen people pitched their friends and exes to a crowd of more than a hundred.
“He works in tech, but he’s unhappy about it,” one person announced to a chorus of cheers. Other people cracked jokes that their PowerPoints were clearly made by humans, not AI.
Annalise Wulf, 26, one of the three cofounders of the “Date My Friend” series, says that although people in San Francisco try to “tech maxx” their lives, more tech workers with crazy schedules are interested in analog, in-person events to go back to the roots of meeting and creating community. “It’s like, ‘I’m here because I’m not using an AI dating app right now. Like I’m trying to do something different,’” Wulf says.
“I do think it’s maybe popular now to be more anti-tech,” says Lucy Segraves, 28, one of the other cofounders. If someone is working for a company that people see as perpetuating war crimes through their technology, she might be more hesitant to date them.
But ultimately, she says, there are more immediate concerns. “As a person with a non-tech job, I never judge someone if they do work in tech,” Lucy says. “Because that’s unfortunately where the money is, and we’re all just trying to make it in life.”

articles.title: How NVIDIA Open Source Tools Are Helping Researchers Build Next-Generation 6G Networks
articles.text:
A year ago, NVIDIA open sourced its Aerial wireless software, joining Sionna and a broader suite of open source tools for accelerating next-generation 6G network development. Together, they give researchers a foundation for testing ideas, comparing results and building on each other’s work — connecting simulation and AI training with experiments on real over-the-air wireless systems.
Today, researchers and developers are using these tools to build 6G-ready networks that do more than just transmit data — receiving signals more effectively, keeping robots and autonomous systems connected when it matters most, and adapting in real time as devices move through the world.
Over the past year, global developer adoption of NVIDIA AI Aerial and NVIDIA Sionna software has grown 10x, while NVIDIA’s open source 5G/6G tools have surpassed 1 million downloads. More than 8,000 research and academic institutions worldwide are using these platforms.
The projects emerging today offer a view of how future networks could look. Each addresses a different challenge, but together point toward a broader ambition for building AI-native 6G networks that deliver connectivity, computing and sensing over a converged software-defined platform for billions of people, machines and agents.
Networks That Help Robots React Faster
A robot picking up an object needs to understand its surroundings and act before they change. When the AI powering that decision runs on a nearby server or in the cloud, the wireless connection becomes part of the response time.
Researchers are exploring a more efficient approach called goal-oriented semantic communications. Instead of sending full images, robots transmit compact descriptions of objects, their positions and their relationships. Transmitting just as much information as needed allows robots to more quickly respond, especially in dynamic environments like workplaces and warehouses.
At King’s College London, researchers connected a camera-equipped robot arm to an NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin running NVIDIA Sionna, which supports both software-defined 5G network and edge AI processing. In fruit-packing and cube-stacking experiments with deliberately introduced faults, the approach reduced robot task completion time by up to 52.6% and improved task success compared with sending periodic images.
In addition to quicker responses and less processing overhead, the system also proved more resilient — detecting dropped objects, recovering from unsuccessful actions and, in configurations using a digital twin, checking planned movements for potential collisions before execution.
Networks That Learn to Receive Signals Better
For a firefighter receiving live drone footage or a rescue team searching for a missing person, timely images can help guide urgent decisions. But interference and changing radio conditions can make wireless signals harder to decode, causing errors and retransmissions that delay information from the field.
AI receivers address this challenge by learning to recover information from incoming signals more effectively. Better reception could help responders maintain a clearer, more current view of a fire scene or search area.
SoftBank demonstrated this by integrating a neural receiver into NVIDIA Aerial CUDA-Accelerated RAN (ACAR) and testing it with a commercial 5G smartphone. In controlled tests with interference, the neural receiver delivered higher uplink throughput than a conventional receiver at all 15 tested settings, with a maximum gain of roughly 60%.
Another way to improve reception is to teach receivers about the environments where they operate. Using NVIDIA Aerial Testbed, ETH Zurich researchers found that tuning neural receivers using local measurements reduced block error rates by more than one-third compared with selected pretrained versions.
Networks That Learn When to Save Power
As 6G connects more devices and supports more AI applications, managing energy demand will become increasingly important.
For example, a network may need enough capacity to serve a busy stadium, but demand changes when the crowd leaves. AI can help identify when spare capacity can power down — and when it needs to come back online — so operators can reduce electricity use without dropping connections.
At the University of Leeds, researchers developed a system that predicts network demand 10 minutes ahead and uses those forecasts to guide base station sleep decisions. Before powering down, it checks that neighboring active stations can continue serving affected devices and monitors for changes that require capacity to be restored.
The team tested their approach using a portable, NVIDIA DGX Spark-powered 5G “network-in-a-box” alongside a digital twin for validating decisions against real wireless equipment. The result: researchers reported a 45.6% reduction in RAN power consumption relative to a full-power baseline while maintaining device connectivity.
Networks That Can Be Tested Faster — Before They’re Built
Before deploying a network, researchers need to know how it will perform when hundreds of devices compete for connections or radio signals run into interference. Simulating these conditions helps teams evaluate designs before committing to costly equipment and field trials. But realistic simulations can take hours, limiting how many ideas researchers can explore.
The Centre Tecnològic de Telecomunicacions de Catalunya (CTTC) is accelerating that process by bringing GPU-accelerated radio channel models, running on ACAR, into CTTC’s open source 5G-LENA network simulator. These models calculate how wireless signals travel between antennas and devices — a computation that grows increasingly demanding as simulated networks grow.
In an early evaluation, the approach reduced simulation runtime from approximately three hours to 10-20 minutes, depending on the integration, while preserving the expected statistical behavior and network performance.
Faster simulations let researchers compare more designs, investigate more demanding scenarios and refine ideas sooner. As the industry develops 6G, this could shorten the path from a proposed innovation to a thoroughly evaluated network design — helping teams build better connectivity before deploying it in the real world.
At NVIDIA GTC Washington, D.C., attend 6G Developer Sessions where researchers and developers will showcase more innovations shaping the future of wireless networks.
NVIDIA AI Aerial and NVIDIA Sionna are available on GitHub.

articles.title: Pinpointing Location of Videos from Background Airplane Sounds - Schneier on Security
articles.text:
Pinpointing Location of Videos from Background Airplane Sounds
This is fascinating:
The video describes a technique that can reveal where an otherwise unidentifiable recording was made by analyzing its audio for the faint sounds of passing aircraft. The technique is both fascinating and frightening.
It works by looking at Doppler curves, which plot the way a plane’s sound changes as it passes overhead because of the Doppler effect. This is the same familiar Doppler effect that causes the frequency of a siren to rise as it approaches and then fall as it passes by and moves away. More generally, it’s the phenomenon whereby the frequency of a wave perceived by an observer changes when the observer and the source of the wave are moving in relation to one another.
[…]
It’s sound that’s relevant here, though, and specifically the sound of aeroplanes. Early in his video, Colsto brings up a map of the flights that were in the air at the time the video he’s tracing was recorded. Much of this information is publicly available. Aircraft equipped with Automatic Dependent Surveillance–Broadcast (ADS-B) transmit data about their position, velocity, and altitude, which flight-tracking services collect and make available to the public. While not every plane is tracked, the system provides an enormous amount of information about aircraft movements.
Wicked Lad • November 6, 2026 12:16 PM
At the risk of stating the obvious, it seems this would also be useful in evaluating the likelihood that a video was taken where and when it is purported to have been taken.

articles.title: Chip Industry Week In Review
articles.text:
HBM smuggling routes into China; Nvidia H200s held in Hong Kong; Micron pauses Taiwan fab work; Samsung expands HBM base-die capacity; Oracle-Tencent AI chip deal collapses; Bosch builds out semiconductors; S. Korea boosts AI and chip spending; Marvell-Lumentum deal draws scrutiny; more acquisitions, market reports and earnings.
HBM from Samsung and SK hynix is reportedly reaching Chinese AI chip developers through smuggling operations that exploit U.S. export-control loopholes. According to The Information, intermediaries package HBM with low-performance server processors, ship the combined components to China, and then remove the memory for resale, including to customers of Huawei.
Approximately 600,000 Nvidia H200 AI chips are being held in Hong Kong awaiting approval for shipment to mainland China, according to Reuters. Beijing has limited imports in an effort to reduce reliance on U.S. technology and encourage adoption of domestically developed processors.
Micron reportedly paused construction of a $4.5B memory-chip plant in Taiwan due to a prolonged labor dispute, according to Bloomberg. Micron has not confirmed the suspension, and the effect on its longer-term Taiwan manufacturing plans remains unclear.
Samsung Electronics is reportedly planning to expand advanced foundry capacity for HBM base dies at two locations.
Separately, Samsung reportedly secured orders from AMD and Nvidia for 2nm HBM base dies to be produced at a proposed second foundry in Taylor, Texas, with mass production targeted for 2030. Note: Samsung has not confirmed the reported Giheung investment or Taylor customer orders.
Oraclereportedly canceled a 5-year agreement worth an estimated $7B to provide Tencent access to up to 100,000 advanced AI chips through data centers in Southeast Asia, following pressure from the Trump administration, according to the Financial Times. U.S. officials raised concerns about Chinese companies accessing advanced processors through overseas cloud services, while officials in China’s Guangdong province urged Tencent to use domestically developed chips.
Bosch plans to establish a dedicated semiconductor division in January 2028, expanding its foundry business and opening more manufacturing capacity to external customers. The company is targeting €5B in semiconductor sales by 2030 and plans to expand its semiconductor test center in Penang, Malaysia, by the mid-2030s.
Marvell‘s pending acquisition of Lumentum, initially valued at $115B, is drawing mixed reactions, with analysts seeing opportunities to challenge Broadcom in AI optical interconnects, but also raising concerns about supplier concentration and customer relationships. Questions about the purchase price and regulatory approval have added to investor concerns.
U.S. election results raised concerns about tighter restrictions on data center development, particularly in major markets such as Texas and Ohio, as well as increased congressional oversight of AI, including AI safety, cybersecurity, and industry practices. Restrictions that delay or reduce data center construction could weaken demand for AI accelerators, HBM, and networking chips, and increased regulatory scrutiny could create additional uncertainty for AI infrastructure investment. (See chip stock impacts here.)
More acquisitions and deals
Onsemiconfirmed it plans to acquireFerric, developer of integrated voltage regulators, for $600M in cash, plus up to $175M in milestone payments.
EntegrisacquiredAdvanced Abrasives and announced plans for a new SiC materials manufacturing line in Taiwan. The company also partnered with Element Six to develop diamond-based thermal-management materials for advanced packaging and expanded its deal with Kioxia on BiCS Flash 3D flash memory.
Supermicro is initially planning to use 10,000 SambaNova SN50 RDUs for its new AI disaggregated inference systems as part of a strategic collaboration.
AI data centers are moving toward 800 VDC power distribution as rack power rises toward megawatt levels, with Nvidia, Google, Microsoft and other industry participants working through OCP on common architectures and interfaces.
Events and Webinars— ACM/IEEE ICCAD, Electronica & SEMICON Europe. Webinars on shift left, verification, and debug of high-power motor controllers.
Global
Americas
UC San Diego and Qualcomm launched a $750K AI-driven chip-design research initiative, funded by a $500K Qualcomm gift and $250K in UCSD matching funds, focused on AI methods for SoC design, processor architectures, hardware accelerators, memory systems, and interconnects.
CSIS examines Albany NanoTech as a model for semiconductor technology clusters, highlighting shared R&D infrastructure, industry partnerships, and workforce development supporting sub-2nm technologies, advanced packaging, photonics, and quantum systems.
The OCPFoundation is opening nominations for project leads across all 12 top-level OCP Projects, ranging from hardware management to the AI computing continuum.
Europe
The European Semiconductor Industry Association (ESIA) called for dedicated semiconductor funding under the EU’s 2028–2034 budget, including support for R&D, pilot production, advanced packaging, and industrial deployment. The association urged policymakers to coordinate national and EU funding, preserve the Chips Joint Undertaking’s cross-sector role, and ease restrictions on intellectual property transfers within multinational companies.
Synopsys and the EU Chips JU signed a deal to expand access to its EDA software for semiconductor startups and research teams through the EuroCDP.
Asia
South Korea reaffirmed plans to spend ₩21.3T (US$16B) on AI and major initiatives covering semiconductors, physical AI, and data centers, in its proposed 2027 budget, nearly doubling this year’s allocation.
Panasonic Industry plans to invest about ¥92B ($583M) to expand AI-related materials production and R&D, including circuit-board materials, capacitors and semiconductor packaging materials.
Two workers were killed and five injured in an explosion and fire at Panasonic Industrial Devices Materials‘ factory in Hsinchu, Taiwan. The facility produces PCB and semiconductor packaging materials. The cause and production impact have not been determined yet.
South Korea’s Techwing plans to invest approximately ₩52.6B ($39M) in a new semiconductor equipment factory in Cheonan to expand production of memory test handlers and HBM cube probers.
Infineon introduced its first automotive MCU platform based on the RISC-V architecture, adding hardware-based physical protection and crypto agility, with support planned for post-quantum security requirements.
Infineon and Qualcomm are collaborating on a microcontroller-based subsystem for Snapdragon Ride reference platforms used in central car computers for automated driving and digital cockpit applications.
STMicro announced a new microcontroller portfolio covering industrial, automotive, and physical AI applications.
Test, measurement
Keysight released XR3, a low-profile 14-bit oscilloscope designed to increase measurement capacity in rack-based test systems.
Siemens introduced an automated component model extraction solution developed with Bosch that cuts frequency-response-function measurement time by up to 93% and produces ISO 20270-compliant models for virtual NVH development.
Cerabyte completed S3 integration testing of its ceramic data storage within established object-storage workflows, in collaboration with CERN openlab.
Design
Arteris exceeded 1,000 customer silicon design starts using its interconnect IP, and released a report showing the evolution of SoC, ASIC, FPGA, and MCU designs across key markets.
Research
MCL, PVA TePla and ASE researchers developed an AI-based image-enhancement method for detecting flip-chip interconnect defects. By improving scanning acoustic microscopy images, the method increased detection of cracks and delamination in extreme-low-k dielectric layers from 5.2% to 100% in tests involving 19 defects across three packages.
TU Munich, Applied Materials et al. evaluated cryogenic 2nm GAA transistors and superconducting interconnects for energy-efficient AI computing. Using a calibrated chip-design flow, they reported a 3x performance increase and 7.7x improvement in energy efficiency for a modeled AI accelerator’s compute fabric, excluding memory, data movement, and refrigeration power.
ETH Zurich-led researchers benchmarked 10 commercial sub-watt edge AI devices, comparing inference performance and energy consumption across convolutional neural networks and small vision transformers. The study found that memory traffic, rather than computational workload, was the primary factor determining latency on the tested neural-network accelerators, highlighting the importance of data movement in low-power AI hardware design.
HUST and PolyU researchers developed annealing-free ferroelectric transistors with ultrathin oxide-semiconductor channels for NVM and neuromorphic computing. The devices achieved a memory window of up to 20.6V, endurance of 10⁶ cycles, and stable 6-bit operation across 64 states. A neuromorphic network evaluation achieved 93.02% recognition accuracy.
AMD issued security bulletins covering a newly discovered EDK II PXE driver vulnerability that can allow pre-boot code execution and a contention-based side-channel technique for exploiting known vulnerabilities in AMD CPUs.
Dell issued BIOS updates for a critical Qualcomm chipset vulnerability affecting five Latitude, Inspiron, and XPS systems. The flaw can cause memory corruption when a malformed RSA key is imported into Qualcomm’s Keystore.
Google banned Videostrong Technology from making certified Android devices after its security researchers determined that the company was responsible for creating an XCPE backdoor that enrolled 1.3 million set-top boxes into a criminal botnet.
Vietnam has its first-ever homegrown security chip after government-backed Viettel Group successfully integrated a domestically developed cryptographic algorithm into silicon.
u-blox announced that it will integrate Kudelski Labs’ embedded security IP into its future chipsets.
Chinese tech giant Tencent released Hy4, its powerful new open-source AI model. Amid growing concerns about agentic hacking, the company said it limited the model’s cybersecurity training data to defensive material only.
Security technical papers
NC State and Princeton researchers proposed a 3D-stacked hardware shield to protect post-quantum cryptography accelerators from side-channel attacks. The design stacks a guard layer above the cryptographic hardware, using decoy-key activity and physical shielding to obscure power leakage from NTT computations.
Accelerating Plug-And-Play Prototyping In Chiplet-Based Designs: Purna Mohanty, CEO of SignatureIP, talks about the impact of chiplets and shared memory resources, the challenges of version control across multiple flavors of I/O, and the challenges engineering teams face when hardware-accelerated tools are running at different speeds than the actual design.
Quantum Hardware
New launches
Universal Quantum launched its iQPU quantum processor, combining a large trapped-ion compute surface, ultra-low-noise integrated control electronics, and chip-to-chip interfaces designed to scale quantum computing systems. The processor is manufactured on a commercial 200mm semiconductor production line.
IBM, ORNL, and AMD opened a new co-design platform for quantum error correction at IBM’s quantum facility in New York, co-locating the 120-qubit IBM Quantum Nighthawk with ORNL’s Umbra HPC system.
Fig. 1: ORNL’s Umbra HPC system. Source: Oak Ridge National Lab
Advances
Researchers from Quantum Motion, UCL, and others demonstrated a superconducting circuit element fabricated using a commercial CMOS process. The titanium-nitride device functions as a compact superinductor and was integrated with a silicon quantum dot to enable sensitive RF charge detection, potentially supporting more compact readout hardware for semiconductor spin qubits.
University of Regensburg-led researchers demonstrated a real-time feedback technique that reduced superconducting-qubit operation errors by approximately 54%, from 0.14% to 0.065%. The approach identifies changes in qubit resonance frequency associated with material defects and adjusts control signals to improve reliability.
Alice & Bob reported extended bit-flip lifetimes in superconducting cat qubits, averaging 44 minutes on a single-qubit test device and reaching 189 to 252 minutes on selected qubits in its 12-qubit Helium 2 processor. The preliminary results demonstrate strong suppression of bit-flip errors during idle operation, with performance during error-correction operations still to be validated.
Workforce, Education
The U.S. Department of Labor opened applications for a $40M apprenticeship incentive fund that includes semiconductor fabrication among several high-growth sectors. Registered apprenticeship sponsors can receive up to $6K per eligible new apprentice.
UCLA named the first 10 doctoral fellows in its Semiconductor Hub, with research spanning 3D ICs, advanced packaging, silicon photonics, compute-in-memory, and AI hardware. Fellows will also intern with one of the Hub’s industry partners, including Synopsys, GlobalFoundries, and others.
In a new Semiconductor Engineering roundtable, industry experts discuss how AI is changing expectations for new engineering graduates. Demand for electrical engineers remains strong, but AI agents are taking over some traditional junior-level tasks, raising expectations for practical experience, AI fluency, and the ability to tackle higher-level engineering work earlier in their careers.
U.S. community colleges are expanding semiconductor technician training programs as the industry faces a potential shortage of 157,000 workers by 2030, according to the Associated Press. More than 200 colleges and universities are coordinating with semiconductor manufacturers, including TSMC, Intel, Samsung, and SK hynix, to develop hands-on training programs supporting new U.S. fabs.
